shlokas.sanskrit: त्वष्टा॑रं वा॒युमृ॑भवो॒ य ओह॑ते॒ दैव्या॒ होता॑रा उ॒षसं॑ स्व॒स्तये॑ । बृह॒स्पतिं॑ वृत्रखा॒दं सु॑मे॒धस॑मिन्द्रि॒यं सोमं॑ धन॒सा उ॑ ईमहे
shlokas.transliteration: tváṣṭāram ǀ vāyúm ǀ ṛbhavaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ óhate ǀ dáivyā ǀ hótārau ǀ uṣásam ǀ svastáye ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ vṛtra-khādám ǀ su-medhásam ǀ indriyám ǀ sómam ǀ dhana-sā́ḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ īmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Desirous of wealth, we solicit thatSoma, the fried ofIndra, who for your welfare,Ṛbhus, brings(hither)Tvaṣṭā,Vāyu, the two divine sacrificers (theAśvins), Dawn,Bṛhaspati, and the wise slayer ofVṛtra.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ब्रह्म॒ गामश्वं॑ ज॒नय॑न्त॒ ओष॑धी॒र्वन॒स्पती॑न्पृथि॒वीं पर्व॑ताँ अ॒पः । सूर्यं॑ दि॒वि रो॒हय॑न्तः सु॒दान॑व॒ आर्या॑ व्र॒ता वि॑सृ॒जन्तो॒ अधि॒ क्षमि॑
shlokas.transliteration: bráhma ǀ gā́m ǀ áśvam ǀ janáyantaḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ vánaspátīn ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ párvatān ǀ apáḥ ǀsū́ryam ǀ diví ǀ roháyantaḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀ ā́ryā ǀ vratā́ ǀ vi-sṛjántaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ kṣámi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “genitive rating food, cows, horses, plural nts, trees, the earth, mountains and waters, elevating the sun inheaven, munificent, promoting sacred observances upon the earth, (they abide everywhere).”

shlokas.sanskrit: भु॒ज्युमंह॑सः पिपृथो॒ निर॑श्विना॒ श्यावं॑ पु॒त्रं व॑ध्रिम॒त्या अ॑जिन्वतम् । क॒म॒द्युवं॑ विम॒दायो॑हथुर्यु॒वं वि॑ष्णा॒प्वं१॒॑ विश्व॑का॒याव॑ सृजथः
shlokas.transliteration: bhujyúm ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǀ pipṛthaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ aśvinā ǀ śyā́vam ǀ putrám ǀ vadhri-matyā́ḥ ǀ ajinvatam ǀkama-dyúvam ǀ vi-madā́ya ǀ ūhathuḥ ǀ yuvám ǀ viṣṇāpvám ǀ víśvakāya ǀ áva ǀ sṛjathaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Aśvins, extricatedBhujyufrom calamity, you gave toVadhrimatīher sonŚyāva; you gaveKamadyu (as a wife) toVimada; you restored (the lost) Viṣṇāpu toViśvaka.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पावी॑रवी तन्य॒तुरेक॑पाद॒जो दि॒वो ध॒र्ता सिन्धु॒राप॑: समु॒द्रिय॑: । विश्वे॑ दे॒वास॑: शृणव॒न्वचां॑सि मे॒ सर॑स्वती स॒ह धी॒भिः पुरं॑ध्या
shlokas.transliteration: pā́vīravī ǀ tanyatúḥ ǀ éka-pāt ǀ ajáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ dhartā́ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ samudríyaḥ ǀvíśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ śṛṇavan ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ me ǀ sárasvatī ǀ sahá ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ púram-dhyā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the armed and thundering (voice of mid-heaven), the upholder of heaven, Aja Ekapād, theocean, the waters of the firmament, the universal gods andSarasvatī, accompanied by sacred rites, andabundant wisdom, hear my words.”

shlokas.sanskrit: विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः स॒ह धी॒भिः पुरं॑ध्या॒ मनो॒र्यज॑त्रा अ॒मृता॑ ऋत॒ज्ञाः । रा॒ति॒षाचो॑ अभि॒षाच॑: स्व॒र्विद॒: स्व१॒॑र्गिरो॒ ब्रह्म॑ सू॒क्तं जु॑षेरत
shlokas.transliteration: víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sahá ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ púram-dhyā ǀ mánoḥ ǀ yájatrāḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀrāti-sā́caḥ ǀ abhi-sā́caḥ ǀ svaḥ-vídaḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ bráhma ǀ su-uktám ǀ juṣerata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the universal gods, accompanied by sacred rites and abundant wisdom, adorable (at thesacrifice) of men, immortal, the knowers of truth, waiting on the oblation to be given, arriving together (at thesacrifice), omniscient, graciously accept all our praises and abundant food with well-sung hymns.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वान्वसि॑ष्ठो अ॒मृता॑न्ववन्दे॒ ये विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒भि प्र॑त॒स्थुः । ते नो॑ रासन्तामुरुगा॒यम॒द्य यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः
shlokas.transliteration: devā́n ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ amṛ́tān ǀ vavande ǀ yé ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhí ǀ pra-tasthúḥ ǀté ǀ naḥ ǀ rāsantām ǀ uru-gāyám ǀ adyá ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Descendant of)Vasiṣṭha, I have glorified the immortal gods who preside over all worlds; may theythis day bestow upon us widely-famed food; do you always cherish us with blessings.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वान्हु॑वे बृ॒हच्छ्र॑वसः स्व॒स्तये॑ ज्योति॒ष्कृतो॑ अध्व॒रस्य॒ प्रचे॑तसः । ये वा॑वृ॒धुः प्र॑त॒रं वि॒श्ववे॑दस॒ इन्द्र॑ज्येष्ठासो अ॒मृता॑ ऋता॒वृध॑:
shlokas.transliteration: devā́n ǀ huve ǀ bṛhát-śravasaḥ ǀ svastáye ǀ jyotiḥ-kṛ́taḥ ǀ adhvarásya ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀyé ǀ vavṛdhúḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ viśvá-vedasaḥ ǀ índra-jyeṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ ṛta-vṛ́dhaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I invoke for the success of the sacrifice the gods, who bestow abundant food, the diffusers of light, theextremely wise who flourish mightily, abounding in all riches, havingIndraas their chief, immortal, augmented bysacrifice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑प्रसूता॒ वरु॑णप्रशिष्टा॒ ये सूर्य॑स्य॒ ज्योति॑षो भा॒गमा॑न॒शुः । म॒रुद्ग॑णे वृ॒जने॒ मन्म॑ धीमहि॒ माघो॑ने य॒ज्ञं ज॑नयन्त सू॒रय॑:
shlokas.transliteration: índra-prasūtāḥ ǀ váruṇa-praśiṣṭāḥ ǀ yé ǀ sū́ryasya ǀ jyótiṣaḥ ǀ bhāgám ǀ ānaśúḥ ǀmarút-gaṇe ǀ vṛjáne ǀ mánma ǀ dhīmahi ǀ mā́ghone ǀ yajñám ǀ janayanta ǀ sūráyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We offer praise to the company of theMaruts, the attendants uponMaghavan, who, encouraged byIndra, and instrumental ucted byVaruṇa, have acquired a portion of the light of the sun; the wise worshippers beget thesacrifice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॒ वसु॑भि॒: परि॑ पातु नो॒ गय॑मादि॒त्यैर्नो॒ अदि॑ति॒: शर्म॑ यच्छतु । रु॒द्रो रु॒द्रेभि॑र्दे॒वो मृ॑ळयाति न॒स्त्वष्टा॑ नो॒ ग्नाभि॑: सुवि॒ताय॑ जिन्वतु
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ pári ǀ pātu ǀ naḥ ǀ gáyam ǀ ādityáiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatu ǀrudráḥ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ mṛḷayāti ǀ naḥ ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ naḥ ǀ gnā́bhiḥ ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ jinvatu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayIndrawith theVasusguard our dwelling; mayAditiwith theĀdityasgrant us felicity; may thedivineRudrawith theRudrasmake us happy;mayTvaṣṭāwith the wives of the gods be favourable to us forour prosperity.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अदि॑ति॒र्द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ऋ॒तं म॒हदिन्द्रा॒विष्णू॑ म॒रुत॒: स्व॑र्बृ॒हत् । दे॒वाँ आ॑दि॒त्याँ अव॑से हवामहे॒ वसू॑न्रु॒द्रान्त्स॑वि॒तारं॑ सु॒दंस॑सम्
shlokas.transliteration: áditiḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ṛtám ǀ mahát ǀ índrāvíṣṇū íti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ bṛhát ǀdevā́n ǀ ādityā́n ǀ ávase ǀ havāmahe ǀ vásūn ǀ rudrā́n ǀ savitā́ram ǀ su-dáṃsasam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Aditi, heaven and earth, the mighty Truth (Agni),Indra,Viṣṇu, theMaruts, the great sun-- (these) weinvoke for our protection, as well as the divineĀdityas, theVasus, theRudras, andSavitā, the accomplisher ofgood works.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सर॑स्वान्धी॒भिर्वरु॑णो धृ॒तव्र॑तः पू॒षा विष्णु॑र्महि॒मा वा॒युर॒श्विना॑ । ब्र॒ह्म॒कृतो॑ अ॒मृता॑ वि॒श्ववे॑दस॒: शर्म॑ नो यंसन्त्रि॒वरू॑थ॒मंह॑सः
shlokas.transliteration: sárasvān ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ dhṛtá-vrataḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ mahimā́ ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀbrahma-kṛ́taḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ viśvá-vedasaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ naḥ ǀ yaṃsan ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MaySarasvatī, (endowed) with intelligences,Varuṇathe observer of oblations,Pūṣan,Viṣṇu, themightyVāyu, theAśvins, (may these) the bestowers of food upon worshippers, immortal, the possessors of allwealth, grant us a habitation triply-guarded from evil.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वृषा॑ य॒ज्ञो वृष॑णः सन्तु य॒ज्ञिया॒ वृष॑णो दे॒वा वृष॑णो हवि॒ष्कृत॑: । वृष॑णा॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ऋ॒ताव॑री॒ वृषा॑ प॒र्जन्यो॒ वृष॑णो वृष॒स्तुभ॑:
shlokas.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ santu ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ haviḥ-kṛ́taḥ ǀvṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ṛtávarī ítyṛtá-varī ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ parjányaḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ vṛṣa-stúbhaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May our sacrifice be the showerer (of benefits); may the gods who are worthy of sacrifice be theshowerers (of benefits); may the priest, may the presenters of the oblation, be the showerers (of benefits); mayheaven and earth receiving adoration be the showerers (of benefits); mayParjanyabe the showerer (of rain);may those who praise (the gods) with showers be showerers.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्नीषोमा॒ वृष॑णा॒ वाज॑सातये पुरुप्रश॒स्ता वृष॑णा॒ उप॑ ब्रुवे । यावी॑जि॒रे वृष॑णो देवय॒ज्यया॒ ता न॒: शर्म॑ त्रि॒वरू॑थं॒ वि यं॑सतः
shlokas.transliteration: agnī́ṣómā ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀ puru-praśastā́ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇau ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀyáu ǀ ījiré ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ deva-yajyáyā ǀ tā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ śárma ǀ tri-várūtham ǀ ví ǀ yaṃsataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I glorify for the obtaining of food the two showerers (of benefits),AgniandSoma, the many-laudedshowerers (of benefits), may these two whom the priests have worshipped with divine worship bestow upon us atriply-guarded dwelling.”

shlokas.sanskrit: धृ॒तव्र॑ताः क्ष॒त्रिया॑ यज्ञनि॒ष्कृतो॑ बृहद्दि॒वा अ॑ध्व॒राणा॑मभि॒श्रिय॑: । अ॒ग्निहो॑तार ऋत॒सापो॑ अ॒द्रुहो॒ऽपो अ॑सृज॒न्ननु॑ वृत्र॒तूर्ये॑
shlokas.transliteration: dhṛtá-vratāḥ ǀ kṣatríyāḥ ǀ yajñaniḥ-kṛ́taḥ ǀ bṛhat-divā́ḥ ǀ adhvarā́ṇām ǀ abhi-śríyaḥ ǀagní-hotāraḥ ǀ ṛta-sā́paḥ ǀ adrúhaḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ asṛ́jan ǀ ánu ǀ vṛtra-tū́rye ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The (gods) observing obligations endowed with vigour, developers of sacrifice, possessed ofabundant brightness, the defenders of sacrifices, havingAgnifor their priest, enjoying truth, unassailable, setfree the waters at the combat with theVṛtra.”

shlokas.sanskrit: द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी ज॑नयन्न॒भि व्र॒ताप॒ ओष॑धीर्व॒निना॑नि य॒ज्ञिया॑ । अ॒न्तरि॑क्षं॒ स्व१॒॑रा प॑प्रुरू॒तये॒ वशं॑ दे॒वास॑स्त॒न्वी॒३॒॑ नि मा॑मृजुः
shlokas.transliteration: dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ janayan ǀ abhí ǀ vratā́ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ vanínāni ǀ yajñíyā ǀantárikṣam ǀ sváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ papruḥ ǀ ūtáye ǀ váśam ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ tanví ǀ ní ǀ mamṛjuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods engendered the heaven and earth with their respective functions, the waters, the plural nts, thesacred trees; they filled the whole firmament (with lustre) for its protection; they graced the desirable (sacrifice) intheir own person ns.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ध॒र्तारो॑ दि॒व ऋ॒भव॑: सु॒हस्ता॑ वातापर्ज॒न्या म॑हि॒षस्य॑ तन्य॒तोः । आप॒ ओष॑धी॒: प्र ति॑रन्तु नो॒ गिरो॒ भगो॑ रा॒तिर्वा॒जिनो॑ यन्तु मे॒ हव॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: dhartā́raḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ su-hástāḥ ǀ vātāparjanyā́ ǀ mahiṣásya ǀ tanyatóḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ prá ǀ tirantu ǀ naḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ rātíḥ ǀ vājínaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ me ǀ hávam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the upholders of the sky, the radiant with truth, the well-armed deities,VātaandParjanya, (theutterers) of the mighty thunder, the waters, the plural nts, amplify our praises; may the liberalBhagaand Vājinscome to my invocation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒मु॒द्रः सिन्धू॒ रजो॑ अ॒न्तरि॑क्षम॒ज एक॑पात्तनयि॒त्नुर॑र्ण॒वः । अहि॑र्बु॒ध्न्य॑: शृणव॒द्वचां॑सि मे॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वास॑ उ॒त सू॒रयो॒ मम॑
shlokas.transliteration: samudráḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ rájaḥ ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ajáḥ ǀ éka-pāt ǀ tanayitnúḥ ǀ arṇaváḥ ǀáhiḥ ǀ budhnyáḥ ǀ śṛṇavat ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ me ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ utá ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ máma ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the flowingSindhu, the atmosphere, the firmament, Aja Ekapād, the rain-bearing thunder-cloud,andAhirbudhnyahear my words; may the wise universal gods (listen to) my (praises).”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्याम॑ वो॒ मन॑वो दे॒ववी॑तये॒ प्राञ्चं॑ नो य॒ज्ञं प्र ण॑यत साधु॒या । आदि॑त्या॒ रुद्रा॒ वस॑व॒: सुदा॑नव इ॒मा ब्रह्म॑ श॒स्यमा॑नानि जिन्वत
shlokas.transliteration: syā́ma ǀ vaḥ ǀ mánavaḥ ǀ devá-vītaye ǀ prā́ñcam ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ prá ǀ nayata ǀ sādhu-yā́ ǀā́dityāḥ ǀ rúdrāḥ ǀ vásavaḥ ǀ sú-dānavaḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ bráhma ǀ śasyámānāni ǀ jinvata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May we men be (diligent in providing) for your food, (O gods); conduct our ancient sacrifice to asuccessful end,Ādityas,Rudras, and genitive rousVasus, graciously accept these hymns which are being recited.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दैव्या॒ होता॑रा प्रथ॒मा पु॒रोहि॑त ऋ॒तस्य॒ पन्था॒मन्वे॑मि साधु॒या । क्षेत्र॑स्य॒ पतिं॒ प्रति॑वेशमीमहे॒ विश्वा॑न्दे॒वाँ अ॒मृताँ॒ अप्र॑युच्छतः
shlokas.transliteration: dáivyā ǀ hótārā ǀ prathamā́ ǀ puráḥ-hitā ǀ ṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǀ ánu ǀ emi ǀ sādhu-yā́ ǀkṣétrasya ǀ pátim ǀ práti-veśam ǀ īmahe ǀ víśvān ǀ devā́n ǀ amṛ́tān ǀ ápra-yucchataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I follow the two chief priests the divine offerers of burnt sacrifices, (I follow) successfully the path ofsacrifice; we solicit (wealth of) the contiguous lord of the field, and the immortal and not unheeding universaldeities.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वसि॑ष्ठासः पितृ॒वद्वाच॑मक्रत दे॒वाँ ईळा॑ना ऋषि॒वत्स्व॒स्तये॑ । प्री॒ता इ॑व ज्ञा॒तय॒: काम॒मेत्या॒स्मे दे॑वा॒सोऽव॑ धूनुता॒ वसु॑
shlokas.transliteration: vásiṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ pitṛ-vát ǀ vā́cam ǀ akrata ǀ devā́n ǀ ī́ḷānāḥ ǀ ṛṣi-vát ǀ svastáye ǀprītā́ḥ-iva ǀ jñātáyaḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ ā-ítya ǀ asmé íti ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ áva ǀ dhūnuta ǀ vásu ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वान्वसि॑ष्ठो अ॒मृता॑न्ववन्दे॒ ये विश्वा॒ भुव॑ना॒भि प्र॑त॒स्थुः । ते नो॑ रासन्तामुरुगा॒यम॒द्य यू॒यं पा॑त स्व॒स्तिभि॒: सदा॑ नः
shlokas.transliteration: devā́n ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀ amṛ́tān ǀ vavande ǀ yé ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhí ǀ pra-tasthúḥ ǀté ǀ naḥ ǀ rāsantām ǀ uru-gāyám ǀ adyá ǀ yūyám ǀ pāta ǀ svastí-bhiḥ ǀ sádā ǀ naḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Descendant of)Vasiṣṭha, I have glorified the immortal gods who preside over all the worlds; maythey this day bestow upon us widely-famed food; do you always cherish us with blessings.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मां धियं॑ स॒प्तशी॑र्ष्णीं पि॒ता न॑ ऋ॒तप्र॑जातां बृह॒तीम॑विन्दत् । तु॒रीयं॑ स्विज्जनयद्वि॒श्वज॑न्यो॒ऽयास्य॑ उ॒क्थमिन्द्रा॑य॒ शंस॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: imā́m ǀ dhíyam ǀ saptá-śīrṣṇīm ǀ pitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ṛtá-prajātām ǀ bṛhatī́m ǀ avindat ǀturī́yam ǀ svit ǀ janayat ǀ viśvá-janyaḥ ǀ ayā́syaḥ ǀ ukthám ǀ índrāya ǀ śáṃsan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “This great seven-headed ceremony, born of truth our father (Aṅgirasa) discovered;Ayāsya, thefrined of all races, engendered the fourth (genitive ration), reciting a hymn toIndra.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒तं शंस॑न्त ऋ॒जु दीध्या॑ना दि॒वस्पु॒त्रासो॒ असु॑रस्य वी॒राः । विप्रं॑ प॒दमङ्गि॑रसो॒ दधा॑ना य॒ज्ञस्य॒ धाम॑ प्रथ॒मं म॑नन्त
shlokas.transliteration: ṛtám ǀ śáṃsantaḥ ǀ ṛjú ǀ dī́dhyānāḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀvípram ǀ padám ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ yajñásya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ prathamám ǀ mananta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Reciting sincere praise, reflecting correctly, theAṅgirasas, the pious sons of the brilliant and powerful(Agni), upholding the intelligent base, the supporter of the sacrifice, praise from the beginning.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हं॒सैरि॑व॒ सखि॑भि॒र्वाव॑दद्भिरश्म॒न्मया॑नि॒ नह॑ना॒ व्यस्य॑न् । बृह॒स्पति॑रभि॒कनि॑क्रद॒द्गा उ॒त प्रास्तौ॒दुच्च॑ वि॒द्वाँ अ॑गायत्
shlokas.transliteration: haṃsáiḥ-iva ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ vā́vadat-bhiḥ ǀ aśman-máyāni ǀ náhanā ǀ vi-ásyan ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ abhi-kánikradat ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ prá ǀ astaut ǀ út ǀ ca ǀ vidvā́n ǀ agāyat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “With his friends (theMaruts) clamouring like geese, throwing open the (asuras') cattle-folds made ofstone,Bṛhaspaticalling aloud (desires to carry off) the cows; knowing all things he praises (the gods) andchants (their laudation).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒वो द्वाभ्यां॑ प॒र एक॑या॒ गा गुहा॒ तिष्ठ॑न्ती॒रनृ॑तस्य॒ सेतौ॑ । बृह॒स्पति॒स्तम॑सि॒ ज्योति॑रि॒च्छन्नुदु॒स्रा आक॒र्वि हि ति॒स्र आव॑:
shlokas.transliteration: aváḥ ǀ dvā́bhyām ǀ paráḥ ǀ ékayā ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ gúhā ǀ tíṣṭhantīḥ ǀ ánṛtasya ǀ sétau ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ támasi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ icchán ǀ út ǀ usrā́ḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ akaḥ ǀ ví ǀ hí ǀ tisráḥ ǀ ā́varítyāvaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bṛhaspatipurposing to bring light into the darkness drove out the cows standing in the cave in theplace of darkness below by two (ways), and those above by one (way); he opened the three (doors of the”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒भिद्या॒ पुरं॑ श॒यथे॒मपा॑चीं॒ निस्त्रीणि॑ सा॒कमु॑द॒धेर॑कृन्तत् । बृह॒स्पति॑रु॒षसं॒ सूर्यं॒ गाम॒र्कं वि॑वेद स्त॒नय॑न्निव॒ द्यौः
shlokas.transliteration: vi-bhídya ǀ púram ǀ śayáthā ǀ īm ǀ ápācīm ǀ níḥ ǀ trī́ṇi ǀ sākám ǀ uda-dhéḥ ǀ akṛntat ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ uṣásam ǀ sū́ryam ǀ gā́m ǀ arkám ǀ viveda ǀ stanáyan-iva ǀ dyáuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Resting near it, demolishing the western city,Bṛhaspatiwrested at once fromValathe three, thedawn, the sun, the cow; thundering like the heaven, he proclaimed the adorable (Sun).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ व॒लं र॑क्षि॒तारं॒ दुघा॑नां क॒रेणे॑व॒ वि च॑कर्ता॒ रवे॑ण । स्वेदा॑ञ्जिभिरा॒शिर॑मि॒च्छमा॒नोऽरो॑दयत्प॒णिमा गा अ॑मुष्णात्
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ valám ǀ rakṣitā́ram ǀ dúghānām ǀ karéṇa-iva ǀ ví ǀ cakarta ǀ ráveṇa ǀsvédāñji-bhiḥ ǀ ā-śíram ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ árodayat ǀ paṇím ǀ ā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ amuṣṇāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrawith his voice as with an (armed)handcloveValathe defender of hte kine; desirous of themixture (of milk andSoma) he with (theMaruts)k, who were shining with person iration, destroyedPaṇiandliberated the cows.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स ईं॑ स॒त्येभि॒: सखि॑भिः शु॒चद्भि॒र्गोधा॑यसं॒ वि ध॑न॒सैर॑दर्दः । ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पति॒र्वृष॑भिर्व॒राहै॑र्घ॒र्मस्वे॑देभि॒र्द्रवि॑णं॒ व्या॑नट्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ īm ǀ satyébhiḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ śucát-bhiḥ ǀ gó-dhāyasam ǀ ví ǀ dhana-sáiḥ ǀ adardarítyadardaḥ ǀbráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣa-bhiḥ ǀ varā́haiḥ ǀ gharmá-svedebhiḥ ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ví ǀ ānaṭ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Together with his true brilliant wealth-winning friendly (Maruts) he destroyed the detainer of the cows;Brahmaṇaspati, with the showerers (of benefits), the conveyers of desirable (water), the frequenters of sacrifice,acquired wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते स॒त्येन॒ मन॑सा॒ गोप॑तिं॒ गा इ॑या॒नास॑ इषणयन्त धी॒भिः । बृह॒स्पति॑र्मि॒थोअ॑वद्यपेभि॒रुदु॒स्रिया॑ असृजत स्व॒युग्भि॑:
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ satyéna ǀ mánasā ǀ gó-patim ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ iyānā́saḥ ǀ iṣaṇayanta ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ mitháḥ-avadyapebhiḥ ǀ út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ asṛjata ǀ svayúk-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They with truthful mind searching for the cows resolved by their exploits to make him the lord of cattle;Bṛhaspatiwith his self-yoked (allied) mutually defending each other from reproach, set free the kind.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तं व॒र्धय॑न्तो म॒तिभि॑: शि॒वाभि॑: सिं॒हमि॑व॒ नान॑दतं स॒धस्थे॑ । बृह॒स्पतिं॒ वृष॑णं॒ शूर॑सातौ॒ भरे॑भरे॒ अनु॑ मदेम जि॒ष्णुम्
shlokas.transliteration: tám ǀ vardháyantaḥ ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ śivā́bhiḥ ǀ siṃhám-iva ǀ nā́nadatam ǀ sadhá-sthe ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ śū́ra-sātau ǀ bháre-bhare ǀ ánu ǀ madema ǀ jiṣṇúm ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Magnifying the victoriousBṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits), roaring in mid-heaven like a lion, letus praise him in the conflicts where heroes win, with auspicious praises.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒दा वाज॒मस॑नद्वि॒श्वरू॑प॒मा द्यामरु॑क्ष॒दुत्त॑राणि॒ सद्म॑ । बृह॒स्पतिं॒ वृष॑णं व॒र्धय॑न्तो॒ नाना॒ सन्तो॒ बिभ्र॑तो॒ ज्योति॑रा॒सा
shlokas.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ vā́jam ǀ ásanat ǀ viśvá-rūpam ǀ ā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ árukṣat ǀ út-tarāṇi ǀ sádma ǀbṛ́haspátim ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇam ǀ vardháyantaḥ ǀ nā́nā ǀ sántaḥ ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ āsā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When he acquires food of various kinds, when he ascends the sky or the northern stations, (the godsare) extollingBṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits), with their mouth, being in various (quarters), bearing light.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒त्यामा॒शिषं॑ कृणुता वयो॒धै की॒रिं चि॒द्ध्यव॑थ॒ स्वेभि॒रेवै॑: । प॒श्चा मृधो॒ अप॑ भवन्तु॒ विश्वा॒स्तद्रो॑दसी शृणुतं विश्वमि॒न्वे
shlokas.transliteration: satyā́m ǀ ā-śíṣam ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ vayaḥ-dhái ǀ kīrím ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ ávatha ǀ svébhiḥ ǀ évaiḥ ǀpaścā́ ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ bhavantu ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ tát ǀ rodasī íti ǀ śṛṇutam ǀ viśvaminvé íti viśvam-invé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Make good our prayer for the bestowal of food; you protect through your movements even (me) yourprayer).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ म॒ह्ना म॑ह॒तो अ॑र्ण॒वस्य॒ वि मू॒र्धान॑मभिनदर्बु॒दस्य॑ । अह॒न्नहि॒मरि॑णात्स॒प्त सिन्धू॑न्दे॒वैर्द्या॑वापृथिवी॒ प्राव॑तं नः
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ arṇavásya ǀ ví ǀ mūrdhā́nam ǀ abhinat ǀ arbudásya ǀáhan ǀ áhim ǀ áriṇāt ǀ saptá ǀ síndhūn ǀ deváiḥ ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ prá ǀ avatam ǀ naḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indraby his might has cleft the brow of the vast watery cloud, he has slain Ahi; he has made the sevenrivers flow; do you, heaven and earth, along with the gods, protect us.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒द॒प्रुतो॒ न वयो॒ रक्ष॑माणा॒ वाव॑दतो अ॒भ्रिय॑स्येव॒ घोषा॑: । गि॒रि॒भ्रजो॒ नोर्मयो॒ मद॑न्तो॒ बृह॒स्पति॑म॒भ्य१॒॑र्का अ॑नावन्
shlokas.transliteration: uda-prútaḥ ǀ ná ǀ váyaḥ ǀ rákṣamāṇāḥ ǀ vā́vadataḥ ǀ abhríyasya-iva ǀ ghóṣāḥ ǀgiri-bhrájaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ūrmáyaḥ ǀ mádantaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátim ǀ abhí ǀ arkā́ḥ ǀ anāvan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Like birds swimming in water when keeping watch, like the sound of the roaring thunder-cloud, likesounding torrents falling from the clouds, the worshippers glorifyBṛhaspati.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सं गोभि॑राङ्गिर॒सो नक्ष॑माणो॒ भग॑ इ॒वेद॑र्य॒मणं॑ निनाय । जने॑ मि॒त्रो न दम्प॑ती अनक्ति॒ बृह॑स्पते वा॒जया॒शूँरि॑वा॒जौ
shlokas.transliteration: sám ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ āṅgirasáḥ ǀ nákṣamāṇaḥ ǀ bhágaḥ-iva ǀ ít ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ nināya ǀjáne ǀ mitráḥ ǀ ná ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ anakti ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ vājáya ǀ āśū́n-iva ǀ ājáu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The son ofAṅgirasapervading him with his brightness has, likeBhaga, broughtAryamanto the cows;asMitra(unites his radiance) with the people, so has he united husband and wife;Bṛhaspati, send (yourwide-spread rays to your worshippers) as (a warrior sends his) horses to battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सा॒ध्व॒र्या अ॑ति॒थिनी॑रिषि॒रा स्पा॒र्हाः सु॒वर्णा॑ अनव॒द्यरू॑पाः । बृह॒स्पति॒: पर्व॑तेभ्यो वि॒तूर्या॒ निर्गा ऊ॑पे॒ यव॑मिव स्थि॒विभ्य॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sādhu-aryā́ḥ ǀ atithínīḥ ǀ iṣirā́ḥ ǀ spārhā́ḥ ǀ su-várṇāḥ ǀ anavadyá-rūpāḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ párvatebhyaḥ ǀ vi-tū́rya ǀ níḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ ūpe ǀ yávam-iva ǀ sthiví-bhyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bṛhaspatibrings unto (the gods), after extricating them from the mountains, the cows that are theyielders of pure (milk), ever in motion, the objects of search and of desire, well-coloured and of unexceptionableform, (as men bring) barley from the granaries.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒प्रु॒षा॒यन्मधु॑न ऋ॒तस्य॒ योनि॑मवक्षि॒पन्न॒र्क उ॒ल्कामि॑व॒ द्योः । बृह॒स्पति॑रु॒द्धर॒न्नश्म॑नो॒ गा भूम्या॑ उ॒द्नेव॒ वि त्वचं॑ बिभेद
shlokas.transliteration: ā-pruṣāyán ǀ mádhunā ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yónim ǀ ava-kṣipán ǀ arkáḥ ǀ ulkā́m-iva ǀ dyóḥ ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ uddháran ǀ áśmanaḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ bhū́myāḥ ǀ udnā́-iva ǀ ví ǀ tvácam ǀ bibheda ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Saturating (the earth) with water, scattering the receptacle of rain, the adorableBṛhaspati, raising upthe cattle from the rock as (he raises) a meteor from the sky, rent the skin of the earth (with the hoofs of thecattle) as (Parjanyarends it) with rain.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अप॒ ज्योति॑षा॒ तमो॑ अ॒न्तरि॑क्षादु॒द्नः शीपा॑लमिव॒ वात॑ आजत् । बृह॒स्पति॑रनु॒मृश्या॑ व॒लस्या॒भ्रमि॑व॒ वात॒ आ च॑क्र॒ आ गाः
shlokas.transliteration: ápa ǀ jyótiṣā ǀ támaḥ ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ udnáḥ ǀ śī́pālam-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ājat ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ anu-mṛ́śya ǀ valásya ǀ abhrám-iva ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ cakre ǀ ā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bṛhaspatidrove away the darkness from the firmament with light as the wind (blows) the Śīpālafrom the water; guessing (them to be there), he swept theVala's cows together to himself as the wind (sweeps)the clouds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒दा व॒लस्य॒ पीय॑तो॒ जसुं॒ भेद्बृह॒स्पति॑रग्नि॒तपो॑भिर॒र्कैः । द॒द्भिर्न जि॒ह्वा परि॑विष्ट॒माद॑दा॒विर्नि॒धीँर॑कृणोदु॒स्रिया॑णाम्
shlokas.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ valásya ǀ pī́yataḥ ǀ jásum ǀ bhét ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ agnitápaḥ-bhiḥ ǀ arkáiḥ ǀdat-bhíḥ ǀ ná ǀ jihvā́ ǀ pári-viṣṭam ǀ ā́dat ǀ āvíḥ ǀ ni-dhī́n ǀ akṛṇot ǀ usríyāṇām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “WhenBṛhaspatidemolished with rays burning like fire the weapon of the malignantVala, he devouredhim (encompassed by his followers) as the tongue (consumes) that which is encompassed by the teeth; he mademanifest the hiding- plural ce of the kine.”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृह॒स्पति॒रम॑त॒ हि त्यदा॑सां॒ नाम॑ स्व॒रीणां॒ सद॑ने॒ गुहा॒ यत् । आ॒ण्डेव॑ भि॒त्त्वा श॑कु॒नस्य॒ गर्भ॒मुदु॒स्रिया॒: पर्व॑तस्य॒ त्मना॑जत्
shlokas.transliteration: bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ ámata ǀ hí ǀ tyát ǀ āsām ǀ nā́ma ǀ svarī́ṇām ǀ sádane ǀ gúhā ǀ yát ǀāṇḍā́-iva ǀ bhittvā́ ǀ śakunásya ǀ gárbham ǀ út ǀ usríyāḥ ǀ párvatasya ǀ tmánā ǀ ājat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “WhenBṛhaspatihad discovered that name of the lowing kine in their plural ce in the cave, by his ownstrength he extricated the cattle from the rock as (breaking) the eggs of a bird (one extricates) the embryo.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अश्नापि॑नद्धं॒ मधु॒ पर्य॑पश्य॒न्मत्स्यं॒ न दी॒न उ॒दनि॑ क्षि॒यन्त॑म् । निष्टज्ज॑भार चम॒सं न वृ॒क्षाद्बृह॒स्पति॑र्विर॒वेणा॑ वि॒कृत्य॑
shlokas.transliteration: áśnā ǀ ápi-naddham ǀ mádhu ǀ pári ǀ apaśyat ǀ mátsyam ǀ ná ǀ dīné ǀ udáni ǀ kṣiyántam ǀníḥ ǀ tát ǀ jabhāra ǀ camasám ǀ ná ǀ vṛkṣā́t ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vi-ravéṇa ǀ vi-kṛ́tya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bṛhaspatilooked round upon the cowsshutup in the cave like fish in a dried up pool; he seized Valawith a shout, cutting him off like a bowl from a tree.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोषाम॑विन्द॒त्स स्व१॒॑: सो अ॒ग्निं सो अ॒र्केण॒ वि ब॑बाधे॒ तमां॑सि । बृह॒स्पति॒र्गोव॑पुषो व॒लस्य॒ निर्म॒ज्जानं॒ न पर्व॑णो जभार
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ uṣā́m ǀ avindat ǀ sáḥ ǀ sváríti sváḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ agním ǀ sáḥ ǀ arkéṇa ǀ ví ǀ babādhe ǀ támāṃsi ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ gó-vapuṣaḥ ǀ valásya ǀ níḥ ǀ majjā́nam ǀ ná ǀ párvaṇaḥ ǀ jabhāra ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bṛhaspatifound the dawn, the sun,Agni; he dispersed the gloom with light; he seized (the cattle fromthe rock)) ofValasurrounded by the kine as (one extracts) marrow from a bone.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हि॒मेव॑ प॒र्णा मु॑षि॒ता वना॑नि॒ बृह॒स्पति॑नाकृपयद्व॒लो गाः । अ॒ना॒नु॒कृ॒त्यम॑पु॒नश्च॑कार॒ यात्सूर्या॒मासा॑ मि॒थ उ॒च्चरा॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: himā́-iva ǀ parṇā́ ǀ muṣitā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ bṛ́haspátinā ǀ akṛpayat ǀ valáḥ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀananu-kṛtyám ǀ apunáríti ǀ cakāra ǀ yā́t ǀ sū́ryāmā́sā ǀ mitháḥ ǀ ut-cárātaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “As the trees (bemoan) their leaves carried off by the winter, soValabemoaned his kine (carried off) byBṛhaspati; he did that which cannot be imitated, which cannot be repeated, whereby sun and moon mutually rise(day and night).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भि श्या॒वं न कृश॑नेभि॒रश्वं॒ नक्ष॑त्रेभिः पि॒तरो॒ द्याम॑पिंशन् । रात्र्यां॒ तमो॒ अद॑धु॒र्ज्योति॒रह॒न्बृह॒स्पति॑र्भि॒नदद्रिं॑ वि॒दद्गाः
shlokas.transliteration: abhí ǀ śyāvám ǀ ná ǀ kṛ́śanebhiḥ ǀ áśvam ǀ nákṣatrebhiḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ apiṃśan ǀrā́tryām ǀ támaḥ ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ áhan ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ bhinát ǀ ádrim ǀ vidát ǀ gā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The protecting (deities) have decorated the heaven with constellations as (men decorate) a brownhorse with golden trappings; they established darkness in the night and light in the day;Bṛhaspatifractured therock and recovered the cows.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒दम॑कर्म॒ नमो॑ अभ्रि॒याय॒ यः पू॒र्वीरन्वा॒नोन॑वीति । बृह॒स्पति॒: स हि गोभि॒: सो अश्वै॒: स वी॒रेभि॒: स नृभि॑र्नो॒ वयो॑ धात्
shlokas.transliteration: idám ǀ akarma ǀ námaḥ ǀ abhriyā́ya ǀ yáḥ ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ā-nónavīti ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ áśvaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ vīrébhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dhāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We have offered this homage toBṛhaspati, who lives in mid-heaven, who recites in order many(sacred stanzas); may he bestow upon us food, with cows, with horses, with son, with dependants.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भ॒द्रा अ॒ग्नेर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॑ सं॒दृशो॑ वा॒मी प्रणी॑तिः सु॒रणा॒ उपे॑तयः । यदीं॑ सुमि॒त्रा विशो॒ अग्र॑ इ॒न्धते॑ घृ॒तेनाहु॑तो जरते॒ दवि॑द्युतत्
shlokas.transliteration: bhadrā́ḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ sam-dṛ́śaḥ ǀ vāmī́ ǀ prá-nītiḥ ǀ su-ráṇāḥ ǀ úpa-itayaḥ ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ su-mitrā́ḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ágre ǀ indháte ǀ ghṛténa ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ jarate ǀ dávidyutat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayAgni's regards be benevolent to Vadhryaśva; may his guidance be auspicious, his approaches(to the sacrifice) favourable; when theSumitrapeople first kindled Agni, then fed with butter and brilliantly blazinghe is glorified.”

shlokas.sanskrit: घृ॒तम॒ग्नेर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॒ वर्ध॑नं घृ॒तमन्नं॑ घृ॒तम्व॑स्य॒ मेद॑नम् । घृ॒तेनाहु॑त उर्वि॒या वि प॑प्रथे॒ सूर्य॑ इव रोचते स॒र्पिरा॑सुतिः
shlokas.transliteration: ghṛtám ǀ agnéḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ várdhanam ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ánnam ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ asya ǀ médanam ǀghṛténa ǀ ā́-hutaḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ paprathe ǀ sū́ryaḥ-iva ǀ rocate ǀ sarpíḥ-āsutiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May ghī be the augmenter of theAgniof Vadhryaśva; may ghī be his food; may ghī be hisnutriment; sacrified to with ghī he expands exceedingly; he shines like the sun, when the clarified butter ispoured out for him.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्ते॒ मनु॒र्यदनी॑कं सुमि॒त्रः स॑मी॒धे अ॑ग्ने॒ तदि॒दं नवी॑यः । स रे॒वच्छो॑च॒ स गिरो॑ जुषस्व॒ स वाजं॑ दर्षि॒ स इ॒ह श्रवो॑ धाः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ te ǀ mánuḥ ǀ yát ǀ ánīkam ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ sam-īdhé ǀ agne ǀ tát ǀ idám ǀ návīyaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ revát ǀ śoca ǀ sáḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ juṣasva ǀ sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ darṣi ǀ sáḥ ǀ ihá ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ dhāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May that your army of flame,Agni, whichManu, whichSumitrahas kindled, be the newest; do youshine wealthily; do you graciously accept our praises; do you destroy the might (of our foes), do you grant usabundance.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यं त्वा॒ पूर्व॑मीळि॒तो व॑ध्र्य॒श्वः स॑मी॒धे अ॑ग्ने॒ स इ॒दं जु॑षस्व । स न॑: स्ति॒पा उ॒त भ॑वा तनू॒पा दा॒त्रं र॑क्षस्व॒ यदि॒दं ते॑ अ॒स्मे
shlokas.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ pū́rvam ǀ īḷitáḥ ǀ vadhri-aśváḥ ǀ sam-īdhé ǀ agne ǀ sáḥ ǀ idám ǀ juṣasva ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sti-pā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ bhava ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǀ dātrám ǀ rakṣasva ǀ yát ǀ idám ǀ te ǀ asmé íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Do you,Agni, whom Vadhryaśva propitiating you formerly kindled, accept this; be the proector of oursacrifices, be the protector of our bodies; preserve this wealth which has been given to us by you.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भवा॑ द्यु॒म्नी वा॑ध्र्यश्वो॒त गो॒पा मा त्वा॑ तारीद॒भिमा॑ति॒र्जना॑नाम् । शूर॑ इव धृ॒ष्णुश्च्यव॑नः सुमि॒त्रः प्र नु वो॑चं॒ वाध्र्य॑श्वस्य॒ नाम॑
shlokas.transliteration: bháva ǀ dyumnī́ ǀ vādhri-aśva ǀ utá ǀ gopā́ḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ tārīt ǀ abhí-mātiḥ ǀ jánānām ǀśū́raḥ-iva ǀ ghṛṣṇúḥ ǀ cyávanaḥ ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ prá ǀ nú ǀ vocam ǀ vā́dhri-aśvasya ǀ nā́ma ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Kinsman of Vadhryaśva, be the possessor of food and our protector; let no one assail you, (for youare) the overcomer of men; like a resolute warrior (you are) the overthrower (of enemies); I,Sumitra, celebratethe names of the kinsmen ofVadhyaśva.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सम॒ज्र्या॑ पर्व॒त्या॒३॒॑ वसू॑नि॒ दासा॑ वृ॒त्राण्यार्या॑ जिगेथ । शूर॑ इव धृ॒ष्णुश्च्यव॑नो॒ जना॑नां॒ त्वम॑ग्ने पृतना॒यूँर॒भि ष्या॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sám ǀ ajryā́ ǀ parvatyā́ ǀ vásūni ǀ dā́sā ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ ā́ryā ǀ jigetha ǀśū́raḥ-iva ǀ ghṛṣṇúḥ ǀ cyávanaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ tvám ǀ agne ǀ pṛtanā-yū́n ǀ abhí ǀ syāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have gained mountain-treasures beneficial to men, (you have defeated the hostilities) of strongmen,DāsasandVṛtras, like a resolute warrior, do you,Agni, the overthrower (of enemies), overcome thosewho are desirous of battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दी॒र्घत॑न्तुर्बृ॒हदु॑क्षा॒यम॒ग्निः स॒हस्र॑स्तरीः श॒तनी॑थ॒ ऋभ्वा॑ । द्यु॒मान्द्यु॒मत्सु॒ नृभि॑र्मृ॒ज्यमा॑नः सुमि॒त्रेषु॑ दीदयो देव॒यत्सु॑
shlokas.transliteration: dīrghá-tantuḥ ǀ bṛhát-ukṣā ǀ ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ sahásra-starīḥ ǀ śatá-nīthaḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀdyu-mā́n ǀ dyumát-su ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ mṛjyámānaḥ ǀ su-mitréṣu ǀ dīdayaḥ ǀ devayát-su ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “ThisAgnito whom a long series (of sacrifices has been addressed), who is bright with many rays,covering thousands (in the form of ghī), the leader of hundreds (of burnt offerings), the mighty one, brilliantamong the brilliant, (is) being glorified by the priests; shine (Agni) upon the devoutSumitras.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वे धे॒नुः सु॒दुघा॑ जातवेदोऽस॒श्चते॑व सम॒ना स॑ब॒र्धुक् । त्वं नृभि॒र्दक्षि॑णावद्भिरग्ने सुमि॒त्रेभि॑रिध्यसे देव॒यद्भि॑:
shlokas.transliteration: tvé íti ǀ dhenúḥ ǀ su-dúghā ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ asaścátā-iva ǀ samanā́ ǀ sabaḥ-dhúk ǀtvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ dákṣiṇāvat-bhiḥ ǀ agne ǀ su-mitrébhiḥ ǀ idhyase ǀ devayát-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In you,Jātavedas, is the cow easy to be milked, yielding ambrosia as it were inexhaustibly in battle,you are kindled,Agni, by the devoutSumitraswho are entitled to the sacrificial donation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वाश्चि॑त्ते अ॒मृता॑ जातवेदो महि॒मानं॑ वाध्र्यश्व॒ प्र वो॑चन् । यत्स॒म्पृच्छं॒ मानु॑षी॒र्विश॒ आय॒न्त्वं नृभि॑रजय॒स्त्वावृ॑धेभिः
shlokas.transliteration: devā́ḥ ǀ cit ǀ te ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ vādhri-aśva ǀ prá ǀ vocan ǀyát ǀ sam-pṛ́ccham ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́yan ǀ tvám ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ ajayaḥ ǀ tvā́-vṛdhebhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The immortal gods have proclaimed your greatness.Jātavedas, Vadhryaśva (Agni); when humanbeings, came to inquire (who would slay theasuras), then you with (the gods), the leaders of all, fostered by youdid overcome (those who impeded the ceremony).”

shlokas.sanskrit: पि॒तेव॑ पु॒त्रम॑बिभरु॒पस्थे॒ त्वाम॑ग्ने वध्र्य॒श्वः स॑प॒र्यन् । जु॒षा॒णो अ॑स्य स॒मिधं॑ यविष्ठो॒त पूर्वाँ॑ अवनो॒र्व्राध॑तश्चित्
shlokas.transliteration: pitā́-iva ǀ putrám ǀ abibhaḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ tvā́m ǀ agne ǀ vadhri-aśváḥ ǀ saparyán ǀjuṣāṇáḥ ǀ asya ǀ sam-ídham ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ utá ǀ pū́rvān ǀ avanoḥ ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ cit ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Vadhryaśva, honouring you,Agni, plural ced you upon the altar as a father (plural ces) his son (upon hislap); plural ased with his fuel, youngest (of the gods), you did slay the ancient obstructers of the rite.”

shlokas.sanskrit: शश्व॑द॒ग्निर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॒ शत्रू॒न्नृभि॑र्जिगाय सु॒तसो॑मवद्भिः । सम॑नं चिददहश्चित्रभा॒नोऽव॒ व्राध॑न्तमभिनद्वृ॒धश्चि॑त्
shlokas.transliteration: śáśvat ǀ agníḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ śátrūn ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ jigāya ǀ sutásomavat-bhiḥ ǀsámanam ǀ cit ǀ adahaḥ ǀ citrabhāno íti citra-bhāno ǀ áva ǀ vrā́dhantam ǀ abhinat ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ cit ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agniby means of the priests of Vadhryaśva pouring out libations always conquers his foes; you(Agni) shining with varied splendour, have consumed the battle; (your praiser) self-fostered has destroyed hispowerful (assailant).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यम॒ग्निर्व॑ध्र्य॒श्वस्य॑ वृत्र॒हा स॑न॒कात्प्रेद्धो॒ नम॑सोपवा॒क्य॑: । स नो॒ अजा॑मीँरु॒त वा॒ विजा॑मीन॒भि ति॑ष्ठ॒ शर्ध॑तो वाध्र्यश्व
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ agníḥ ǀ vadhri-aśvásya ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ sanakā́t ǀ prá-iddhaḥ ǀ námasā ǀ upa-vākyáḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ájāmīn ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ ví-jāmīn ǀ abhí ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ śárdhataḥ ǀ vādhri-aśva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From a long period has thisAgnithe slayer of foes been kindled (by the oblation) of Vadhryaśva; (heis) to be addressed with reverence; do you, (Agni, kindled in the) family of Vadhryaśva, overcome our enemies,both those who have no kinsmen and those who have many kinsmen.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मां मे॑ अग्ने स॒मिधं॑ जुषस्वे॒ळस्प॒दे प्रति॑ हर्या घृ॒ताची॑म् । वर्ष्म॑न्पृथि॒व्याः सु॑दिन॒त्वे अह्ना॑मू॒र्ध्वो भ॑व सुक्रतो देवय॒ज्या
shlokas.transliteration: imā́m ǀ me ǀ agne ǀ sam-ídham ǀ juṣasva ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀ práti ǀ harya ǀ ghṛtā́cīm ǀvárṣman ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ sudina-tvé ǀ áhnām ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ bhava ǀ sukrato íti su-krato ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Graciously accept,Agni, this my fuel (plural ced) on the plural ce of libation (the altar); delight in thebutter-laden (spoon); most wise, rise up upon the lofty plural ce of the earth for the propitiousness of the daysthrough the worship of the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ दे॒वाना॑मग्र॒यावे॒ह या॑तु॒ नरा॒शंसो॑ वि॒श्वरू॑पेभि॒रश्वै॑: । ऋ॒तस्य॑ प॒था नम॑सा मि॒येधो॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ दे॒वत॑मः सुषूदत्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ devā́nām ǀ agra-yā́vā ǀ ihá ǀ yātu ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ viśvá-rūpebhiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ pathā́ ǀ námasā ǀ miyédhaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ devá-tamaḥ ǀ susūdat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May Narāśaṃsa, the preceder of the gods, come here with his horses of various forms; deserving ofadoration, chief of the gods, may he effuse (oblations) to the gods by the path of the sacrifice with praise.”

shlokas.sanskrit: श॒श्व॒त्त॒ममी॑ळते दू॒त्या॑य ह॒विष्म॑न्तो मनु॒ष्या॑सो अ॒ग्निम् । वहि॑ष्ठै॒रश्वै॑: सु॒वृता॒ रथे॒ना दे॒वान्व॑क्षि॒ नि ष॑दे॒ह होता॑
shlokas.transliteration: śaśvat-tamám ǀ īḷate ǀ dūtyā́ya ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́saḥ ǀ agním ǀváhiṣṭhaiḥ ǀ áśvaiḥ ǀ su-vṛ́tā ǀ ráthena ǀ ā́ ǀ devā́n ǀ vakṣi ǀ ní ǀ sada ǀ ihá ǀ hótā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Men offering oblations adore the eternalAgnito (induce him to perform) the duty of messenger (to thegods); do you with your stalwart draught horses and your well-turning chariots bear (our offering) to the gods,and sit down here as the ministrant priest.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि प्र॑थतां दे॒वजु॑ष्टं तिर॒श्चा दी॒र्घं द्रा॒घ्मा सु॑र॒भि भू॑त्व॒स्मे । अहे॑ळता॒ मन॑सा देव बर्हि॒रिन्द्र॑ज्येष्ठाँ उश॒तो य॑क्षि दे॒वान्
shlokas.transliteration: ví ǀ prathatām ǀ devá-juṣṭam ǀ tiraścā́ ǀ dīrghám ǀ drāghmā́ ǀ surabhí ǀ bhūtu ǀ asmé íti ǀáheḷatā ǀ mánasā ǀ deva ǀ barhiḥ ǀ índra-jyeṣṭhān ǀ uśatáḥ ǀ yakṣi ǀ devā́n ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May our (sacred grass) acceptable to the gods, twining crookedly be stretched out, may it be long,lengthy, and fragrant; with mind free from wrath, divineBarhis, offer worship to the gods desiring (the sacrifice),of whomIndrais the chief.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दि॒वो वा॒ सानु॑ स्पृ॒शता॒ वरी॑यः पृथि॒व्या वा॒ मात्र॑या॒ वि श्र॑यध्वम् । उ॒श॒तीर्द्वा॑रो महि॒ना म॒हद्भि॑र्दे॒वं रथं॑ रथ॒युर्धा॑रयध्वम्
shlokas.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ vā ǀ sā́nu ǀ spṛśáta ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ vā ǀ mā́trayā ǀ ví ǀ śrayadhvam ǀuśatī́ḥ ǀ dvāraḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ mahát-bhiḥ ǀ devám ǀ rátham ǀ ratha-yúḥ ǀ dhārayadhvam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Be in contact, doors, with the lofty height of heaven, or expand according to the measure of the earth;desiring the gods, desiring a chariot, sustain without might the shining chariot (that is mounted) by the mightygods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वी दि॒वो दु॑हि॒तरा॑ सुशि॒ल्पे उ॒षासा॒नक्ता॑ सदतां॒ नि योनौ॑ । आ वां॑ दे॒वास॑ उशती उ॒शन्त॑ उ॒रौ सी॑दन्तु सुभगे उ॒पस्थे॑
shlokas.transliteration: devī́ íti ǀ diváḥ ǀ duhitárā ǀ suśilpé íti su-śilpé ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ sadatām ǀ ní ǀ yónau ǀā́ ǀ vām ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ uśatī íti ǀ uśántaḥ ǀ uráu ǀ sīdantu ǀ subhage íti su-bhage ǀ upá-sthe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Radiant daughters of heaven, Dawn and Night, sit down on the plural ce of sacrifice; O you, who aredesirous and possessed of affluence, may the gods desirous (of oblations) sit down on your spacious lap.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊ॒र्ध्वो ग्रावा॑ बृ॒हद॒ग्निः समि॑द्धः प्रि॒या धामा॒न्यदि॑तेरु॒पस्थे॑ । पु॒रोहि॑तावृत्विजा य॒ज्ञे अ॒स्मिन्वि॒दुष्ट॑रा॒ द्रवि॑ण॒मा य॑जेथाम्
shlokas.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ grā́vā ǀ bṛhát ǀ agníḥ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ priyā́ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ áditeḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀpuráḥ-hitau ǀ ṛtvijā ǀ yajñé ǀ asmín ǀ vidúḥ-tarā ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ā́ ǀ yajethām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(When) the grinding-stone is uplifted, the mightyAgnikindled, the acceptable vessels (ready) on thelap of earth; (then), most learned priests, who take the foremost plural ce, bestow wealth upon us at this sacrifice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तिस्रो॑ देवीर्ब॒र्हिरि॒दं वरी॑य॒ आ सी॑दत चकृ॒मा व॑: स्यो॒नम् । म॒नु॒ष्वद्य॒ज्ञं सुधि॑ता ह॒वींषीळा॑ दे॒वी घृ॒तप॑दी जुषन्त
shlokas.transliteration: tísraḥ ǀ devīḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ idám ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sīdata ǀ cakṛmá ǀ vaḥ ǀ syonám ǀmanuṣvát ǀ yajñám ǀ sú-dhitā ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ íḷā ǀ devī́ ǀ ghṛtá-padī ǀ juṣanta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sit down, you three goddesses, upon this broadbarhis, we have spread it out for you; Iḷā, radiant(Sarasvatī) and bright-footed (bhāratī) accept our sacrifice and well-presented oblations as if they wereManu's.”

shlokas.sanskrit: देव॑ त्वष्ट॒र्यद्ध॑ चारु॒त्वमान॒ड्यदङ्गि॑रसा॒मभ॑वः सचा॒भूः । स दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॒ उप॒ प्र वि॒द्वाँ उ॒शन्य॑क्षि द्रविणोदः सु॒रत्न॑:
shlokas.transliteration: déva ǀ tvaṣṭaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ha ǀ cāru-tvám ǀ ā́naṭ ǀ yát ǀ áṅgirasām ǀ ábhavaḥ ǀ sacā-bhū́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ vidvā́n ǀ uśán ǀ yakṣi ǀ draviṇaḥ-daḥ ǀ su-rátnaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “DivineTvaṣṭā, since you have attained to beauty (through our oblations), and have become theassociate of theAṅgirasas, do you, the bestower of wealth, possessed of precious treasure, and knowing (towhom each portion belongs), offer the food of the gods (to them).”

shlokas.sanskrit: वन॑स्पते रश॒नया॑ नि॒यूया॑ दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॒ उप॑ वक्षि वि॒द्वान् । स्वदा॑ति दे॒वः कृ॒णव॑द्ध॒वींष्यव॑तां॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी हवं॑ मे
shlokas.transliteration: vánaspate ǀ raśanáyā ǀ ni-yū́ya ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ úpa ǀ vakṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǀsvádāti ǀ deváḥ ǀ kṛṇávat ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀ ávatām ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ hávam ǀ me ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Vanaspati, who are intelligent, having fastened it with a rope, convey the food of the gods; may thedivine (Vanaspati) taste it, may he take the oblations (to the gods); may heaven and earth protect my invocatioṇ”

shlokas.sanskrit: आग्ने॑ वह॒ वरु॑णमि॒ष्टये॑ न॒ इन्द्रं॑ दि॒वो म॒रुतो॑ अ॒न्तरि॑क्षात् । सीद॑न्तु ब॒र्हिर्विश्व॒ आ यज॑त्रा॒: स्वाहा॑ दे॒वा अ॒मृता॑ मादयन्ताम्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ agne ǀ vaha ǀ váruṇam ǀ iṣṭáye ǀ naḥ ǀ índram ǀ diváḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ antárikṣāt ǀsī́dantu ǀ barhíḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ā́ ǀ yájatrāḥ ǀ svā́hā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́tāḥ ǀ mādayantām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bring,Agni, to our sacrificeVaruṇaandIndrafrom heaven, and theMarutsfrom the firmament, maythe adorable universal gods sit down on the sacred grass, and may the immortal deities rejoice in (the oblationpresented with) thesvāhā.”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृह॑स्पते प्रथ॒मं वा॒चो अग्रं॒ यत्प्रैर॑त नाम॒धेयं॒ दधा॑नाः । यदे॑षां॒ श्रेष्ठं॒ यद॑रि॒प्रमासी॑त्प्रे॒णा तदे॑षां॒ निहि॑तं॒ गुहा॒विः
shlokas.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ prathamám ǀ vācáḥ ǀ ágram ǀ yát ǀ prá ǀ áirata ǀ nāma-dhéyam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀyát ǀ eṣām ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ yát ǀ ariprám ǀ ā́sīt ǀ preṇā́ ǀ tát ǀ eṣām ǀ ní-hitam ǀ gúhā ǀ āvíḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “That,Bṛhaspati, is the best (part) of speech which those giving a name (to objects) first utter; thatwhich was the best of those (words) and free from defect, (Sarasvatī) reveals it though secretly imparted, bymeans of affection.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सक्तु॑मिव॒ तित॑उना पु॒नन्तो॒ यत्र॒ धीरा॒ मन॑सा॒ वाच॒मक्र॑त । अत्रा॒ सखा॑यः स॒ख्यानि॑ जानते भ॒द्रैषां॑ ल॒क्ष्मीर्निहि॒ताधि॑ वा॒चि
shlokas.transliteration: sáktum-iva ǀ títa-unā ǀ punántaḥ ǀ yátra ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ vā́cam ǀ ákrata ǀátra ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ sakhyā́ni ǀ jānate ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ lakṣmī́ḥ ǀ ní-hitā ǀ ádhi ǀ vācí ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When the wise create Speech through wisdom winnowing (it) as (men winnow) barley with a sieve,then friends know friendship; good fortune is plural ced upon their word.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒ज्ञेन॑ वा॒चः प॑द॒वीय॑माय॒न्तामन्व॑विन्द॒न्नृषि॑षु॒ प्रवि॑ष्टाम् । तामा॒भृत्या॒ व्य॑दधुः पुरु॒त्रा तां स॒प्त रे॒भा अ॒भि सं न॑वन्ते
shlokas.transliteration: yajñéna ǀ vācáḥ ǀ pada-vī́yam ǀ āyan ǀ tā́m ǀ ánu ǀ avindan ǀ ṛ́ṣiṣu ǀ prá-viṣṭām ǀtā́m ǀ ā-bhṛ́tya ǀ ví ǀ adadhuḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǀ tā́m ǀ saptá ǀ rebhā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ sám ǀ navante ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त त्व॒: पश्य॒न्न द॑दर्श॒ वाच॑मु॒त त्व॑: शृ॒ण्वन्न शृ॑णोत्येनाम् । उ॒तो त्व॑स्मै त॒न्वं१॒॑ वि स॑स्रे जा॒येव॒ पत्य॑ उश॒ती सु॒वासा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ tvaḥ ǀ páśyan ǀ ná ǀ dadarśa ǀ vā́cam ǀ utá ǀ tvaḥ ǀ śṛṇván ǀ ná ǀ śṛṇoti ǀ enām ǀutó íti ǀ tvasmai ǀ tanvám ǀ ví ǀ sasre ǀ jāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ uśatī́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “One (man) indeed seeing Speech has not seen her; another (man) hearing her has not heard her; butto another she delivers her person n as a loving wife well-attired presents herself to her husband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त त्वं॑ स॒ख्ये स्थि॒रपी॑तमाहु॒र्नैनं॑ हिन्व॒न्त्यपि॒ वाजि॑नेषु । अधे॑न्वा चरति मा॒ययै॒ष वाचं॑ शुश्रु॒वाँ अ॑फ॒लाम॑पु॒ष्पाम्
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ tvam ǀ sakhyé ǀ sthirá-pītam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ ná ǀ enam ǀ hinvanti ǀ ápi ǀ vā́jineṣu ǀádhenvā ǀ carati ǀ māyáyā ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ śuśru-vā́n ǀ aphalā́m ǀ apuṣpā́m ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They call one man firmly established in the friendship (of Speech), they do not exclude him from (thesociety of) the powerful (in knowledge); another wanders with an illusion that is barren, bearing Speech that iswithout fruit, without flowers.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्ति॒त्याज॑ सचि॒विदं॒ सखा॑यं॒ न तस्य॑ वा॒च्यपि॑ भा॒गो अ॑स्ति । यदीं॑ शृ॒णोत्यल॑कं शृणोति न॒हि प्र॒वेद॑ सुकृ॒तस्य॒ पन्था॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ tityā́ja ǀ saci-vídam ǀ sákhāyam ǀ ná ǀ tásya ǀ vācí ǀ ápi ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ asti ǀyát ǀ īm ǀ śṛṇóti ǀ álakam ǀ śṛṇoti ǀ nahí ǀ pra-véda ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ pánthām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who has abandoned the friend who knows the duty of a friend, in his speech there is not a particle(of sense); what he hears, he hears amiss; for he knows not the path of righteousness.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒क्ष॒ण्वन्त॒: कर्ण॑वन्त॒: सखा॑यो मनोज॒वेष्वस॑मा बभूवुः । आ॒द॒घ्नास॑ उपक॒क्षास॑ उ त्वे ह्र॒दा इ॑व॒ स्नात्वा॑ उ त्वे ददृश्रे
shlokas.transliteration: akṣaṇ-vántaḥ ǀ kárṇa-vantaḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ manaḥ-javéṣu ǀ ásamāḥ ǀ babhūvuḥ ǀādaghnā́saḥ ǀ upa-kakṣā́saḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǀ hradā́ḥ-iva ǀ snā́tvāḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǀ dadṛśre ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Friends possessing eyes, possessing ears, were (yet) unequal in mental apprehension; some seemedlike pools reaching to the mouth, others reaching to the loins, others like pools in which one can bathe.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हृ॒दा त॒ष्टेषु॒ मन॑सो ज॒वेषु॒ यद्ब्रा॑ह्म॒णाः सं॒यज॑न्ते॒ सखा॑यः । अत्राह॑ त्वं॒ वि ज॑हुर्वे॒द्याभि॒रोह॑ब्रह्माणो॒ वि च॑रन्त्यु त्वे
shlokas.transliteration: hṛdā́ ǀ taṣṭéṣu ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ javéṣu ǀ yát ǀ brāhmaṇā́ḥ ǀ sam-yájante ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀátra ǀ áha ǀ tvam ǀ ví ǀ jahuḥ ǀ vedyā́bhiḥ ǀ óha-brahmāṇaḥ ǀ ví ǀ caranti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tve ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “AlthoughBrāhmaṇaswho are friends concur in the mental apprehensions which are conceived bythe heart (of the wise), yet in this (assembly) they abandon one man (to ignorance of the sciences) that are to beknown, others again who are reckoned as Brāhmaṇas (wander at will in the meanings of theVeda).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मे ये नार्वाङ्न प॒रश्चर॑न्ति॒ न ब्रा॑ह्म॒णासो॒ न सु॒तेक॑रासः । त ए॒ते वाच॑मभि॒पद्य॑ पा॒पया॑ सि॒रीस्तन्त्रं॑ तन्वते॒ अप्र॑जज्ञयः
shlokas.transliteration: imé ǀ yé ǀ ná ǀ arvā́k ǀ ná ǀ paráḥ ǀ cáranti ǀ ná ǀ brāhmaṇā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ suté-karāsaḥ ǀté ǀ eté ǀ vā́cam ǀ abhi-pádya ǀ pāpáyā ǀ sirī́ḥ ǀ tántram ǀ tanvate ǀ ápra-jajñayaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Those who do not walk (with theBrāhmaṇas) in this lower world not (with the gods) in the upperworld-- they are neither Brāhmaṇas nor offerers of libations; they, devoid of wisdom, attaining Speech, havingsin producing (Speech), becoming plural ughmen pursue agriculture.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सर्वे॑ नन्दन्ति य॒शसाग॑तेन सभासा॒हेन॒ सख्या॒ सखा॑यः । कि॒ल्बि॒ष॒स्पृत्पि॑तु॒षणि॒र्ह्ये॑षा॒मरं॑ हि॒तो भव॑ति॒ वाजि॑नाय
shlokas.transliteration: sárve ǀ nandanti ǀ yaśásā ǀ ā́-gatena ǀ sabhā-sāhéna ǀ sákhyā ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀkilbiṣa-spṛ́t ǀ pitu-sániḥ ǀ hí ǀ eṣām ǀ áram ǀ hitáḥ ǀ bhávati ǀ vā́jināya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “All frinends rejoice when the friendly (libation), the support of the assembly (of the priests), has arrived(at the sacrifice); for (Soma), the remover of iniquity, the giver of sustenance, being plural ced (in the vessels), issufficient for their invigoration.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒चां त्व॒: पोष॑मास्ते पुपु॒ष्वान्गा॑य॒त्रं त्वो॑ गायति॒ शक्व॑रीषु । ब्र॒ह्मा त्वो॒ वद॑ति जातवि॒द्यां य॒ज्ञस्य॒ मात्रां॒ वि मि॑मीत उ त्वः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛcā́m ǀ tvaḥ ǀ póṣam ǀ āste ǀ pupuṣvā́n ǀ gāyatrám ǀ tvaḥ ǀ gāyati ǀ śákvarīṣu ǀbrahmā́ ǀ tvaḥ ǀ vádati ǀ jāta-vidyā́m ǀ yajñásya ǀ mā́trām ǀ ví ǀ mimīte ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “One (theHotā) is diligent in the repitition of the verses (of the Ṛk); another (theUdgātā) chantstheGāyatra(theSāman) in the Śakvarī metre; another theBrahmadeclares the knowledge of what is to bedone; another (theAdhvaryu) measures the materials of the sacrifice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वानां॒ नु व॒यं जाना॒ प्र वो॑चाम विप॒न्यया॑ । उ॒क्थेषु॑ श॒स्यमा॑नेषु॒ यः पश्या॒दुत्त॑रे यु॒गे
shlokas.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ nú ǀ vayám ǀ jā́nā ǀ prá ǀ vocāma ǀ vipanyáyā ǀukthéṣu ǀ śasyámāneṣu ǀ yáḥ ǀ páśyāt ǀ út-tare ǀ yugé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let us proclaim with a clear voice the genitive rations of the gods (the divine company), who, when theirpraises are recited, look (favourably on the worshipper) in this latter age.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ब्रह्म॑ण॒स्पति॑रे॒ता सं क॒र्मार॑ इवाधमत् । दे॒वानां॑ पू॒र्व्ये यु॒गेऽस॑त॒: सद॑जायत
shlokas.transliteration: bráhmaṇaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ etā́ ǀ sám ǀ karmā́raḥ-iva ǀ adhamat ǀdevā́nām ǀ pūrvyé ǀ yugé ǀ ásataḥ ǀ sát ǀ ajāyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Brahmaṇaspatifilled these (genitive rations of the gods) with breath as a blacksmith (his bellows); in thefirst age of the gods the existent was born of the non-existent.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वानां॑ यु॒गे प्र॑थ॒मेऽस॑त॒: सद॑जायत । तदाशा॒ अन्व॑जायन्त॒ तदु॑त्ता॒नप॑द॒स्परि॑
shlokas.transliteration: devā́nām ǀ yugé ǀ prathamé ǀ ásataḥ ǀ sát ǀ ajāyata ǀtát ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ajāyanta ǀ tát ǀ uttāná-padaḥ ǀ pári ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In the firsst age of the gods the existent was born of the non- existent; after that the quarters (of thehorizon) were born, and after them the upward-growing (trees).”

shlokas.sanskrit: भूर्ज॑ज्ञ उत्ता॒नप॑दो भु॒व आशा॑ अजायन्त । अदि॑ते॒र्दक्षो॑ अजायत॒ दक्षा॒द्वदि॑ति॒: परि॑
shlokas.transliteration: bhū́ḥ ǀ jajñe ǀ uttāná-padaḥ ǀ bhuváḥ ǀ ā́śāḥ ǀ ajāyanta ǀáditeḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ ajāyata ǀ dákṣāt ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ áditiḥ ǀ pári ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The earth was born from the upward-growing (tree), the quarters were born from the earth; Dakṣawas born fromAditi, and afterwards Aditi fromDakṣa.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अदि॑ति॒र्ह्यज॑निष्ट॒ दक्ष॒ या दु॑हि॒ता तव॑ । तां दे॒वा अन्व॑जायन्त भ॒द्रा अ॒मृत॑बन्धवः
shlokas.transliteration: áditiḥ ǀ hí ǀ ájaniṣṭa ǀ dákṣa ǀ yā́ ǀ duhitā́ ǀ táva ǀtā́m ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ajāyanta ǀ bhadrā́ḥ ǀ amṛ́ta-bandhavaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Aditi, who was your daughter,Dakṣa, was born; after her the gods were born adorable, freed from thebonds of death.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्दे॑वा अ॒दः स॑लि॒ले सुसं॑रब्धा॒ अति॑ष्ठत । अत्रा॑ वो॒ नृत्य॑तामिव ती॒व्रो रे॒णुरपा॑यत
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ devāḥ ǀ adáḥ ǀ salilé ǀ sú-saṃrabdhāḥ ǀ átiṣṭhata ǀátra ǀ vaḥ ǀ nṛ́tyatām-iva ǀ tīvráḥ ǀ reṇúḥ ǀ ápa ǀ āyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, goeds, your abode in this pool well-arranged, then a pungent dust went forth from you as if youwere dancing.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्दे॑वा॒ यत॑यो यथा॒ भुव॑ना॒न्यपि॑न्वत । अत्रा॑ समु॒द्र आ गू॒ळ्हमा सूर्य॑मजभर्तन
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ devāḥ ǀ yátayaḥ ǀ yathā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ ápinvata ǀátra ǀ samudré ǀ ā́ ǀ gūḷhám ǀ ā́ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ ajabhartana ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, gods, you filled the worlds (with your radiance) as clouds (fill the earth with rain), then youbrought forth the wun hidden in the ocean.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ष्टौ पु॒त्रासो॒ अदि॑ते॒र्ये जा॒तास्त॒न्व१॒॑स्परि॑ । दे॒वाँ उप॒ प्रैत्स॒प्तभि॒: परा॑ मार्ता॒ण्डमा॑स्यत्
shlokas.transliteration: aṣṭáu ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ áditeḥ ǀ yé ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ pári ǀdevā́n ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ ait ǀ saptá-bhiḥ ǀ párā ǀ mārtāṇḍám ǀ āsyat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Eight sons (there were) ofĀdityawho were born from her body; she approached the gods withseven, she sent forthMārtāṇḍaon high (TaittirīyaĀraṇyaka1.13.3)”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒प्तभि॑: पु॒त्रैरदि॑ति॒रुप॒ प्रैत्पू॒र्व्यं यु॒गम् । प्र॒जायै॑ मृ॒त्यवे॑ त्व॒त्पुन॑र्मार्ता॒ण्डमाभ॑रत्
shlokas.transliteration: saptá-bhiḥ ǀ putráiḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ prá ǀ ait ǀ pūrvyám ǀ yugám ǀpra-jā́yai ǀ mṛtyáve ǀ tvat ǀ púnaḥ ǀ mārtāṇḍám ǀ ā́ ǀ abharat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “With seven sonsAditiwent to a former genitive ration, but she boreMārtāṇḍafor the birth and death(of human beings).”

shlokas.sanskrit: जनि॑ष्ठा उ॒ग्रः सह॑से तु॒राय॑ म॒न्द्र ओजि॑ष्ठो बहु॒लाभि॑मानः । अव॑र्ध॒न्निन्द्रं॑ म॒रुत॑श्चि॒दत्र॑ मा॒ता यद्वी॒रं द॒धन॒द्धनि॑ष्ठा
shlokas.transliteration: jániṣṭhāḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ sáhase ǀ turā́ya ǀ mandráḥ ǀ ójiṣṭhaḥ ǀ bahulá-abhimānaḥ ǀávardhan ǀ índram ǀ marútaḥ ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀ mātā́ ǀ yát ǀ vīrám ǀ dadhánat ǀ dhániṣṭhā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have been born, (Indra), for strength, for slaying (enemies); powerful, adorable, most mighty,extremely proud; theMarutsanimated Indra in the (Vṛtra-fight) when (his) sustaining mother sustained the hero.”

shlokas.sanskrit: द्रु॒हो निष॑त्ता पृश॒नी चि॒देवै॑: पु॒रू शंसे॑न वावृधु॒ष्ट इन्द्र॑म् । अ॒भीवृ॑तेव॒ ता म॑हाप॒देन॑ ध्वा॒न्तात्प्र॑पि॒त्वादुद॑रन्त॒ गर्भा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: druháḥ ǀ ní-sattā ǀ pṛśanī́ ǀ cit ǀ évaiḥ ǀ purú ǀ śáṃsena ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǀ té ǀ índram ǀabhívṛtā-iva ǀ tā́ ǀ mahā-padéna ǀ dhvāntā́t ǀ pra-pitvā́t ǀ út ǀ aranta ǀ gárbhāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The material troop of (Indra) the injurer encamped around Indra, (accompanied) by the swift-moving(maruts); they animated him with abundant praise; like (cattle) penned up within a great stall, the embryonic(waters) issued from the (Vṛtra) who had arrived in the form of darkness.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒ष्वा ते॒ पादा॒ प्र यज्जिगा॒स्यव॑र्ध॒न्वाजा॑ उ॒त ये चि॒दत्र॑ । त्वमि॑न्द्र सालावृ॒कान्त्स॒हस्र॑मा॒सन्द॑धिषे अ॒श्विना व॑वृत्याः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛṣvā́ ǀ te ǀ pā́dā ǀ prá ǀ yát ǀ jígāsi ǀ ávardhan ǀ vā́jāḥ ǀ utá ǀ yé ǀ cit ǀ átra ǀtvám ǀ indra ǀ sālāvṛkā́n ǀ sahásram ǀ āsán ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ aśvínā ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtyāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Vast, (Indra), are your feet; when you advance, theVājas, and whatsoever (deities are) thereanimated you; you, Indra, hold a thousand jackals in yourmouth, may you bring back theAśvins.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒म॒ना तूर्णि॒रुप॑ यासि य॒ज्ञमा नास॑त्या स॒ख्याय॑ वक्षि । व॒साव्या॑मिन्द्र धारयः स॒हस्रा॒श्विना॑ शूर ददतुर्म॒घानि॑
shlokas.transliteration: samanā́ ǀ tū́rṇiḥ ǀ úpa ǀ yāsi ǀ yajñám ǀ ā́ ǀ nā́satyā ǀ sakhyā́ya ǀ vakṣi ǀvasā́vyām ǀ indra ǀ dhārayaḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ aśvínā ǀ śūra ǀ dadatuḥ ǀ maghā́ni ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Hastening in battle you approach the sacrifice; you bring the twoNāsatyāsto friendship (with us);you,Indra, possess a heap of treasures, thousands (in numbers); theAśvins, hero, gave us riches.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मन्द॑मान ऋ॒तादधि॑ प्र॒जायै॒ सखि॑भि॒रिन्द्र॑ इषि॒रेभि॒रर्थ॑म् । आभि॒र्हि मा॒या उप॒ दस्यु॒मागा॒न्मिह॒: प्र त॒म्रा अ॑वप॒त्तमां॑सि
shlokas.transliteration: mándamānaḥ ǀ ṛtā́t ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-jā́yai ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ iṣirébhiḥ ǀ ártham ǀā́ ǀ ābhiḥ ǀ hí ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ dásyum ǀ ā́ ǀ ágāt ǀ míhaḥ ǀ prá ǀ tamrā́ḥ ǀ avapat ǀ támāṃsi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrarejoicing at the sacrifice accompanied by hisswift-moving riends (theMaruts, gave) wealth to thepeople; he has come with them against theDasyuto destroy his illusions; he has scattered the dark rain-cloudsand the gloom.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सना॑माना चिद्ध्वसयो॒ न्य॑स्मा॒ अवा॑ह॒न्निन्द्र॑ उ॒षसो॒ यथान॑: । ऋ॒ष्वैर॑गच्छ॒: सखि॑भि॒र्निका॑मैः सा॒कं प्र॑ति॒ष्ठा हृद्या॑ जघन्थ
shlokas.transliteration: sá-nāmānā ǀ cit ǀ dhvasayaḥ ǀ ní ǀ asmai ǀ áva ǀ ahan ǀ índraḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ánaḥ ǀṛṣváiḥ ǀ agacchaḥ ǀ sákhi-bhiḥ ǀ ní-kāmaiḥ ǀ sākám ǀ prati-sthā́ ǀ hṛ́dyā ǀ jaghantha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have expelled the two of the same name, you have destroyed theVṛtraas (he destroyed) the cartof the dawn; you advance with the mighty friends (theMaruts), who were eager (to slay the Vṛtra); youdemolished his precious limbs.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं ज॑घन्थ॒ नमु॑चिं मख॒स्युं दासं॑ कृण्वा॒न ऋष॑ये॒ विमा॑यम् । त्वं च॑कर्थ॒ मन॑वे स्यो॒नान्प॒थो दे॑व॒त्राञ्ज॑सेव॒ याना॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ jaghantha ǀ námucim ǀ makhasyúm ǀ dā́sam ǀ kṛṇvānáḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣaye ǀ ví-māyam ǀtvám ǀ cakartha ǀ mánave ǀ syonā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ áñjasā-iva ǀ yā́nān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have slain the slaveNamuciendeavouring (to disturb) the sacrifice, making his illusionspowerless against the Ṛṣi; you have made easy forManuthe paths to the gods, so as (to make) the waysstraight.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वमे॒तानि॑ पप्रिषे॒ वि नामेशा॑न इन्द्र दधिषे॒ गभ॑स्तौ । अनु॑ त्वा दे॒वाः शव॑सा मदन्त्यु॒परि॑बुध्नान्व॒निन॑श्चकर्थ
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ etā́ni ǀ papriṣe ǀ ví ǀ nā́ma ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ indra ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ gábhastau ǀánu ǀ tvā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ śávasā ǀ madanti ǀ upári-budhnān ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ cakartha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have filled these waters, you,Indra, who are the lord (of all) bear (the thunderbolt) in yourhands;the gods glorify you (who are endowed) with strength; you have made the clouds with their roots upwards.”

shlokas.sanskrit: च॒क्रं यद॑स्या॒प्स्वा निष॑त्तमु॒तो तद॑स्मै॒ मध्विच्च॑च्छद्यात् । पृ॒थि॒व्यामति॑षितं॒ यदूध॒: पयो॒ गोष्वद॑धा॒ ओष॑धीषु
shlokas.transliteration: cakrám ǀ yát ǀ asya ǀ ap-sú ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-sattam ǀ utó íti ǀ tát ǀ asmai ǀ mádhu ǀ ít ǀ cacchadyāt ǀpṛthivyā́m ǀ áti-sitam ǀ yát ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ páyaḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ ádadhāḥ ǀ óṣadhīṣu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When his thunderbolt rode everywhere in the firmament, it also subjugated the water to him; the waterwhich is let loose upon the earth puts milk into cows and herbs.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अश्वा॑दिया॒येति॒ यद्वद॒न्त्योज॑सो जा॒तमु॒त म॑न्य एनम् । म॒न्योरि॑याय ह॒र्म्येषु॑ तस्थौ॒ यत॑: प्रज॒ज्ञ इन्द्रो॑ अस्य वेद
shlokas.transliteration: áśvāt ǀ iyāya ǀ íti ǀ yát ǀ vádanti ǀ ójasaḥ ǀ jātám ǀ utá ǀ manye ǀ enam ǀmanyóḥ ǀ iyāya ǀ harmyéṣu ǀ tasthau ǀ yátaḥ ǀ pra-jajñé ǀ índraḥ ǀ asya ǀ veda ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Although (some) say he came from the horse (the sun), I know that he is the offspring of strength; hecame from wrath, he stands in the homes (of his enemies);Indraknows whence he was born.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वय॑: सुप॒र्णा उप॑ सेदु॒रिन्द्रं॑ प्रि॒यमे॑धा॒ ऋष॑यो॒ नाध॑मानाः । अप॑ ध्वा॒न्तमू॑र्णु॒हि पू॒र्धि चक्षु॑र्मुमु॒ग्ध्य१॒॑स्मान्नि॒धये॑व ब॒द्धान्
shlokas.transliteration: váyaḥ ǀ su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ úpa ǀ seduḥ ǀ índram ǀ priyá-medhāḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ nā́dhamānāḥ ǀápa ǀ dhvāntám ǀ ūrṇuhí ǀ pūrdhí ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ mumugdhí ǀ asmā́n ǀ nidháyā-iva ǀ baddhā́n ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The swift-moving well-flying (rays of the sun), living sacrifices, discerning (the future), deservingknowledge, investedIndra, dissipate the darkness, fill out the light; release us like men bound with a net.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वसू॑नां वा चर्कृष॒ इय॑क्षन्धि॒या वा॑ य॒ज्ञैर्वा॒ रोद॑स्योः । अर्व॑न्तो वा॒ ये र॑यि॒मन्त॑: सा॒तौ व॒नंअ वा॒ ये सु॒श्रुणं॑ सु॒श्रुतो॒ धुः
shlokas.transliteration: vásūnām ǀ vā ǀ carkṛṣe ǀ íyakṣan ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ vā ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ vā ǀ ródasyoḥ ǀárvantaḥ ǀ vā ǀ yé ǀ rayi-mántaḥ ǀ sātáu ǀ vanúm ǀ vā ǀ yé ǀ su-śrúṇam ǀ su-śrútaḥ ǀ dhúríti dhúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indradesiring to bestow (wealth) is attracted by the inhabitants of heaven and earth (for theacquisition) of riches, either by pious acts or by sacrifices; (he is attracted) either by those swift-moving (person ns)who acquire wealth in battle or by those who being successful (inflict) successful injury.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हव॑ एषा॒मसु॑रो नक्षत॒ द्यां श्र॑वस्य॒ता मन॑सा निंसत॒ क्षाम् । चक्षा॑णा॒ यत्र॑ सुवि॒ताय॑ दे॒वा द्यौर्न वारे॑भिः कृ॒णव॑न्त॒ स्वैः
shlokas.transliteration: hávaḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ ásuraḥ ǀ nakṣata ǀ dyā́m ǀ śravasyatā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ niṃsata ǀ kṣā́m ǀcákṣāṇāḥ ǀ yátra ǀ suvitā́ya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́rebhiḥ ǀ kṛṇávanta ǀ sváiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The animating invocation of these (Aṅgirasas) pervaded heaven; (the gods) with minds desirous offood kissed the earth; and there beholding (the lost cattle), the gods for their own benefit made (illumination) likethe sun by their glorious radiance.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒यमे॑षाम॒मृता॑नां॒ गीः स॒र्वता॑ता॒ ये कृ॒पण॑न्त॒ रत्न॑म् । धियं॑ च य॒ज्ञं च॒ साध॑न्त॒स्ते नो॑ धान्तु वस॒व्य१॒॑मसा॑मि
shlokas.transliteration: iyám ǀ eṣām ǀ amṛ́tānām ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ sarvá-tātā ǀ yé ǀ kṛpáṇanta ǀ rátnam ǀdhíyam ǀ ca ǀ yajñám ǀ ca ǀ sā́dhantaḥ ǀ té ǀ naḥ ǀ dhāntu ǀ vasavyám ǀ ásāmi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “This (is) the praise of these immortal (Gods), who bestow wealth at the sacrifice; perfecting our praiseand sacrifice, may they bestow upon us unequalled riches.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ तत्त॑ इन्द्रा॒यव॑: पनन्ता॒भि य ऊ॒र्वं गोम॑न्तं॒ तितृ॑त्सान् । स॒कृ॒त्स्वं१॒॑ ये पु॑रुपु॒त्रां म॒हीं स॒हस्र॑धारां बृह॒तीं दुदु॑क्षन्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ āyávaḥ ǀ pananta ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ ūrvám ǀ gó-mantam ǀ títṛtsān ǀsakṛt-svám ǀ yé ǀ puru-putrā́m ǀ mahī́m ǀ sahásra-dhārām ǀ bṛhatī́m ǀ dúdhukṣan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Your men praised (you) then,Indra, (those) who wished to break into the vast (stall) full of cattle; whomilked the extensive once-genitive rating earth, mother of many children, the showerer of thousands (of blessings).”

shlokas.sanskrit: शची॑व॒ इन्द्र॒मव॑से कृणुध्व॒मना॑नतं द॒मय॑न्तं पृत॒न्यून् । ऋ॒भु॒क्षणं॑ म॒घवा॑नं सुवृ॒क्तिं भर्ता॒ यो वज्रं॒ नर्यं॑ पुरु॒क्षुः
shlokas.transliteration: śácī-vaḥ ǀ índram ǀ ávase ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ ánānatam ǀ damáyantam ǀ pṛtanyū́n ǀṛbhukṣáṇam ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ su-vṛktím ǀ bhártā ǀ yáḥ ǀ vájram ǀ náryam ǀ puru-kṣúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Celebrators of holy rites, select for your protectionIndrathe unsubdued, the tamer of hostile hosts;mighty, opulent, much glorified, who, loud-shouting, is the bearer of the thunderbolt, which is friendly to man.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्वा॒वान॑ पुरु॒तमं॑ पुरा॒षाळा वृ॑त्र॒हेन्द्रो॒ नामा॑न्यप्राः । अचे॑ति प्रा॒सह॒स्पति॒स्तुवि॑ष्मा॒न्यदी॑मु॒श्मसि॒ कर्त॑वे॒ कर॒त्तत्
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ vavā́na ǀ puru-támam ǀ purāṣā́ṭ ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ nā́māni ǀ aprāḥ ǀáceti ǀ pra-sáhaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ túviṣmān ǀ yát ǀ īm ǀ uśmási ǀ kártave ǀ kárat ǀ tát ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “WhenIndra, the destroyer of cities, had slain the most mighty (Vṛtra), then he the Vṛtra-slayer filledthe waters; he was manifest (to all), the subduer of enemies, the lord of all, the most opulent; may he do thatwhich we desire to have done.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र सु व॑ आपो महि॒मान॑मुत्त॒मं का॒रुर्वो॑चाति॒ सद॑ने वि॒वस्व॑तः । प्र स॒प्तस॑प्त त्रे॒धा हि च॑क्र॒मुः प्र सृत्व॑रीणा॒मति॒ सिन्धु॒रोज॑सा
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ sú ǀ vaḥ ǀ āpaḥ ǀ mahimā́nam ǀ ut-tamám ǀ kārúḥ ǀ vocāti ǀ sádane ǀ vivásvataḥ ǀprá ǀ saptá-sapta ǀ tredhā́ ǀ hí ǀ cakramúḥ ǀ prá ǀ sṛ́tvarīṇām ǀ áti ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ ójasā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Waters, the worshipper addresses to you excellent praise in the dwelling of the instrumental tutor of the rite;they flowed by sevens through the three (worlds); but theSindhusurpasses (all) the (other) streams in strength.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र ते॑ऽरद॒द्वरु॑णो॒ यात॑वे प॒थः सिन्धो॒ यद्वाजाँ॑ अ॒भ्यद्र॑व॒स्त्वम् । भूम्या॒ अधि॑ प्र॒वता॑ यासि॒ सानु॑ना॒ यदे॑षा॒मग्रं॒ जग॑तामिर॒ज्यसि॑
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ aradat ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ yā́tave ǀ patháḥ ǀ síndho íti ǀ yát ǀ vā́jān ǀ abhí ǀ ádravaḥ ǀ tvám ǀbhū́myāḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ pra-vátā ǀ yāsi ǀ sā́nunā ǀ yát ǀ eṣām ǀ ágram ǀ jágatām ǀ irajyási ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “For your course,Sindhu,Varuṇatore open a path, since you hastened towards food; you go by alofty road down upon the earth, by which (road) you reign in the sight of all worlds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दि॒वि स्व॒नो य॑तते॒ भूम्यो॒पर्य॑न॒न्तं शुष्म॒मुदि॑यर्ति भा॒नुना॑ । अ॒भ्रादि॑व॒ प्र स्त॑नयन्ति वृ॒ष्टय॒: सिन्धु॒र्यदेति॑ वृष॒भो न रोरु॑वत्
shlokas.transliteration: diví ǀ svanáḥ ǀ yatate ǀ bhū́myā ǀ upári ǀ anantám ǀ śúṣmam ǀ út ǀ iyarti ǀ bhānúnā ǀabhrā́t-iva ǀ prá ǀ stanayanti ǀ vṛṣṭáyaḥ ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ yát ǀ éti ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ róruvat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The sound goes forth in heaven above the earth; (Sindhu) with shining wave animates his endlessspeed; as rains issue thundering from the cloud, so Sindhu (thunders) when he advances roaring like a bull.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भि त्वा॑ सिन्धो॒ शिशु॒मिन्न मा॒तरो॑ वा॒श्रा अ॑र्षन्ति॒ पय॑सेव धे॒नव॑: । राजे॑व॒ युध्वा॑ नयसि॒ त्वमित्सिचौ॒ यदा॑सा॒मग्रं॑ प्र॒वता॒मिन॑क्षसि
shlokas.transliteration: abhí ǀ tvā ǀ sindho íti ǀ śíśum ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ mātáraḥ ǀ vāśrā́ḥ ǀ arṣanti ǀ páyasā-iva ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀrā́jā-iva ǀ yúdhvā ǀ nayasi ǀ tvám ǀ ít ǀ sícau ǀ yát ǀ āsām ǀ ágram ǀ pra-vátām ǀ ínakṣasi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Like mothers crying for their sons, (the other rivers) hasten towards you,Sindhu, like cows with theirmilk; you lead your two wings like a king going to battle when you march in the van of the streams that aredescending (with you).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मं मे॑ गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति॒ शुतु॑द्रि॒ स्तोमं॑ सचता॒ परु॒ष्ण्या । अ॒सि॒क्न्या म॑रुद्वृधे वि॒तस्त॒यार्जी॑कीये शृणु॒ह्या सु॒षोम॑या
shlokas.transliteration: imám ǀ me ǀ gaṅge ǀ yamune ǀ sarasvati ǀ śútudri ǀ stómam ǀ sacata ǀ páruṣṇi ǀ ā́ ǀasiknyā́ ǀ marut-vṛdhe ǀ vitástayā ǀ ā́rjīkīye ǀ śṛṇuhí ǀ ā́ ǀ su-sómayā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Accept this my praise,Gaṅgā,Yamunā,Sarasvatī,Śutudri, Paruṣṇi,MarudvṛdhawithAsiknī,and Vitazstā; listen, Ārjikīya withSuṣomā.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तृ॒ष्टाम॑या प्रथ॒मं यात॑वे स॒जूः सु॒सर्त्वा॑ र॒सया॑ श्वे॒त्या त्या । त्वं सि॑न्धो॒ कुभ॑या गोम॒तीं क्रुमुं॑ मेह॒त्न्वा स॒रथं॒ याभि॒रीय॑से
shlokas.transliteration: tṛṣṭá-amayā ǀ prathamám ǀ yā́tave ǀ sa-jū́ḥ ǀ su-sártvā ǀ rasáyā ǀ śvetyā́ ǀ tyā́ ǀtvám ǀ sindho íti ǀ kúbhayā ǀ go-matī́m ǀ krúmum ǀ mehatnvā́ ǀ sa-rátham ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ ī́yase ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Sindhu, in order to reach the swift-movingGomatī, have united, yourself first with theTṛṣṭāmā; (now be united) with theSusartu, theRasā, the Śveti, theKubha, and the Mehatnu, inconjunction with which streams you do advance.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋजी॒त्येनी॒ रुश॑ती महि॒त्वा परि॒ ज्रयां॑सि भरते॒ रजां॑सि । अद॑ब्धा॒ सिन्धु॑र॒पसा॑म॒पस्त॒माश्वा॒ न चि॒त्रा वपु॑षीव दर्श॒ता
shlokas.transliteration: ṛ́jītī ǀ énī ǀ rúśatī ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ pári ǀ jráyāṃsi ǀ bharate ǀ rájāṃsi ǀádabdhā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ apásām ǀ apáḥ-tamā ǀ áśvā ǀ ná ǀ citrā́ ǀ vápuṣī-iva ǀ darśatā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Straight-flowing, white-coloured, bright-shining (Sindhu) bear along in its might the rapid waters; theinviolable Sindhu, the most efficacious of the efficacious, is speckled like a mare, beautiful as a handsomewoman.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्वश्वा॒ सिन्धु॑: सु॒रथा॑ सु॒वासा॑ हिर॒ण्ययी॒ सुकृ॑ता वा॒जिनी॑वती । ऊर्णा॑वती युव॒तिः सी॒लमा॑वत्यु॒ताधि॑ वस्ते सु॒भगा॑ मधु॒वृध॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: su-áśvā ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ su-ráthā ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǀ hiraṇyáyī ǀ sú-kṛtā ǀ vājínī-vatī ǀū́rṇā-vatī ǀ yuvatíḥ ǀ sīlámā-vatī ǀ utá ǀ ádhi ǀ vaste ǀ su-bhágā ǀ madhu-vṛ́dham ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheSindhuis rich in horses, rich in chariots, rich in clothes, rich in gold ornaments, well-made, rich infood, rich inwool, ever fresh, abounding Sīlamā plural nts, and the auspicious river wears honey-growing(flowers).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒खं रथं॑ युयुजे॒ सिन्धु॑र॒श्विनं॒ तेन॒ वाजं॑ सनिषद॒स्मिन्ना॒जौ । म॒हान्ह्य॑स्य महि॒मा प॑न॒स्यतेऽद॑ब्धस्य॒ स्वय॑शसो विर॒प्शिन॑:
shlokas.transliteration: su-khám ǀ rátham ǀ yuyuje ǀ síndhuḥ ǀ aśvínam ǀ téna ǀ vā́jam ǀ saniṣat ǀ asmín ǀ ājáu ǀmahā́n ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ panasyáte ǀ ádabdhasya ǀ svá-yaśasaḥ ǀ vi-rapśínaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sindhuhas harnessed his easy-going, well-horsed, chariot, with it may he bring (us) food; the might ofthis inviolable, great, renowned (chariot) at this sacrifice is praised as mighty.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ व॑ ऋञ्जस ऊ॒र्जां व्यु॑ष्टि॒ष्विन्द्रं॑ म॒रुतो॒ रोद॑सी अनक्तन । उ॒भे यथा॑ नो॒ अह॑नी सचा॒भुवा॒ सद॑:सदो वरिव॒स्यात॑ उ॒द्भिदा॑
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ṛñjase ǀ ūrjā́m ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀ índram ǀ marútaḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ anaktana ǀubhé íti ǀ yáthā ǀ naḥ ǀ áhanī íti ǀ sacā-bhúvā ǀ sádaḥ-sadaḥ ǀ varivasyā́taḥ ǀ ut-bhídā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I propitiate you at the commencement of the food-possessing (dawns); you revealIndra, theMaruts,heaven and earth; both heaven and earth being united attend on us in all the chambers of sacrifice; (may they fillus) with wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तदु॒ श्रेष्ठं॒ सव॑नं सुनोत॒नात्यो॒ न हस्त॑यतो॒ अद्रि॑: सो॒तरि॑ । वि॒दद्ध्य१॒॑र्यो अ॒भिभू॑ति॒ पौंस्यं॑ म॒हो रा॒ये चि॑त्तरुते॒ यदर्व॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: tát ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ śréṣṭham ǀ sávanam ǀ sunotana ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ hásta-yataḥ ǀ ádriḥ ǀ sotári ǀvidát ǀ hí ǀ aryáḥ ǀ abhí-bhūti ǀ páuṃsyam ǀ maháḥ ǀ rāyé ǀ cit ǀ tarute ǀ yát ǀ árvataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Pour forth this excellent libation; the stone grasped by thehandis like a horse when the grinder(effuses theSoma). The animating (worshipper) acquires virile strength overpowering (his foes) when (the stone)bestows horses for the sake of great wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तदिद्ध्य॑स्य॒ सव॑नं वि॒वेर॒पो यथा॑ पु॒रा मन॑वे गा॒तुमश्रे॑त् । गोअ॑र्णसि त्वा॒ष्ट्रे अश्व॑निर्णिजि॒ प्रेम॑ध्व॒रेष्व॑ध्व॒राँ अ॑शिश्रयुः
shlokas.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ hí ǀ asya ǀ sávanam ǀ vivéḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ purā́ ǀ mánave ǀ gātúm ǀ áśret ǀgó-arṇasi ǀ tvāṣṭré ǀ áśva-nirniji ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ adhvarā́n ǀ aśiśrayuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May this (sacrificial) work of this grinding-stone the effusion of theSoma, spread as it went formerlyalong the path toManu; when the son ofTvaṣṭā, hidden by the (stolen) cows, and assuming the form of ahorse, (was to be slain), the worshippers had recourse at the sacrifices to the inviolable (upper grinding-stones).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अप॑ हत र॒क्षसो॑ भङ्गु॒राव॑त स्कभा॒यत॒ निॠ॑तिं॒ सेध॒ताम॑तिम् । आ नो॑ र॒यिं सर्व॑वीरं सुनोतन देवा॒व्यं॑ भरत॒ श्लोक॑मद्रयः
shlokas.transliteration: ápa ǀ hata ǀ rakṣásaḥ ǀ bhaṅgurá-vataḥ ǀ skabhāyáta ǀ níḥ-ṛtim ǀ sédhata ǀ ámatim ǀā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ rayím ǀ sárva-vīram ǀ sunotana ǀ deva-avyám ǀ bharata ǀ ślókam ǀ adrayaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Drive away the disturbingrākṣasas; keep offNirṛti; prohibit all malignity; effuse for us riches withmale progeny; bear, stones, the praise that delights the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दि॒वश्चि॒दा वोऽम॑वत्तरेभ्यो वि॒भ्वना॑ चिदा॒श्व॑पस्तरेभ्यः । वा॒योश्चि॒दा सोम॑रभस्तरेभ्यो॒ऽग्नेश्चि॑दर्च पितु॒कृत्त॑रेभ्यः
shlokas.transliteration: diváḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ámavat-tarebhyaḥ ǀ vi-bhvánā ǀ cit ǀ āśvápaḥ-tarebhyaḥ ǀvāyóḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ sómarabhaḥ-tarebhyaḥ ǀ agnéḥ ǀ cit ǀ arca ǀ pitukṛ́t-tarebhyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheAdhvaryu) praises you who are stronger even than heaven, quicker in work that Vibhvan, morediffusive of theSomathanVāyu, more bountiful of food thanAgni.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भु॒रन्तु॑ नो य॒शस॒: सोत्वन्ध॑सो॒ ग्रावा॑णो वा॒चा दि॒विता॑ दि॒वित्म॑ता । नरो॒ यत्र॑ दुह॒ते काम्यं॒ मध्वा॑घो॒षय॑न्तो अ॒भितो॑ मिथ॒स्तुर॑:
shlokas.transliteration: bhurántu ǀ naḥ ǀ yaśásaḥ ǀ sótu ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ vācā́ ǀ divítā ǀ divítmatā ǀnáraḥ ǀ yátra ǀ duhaté ǀ kā́myam ǀ mádhu ǀ ā-ghoṣáyantaḥ ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ mithaḥ-túraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the renowned stones bring us the effusedSoma, (may they establish us) with brilliant praise inthe brilliant (Soma-sacrifice), where the priests milk forth the desirable Soma, crying out all around, and racingeach other.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒न्वन्ति॒ सोमं॑ रथि॒रासो॒ अद्र॑यो॒ निर॑स्य॒ रसं॑ ग॒विषो॑ दुहन्ति॒ ते । दु॒हन्त्यूध॑रुप॒सेच॑नाय॒ कं नरो॑ ह॒व्या न म॑र्जयन्त आ॒सभि॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sunvánti ǀ sómam ǀ rathirā́saḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ asya ǀ rásam ǀ go-íṣaḥ ǀ duhanti ǀ té ǀduhánti ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ upa-sécanāya ǀ kám ǀ náraḥ ǀ havyā́ ǀ ná ǀ marjayante ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The swiftly-moving grinding-stones effuse theSoma, desiring praise, they milk forth Soma; they milkforth for the spinkling (ofAgni); the leaders (of rites) purify the oblations with their mouths.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒ते न॑र॒: स्वप॑सो अभूतन॒ य इन्द्रा॑य सुनु॒थ सोम॑मद्रयः । वा॒मंवा॑मं वो दि॒व्याय॒ धाम्ने॒ वसु॑वसु व॒: पार्थि॑वाय सुन्व॒ते
shlokas.transliteration: eté ǀ naraḥ ǀ su-ápasaḥ ǀ abhūtana ǀ yé ǀ índrāya ǀ sunuthá ǀ sómam ǀ adrayaḥ ǀvāmám-vāmam ǀ vaḥ ǀ divyā́ya ǀ dhā́mne ǀ vásu-vasu ǀ vaḥ ǀ pā́rthivāya ǀ sunvaté ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You stones, leaders (of rites), youu are the doers of good works; you who express theSomaforIndra,(make) all desirable wealth for the glory of heaven; you (give) all treasures to the earthly effuser.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भ्र॒प्रुषो॒ न वा॒चा प्रु॑षा॒ वसु॑ ह॒विष्म॑न्तो॒ न य॒ज्ञा वि॑जा॒नुष॑: । सु॒मारु॑तं॒ न ब्र॒ह्माण॑म॒र्हसे॑ ग॒णम॑स्तोष्येषां॒ न शो॒भसे॑
shlokas.transliteration: abhra-prúṣaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vācā́ ǀ pruṣa ǀ vásu ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yajñā́ḥ ǀ vi-jānúṣaḥ ǀsu-mā́rutam ǀ ná ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ arháse ǀ gaṇám ǀ astoṣi ǀ eṣām ǀ ná ǀ śobháse ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheMaruts), plural ased with our praise like water-drops sent down by clouds, shower wealth; they arethe genitive rators (of the world) like sacrifices abounding with oblations; I have not praised the mighty band ofMaruts (adequately) for their honour or of their glory.”

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रि॒ये मर्या॑सो अ॒ञ्जीँर॑कृण्वत सु॒मारु॑तं॒ न पू॒र्वीरति॒ क्षप॑: । दि॒वस्पु॒त्रास॒ एता॒ न ये॑तिर आदि॒त्यास॒स्ते अ॒क्रा न वा॑वृधुः
shlokas.transliteration: śriyé ǀ máryāsaḥ ǀ añjī́n ǀ akṛṇvata ǀ su-mā́rutam ǀ ná ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ áti ǀ kṣápaḥ ǀdiváḥ ǀ putrā́saḥ ǀ étāḥ ǀ ná ǀ yetire ǀ ādityā́saḥ ǀ té ǀ akrā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ vavṛdhuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The destructive (Maruts) made ornaments for their decoration many hostile hosts cannot overcomethe band of Maruts; the moving sons of heaven do not issue forth, the swift-going sons ofAditido not increase (inglory).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र ये दि॒वः पृ॑थि॒व्या न ब॒र्हणा॒ त्मना॑ रिरि॒च्रे अ॒भ्रान्न सूर्य॑: । पाज॑स्वन्तो॒ न वी॒राः प॑न॒स्यवो॑ रि॒शाद॑सो॒ न मर्या॑ अ॒भिद्य॑वः
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ diváḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ barháṇā ǀ tmánā ǀ riricré ǀ abhrā́t ǀ ná ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀpā́jasvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ panasyávaḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheMaruts), who through the might of heaven and earth have emerged from their own person ns asthe sun emerges from the cloud, (are) desirous of praise like powerful heroes, and radiant like men whooverpower their enemies.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यु॒ष्माकं॑ बु॒ध्ने अ॒पां न याम॑नि विथु॒र्यति॒ न म॒ही श्र॑थ॒र्यति॑ । वि॒श्वप्सु॑र्य॒ज्ञो अ॒र्वाग॒यं सु व॒: प्रय॑स्वन्तो॒ न स॒त्राच॒ आ ग॑त
shlokas.transliteration: yuṣmā́kam ǀ budhné ǀ apā́m ǀ ná ǀ yā́mani ǀ vithuryáti ǀ ná ǀ mahī́ ǀ śratharyáti ǀviśvá-psuḥ ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ arvā́k ǀ ayám ǀ sú ǀ vaḥ ǀ práyasvantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ satrā́caḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In your collision, as in the transit of waters, the earth is not shaken, is not shattered; this manifoldsacrifice comes towards you; approach united as if laden with food.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यू॒यं धू॒र्षु प्र॒युजो॒ न र॒श्मिभि॒र्ज्योति॑ष्मन्तो॒ न भा॒सा व्यु॑ष्टिषु । श्ये॒नासो॒ न स्वय॑शसो रि॒शाद॑सः प्र॒वासो॒ न प्रसि॑तासः परि॒प्रुष॑:
shlokas.transliteration: yūyám ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ pra-yújaḥ ǀ ná ǀ raśmí-bhiḥ ǀ jyótiṣmantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhāsā́ ǀ ví-uṣṭiṣu ǀśyenā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ svá-yaśasaḥ ǀ riśā́dasaḥ ǀ pravā́saḥ ǀ ná ǀ prá-sitāsaḥ ǀ pari-prúṣaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You (move along) like horses harnessed to the chariot-poles with reins; at break of day you (areendowed) with radiance like the luminaries (of heaven); you are like hawks, like the destroyers of foes, desirousof renown; you cover the ground like travellers, you move everywhere.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र यद्वह॑ध्वे मरुतः परा॒काद्यू॒यं म॒हः सं॒वर॑णस्य॒ वस्व॑: । वि॒दा॒नासो॑ वसवो॒ राध्य॑स्या॒राच्चि॒द्द्वेष॑: सनु॒तर्यु॑योत
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ yát ǀ váhadhve ǀ marutaḥ ǀ parākā́t ǀ yūyám ǀ maháḥ ǀ sam-váraṇasya ǀ vásvaḥ ǀvidānā́saḥ ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ rā́dhyasya ǀ ārā́t ǀ cit ǀ dvéṣaḥ ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyota ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When,Maruts, you come from a distance, then,Vasus, distributors of abundant, desirable, covetedwealth, do you scatter afar our concealed foes.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य उ॒दृचि॑ य॒ज्ञे अ॑ध्वरे॒ष्ठा म॒रुद्भ्यो॒ न मानु॑षो॒ ददा॑शत् । रे॒वत्स वयो॑ दधते सु॒वीरं॒ स दे॒वाना॒मपि॑ गोपी॒थे अ॑स्तु
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ ut-ṛ́ci ǀ yajñé ǀ adhvare-sthā́ḥ ǀ marút-bhyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ dádāśat ǀrevát ǀ sáḥ ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhate ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ sáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ ápi ǀ go-pīthé ǀ astu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The worshipper who engaged in worship at the sacrifice, accompanied with praise, presentsdonations (to the priests) as if to theMaruts, he enjoys food with riches, andmaleprogeny; may he be present atthe god'ssoma-drinking.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते हि य॒ज्ञेषु॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑स॒ ऊमा॑ आदि॒त्येन॒ नाम्ना॒ शम्भ॑विष्ठाः । ते नो॑ऽवन्तु रथ॒तूर्म॑नी॒षां म॒हश्च॒ याम॑न्नध्व॒रे च॑का॒नाः
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ ū́māḥ ǀ ādityéna ǀ nā́mnā ǀ śám-bhaviṣṭhāḥ ǀté ǀ naḥ ǀ avantu ǀ ratha-tū́ḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ maháḥ ǀ ca ǀ yā́man ǀ adhvaré ǀ cakānā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May those protecting deities who are entitled to be worshipped at sacrifices, who under the name ofĀdityas are the bestowers of felicity, may they (theMaruts) accelerating their chariots, and desirous of theample (oblation), upon their arrival at the sacrificed protect our praise.”

shlokas.sanskrit: विप्रा॑सो॒ न मन्म॑भिः स्वा॒ध्यो॑ देवा॒व्यो॒३॒॑ न य॒ज्ञैः स्वप्न॑सः । राजा॑नो॒ न चि॒त्राः सु॑सं॒दृश॑: क्षिती॒नां न मर्या॑ अरे॒पस॑:
shlokas.transliteration: víprāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mánma-bhiḥ ǀ su-ādhyáḥ ǀ deva-avyáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yajñáiḥ ǀ su-ápnasaḥ ǀrā́jānaḥ ǀ ná ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ su-sandṛ́śaḥ ǀ kṣitīnā́m ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They (theMaruts) are likeBrāhmaṇassanctified by pious praises, they are instrumental tutors of holy riteslike the propitiators of the gods by sacrifices; decked with various ornaments, and handsome like kings, devoid ofsin like men (who are the lords) of habitations.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निर्न ये भ्राज॑सा रु॒क्मव॑क्षसो॒ वाता॑सो॒ न स्व॒युज॑: स॒द्यऊ॑तयः । प्र॒ज्ञा॒तारो॒ न ज्येष्ठा॑: सुनी॒तय॑: सु॒शर्मा॑णो॒ न सोमा॑ ऋ॒तं य॒ते
shlokas.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ bhrā́jasā ǀ rukmá-vakṣasaḥ ǀ vā́tāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sva-yújaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ-ūtayaḥ ǀpra-jñātā́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ jyéṣṭhāḥ ǀ su-nītáyaḥ ǀ su-śármāṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sómāḥ ǀ ṛtám ǀ yaté ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(You) who likeAgni(are endowed) with splendour, who have golden ornaments upon your breasts,who like the winds (are) self-yoked, swift-moving, who like the extremely wise (are) venerable and able guides,and like theSomathe giver of delight, (do you com) to the (worshipper) going to the sacrifice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वाता॑सो॒ न ये धुन॑यो जिग॒त्नवो॑ऽग्नी॒नां न जि॒ह्वा वि॑रो॒किण॑: । वर्म॑ण्वन्तो॒ न यो॒धाः शिमी॑वन्तः पितॄ॒णां न शंसा॑: सुरा॒तय॑:
shlokas.transliteration: vā́tāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǀ jigatnávaḥ ǀ agnīnā́m ǀ ná ǀ jihvā́ḥ ǀ vi-rokíṇaḥ ǀvármaṇ-vantaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yodhā́ḥ ǀ śímī-vantaḥ ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ná ǀ śáṃsāḥ ǀ su-rātáyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheMaruts), who like the winds cause (the gods) to tremble and move swift; blazing like the flames offires, (who are) the achievers of heroic deeds like warriors clad in mail; munificent donors like the praises ofancestors.”

shlokas.sanskrit: रथा॑नां॒ न ये॒३॒॑ऽराः सना॑भयो जिगी॒वांसो॒ न शूरा॑ अ॒भिद्य॑वः । व॒रे॒यवो॒ न मर्या॑ घृत॒प्रुषो॑ऽभिस्व॒र्तारो॑ अ॒र्कं न सु॒ष्टुभ॑:
shlokas.transliteration: ráthānām ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ arā́ḥ ǀ sá-nābhayaḥ ǀ jigīvā́ṃsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śū́rāḥ ǀ abhí-dyavaḥ ǀvare-yávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ máryāḥ ǀ ghṛta-prúṣaḥ ǀ abhi-svartā́raḥ ǀ arkám ǀ ná ǀ su-stúbhaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Who (are) united to a common centre like the spokes (of the wheels) of chariots, brilliant like victoriousheroes, sprinkling water like benevolent men, sweet-voiced like men who recite praise.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अश्वा॑सो॒ न ये ज्येष्ठा॑स आ॒शवो॑ दिधि॒षवो॒ न र॒थ्य॑: सु॒दान॑वः । आपो॒ न नि॒म्नैरु॒दभि॑र्जिग॒त्नवो॑ वि॒श्वरू॑पा॒ अङ्गि॑रसो॒ न साम॑भिः
shlokas.transliteration: áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yé ǀ jyéṣṭhāsaḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ didhiṣávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ su-dā́navaḥ ǀā́paḥ ǀ ná ǀ nimnáiḥ ǀ udá-bhiḥ ǀ jigatnávaḥ ǀ viśvá-rūpāḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sā́ma-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Who (are) most excellent and swift like horses, lords of cars and munificent like the possessors ofwealth, swiftly moving like rivers with water flowing from a height, (accompanied) everywhere with hymns like themultiformAṅgirasas.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ग्रावा॑णो॒ न सू॒रय॒: सिन्धु॑मातर आदर्दि॒रासो॒ अद्र॑यो॒ न वि॒श्वहा॑ । शि॒शूला॒ न क्री॒ळय॑: सुमा॒तरो॑ महाग्रा॒मो न याम॑न्नु॒त त्वि॒षा
shlokas.transliteration: grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sūráyaḥ ǀ síndhu-mātaraḥ ǀ ā-dardirā́saḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ ná ǀ viśváhā ǀśiśū́lāḥ ǀ ná ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ su-mātáraḥ ǀ mahā-grāmáḥ ǀ ná ǀ yā́man ǀ utá ǀ tviṣā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Having streams for mothers like the grinding-stones which send forth moisture; ever destroying(enemies) like destructive thunderbolts; having tender mothers like sportive infants; (endowed) with splendourlike a great crowd of men in a procession.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒षसां॒ न के॒तवो॑ऽध्वर॒श्रिय॑: शुभं॒यवो॒ नाञ्जिभि॒र्व्य॑श्वितन् । सिन्ध॑वो॒ न य॒यियो॒ भ्राज॑दृष्टयः परा॒वतो॒ न योज॑नानि ममिरे
shlokas.transliteration: uṣásām ǀ ná ǀ ketávaḥ ǀ adhvara-śríyaḥ ǀ śubham-yávaḥ ǀ ná ǀ añjí-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśvitan ǀsíndhavaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yayíyaḥ ǀ bhrā́jat-ṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ parā-vátaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yójanāni ǀ mamire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Who, radiant in sacrifices like the rays of the dawn, shine with their ornaments like those expectant ofgood fortune, (who) swift-moving like rivers, having bright weapons, have traversed leagues like mares who havejourneyed from far, (may they come to our sacrifice).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒भा॒गान्नो॑ देवाः कृणुता सु॒रत्ना॑न॒स्मान्त्स्तो॒तॄन्म॑रुतो वावृधा॒नाः । अधि॑ स्तो॒त्रस्य॑ स॒ख्यस्य॑ गात स॒नाद्धि वो॑ रत्न॒धेया॑नि॒ सन्ति॑
