shlokas.transliteration: su-bhāgā́n ǀ naḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ kṛṇuta ǀ su-rátnān ǀ asmā́n ǀ stotṝ́n ǀ marutaḥ ǀ vavṛdhānā́ḥ ǀádhi ǀ stotrásya ǀ sakhyásya ǀ gāta ǀ sanā́t ǀ hí ǀ vaḥ ǀ ratna-dhéyāni ǀ sánti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “DivineMaruts, magnified (by our praise), render us, your praisers, prosperous and opulent; come tothis friendly laudation, for your precious bounties have been long (bestowed upon us).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अप॑श्यमस्य मह॒तो म॑हि॒त्वमम॑र्त्यस्य॒ मर्त्या॑सु वि॒क्षु । नाना॒ हनू॒ विभृ॑ते॒ सं भ॑रेते॒ असि॑न्वती॒ बप्स॑ती॒ भूर्य॑त्तः
shlokas.transliteration: ápaśyam ǀ asya ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ mahi-tvám ǀ ámartyasya ǀ mártyāsu ǀ vikṣú ǀnā́nā ǀ hánū íti ǀ víbhṛte íti ví-bhṛte ǀ sám ǀ bharete íti ǀ ásinvatī íti ǀ bápsatī íti ǀ bhū́ri ǀ attaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I have beheld the might of the adorable (Agni) immortal in (the hearts of) mortal beings; his two jaws,divided asunder,shuttogether; devouring without masticating consume much (fuel).”

shlokas.sanskrit: गुहा॒ शिरो॒ निहि॑त॒मृध॑ग॒क्षी असि॑न्वन्नत्ति जि॒ह्वया॒ वना॑नि । अत्रा॑ण्यस्मै प॒ड्भिः सं भ॑रन्त्युत्ता॒नह॑स्ता॒ नम॒साधि॑ वि॒क्षु
shlokas.transliteration: gúhā ǀ śíraḥ ǀ ní-hitam ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ akṣī́ íti ǀ ásinvan ǀ atti ǀ jihváyā ǀ vánāni ǀátrāṇi ǀ asmai ǀ paṭ-bhíḥ ǀ sám ǀ bharanti ǀ uttāná-hastāḥ ǀ námasā ǀ ádhi ǀ vikṣú ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “His head is deposited in a cavern; his eyes are wide apart; with his tongue he devours the woodwithout masticating; (the priests) approaching on food reverently offer him oblations among the people withupliftedhands.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र मा॒तुः प्र॑त॒रं गुह्य॑मि॒च्छन्कु॑मा॒रो न वी॒रुध॑: सर्पदु॒र्वीः । स॒सं न प॒क्वम॑विदच्छु॒चन्तं॑ रिरि॒ह्वांसं॑ रि॒प उ॒पस्थे॑ अ॒न्तः
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ mātúḥ ǀ pra-tarám ǀ gúhyam ǀ icchán ǀ kumāráḥ ǀ ná ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ sarpat ǀ urvī́ḥ ǀsamám ǀ ná ǀ pakvám ǀ avidat ǀ śucántam ǀ ririhvā́ṃsam ǀ ripáḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ antáríti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Longing for the abundant creepers of the maternal (earth, longing for) their more excellent concealed(root), he creeps like a child; he has found the tree shining like ripe grain, upon the lap of tthe earth, tasting (theether).”

shlokas.sanskrit: तद्वा॑मृ॒तं रो॑दसी॒ प्र ब्र॑वीमि॒ जाय॑मानो मा॒तरा॒ गर्भो॑ अत्ति । नाहं दे॒वस्य॒ मर्त्य॑श्चिकेता॒ग्निर॒ङ्ग विचे॑ता॒: स प्रचे॑ताः
shlokas.transliteration: tát ǀ vām ǀ ṛtám ǀ rodasī íti ǀ prá ǀ bravīmi ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ mātárā ǀ gárbhaḥ ǀ atti ǀná ǀ ahám ǀ devásya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ ciketa ǀ agníḥ ǀ aṅgá ǀ ví-cetāḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “This (that) I declare unto you, heaven and earth, (is) the truth; as soon as born, the embryo devoursthe parents; I who am a mortal know not (the condition) of the deity;Agni, (OVaiśvānara), is discriminating, heis exceedingly wise.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यो अ॑स्मा॒ अन्नं॑ तृ॒ष्वा॒३॒॑दधा॒त्याज्यै॑र्घृ॒तैर्जु॒होति॒ पुष्य॑ति । तस्मै॑ स॒हस्र॑म॒क्षभि॒र्वि च॒क्षेऽग्ने॑ वि॒श्वत॑: प्र॒त्यङ्ङ॑सि॒ त्वम्
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ asmai ǀ ánnam ǀ tṛṣú ǀ ā-dádhāti ǀ ā́jyaiḥ ǀ ghṛtáiḥ ǀ juhóti ǀ púṣyati ǀtásmai ǀ sahásram ǀ akṣá-bhiḥ ǀ ví ǀ cakṣe ǀ ágne ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ asi ǀ tvám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who quickly offers him food, makes oblations to him with drippingSoma, and delights him (withfood); (Agni) looks upon him with a thousand eyes; you, Agni, are everywhere present.”

shlokas.sanskrit: किं दे॒वेषु॒ त्यज॒ एन॑श्चक॒र्थाग्ने॑ पृ॒च्छामि॒ नु त्वामवि॑द्वान् । अक्री॑ळ॒न्क्रीळ॒न्हरि॒रत्त॑वे॒ऽदन्वि प॑र्व॒शश्च॑कर्त॒ गामि॑वा॒सिः
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ devéṣu ǀ tyájaḥ ǀ énaḥ ǀ cakartha ǀ ágne ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ nú ǀ tvā́m ǀ ávidvān ǀákrīḷan ǀ krī́ḷan ǀ háriḥ ǀ áttave ǀ adán ǀ ví ǀ parva-śáḥ ǀ cakarta ǀ gā́m-iva ǀ asíḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “What wrathful act, what sin have you committed among the gods? Ignorant I ask you,Agni, sporting(here) not sporting (there), golden-hued; eating what is to be eaten, you cut (your food) into pieces as the knife(cuts up) the cow.”

shlokas.sanskrit: विषू॑चो॒ अश्वा॑न्युयुजे वने॒जा ऋजी॑तिभी रश॒नाभि॑र्गृभी॒तान् । च॒क्ष॒दे मि॒त्रो वसु॑भि॒: सुजा॑त॒: समा॑नृधे॒ पर्व॑भिर्वावृधा॒नः
shlokas.transliteration: víṣūcaḥ ǀ áśvān ǀ yuyuje ǀ vane-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́jīti-bhiḥ ǀ raśanā́bhiḥ ǀ gṛbhītā́n ǀcakṣadé ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ sám ǀ ānṛdhe ǀ párva-bhiḥ ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Born in the woods, he has harnessed his steeds which move everywhere held in by straight-guidingreins; friendly and augmented by rays, he has distributed (wealth); he grows in strength nourished with logs ofwood.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निः सप्तिं॑ वाजम्भ॒रं द॑दात्य॒ग्निर्वी॒रं श्रुत्यं॑ कर्मनि॒ष्ठाम् । अ॒ग्नी रोद॑सी॒ वि च॑रत्सम॒ञ्जन्न॒ग्निर्नारीं॑ वी॒रकु॑क्षिं॒ पुरं॑धिम्
shlokas.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ sáptim ǀ vājam-bharám ǀ dadāti ǀ agníḥ ǀ vīrám ǀ śrútyam ǀ karmaniḥ-sthā́m ǀagníḥ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ví ǀ carat ǀ sam-añján ǀ agníḥ ǀ nā́rīm ǀ vīrá-kukṣim ǀ púram-dhim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agnigives (his worshipper) a food-acquiring steed, Agni gives (him) a valiant son, renowned,assiduous in pious works; Agni travels beautifying heaven and earth; Agni (makes) as woman the bearer of maleoff-spring (and) intelligent.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्नेरप्न॑सः स॒मिद॑स्तु भ॒द्राग्निर्म॒ही रोद॑सी॒ आ वि॑वेश । अ॒ग्निरेकं॑ चोदयत्स॒मत्स्व॒ग्निर्वृ॒त्राणि॑ दयते पु॒रूणि॑
shlokas.transliteration: agnéḥ ǀ ápnasaḥ ǀ sam-ít ǀ astu ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ mahī́ íti ǀ ródasī íti ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǀagníḥ ǀ ékam ǀ codayat ǀ samát-su ǀ agníḥ ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ dayate ǀ purū́ṇi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the fuel of the efficientAgnibe auspicious; Agni has penetrated the vast heaven and earth; Agnianimates (the worshipper) alone in battles; Agni destroys numerous enemies.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निर्ह॒ त्यं जर॑त॒: कर्ण॑मावा॒ग्निर॒द्भ्यो निर॑दह॒ज्जरू॑थम् । अ॒ग्निरत्रिं॑ घ॒र्म उ॑रुष्यद॒न्तर॒ग्निर्नृ॒मेधं॑ प्र॒जया॑सृज॒त्सम्
shlokas.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ ha ǀ tyám ǀ járataḥ ǀ kárṇam ǀ āva ǀ agníḥ ǀ at-bhyáḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ adahat ǀ járūtham ǀagníḥ ǀ átrim ǀ gharmé ǀ uruṣyat ǀ antáḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ nṛ-médham ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ asṛjat ǀ sám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agniverily has protected Jaratkarṇa; he has consumed Jarūtha with his flames; Agni rescuedAtriinthe hot fissure; Agni furnished Nṛmedha with progeny.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निर्दा॒द्द्रवि॑णं वी॒रपे॑शा अ॒ग्निॠषिं॒ यः स॒हस्रा॑ स॒नोति॑ । अ॒ग्निर्दि॒वि ह॒व्यमा त॑ताना॒ग्नेर्धामा॑नि॒ विभृ॑ता पुरु॒त्रा
shlokas.transliteration: agníḥ ǀ dāt ǀ dráviṇam ǀ vīrá-peśāḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ yáḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ sanóti ǀagníḥ ǀ diví ǀ havyám ǀ ā́ ǀ tatāna ǀ agnéḥ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ ví-bhṛtā ǀ puru-trā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agnisending forth flames bestows wealth; Agni (gives a son to) the Ṛṣi who acquires a thousandcows; Agni spreads the oblation through heaven, the forms of Agni are manifested in many plural ces.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निमु॒क्थैॠष॑यो॒ वि ह्व॑यन्ते॒ऽग्निं नरो॒ याम॑नि बाधि॒तास॑: । अ॒ग्निं वयो॑ अ॒न्तरि॑क्षे॒ पत॑न्तो॒ऽग्निः स॒हस्रा॒ परि॑ याति॒ गोना॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: agním ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ví ǀ hvayante ǀ agním ǀ náraḥ ǀ yā́mani ǀ bādhitā́saḥ ǀagním ǀ váyaḥ ǀ antárikṣe ǀ pátantaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ sahásrā ǀ pári ǀ yāti ǀ gónām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The Ṛṣis variously invokeAgniwith hymns; men when hard pressed in battle (invoke) Agni; the birdsflying in mid-heaven (invoke) Agni; Agni circumambulates thousands of cattle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निं विश॑ ईळते॒ मानु॑षी॒र्या अ॒ग्निं मनु॑षो॒ नहु॑षो॒ वि जा॒ताः । अ॒ग्निर्गान्ध॑र्वीं प॒थ्या॑मृ॒तस्या॒ग्नेर्गव्यू॑तिर्घृ॒त आ निष॑त्ता
shlokas.transliteration: agním ǀ víśaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ agním ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ ví ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀagníḥ ǀ gā́ndharvīm ǀ pathyā́m ǀ ṛtásya ǀ agnéḥ ǀ gávyūtiḥ ǀ ghṛté ǀ ā́ ǀ ní-sattā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The races who are of human birth praise (Agni, so do the men descended from kingNahuṣa; Agni,(hears) the voice which is fit for the path of sacrifice; Agni's path lies everywhere in ghī.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्नये॒ ब्रह्म॑ ऋ॒भव॑स्ततक्षुर॒ग्निं म॒हाम॑वोचामा सुवृ॒क्तिम् । अग्ने॒ प्राव॑ जरि॒तारं॑ यवि॒ष्ठाग्ने॒ महि॒ द्रवि॑ण॒मा य॑जस्व
shlokas.transliteration: agnáye ǀ bráhma ǀ ṛbhávaḥ ǀ tatakṣuḥ ǀ agním ǀ mahā́m ǀ avocāma ǀ su-vṛktím ǀágne ǀ prá ǀ ava ǀ jaritā́ram ǀ yaviṣṭha ǀ ágne ǀ máhi ǀ dráviṇam ǀ ā́ ǀ yajasva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheṚbhushave fabricated praise forAgni; we have recited pious praise to the mighty Agni; Agni,youngest (of the gods), protect your worshipper; Agni, bestow (on him) abundant wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य इ॒मा विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि॒ जुह्व॒दृषि॒र्होता॒ न्यसी॑दत्पि॒ता न॑: । स आ॒शिषा॒ द्रवि॑णमि॒च्छमा॑नः प्रथम॒च्छदव॑राँ॒ आ वि॑वेश
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ júhvat ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ní ǀ ásīdat ǀ pitā́ ǀ naḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ ā-śíṣā ǀ dráviṇam ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ prathama-chát ǀ ávarān ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: किं स्वि॑दासीदधि॒ष्ठान॑मा॒रम्भ॑णं कत॒मत्स्वि॑त्क॒थासी॑त् । यतो॒ भूमिं॑ ज॒नय॑न्वि॒श्वक॑र्मा॒ वि द्यामौर्णो॑न्महि॒ना वि॒श्वच॑क्षाः
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ āsīt ǀ adhi-sthā́nam ǀ ā-rámbhaṇam ǀ katamát ǀ svit ǀ kathā́ ǀ āsīt ǀyátaḥ ǀ bhū́mim ǀ janáyan ǀ viśvá-karmā ǀ ví ǀ dyā́m ǀ áurṇot ǀ mahinā́ ǀ viśvá-cakṣāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “What was the station? What was the material? How was (it done)? So that the beholder of all,Viśvakarman(was) genitive rating and disclosed heaven by his might.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒श्वत॑श्चक्षुरु॒त वि॒श्वतो॑मुखो वि॒श्वतो॑बाहुरु॒त वि॒श्वत॑स्पात् । सं बा॒हुभ्यां॒ धम॑ति॒ सं पत॑त्रै॒र्द्यावा॒भूमी॑ ज॒नय॑न्दे॒व एक॑:
shlokas.transliteration: viśvátaḥ-cakṣuḥ ǀ utá ǀ viśvátaḥ-mukhaḥ ǀ viśvátaḥ-bāhuḥ ǀ utá ǀ viśvátaḥ-pāt ǀsám ǀ bāhú-bhyām ǀ dhámati ǀ sám ǀ pátatraiḥ ǀ dyā́vābhū́mī íti ǀ janáyan ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Having eyes everywhere, and having a face everywhere, having arms everywhere, and having feeteverywhere, he traverses (heaven) with his arms, (earth) with his swift-moving (feet), and exists a god withoutcompanion genitive rating heaven and earth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: किं स्वि॒द्वनं॒ क उ॒ स वृ॒क्ष आ॑स॒ यतो॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी नि॑ष्टत॒क्षुः । मनी॑षिणो॒ मन॑सा पृ॒च्छतेदु॒ तद्यद॒ध्यति॑ष्ठ॒द्भुव॑नानि धा॒रय॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ svit ǀ vánam ǀ káḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sáḥ ǀ vṛkṣáḥ ǀ āsa ǀ yátaḥ ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ niḥ-tatakṣúḥ ǀmánīṣiṇaḥ ǀ mánasā ǀ pṛccháta ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tát ǀ yát ǀ adhi-átiṣṭhat ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ dhāráyan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Which was the forest, which the tree, from which they fabricated heaven and earth? Inquire, sages, inyour minds what (plural ce) he was stationed in when holding the worlds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: या ते॒ धामा॑नि पर॒माणि॒ याव॒मा या म॑ध्य॒मा वि॑श्वकर्मन्नु॒तेमा । शिक्षा॒ सखि॑भ्यो ह॒विषि॑ स्वधावः स्व॒यं य॑जस्व त॒न्वं॑ वृधा॒नः
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ ǀ te ǀ dhā́māni ǀ paramā́ṇi ǀ yā́ ǀ avamā́ ǀ yā́ ǀ madhyamā́ ǀ viśva-karman ǀ utá ǀ imā́ ǀśíkṣa ǀ sákhi-bhyaḥ ǀ havíṣi ǀ svadhā-vaḥ ǀ svayám ǀ yajasva ǀ tanvám ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Grant to your friends,Viśvakarman, at the oblation, your best, your worst and your intermediate forms,and to these do you yourself, possessor of the oblation, becoming augmented in person n (by oblations), offerworship.”

shlokas.sanskrit: विश्व॑कर्मन्ह॒विषा॑ वावृधा॒नः स्व॒यं य॑जस्व पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्याम् । मुह्य॑न्त्व॒न्ये अ॒भितो॒ जना॑स इ॒हास्माकं॑ म॒घवा॑ सू॒रिर॑स्तु
shlokas.transliteration: víśva-karman ǀ havíṣā ǀ vavṛdhānáḥ ǀ svayám ǀ yajasva ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǀmúhyantu ǀ anyé ǀ abhítaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ asmā́kam ǀ maghá-vā ǀ sūríḥ ǀ astu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “VIśvakarman, magnified by the oblation, do you of yourself worship earth and heaven; let other men(who offer no oblations) be everywhere confounded; may he, rich in oblations, be the granter of heaven at thisour (sacrifice).”

shlokas.sanskrit: वा॒चस्पतिं॑ वि॒श्वक॑र्माणमू॒तये॑ मनो॒जुवं॒ वाजे॑ अ॒द्या हु॑वेम । स नो॒ विश्वा॑नि॒ हव॑नानि जोषद्वि॒श्वश॑म्भू॒रव॑से सा॒धुक॑र्मा
shlokas.transliteration: vācáḥ ǀ pátim ǀ viśvá-karmāṇam ǀ ūtáye ǀ manaḥ-júvam ǀ vā́je ǀ adyá ǀ huvema ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ hávanāni ǀ joṣat ǀ viśvá-śambhūḥ ǀ ávase ǀ sādhú-karmā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let us this day invoke for our protection the lord of speech, the creator of all, who is swift as thought;may he, the bestower of all happiness, the doer of good works, be propitiated by all our oblations, (so as) togrant us his protection.”

shlokas.sanskrit: चक्षु॑षः पि॒ता मन॑सा॒ हि धीरो॑ घृ॒तमे॑ने अजन॒न्नन्न॑माने । य॒देदन्ता॒ अद॑दृहन्त॒ पूर्व॒ आदिद्द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी अ॑प्रथेताम्
shlokas.transliteration: cákṣuṣaḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ mánasā ǀ hí ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ ghṛtám ǀ ene íti ǀ ajanat ǀ námnamāne íti ǀyadā́ ǀ ít ǀ ántāḥ ǀ ádadṛhanta ǀ pū́rve ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ aprathetām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The maker of the senses, resolute in mind, engendered the water, (and then) these two (heaven andearth) floating (on the waters); when those ancient boundaries were fixed, then the heaven and earth wereexpanded.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒श्वक॑र्मा॒ विम॑ना॒ आद्विहा॑या धा॒ता वि॑धा॒ता प॑र॒मोत सं॒दृक् । तेषा॑मि॒ष्टानि॒ समि॒षा म॑दन्ति॒ यत्रा॑ सप्तऋ॒षीन्प॒र एक॑मा॒हुः
shlokas.transliteration: viśvá-karmā ǀ ví-manāḥ ǀ ā́t ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ dhātā́ ǀ vi-dhātā́ ǀ paramā́ ǀ utá ǀ sam-dṛ́k ǀtéṣām ǀ iṣṭā́ni ǀ sám ǀ iṣā́ ǀ madanti ǀ yátra ǀ sapta-ṛṣī́n ǀ paráḥ ǀ ékam ǀ āhúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Viśvakarman, of comprehensive mind and manifold greatness, is all- pervading, the creator, thearranger and the supreme supervisor; him in whom the desires of their (senses) are satisfied with food, they callsecond line of the ṛca: him in whom they delight their forms (or plural ces) with water, him, those who are skille dinViśvakarman;Niruktanotes that at the universal sacrifice ViśvakarmanBhauvanaoffered up all beings and thenhimself].”

shlokas.sanskrit: यो न॑: पि॒ता ज॑नि॒ता यो वि॑धा॒ता धामा॑नि॒ वेद॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ । यो दे॒वानां॑ नाम॒धा एक॑ ए॒व तं स॑म्प्र॒श्नं भुव॑ना यन्त्य॒न्या
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ janitā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ vi-dhātā́ ǀ dhā́māni ǀ véda ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀyáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ nāma-dhā́ḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀ evá ǀ tám ǀ sam-praśnám ǀ bhúvanā ǀ yanti ǀ anyā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who is our preserver, our parent, the creator (of all), who knows our abodes (and knows) allbeings, who is the name-giver of the gods-- he is one; other beings come to him to inquire.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त आय॑जन्त॒ द्रवि॑णं॒ सम॑स्मा॒ ऋष॑य॒: पूर्वे॑ जरि॒तारो॒ न भू॒ना । अ॒सूर्ते॒ सूर्ते॒ रज॑सि निष॒त्ते ये भू॒तानि॑ स॒मकृ॑ण्वन्नि॒मानि॑
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ ā́ ǀ ayajanta ǀ dráviṇam ǀ sám ǀ asmai ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ pū́rve ǀ jaritā́raḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhūnā́ ǀasū́rte ǀ sū́rte ǀ rájasi ǀ ni-satté ǀ yé ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ sam-ákṛṇvan ǀ imā́ni ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Those ancient Ṛṣis who adorned (with light) these beings in the animate and inanimate world, offerto him wealth (of sacrifice) as praisers with abundant (laudation).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प॒रो दि॒वा प॒र ए॒ना पृ॑थि॒व्या प॒रो दे॒वेभि॒रसु॑रै॒र्यदस्ति॑ । कं स्वि॒द्गर्भं॑ प्रथ॒मं द॑ध्र॒ आपो॒ यत्र॑ दे॒वाः स॒मप॑श्यन्त॒ विश्वे॑
shlokas.transliteration: paráḥ ǀ divā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ enā́ ǀ pṛthivyā́ ǀ paráḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ ásuraiḥ ǀ yát ǀ ásti ǀkám ǀ svit ǀ gárbham ǀ prathamám ǀ dadhre ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yátra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sam-ápaśyanta ǀ víśve ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “What was that embryo which was beyond the heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods, beyondtheasuras, which the waters first retained, in which all the gods contemplated each other?”

shlokas.sanskrit: तमिद्गर्भं॑ प्रथ॒मं द॑ध्र॒ आपो॒ यत्र॑ दे॒वाः स॒मग॑च्छन्त॒ विश्वे॑ । अ॒जस्य॒ नाभा॒वध्येक॒मर्पि॑तं॒ यस्मि॒न्विश्वा॑नि॒ भुव॑नानि त॒स्थुः
shlokas.transliteration: tám ǀ ít ǀ gárbham ǀ prathamám ǀ dadhre ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ yátra ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sam-ágacchanta ǀ víśve ǀajásya ǀ nā́bhau ǀ ádhi ǀ ékam ǀ árpitam ǀ yásmin ǀ víśvāni ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tasthúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The waters verily first retained the embryo in which all the gods were aggregated, single deposited onthe navel of the unborn (creator), in which all beings abide.”

shlokas.sanskrit: न तं वि॑दाथ॒ य इ॒मा ज॒जाना॒न्यद्यु॒ष्माक॒मन्त॑रं बभूव । नी॒हा॒रेण॒ प्रावृ॑ता॒ जल्प्या॑ चासु॒तृप॑ उक्थ॒शास॑श्चरन्ति
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ tám ǀ vidātha ǀ yáḥ ǀ imā́ ǀ jajā́na ǀ anyát ǀ yuṣmā́kam ǀ ántaram ǀ babhūva ǀnīhāréṇa ǀ prā́vṛtāḥ ǀ jálpyā ǀ ca ǀ asu-tṛ́paḥ ǀ uktha-śásaḥ ǀ caranti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You know not him who has genitive rated these (beings); (his life) is another, different from yours;wrapped in fog, and foolish speech (do they) wander (who are) gluttonous and engaged in devotion.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्ते॑ म॒न्योऽवि॑धद्वज्र सायक॒ सह॒ ओज॑: पुष्यति॒ विश्व॑मानु॒षक् । सा॒ह्याम॒ दास॒मार्यं॒ त्वया॑ यु॒जा सह॑स्कृतेन॒ सह॑सा॒ सह॑स्वता
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ te ǀ manyo íti ǀ ávidhat ǀ vajra ǀ sāyaka ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ puṣyati ǀ víśvam ǀ ānuṣák ǀsahyā́ma ǀ dā́sam ǀ ā́ryam ǀ tváyā ǀ yujā́ ǀ sáhaḥ-kṛtena ǀ sáhasā ǀ sáhasvatā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who worships you,Manyu, the thunderbolt, the destroyer (of enemies), enjoys all might andstrength, combined; may we oversome theDāsaand theĀryawith you for our ally, invigorating, strong andvigorous.”

shlokas.sanskrit: म॒न्युरिन्द्रो॑ म॒न्युरे॒वास॑ दे॒वो म॒न्युर्होता॒ वरु॑णो जा॒तवे॑दाः । म॒न्युं विश॑ ईळते॒ मानु॑षी॒र्याः पा॒हि नो॑ मन्यो॒ तप॑सा स॒जोषा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: manyúḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ manyúḥ ǀ evá ǀ āsa ǀ deváḥ ǀ manyúḥ ǀ hótā ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǀmanyúm ǀ víśaḥ ǀ īḷate ǀ mā́nuṣīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ pāhí ǀ naḥ ǀ manyo íti ǀ tápasā ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “ManyuisIndra; Manyu verily was a god; Manyu is the sacrificing priest (Agni), the omniscientVaruṇa;the people who are of human descent, praise Manyu; protect us, Manyu, well plural ased along withTapas.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भी॑हि मन्यो त॒वस॒स्तवी॑या॒न्तप॑सा यु॒जा वि ज॑हि॒ शत्रू॑न् । अ॒मि॒त्र॒हा वृ॑त्र॒हा द॑स्यु॒हा च॒ विश्वा॒ वसू॒न्या भ॑रा॒ त्वं न॑:
shlokas.transliteration: abhí ǀ ihi ǀ manyo íti ǀ tavásaḥ ǀ távīyān ǀ tápasā ǀ yujā́ ǀ ví ǀ jahi ǀ śátrūn ǀamitra-hā́ ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ dasyu-hā́ ǀ ca ǀ víśvā ǀ vásūni ǀ ā́ ǀ bhara ǀ tvám ǀ naḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Come to us Manyuu, who are the strongest of the strong; withTapasas your ally overthrow ourenemies; do you who are the slayer of enemies, the slayer of adversaries, the slayer of foes, bring to us allriches.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं हि म॑न्यो अ॒भिभू॑त्योजाः स्वय॒म्भूर्भामो॑ अभिमातिषा॒हः । वि॒श्वच॑र्षणि॒: सहु॑रि॒: सहा॑वान॒स्मास्वोज॒: पृत॑नासु धेहि
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ hí ǀ manyo íti ǀ abhíbhūti-ojāḥ ǀ svayam-bhū́ḥ ǀ bhā́maḥ ǀ abhimāti-saháḥ ǀviśvá-carṣaṇiḥ ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ sáhāvān ǀ asmā́su ǀ ójaḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāsu ǀ dhehi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Do you,Manyu, who are possessed of over-powering strength, self- existent, irate, the overcomer ofenemies, the beholder of all, enduring, vigorous, grant us strength in battles.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भा॒गः सन्नप॒ परे॑तो अस्मि॒ तव॒ क्रत्वा॑ तवि॒षस्य॑ प्रचेतः । तं त्वा॑ मन्यो अक्र॒तुर्जि॑हीळा॒हं स्वा त॒नूर्ब॑ल॒देया॑य॒ मेहि॑
shlokas.transliteration: abhāgáḥ ǀ sán ǀ ápa ǀ párā-itaḥ ǀ asmi ǀ táva ǀ krátvā ǀ taviṣásya ǀ praceta íti pra-cetaḥ ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ manyo íti ǀ akratúḥ ǀ jihīḷa ǀ ahám ǀ svā́ ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ bala-déyāya ǀ mā ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “SageManyu, taking no part in the worship of you, the powerful one, I have retreated (from before myfoes); worshipping not, I was angry with you; (yet) being (incorporated with) my body, approach me to give mestrength.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यं ते॑ अ॒स्म्युप॒ मेह्य॒र्वाङ्प्र॑तीची॒नः स॑हुरे विश्वधायः । मन्यो॑ वज्रिन्न॒भि मामा व॑वृत्स्व॒ हना॑व॒ दस्यूँ॑रु॒त बो॑ध्या॒पेः
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ te ǀ asmi ǀ úpa ǀ mā ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǀ pratīcīnáḥ ǀ sahure ǀ viśva-dhāyaḥ ǀmányo íti ǀ vajrin ǀ abhí ǀ mā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtsva ǀ hánāva ǀ dásyūn ǀ utá ǀ bodhi ǀ āpéḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भि प्रेहि॑ दक्षिण॒तो भ॑वा॒ मेऽधा॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ जङ्घनाव॒ भूरि॑ । जु॒होमि॑ ते ध॒रुणं॒ मध्वो॒ अग्र॑मु॒भा उ॑पां॒शु प्र॑थ॒मा पि॑बाव
shlokas.transliteration: abhí ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ dakṣiṇatáḥ ǀ bhava ǀ me ǀ ádha ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ jaṅghanāva ǀ bhū́ri ǀjuhómi ǀ te ǀ dharúṇam ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ ágram ǀ ubháu ǀ upa-aṃśú ǀ prathamā́ ǀ pibāva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Approach, be upon my right, let us slay a multitude of foes; I offer to you the bestSoma, the sustainer;let us both drink it first in privacy.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वया॑ मन्यो स॒रथ॑मारु॒जन्तो॒ हर्ष॑माणासो धृषि॒ता म॑रुत्वः । ति॒ग्मेष॑व॒ आयु॑धा सं॒शिशा॑ना अ॒भि प्र य॑न्तु॒ नरो॑ अ॒ग्निरू॑पाः
shlokas.transliteration: tváyā ǀ manyo íti ǀ sa-rátham ǀ ā-rujántaḥ ǀ hárṣamāṇāsaḥ ǀ dhṛṣitā́ḥ ǀ marutvaḥ ǀtigmá-iṣavaḥ ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ sam-śíśānāḥ ǀ abhí ǀ prá ǀ yantu ǀ náraḥ ǀ agní-rūpāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the leaders (of rites) wearing the form ofAgni, (ascending) the same car with you,Manyu, whoare accompanied by theMaruts, proceed to combat, advancing, exulting, indignant, armed with sharp arrow,whetting their weapons.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒ग्निरि॑व मन्यो त्विषि॒तः स॑हस्व सेना॒नीर्न॑: सहुरे हू॒त ए॑धि । ह॒त्वाय॒ शत्रू॒न्वि भ॑जस्व॒ वेद॒ ओजो॒ मिमा॑नो॒ वि मृधो॑ नुदस्व
shlokas.transliteration: agníḥ-iva ǀ manyo íti ǀ tviṣitáḥ ǀ sahasva ǀ senā-nī́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ sahure ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ edhi ǀhatvā́ya ǀ śátrūn ǀ ví ǀ bhajasva ǀ védaḥ ǀ ójaḥ ǀ mímānaḥ ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ nudasva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Manyu, blazing likeAgni, overthrow (our foes), come as our genitive ral, enduring (manyu) when invoked(by us) in battle; having slain the enemies divide (among us) the treasure; granting (us) strength, scatter (our)foes.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सह॑स्व मन्यो अ॒भिमा॑तिम॒स्मे रु॒जन्मृ॒णन्प्र॑मृ॒णन्प्रेहि॒ शत्रू॑न् । उ॒ग्रं ते॒ पाजो॑ न॒न्वा रु॑रुध्रे व॒शी वशं॑ नयस एकज॒ त्वम्
shlokas.transliteration: sáhasva ǀ manyo íti ǀ abhí-mātim ǀ asmé íti ǀ ruján ǀ mṛṇán ǀ pra-mṛṇán ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ śátrūn ǀugrám ǀ te ǀ pā́jaḥ ǀ nanú ǀ ā́ ǀ rurudhre ǀ vaśī́ ǀ váśam ǀ nayase ǀ eka-ja ǀ tvám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Overthrow,Manyu, our assailant; advance against our foes, wounding, killing, annihilating them; (who)can resist your fierce might? O you who are without companion, subjecting them you lead them subject.”

shlokas.sanskrit: एको॑ बहू॒नाम॑सि मन्यवीळि॒तो विशं॑विशं यु॒धये॒ सं शि॑शाधि । अकृ॑त्तरु॒क्त्वया॑ यु॒जा व॒यं द्यु॒मन्तं॒ घोषं॑ विज॒याय॑ कृण्महे
shlokas.transliteration: ékaḥ ǀ bahūnā́m ǀ asi ǀ manyo íti ǀ īḷitáḥ ǀ víśam-viśam ǀ yudháye ǀ sám ǀ śiśādhi ǀákṛtta-ruk ǀ tváyā ǀ yujā́ ǀ vayám ǀ dyu-mántam ǀ ghóṣam ǀ vi-jayā́ya ǀ kṛṇmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You are praised,Manyu, as (the conqueror) alone of many; animate us to contend with all men; withyyou, O you of unshorn radiance, for our ally, we raise aloud shout for victory.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒जे॒ष॒कृदिन्द्र॑ इवानवब्र॒वो॒३॒॑ऽस्माकं॑ मन्यो अधि॒पा भ॑वे॒ह । प्रि॒यं ते॒ नाम॑ सहुरे गृणीमसि वि॒द्मा तमुत्सं॒ यत॑ आब॒भूथ॑
shlokas.transliteration: vijeṣa-kṛ́t ǀ índraḥ-iva ǀ anava-braváḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ manyo íti ǀ adhi-pā́ḥ ǀ bhava ǀ ihá ǀpriyám ǀ te ǀ nā́ma ǀ sahure ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀ vidmá ǀ tám ǀ útsam ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā-babhū́tha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Manyu, the giver of victory likeIndra, irreproachable, be you our protector at this (sacrifice); enduringone, we sing to you acceptable praise; we know this to be the source whence you have become (mighty).”

shlokas.sanskrit: आभू॑त्या सह॒जा व॑ज्र सायक॒ सहो॑ बिभर्ष्यभिभूत॒ उत्त॑रम् । क्रत्वा॑ नो मन्यो स॒ह मे॒द्ये॑धि महाध॒नस्य॑ पुरुहूत सं॒सृजि॑
shlokas.transliteration: ā́-bhūtyā ǀ saha-jā́ḥ ǀ vajra ǀ sāyaka ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ bibharṣi ǀ abhi-bhūte ǀ út-taram ǀkrátvā ǀ naḥ ǀ manyo íti ǀ sahá ǀ medī́ ǀ edhi ǀ mahā-dhanásya ǀ puru-hūta ǀ sam-sṛ́ji ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Manyu), your destructive thunderbolt, the over-powerer (of foes), twin-born with victory, you possessexceeding strength; be favourable to us, Manyu, in deeds, you who are invoked by many in the shock of battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: संसृ॑ष्टं॒ धन॑मु॒भयं॑ स॒माकृ॑तम॒स्मभ्यं॑ दत्तां॒ वरु॑णश्च म॒न्युः । भियं॒ दधा॑ना॒ हृद॑येषु॒ शत्र॑व॒: परा॑जितासो॒ अप॒ नि ल॑यन्ताम्
shlokas.transliteration: sám-sṛṣṭam ǀ dhánam ǀ ubháyam ǀ sam-ā́kṛtam ǀ asmábhyam ǀ dattām ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ manyúḥ ǀbhíyam ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ hṛ́dayeṣu ǀ śátravaḥ ǀ párā-jitāsaḥ ǀ ápa ǀ ní ǀ layantām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayVaruṇaandManyubestow upon us wealth of both kinds, undivided and completely our own, andmay our enemies, bearing fear within their hearts, be overcome and utterly destroyed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒त्येनोत्त॑भिता॒ भूमि॒: सूर्ये॒णोत्त॑भिता॒ द्यौः । ऋ॒तेना॑दि॒त्यास्ति॑ष्ठन्ति दि॒वि सोमो॒ अधि॑ श्रि॒तः
shlokas.transliteration: satyéna ǀ úttabhitā ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ úttabhitā ǀ dyáuḥ ǀṛténa ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ tiṣṭhanti ǀ diví ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ śritáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Earth is upheld by truth; heaven is upheld by the sun; theĀdityasare supported by sacrifice,Somaissupreme in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमे॑नादि॒त्या ब॒लिन॒: सोमे॑न पृथि॒वी म॒ही । अथो॒ नक्ष॑त्राणामे॒षामु॒पस्थे॒ सोम॒ आहि॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: sómena ǀ ādityā́ḥ ǀ balínaḥ ǀ sómena ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ mahī́ ǀátho íti ǀ nákṣatrāṇām ǀ eṣā́m ǀ upá-sthe ǀ sómaḥ ǀ ā́-hitaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “BySomatheĀdityasare strong; by Soma the earth is great; Soma is stationed in the vicinity of theseNakṣatras.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमं॑ मन्यते पपि॒वान्यत्स॑म्पिं॒षन्त्योष॑धिम् । सोमं॒ यं ब्र॒ह्माणो॑ वि॒दुर्न तस्या॑श्नाति॒ कश्च॒न
shlokas.transliteration: sómam ǀ manyate ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ yát ǀ sam-piṃṣánti ǀ óṣadhim ǀsómam ǀ yám ǀ brahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ vidúḥ ǀ ná ǀ tásya ǀ aśnāti ǀ káḥ ǀ caná ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who has drunk thinks that the herb which men crush is theSoma; (but) that which theBrāhmaṇas know to be Soma,, of that no one partakes. {i.e., no one partakes of it unless he has sacrificed; ifthe Soma be taken as the moon, 'no one' will mean 'no one but the gods'].”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒च्छद्वि॑धानैर्गुपि॒तो बार्ह॑तैः सोम रक्षि॒तः । ग्राव्णा॒मिच्छृ॒ण्वन्ति॑ष्ठसि॒ न ते॑ अश्नाति॒ पार्थि॑वः
shlokas.transliteration: ācchát-vidhānaiḥ ǀ gupitáḥ ǀ bā́rhataiḥ ǀ soma ǀ rakṣitáḥ ǀgrā́vṇām ǀ ít ǀ śṛṇván ǀ tiṣṭhasi ǀ ná ǀ te ǀ aśnāti ǀ pā́rthivaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Concealed by means of coverings, protected by the Bārhats, OSoma, you abide listening to thegrinding-stones; no terrestrial being partakes of you.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्त्वा॑ देव प्र॒पिब॑न्ति॒ तत॒ आ प्या॑यसे॒ पुन॑: । वा॒युः सोम॑स्य रक्षि॒ता समा॑नां॒ मास॒ आकृ॑तिः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ tvā ǀ deva ǀ pra-píbanti ǀ tátaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ pyāyase ǀ púnaríti ǀvāyúḥ ǀ sómasya ǀ rakṣitā́ ǀ sámānām ǀ mā́saḥ ǀ ā́-kṛtiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, O god, they quaff you, then do you renew yourself again;Vāyuis the guardian ofSoma, themaker of years and months.”

shlokas.sanskrit: रैभ्या॑सीदनु॒देयी॑ नाराशं॒सी न्योच॑नी । सू॒र्याया॑ भ॒द्रमिद्वासो॒ गाथ॑यैति॒ परि॑ष्कृतम्
shlokas.transliteration: ráibhī ǀ āsīt ǀ anu-déyī ǀ nārāśaṃsī́ ǀ ni-ócanī ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ bhadrám ǀ ít ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ gā́thayā ǀ eti ǀ pári-kṛtam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Raibhi was her companion; Nārāśaṃsī her slave;Sūrya's lovely dress was adorned byGātha.”

shlokas.sanskrit: चित्ति॑रा उप॒बर्ह॑णं॒ चक्षु॑रा अ॒भ्यञ्ज॑नम् । द्यौर्भूमि॒: कोश॑ आसी॒द्यदया॑त्सू॒र्या पति॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: cíttiḥ ǀ āḥ ǀ upa-bárhaṇam ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ āḥ ǀ abhi-áñjanam ǀdyáuḥ ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ kóśaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ yát ǀ áyāt ǀ sūryā́ ǀ pátim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Citti(mind) was the pillow, the eye was the collyrium; heaven and earth were the box when Sūryawent to her husband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्तोमा॑ आसन्प्रति॒धय॑: कु॒रीरं॒ छन्द॑ ओप॒शः । सू॒र्याया॑ अ॒श्विना॑ व॒राग्निरा॑सीत्पुरोग॒वः
shlokas.transliteration: stómāḥ ǀ āsan ǀ prati-dháyaḥ ǀ kurī́ram ǀ chándaḥ ǀ opaśáḥ ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ aśvínā ǀ varā́ ǀ agníḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ puraḥ-gaváḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Hymns were the cross-bars (of the car); the Kurīra metre was the thong of the whip; theAśvinswereSūrya's groomsmen;Agniwas the leader of the procession.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमो॑ वधू॒युर॑भवद॒श्विना॑स्तामु॒भा व॒रा । सू॒र्यां यत्पत्ये॒ शंस॑न्तीं॒ मन॑सा सवि॒ताद॑दात्
shlokas.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ vadhū-yúḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ aśvínā ǀ āstām ǀ ubhā́ ǀ varā́ ǀsūryā́m ǀ yát ǀ pátye ǀ śáṃsantīm ǀ mánasā ǀ savitā́ ǀ ádadāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Somawas desirous of a bride; the twoAśvinswere the two groomsmen whenSavitāgaveSūrya,who was ripe for a husband, (to Soma endowed) with intelligence.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मनो॑ अस्या॒ अन॑ आसी॒द्द्यौरा॑सीदु॒त च्छ॒दिः । शु॒क्राव॑न॒ड्वाहा॑वास्तां॒ यदया॑त्सू॒र्या गृ॒हम्
shlokas.transliteration: mánaḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ ánaḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ utá ǀ chadíḥ ǀśukráu ǀ anaḍvā́hau ǀ āstām ǀ yát ǀ áyāt ǀ sūryā́ ǀ gṛhám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Mind was her chariot, and heaven was the covering, the two shining (orbs) were the oxen whenSūrya went to (her husband's) dwelling.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒क्सा॒माभ्या॑म॒भिहि॑तौ॒ गावौ॑ ते साम॒नावि॑तः । श्रोत्रं॑ ते च॒क्रे आ॑स्तां दि॒वि पन्था॑श्चराचा॒रः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛk-sāmā́bhyām ǀ abhí-hitau ǀ gā́vau ǀ te ǀ sāmanáu ǀ itaḥ ǀśrótram ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ āstām ǀ diví ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ carācaráḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Those two oxen yoked by the Ṛk and theSāmanmarch equally; the two wheels were your ears; themoving path (was) in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: शुची॑ ते च॒क्रे या॒त्या व्या॒नो अक्ष॒ आह॑तः । अनो॑ मन॒स्मयं॑ सू॒र्यारो॑हत्प्रय॒ती पति॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: śúcī íti ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ yātyā́ḥ ǀ vi-ānáḥ ǀ ákṣaḥ ǀ ā́-hataḥ ǀánaḥ ǀ manasmáyam ǀ sūryā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ arohat ǀ pra-yatī́ ǀ pátim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The two swift-moving wheels were your pure (cars).Vāyuwas the fastened axle,Sūryamountedthe chariot of the Mind, going to her lord.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सू॒र्याया॑ वह॒तुः प्रागा॑त्सवि॒ता यम॒वासृ॑जत् । अ॒घासु॑ हन्यन्ते॒ गावोऽर्जु॑न्यो॒: पर्यु॑ह्यते
shlokas.transliteration: sūryā́yāḥ ǀ vahatúḥ ǀ prá ǀ agāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ yám ǀ ava-ásṛjat ǀaghā́su ǀ hanyante ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ árjunyoḥ ǀ pári ǀ uhyate ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sūrya's bridal procession whichSavitādespatched has advanced; the oxen are whipped along intheMagha(constellations); she is borne (to her husband's house) in theArjunī(constellations).”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद॑श्विना पृ॒च्छमा॑ना॒वया॑तं त्रिच॒क्रेण॑ वह॒तुं सू॒र्याया॑: । विश्वे॑ दे॒वा अनु॒ तद्वा॑मजानन्पु॒त्रः पि॒तरा॑ववृणीत पू॒षा
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ aśvinā ǀ pṛcchámānau ǀ áyātam ǀ tri-cakréṇa ǀ vahatúm ǀ sūryā́yāḥ ǀvíśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ánu ǀ tát ǀ vām ǀ ajānan ǀ putráḥ ǀ pitárau ǀ avṛṇīta ǀ pūṣā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When,Aśvins, you came in your three-wheeled car soliciting the marriage ofSūrya, then all thegods, assented andPūṣan(your) son chose (you as) his parents.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यदया॑तं शुभस्पती वरे॒यं सू॒र्यामुप॑ । क्वैकं॑ च॒क्रं वा॑मासी॒त्क्व॑ दे॒ष्ट्राय॑ तस्थथुः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ áyātam ǀ śubhaḥ ǀ patī íti ǀ vare-yám ǀ sūryā́m ǀ úpa ǀkvá ǀ ékam ǀ cakrám ǀ vām ǀ āsīt ǀ kvá ǀ deṣṭrā́ya ǀ tasthathuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, lords of water, you came to the giver-away (to get)Sūrya, where was the one wheel of yourcar, where did you stand to make the gift?”

shlokas.sanskrit: द्वे ते॑ च॒क्रे सू॑र्ये ब्र॒ह्माण॑ ऋतु॒था वि॑दुः । अथैकं॑ च॒क्रं यद्गुहा॒ तद॑द्धा॒तय॒ इद्वि॑दुः
shlokas.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ te ǀ cakré íti ǀ sūrye ǀ brahmā́ṇaḥ ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ viduḥ ǀátha ǀ ékam ǀ cakrám ǀ yát ǀ gúhā ǀ tát ǀ addhātáyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ viduḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sūrya, theBrāhmaṇasknow your chariot wheels in their season; the single wheel that isconcealed, the sages know it also.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सू॒र्यायै॑ दे॒वेभ्यो॑ मि॒त्राय॒ वरु॑णाय च । ये भू॒तस्य॒ प्रचे॑तस इ॒दं तेभ्यो॑ऽकरं॒ नम॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sūryā́yai ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ mitrā́ya ǀ váruṇāya ǀ ca ǀyé ǀ bhūtásya ǀ prá-cetasaḥ ǀ idám ǀ tébhyaḥ ǀ akaram ǀ námaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I offer this adoration toSūrya, to the gods, toMitraandVaruṇa, (and to all those) who areconsiderate to created beings.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पू॒र्वा॒प॒रं च॑रतो मा॒ययै॒तौ शिशू॒ क्रीळ॑न्तौ॒ परि॑ यातो अध्व॒रम् । विश्वा॑न्य॒न्यो भुव॑नाभि॒चष्ट॑ ऋ॒तूँर॒न्यो वि॒दध॑ज्जायते॒ पुन॑:
shlokas.transliteration: pūrva-aparám ǀ carataḥ ǀ māyáyā ǀ etáu ǀ śíśū íti ǀ krī́ḷantau ǀ pári ǀ yātaḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀvíśvāni ǀ anyáḥ ǀ bhúvanā ǀ abhi-cáṣṭe ǀ ṛtū́n ǀ anyáḥ ǀ vi-dádhat ǀ jāyate ǀ púnaríti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These two (the sun and moon) wandering in thought one after the other, youthful, sportive, approachthe sacrifice; one (of them) looks over all worlds, the other regulating the seasons is born repeatedly.”

shlokas.sanskrit: नवो॑नवो भवति॒ जाय॑मा॒नोऽह्नां॑ के॒तुरु॒षसा॑मे॒त्यग्र॑म् । भा॒गं दे॒वेभ्यो॒ वि द॑धात्या॒यन्प्र च॒न्द्रमा॑स्तिरते दी॒र्घमायु॑:
shlokas.transliteration: návaḥ-navaḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ jā́yamānaḥ ǀ áhnām ǀ ketúḥ ǀ uṣásām ǀ eti ǀ ágram ǀbhāgám ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ dadhāti ǀ ā-yán ǀ prá ǀ candrámāḥ ǀ tirate ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “New every day (the moon) is born; the manifester of days he goes on front of the Dawns; hedistributes their portion to the gods as he goes; the moon protracts a long existence.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒किं॒शु॒कं श॑ल्म॒लिं वि॒श्वरू॑पं॒ हिर॑ण्यवर्णं सु॒वृतं॑ सुच॒क्रम् । आ रो॑ह सूर्ये अ॒मृत॑स्य लो॒कं स्यो॒नं पत्ये॑ वह॒तुं कृ॑णुष्व
shlokas.transliteration: su-kiṃśukám ǀ śalmalím ǀ viśvá-rūpam ǀ híraṇya-varṇam ǀ su-vṛ́tam ǀ su-cakrám ǀā́ ǀ roha ǀ sūrye ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ lokám ǀ syonám ǀ pátye ǀ vahatúm ǀ kṛṇuṣva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Ascend,Sūrya, the chariot made of goodkiṃśukawood and ofśalmali, multiform, decorated withgold, well-covered, well-wheeled, prepare the happy world of the immortals, your marriage procession to yourhusband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उदी॒र्ष्वात॒: पति॑वती॒ ह्ये॒३॒॑षा वि॒श्वाव॑सुं॒ नम॑सा गी॒र्भिरी॑ळे । अ॒न्यामि॑च्छ पितृ॒षदं॒ व्य॑क्तां॒ स ते॑ भा॒गो ज॒नुषा॒ तस्य॑ विद्धि
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ īrṣva ǀ átaḥ ǀ páti-vatī ǀ hí ǀ eṣā́ ǀ viśvá-vasum ǀ námasā ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ īḷe ǀanyā́m ǀ iccha ǀ pitṛ-sádam ǀ ví-aktām ǀ sáḥ ǀ te ǀ bhāgáḥ ǀ janúṣā ǀ tásya ǀ viddhi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Rise up from hence, for this (damsel) has a husband; I worshipViśvāvasuwith reverence and withhymns; seek for another maiden still dwelling in her father's house, decorated with ornaments; that is yourportion, know this (to your portion, take it) from your birth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उदी॒र्ष्वातो॑ विश्वावसो॒ नम॑सेळा महे त्वा । अ॒न्यामि॑च्छ प्रफ॒र्व्यं१॒॑ सं जा॒यां पत्या॑ सृज
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ īrṣva ǀ átaḥ ǀ viśvavaso íti viśva-vaso ǀ námasā ǀ īḷāmahe ǀ tvā ǀanyā́m ǀ iccha ǀ pra-pharvyám ǀ sám ǀ jāyā́m ǀ pátyā ǀ sṛja ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Rise up from here,Viśvāvasu, we worship you with reverence; seek another maiden, one with largehips; leave the bride with her husband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒नृ॒क्ष॒रा ऋ॒जव॑: सन्तु॒ पन्था॒ येभि॒: सखा॑यो॒ यन्ति॑ नो वरे॒यम् । सम॑र्य॒मा सं भगो॑ नो निनीया॒त्सं जा॑स्प॒त्यं सु॒यम॑मस्तु देवाः
shlokas.transliteration: anṛkṣarā́ḥ ǀ ṛjávaḥ ǀ santu ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ yébhiḥ ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ yánti ǀ naḥ ǀ vare-yám ǀsám ǀ aryamā́ ǀ sám ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ninīyāt ǀ sám ǀ jāḥ-patyám ǀ su-yámam ǀ astu ǀ devāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Smooth and straight be the paths by which our friends repair to the bride's father; mayAryaman, mayBhaga conduct us, and may the union of the wife and husband be easily accomplished, O gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र त्वा॑ मुञ्चामि॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ पाशा॒द्येन॒ त्वाब॑ध्नात्सवि॒ता सु॒शेव॑: । ऋ॒तस्य॒ योनौ॑ सुकृ॒तस्य॑ लो॒केऽरि॑ष्टां त्वा स॒ह पत्या॑ दधामि
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ tvā ǀ muñcāmi ǀ váruṇasya ǀ pā́śāt ǀ yéna ǀ tvā ǀ ábadhnāt ǀ savitā́ ǀ su-śévaḥ ǀṛtásya ǀ yónau ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ loké ǀ áriṣṭām ǀ tvā ǀ sahá ǀ pátyā ǀ dadhāmi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I set you free from the noose ofVaruṇa, wherewith the adorableSavitāhad bound you; in the plural ceof sacrifice in the world of good deeds I unite you, unharmed, with your husband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रेतो मु॒ञ्चामि॒ नामुत॑: सुब॒द्धाम॒मुत॑स्करम् । यथे॒यमि॑न्द्र मीढ्वः सुपु॒त्रा सु॒भगास॑ति
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ itáḥ ǀ muñcā́mi ǀ ná ǀ amútaḥ ǀ su-baddhā́m ǀ amútaḥ ǀ karam ǀyáthā ǀ iyám ǀ indra ǀ mīḍhvaḥ ǀ su-putrā́ ǀ su-bhágā ǀ ásati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I set you free from there, not from here; I plural ce you here firmly bound; grant,Indra, showerer, that this(damsel) may have excellent children, and be very fortunate.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पू॒षा त्वे॒तो न॑यतु हस्त॒गृह्या॒श्विना॑ त्वा॒ प्र व॑हतां॒ रथे॑न । गृ॒हान्ग॑च्छ गृ॒हप॑त्नी॒ यथासो॑ व॒शिनी॒ त्वं वि॒दथ॒मा व॑दासि
shlokas.transliteration: pūṣā́ ǀ tvā ǀ itáḥ ǀ nayatu ǀ hasta-gṛ́hya ǀ aśvínā ǀ tvā ǀ prá ǀ vahatām ǀ ráthena ǀgṛhā́n ǀ gaccha ǀ gṛhá-patnī ǀ yáthā ǀ ásaḥ ǀ vaśínī ǀ tvám ǀ vidátham ǀ ā́ ǀ vadāsi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayPūṣanlead you hence, taking you by thehand; may theAśvinsconvey you away in their car,go to the dwelling (of your husband) as you are the mistress of the house; you, submissive (to your husband),give orders to his household.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒ह प्रि॒यं प्र॒जया॑ ते॒ समृ॑ध्यताम॒स्मिन्गृ॒हे गार्ह॑पत्याय जागृहि । ए॒ना पत्या॑ त॒न्वं१॒॑ सं सृ॑ज॒स्वाधा॒ जिव्री॑ वि॒दथ॒मा व॑दाथः
shlokas.transliteration: ihá ǀ priyám ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ te ǀ sám ǀ ṛdhyatām ǀ asmín ǀ gṛhé ǀ gā́rha-patyāya ǀ jāgṛhi ǀenā́ ǀ pátyā ǀ tanvám ǀ sám ǀ sṛjasva ǀ ádha ǀ jívrī íti ǀ vidátham ǀ ā́ ǀ vadāthaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In this your (husband's family) may affection increase with offspring, be watchful over the domestic firein this house; unite your person n with this your husband; and both growing old together govern your household.”

shlokas.sanskrit: नी॒ल॒लो॒हि॒तं भ॑वति कृ॒त्यास॒क्तिर्व्य॑ज्यते । एध॑न्ते अस्या ज्ञा॒तय॒: पति॑र्ब॒न्धेषु॑ बध्यते
shlokas.transliteration: nīla-lohitám ǀ bhavati ǀ kṛtyā́ ǀ āsaktíḥ ǀ ví ǀ ajyate ǀédhante ǀ asyāḥ ǀ jñātáyaḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ bandhéṣu ǀ badhyate ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Blue and red is (her form); devoted (to her) is left behind; her kinsmen prosper, the husband is boundin bonds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: परा॑ देहि शामु॒ल्यं॑ ब्र॒ह्मभ्यो॒ वि भ॑जा॒ वसु॑ । कृ॒त्यैषा प॒द्वती॑ भू॒त्व्या जा॒या वि॑शते॒ पति॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: párā ǀ dehi ǀ śāmulyám ǀ brahmá-bhyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ bhaja ǀ vásu ǀkṛtyā́ ǀ eṣā́ ǀ pat-vátī ǀ bhūtvī́ ǀ ā́ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ viśate ǀ pátim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Put away the garment soiled by the body; give wealth to theBrāhmaṇas; thisKṛtyāhaving becomeendowed with feet, enters the husband's heart as his wife.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒श्री॒रा त॒नूर्भ॑वति॒ रुश॑ती पा॒पया॑मु॒या । पति॒र्यद्व॒ध्वो॒३॒॑ वास॑सा॒ स्वमङ्ग॑मभि॒धित्स॑ते
shlokas.transliteration: aśrīrā́ ǀ tanū́ḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ rúśatī ǀ pāpáyā ǀ amuyā́ ǀpátiḥ ǀ yát ǀ vadhváḥ ǀ vā́sasā ǀ svám ǀ áṅgam ǀ abhi-dhítsate ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The (bridegroom's)bodyis lacking in beauty; shining with this wicked (Kṛtyā), when he wishes to clothe his own limbs with his wife's garments.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ये व॒ध्व॑श्च॒न्द्रं व॑ह॒तुं यक्ष्मा॒ यन्ति॒ जना॒दनु॑ । पुन॒स्तान्य॒ज्ञिया॑ दे॒वा नय॑न्तु॒ यत॒ आग॑ताः
shlokas.transliteration: yé ǀ vadhváḥ ǀ candrám ǀ vahatúm ǀ yákṣmāḥ ǀ yánti ǀ jánāt ǀ ánu ǀpúnaríti ǀ tā́n ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ náyantu ǀ yátaḥ ǀ ā́-gatāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the adorable gods drive back again to the plural ce whence they came the diseases which followfrom (other) people the wife's golden bridal procession.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मा वि॑दन्परिप॒न्थिनो॒ य आ॒सीद॑न्ति॒ दम्प॑ती । सु॒गेभि॑र्दु॒र्गमती॑ता॒मप॑ द्रा॒न्त्वरा॑तयः
shlokas.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vidan ǀ pari-panthínaḥ ǀ yé ǀ ā-sī́danti ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀsu-gébhiḥ ǀ duḥ-gám ǀ áti ǀ itām ǀ ápa ǀ drāntu ǀ árātayaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let not the robbers who approach the husband and wife reach them; may they by easy roads pass thedifficulty; may enemies keep aloof.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒म॒ङ्ग॒लीरि॒यं व॒धूरि॒मां स॒मेत॒ पश्य॑त । सौभा॑ग्यमस्यै द॒त्त्वायाथास्तं॒ वि परे॑तन
shlokas.transliteration: su-maṅgalī́ḥ ǀ iyám ǀ vadhū́ḥ ǀ imā́m ǀ sam-éta ǀ páśyata ǀsáubhāgyam ǀ asyai ǀ dattvā́ya ǀ átha ǀ ástam ǀ ví ǀ párā ǀ itana ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Fortunate is this bride, approach, behold her; having given her your congratulations, depart to yourseveral homes.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तृ॒ष्टमे॒तत्कटु॑कमे॒तद॑पा॒ष्ठव॑द्वि॒षव॒न्नैतदत्त॑वे । सू॒र्यां यो ब्र॒ह्मा वि॒द्यात्स इद्वाधू॑यमर्हति
shlokas.transliteration: tṛṣṭám ǀ etát ǀ káṭukam ǀ etát ǀ apāṣṭhá-vat ǀ viṣá-vat ǀ ná ǀ etát ǀ áttave ǀsūryā́m ǀ yáḥ ǀ brahmā́ ǀ vidyā́t ǀ sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ vā́dhū-yam ǀ arhati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “This (garment) is inflaming, it is pungent; it is like staleSoma; it is like poison; it is not fit to eat; theBrāhmaṇa, who knowsSūrya, verily desires the bridal (garment).”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒शस॑नं वि॒शस॑न॒मथो॑ अधिवि॒कर्त॑नम् । सू॒र्याया॑: पश्य रू॒पाणि॒ तानि॑ ब्र॒ह्मा तु शु॑न्धति
shlokas.transliteration: ā-śásanam ǀ vi-śásanam ǀ átho íti ǀ adhi-vikártanam ǀsūryā́yāḥ ǀ paśya ǀ rūpā́ṇi ǀ tā́ni ǀ brahmā́ ǀ tú ǀ śundhati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Behold the forms ofSūrya, the āśasana (bordercloth) theviśasana(headcloth), the adhivikartana(divided skirt); of these theBrāhmaṇarelieves her.”

shlokas.sanskrit: गृ॒भ्णामि॑ ते सौभग॒त्वाय॒ हस्तं॒ मया॒ पत्या॑ ज॒रद॑ष्टि॒र्यथास॑: । भगो॑ अर्य॒मा स॑वि॒ता पुरं॑धि॒र्मह्यं॑ त्वादु॒र्गार्ह॑पत्याय दे॒वाः
shlokas.transliteration: gṛbhṇā́mi ǀ te ǀ saubhaga-tvā́ya ǀ hástam ǀ máyā ǀ pátyā ǀ jarát-aṣṭiḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásaḥ ǀbhágaḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ savitā́ ǀ púram-dhiḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ tvā ǀ aduḥ ǀ gā́rha-patyāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I take yourhandfor good fortune, that you may attain old age with me as your husband; the godsBhaga,Aryaman,Savitā, Purandhi have given you to me, that I may be the master of a household.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तां पू॑षञ्छि॒वत॑मा॒मेर॑यस्व॒ यस्यां॒ बीजं॑ मनु॒ष्या॒३॒॑ वप॑न्ति । या न॑ ऊ॒रू उ॑श॒ती वि॒श्रया॑ते॒ यस्या॑मु॒शन्त॑: प्र॒हरा॑म॒ शेप॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: tā́m ǀ pūṣan ǀ śivá-tamām ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayasva ǀ yásyām ǀ bī́jam ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ vápanti ǀyā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ ūrū́ íti ǀ uśatī́ ǀ vi-śráyāte ǀ yásyām ǀ uśántaḥ ǀ pra-hárāma ǀ śépam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Pūṣan, inspire her who is most auspicious, in whom men may now seed, who most affectionate maybe devoted to us, and in whom animated by desire we may beget progeny.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तुभ्य॒मग्रे॒ पर्य॑वहन्त्सू॒र्यां व॑ह॒तुना॑ स॒ह । पुन॒: पति॑भ्यो जा॒यां दा अ॑ग्ने प्र॒जया॑ स॒ह
shlokas.transliteration: túbhyam ǀ ágre ǀ pári ǀ avahan ǀ sūryā́m ǀ vahatúnā ǀ sahá ǀpúnaríti ǀ páti-bhyaḥ ǀ jāyā́m ǀ dā́ḥ ǀ agne ǀ pra-jáyā ǀ sahá ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheGandharvas) gaveSūryato you,Agni, with her bridal ornaments; do you, Agni, give (us)husbands our wife back again withmaleoffspring.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पुन॒: पत्नी॑म॒ग्निर॑दा॒दायु॑षा स॒ह वर्च॑सा । दी॒र्घायु॑रस्या॒ यः पति॒र्जीवा॑ति श॒रद॑: श॒तम्
shlokas.transliteration: púnaríti ǀ pátnīm ǀ agníḥ ǀ adāt ǀ ā́yuṣā ǀ sahá ǀ várcasā ǀdīrghá-āyuḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ jī́vāti ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ śatám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agnigave the wife back again with life and splendour; may he who is her husband enjoying long lifelive a hundred years.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोम॑: प्रथ॒मो वि॑विदे गन्ध॒र्वो वि॑विद॒ उत्त॑रः । तृ॒तीयो॑ अ॒ग्निष्टे॒ पति॑स्तु॒रीय॑स्ते मनुष्य॒जाः
shlokas.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ vivide ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ vivide ǀ út-taraḥ ǀtṛtī́yaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ te ǀ pátiḥ ǀ turī́yaḥ ǀ te ǀ manuṣya-jā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Somafirst obtained the bride; theGandharvaobtained her next.Agniwas your third husband; yourfourth (husband) is born of man.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमो॑ ददद्गन्ध॒र्वाय॑ गन्ध॒र्वो द॑दद॒ग्नये॑ । र॒यिं च॑ पु॒त्राँश्चा॑दाद॒ग्निर्मह्य॒मथो॑ इ॒माम्
shlokas.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ dadat ǀ gandharvā́ya ǀ gandharváḥ ǀ dadat ǀ agnáye ǀrayím ǀ ca ǀ putrā́n ǀ ca ǀ adāt ǀ agníḥ ǀ máhyam ǀ átho íti ǀ imā́m ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Somagave her to theGandharva; the Gandharva gave her toAgni; Agni has given her to me andwealth and sons.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒हैव स्तं॒ मा वि यौ॑ष्टं॒ विश्व॒मायु॒र्व्य॑श्नुतम् । क्रीळ॑न्तौ पु॒त्रैर्नप्तृ॑भि॒र्मोद॑मानौ॒ स्वे गृ॒हे
shlokas.transliteration: ihá ǀ evá ǀ stam ǀ mā́ ǀ ví ǀ yauṣṭam ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́yuḥ ǀ ví ǀ aśnutam ǀkrī́ḷantau ǀ putráiḥ ǀ náptṛ-bhiḥ ǀ módamānau ǀ své ǀ gṛhé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Abide here together; may you never be separated; live together all your lives, sporting with sons andgrandsons, happy in your own home.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ न॑: प्र॒जां ज॑नयतु प्र॒जाप॑तिराजर॒साय॒ सम॑नक्त्वर्य॒मा । अदु॑र्मङ्गलीः पतिलो॒कमा वि॑श॒ शं नो॑ भव द्वि॒पदे॒ शं चतु॑ष्पदे
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ pra-jā́m ǀ janayatu ǀ prajā́-patiḥ ǀ ā-jarasā́ya ǀ sám ǀ anaktu ǀ aryamā́ ǀáduḥ-maṅgalīḥ ǀ pati-lokám ǀ ā́ ǀ viśa ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayPrajāpatigrant us progeny, mayAryamanunite us together until old age; free from all evil omensenter your husband's abode, be the bringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अघो॑रचक्षु॒रप॑तिघ्न्येधि शि॒वा प॒शुभ्य॑: सु॒मना॑: सु॒वर्चा॑: । वी॒र॒सूर्दे॒वका॑मा स्यो॒ना शं नो॑ भव द्वि॒पदे॒ शं चतु॑ष्पदे
shlokas.transliteration: ághora-cakṣuḥ ǀ ápati-ghnī ǀ edhi ǀ śivā́ ǀ paśú-bhyaḥ ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ su-várcāḥ ǀvīra-sū́ḥ ǀ devá-kāmā ǀ syonā́ ǀ śám ǀ naḥ ǀ bhava ǀ dvi-páde ǀ śám ǀ cátuḥ-pade ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Look upon your husband) with no angry eye, be not hostile to your lord, be tender to animals, beamiable, be very glorious; be the mother ofmales, be devoted to the gods, be the bestower of happiness, be thebringer of prosperity to our bipeds and quadrupeds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मां त्वमि॑न्द्र मीढ्वः सुपु॒त्रां सु॒भगां॑ कृणु । दशा॑स्यां पु॒त्राना धे॑हि॒ पति॑मेकाद॒शं कृ॑धि
shlokas.transliteration: imā́m ǀ tvám ǀ indra ǀ mīḍhvaḥ ǀ su-putrā́m ǀ su-bhágām ǀ kṛṇu ǀdáśa ǀ asyām ǀ putrā́n ǀ ā́ ǀ dhehi ǀ pátim ǀ ekādaśám ǀ kṛdhi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, showerer, make her the mother of sons, plural asing (to her husband); give her ten sons, make herhusband the eleventh.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒म्राज्ञी॒ श्वशु॑रे भव स॒म्राज्ञी॑ श्व॒श्र्वां भ॑व । नना॑न्दरि स॒म्राज्ञी॑ भव स॒म्राज्ञी॒ अधि॑ दे॒वृषु॑
shlokas.transliteration: sam-rā́jñī ǀ śváśure ǀ bhava ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ śvaśrvā́m ǀ bhava ǀnánāndari ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ bhava ǀ sam-rā́jñī ǀ ádhi ǀ devṛ́ṣu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Be aqueento your father-in-law, be a queen to your mother-in-law, be a queen to your husband'ssister, be a queen to your husband's brother.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सम॑ञ्जन्तु॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः समापो॒ हृद॑यानि नौ । सं मा॑त॒रिश्वा॒ सं धा॒ता समु॒ देष्ट्री॑ दधातु नौ
shlokas.transliteration: sám ǀ añjantu ǀ víśve ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ hṛ́dayāni ǀ nau ǀsám ǀ mātaríśvā ǀ sám ǀ dhātā́ ǀ sám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ déṣṭrī ǀ dadhātu ǀ nau ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the universal gods unite both our hearts; may the waters unite them; mayMātariśvan, Dhātāand the bountiful (Sarasvatī) unite both our hearts.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि हि सोतो॒रसृ॑क्षत॒ नेन्द्रं॑ दे॒वम॑मंसत । यत्राम॑दद्वृ॒षाक॑पिर॒र्यः पु॒ष्टेषु॒ मत्स॑खा॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ví ǀ hí ǀ sótoḥ ǀ ásṛkṣata ǀ ná ǀ índram ǀ devám ǀ amaṃsata ǀyátra ǀ ámadat ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ aryáḥ ǀ puṣṭéṣu ǀ mát-sakhā ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: परा॒ ही॑न्द्र॒ धाव॑सि वृ॒षाक॑पे॒रति॒ व्यथि॑: । नो अह॒ प्र वि॑न्दस्य॒न्यत्र॒ सोम॑पीतये॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: párā ǀ hí ǀ indra ǀ dhā́vasi ǀ vṛṣā́kapeḥ ǀ áti ǀ vyáthiḥ ǀnó íti ǀ áha ǀ prá ǀ vindasi ǀ anyátra ǀ sóma-pītaye ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrāṇīspeaks: You,Indra, much annoyed, hasten towardsVṛṣākapi; and yet you find no otherplace to drink theSoma; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: किम॒यं त्वां वृ॒षाक॑पिश्च॒कार॒ हरि॑तो मृ॒गः । यस्मा॑ इर॒स्यसीदु॒ न्व१॒॑र्यो वा॑ पुष्टि॒मद्वसु॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ ayám ǀ tvā́m ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ cakā́ra ǀ háritaḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀyásmai ǀ irasyási ǀ ít ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nú ǀ aryáḥ ǀ vā ǀ puṣṭi-mát ǀ vásu ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “What (favour) has this tawny deerVṛṣākapidone to you that you should like a liberal (benefactor)bestow upon him wealth and nourish me;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: यमि॒मं त्वं वृ॒षाक॑पिं प्रि॒यमि॑न्द्राभि॒रक्ष॑सि । श्वा न्व॑स्य जम्भिष॒दपि॒ कर्णे॑ वराह॒युर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: yám ǀ imám ǀ tvám ǀ vṛṣā́kapim ǀ priyám ǀ indra ǀ abhi-rákṣasi ǀśvā́ ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ jambhiṣat ǀ ápi ǀ kárṇe ǀ varāha-yúḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “ThisVṛṣākapiwhom you,Indra, cherish as your dear (son)-- may the dog which chases the boar(seize) him by the ear (and) devour him; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रि॒या त॒ष्टानि॑ मे क॒पिर्व्य॑क्ता॒ व्य॑दूदुषत् । शिरो॒ न्व॑स्य राविषं॒ न सु॒गं दु॒ष्कृते॑ भुवं॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: priyā́ ǀ taṣṭā́ni ǀ me ǀ kapíḥ ǀ ví-aktā ǀ ví ǀ adūduṣat ǀśíraḥ ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ rāviṣam ǀ ná ǀ su-gám ǀ duḥ-kṛ́te ǀ bhuvam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The ape has spoiled the beloved ghī-adorned (oblations) made to me (by worshippers); let mequickly cut off his head, let me not be the giver of happiness to one who works evil;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: न मत्स्त्री सु॑भ॒सत्त॑रा॒ न सु॒याशु॑तरा भुवत् । न मत्प्रति॑च्यवीयसी॒ न सक्थ्युद्य॑मीयसी॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ mát ǀ strī́ ǀ subhasát-tarā ǀ ná ǀ suyā́śu-tarā ǀ bhuvat ǀná ǀ mát ǀ práti-cyavīyasī ǀ ná ǀ sákthi ǀ út-yamīyasī ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “There is no woman more amiable than I am, not one who bears fairer sons than I; nor one moretractable not one more ardent;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒वे अ॑म्ब सुलाभिके॒ यथे॑वा॒ङ्ग भ॑वि॒ष्यति॑ । भ॒सन्मे॑ अम्ब॒ सक्थि॑ मे॒ शिरो॑ मे॒ वी॑व हृष्यति॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: uvé ǀ amba ǀ sulābhike ǀ yáthā-iva ǀ aṅgá ǀ bhaviṣyáti ǀbhasát ǀ me ǀ amba ǀ sákthi ǀ me ǀ śíraḥ ǀ me ǀ ví-iva ǀ hṛṣyati ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Vṛṣākapispeaks]: O mother, who are easy of access, it will quickly be as (you have said); may my(father) and you, mother, be united; may it delight my (father) and your head like a bird;Indrais above all (theworld).”

shlokas.sanskrit: किं सु॑बाहो स्वङ्गुरे॒ पृथु॑ष्टो॒ पृथु॑जाघने । किं शू॑रपत्नि न॒स्त्वम॒भ्य॑मीषि वृ॒षाक॑पिं॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ subāho íti su-bāho ǀ su-aṅgure ǀ pṛ́thusto íti pṛthu-sto ǀ pṛ́thu-jaghane ǀkím ǀ śūra-patni ǀ naḥ ǀ tvám ǀ abhí ǀ amīṣi ǀ vṛṣā́kapim ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indraspeaks]: You who have beautiful arms, who have beautiful fingers, long-haired, broad-hipped,why are you angry with ourVṛṣākapi, O you wife of a hero; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒वीरा॑मिव॒ माम॒यं श॒रारु॑र॒भि म॑न्यते । उ॒ताहम॑स्मि वी॒रिणीन्द्र॑पत्नी म॒रुत्स॑खा॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: avī́rām-iva ǀ mā́m ǀ ayám ǀ śarā́ruḥ ǀ abhí ǀ manyate ǀutá ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǀ vīríṇī ǀ índra-patnī ǀ marút-sakhā ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indrāṇīspeaks]: This savage beast (Vṛṣākapi) despises me as one who has nomale(protector),and yet I am the mother of male offspring, the wife ofIndra, the friend of theMaruts; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सं॒हो॒त्रं स्म॑ पु॒रा नारी॒ सम॑नं॒ वाव॑ गच्छति । वे॒धा ऋ॒तस्य॑ वी॒रिणीन्द्र॑पत्नी महीयते॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: sam-hotrám ǀ sma ǀ purā́ ǀ nā́rī ǀ sámanam ǀ vā ǀ áva ǀ gacchati ǀvedhā́ḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vīríṇī ǀ índra-patnī ǀ mahīyate ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The mother who is the instrumental tutress of the ceremony, the mother ofmaleoffspring, the wife ofIndra,goes first to the united sacrifice to battle, (and) is honoured (by the praisers); Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒न्द्रा॒णीमा॒सु नारि॑षु सु॒भगा॑म॒हम॑श्रवम् । न॒ह्य॑स्या अप॒रं च॒न ज॒रसा॒ मर॑ते॒ पति॒र्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: indrāṇī́m ǀ āsú ǀ nā́riṣu ǀ su-bhágām ǀ ahám ǀ aśravam ǀnahí ǀ asyāḥ ǀ aparám ǀ caná ǀ jarásā ǀ márate ǀ pátiḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Indraspeaks]: I have heard thatIndrāṇīis the most fortunate among these women, for her lordIndra, who is above all (the world), does ot die of old age like other (men).”

shlokas.sanskrit: नाहमि॑न्द्राणि रारण॒ सख्यु॑र्वृ॒षाक॑पेॠ॒ते । यस्ये॒दमप्यं॑ ह॒विः प्रि॒यं दे॒वेषु॒ गच्छ॑ति॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ indrāṇi ǀ raraṇa ǀ sákhyuḥ ǀ vṛṣā́kapeḥ ǀ ṛté ǀyásya ǀ idám ǀ ápyam ǀ havíḥ ǀ priyám ǀ devéṣu ǀ gácchati ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I am not happy,Indrāṇi, without my friendVṛṣākapi; whose acceptable oblation here, purified withwater, proceeds to the gods;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: वृषा॑कपायि॒ रेव॑ति॒ सुपु॑त्र॒ आदु॒ सुस्नु॑षे । घस॑त्त॒ इन्द्र॑ उ॒क्षण॑: प्रि॒यं का॑चित्क॒रं ह॒विर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: vṛ́ṣākapāyi ǀ révati ǀ sú-putre ǀ ā́t ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sú-snuṣe ǀghásat ǀ te ǀ índraḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ priyám ǀ kācit-karám ǀ havíḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Vṛṣākapispeaks]: O mother of Vṛṣākapi, wealthy, possessing excellent sons, possessingexcellent daughters-in-law, letIndraeat your bulls, (give him) the beloved and most delightful ghī, Indra is aboveall (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒क्ष्णो हि मे॒ पञ्च॑दश सा॒कं पच॑न्ति विंश॒तिम् । उ॒ताहम॑द्मि॒ पीव॒ इदु॒भा कु॒क्षी पृ॑णन्ति मे॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ukṣṇáḥ ǀ hí ǀ me ǀ páñca-daśa ǀ sākám ǀ pácanti ǀ viṃśatím ǀutá ǀ ahám ǀ admi ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ubhā́ ǀ kukṣī́ íti ǀ pṛṇanti ǀ me ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indraspeaks]: The worshippers dress for me fifteen (and) twenty bulls; I eat them and (become) fat,they fill both sides of my belly; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: वृ॒ष॒भो न ति॒ग्मशृ॑ङ्गो॒ऽन्तर्यू॒थेषु॒ रोरु॑वत् । म॒न्थस्त॑ इन्द्र॒ शं हृ॒दे यं ते॑ सु॒नोति॑ भाव॒युर्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ tigmá-śṛṅgaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ yūthéṣu ǀ róruvat ǀmantháḥ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ śám ǀ hṛdé ǀ yám ǀ te ǀ sunóti ǀ bhāvayúḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indrāṇīspeaks]: Like a sharp-horned bull roaring among the herds, so may your libation plural aseworld).”

shlokas.sanskrit: न सेशे॒ यस्य॒ रम्ब॑तेऽन्त॒रा स॒क्थ्या॒३॒॑ कपृ॑त् । सेदी॑शे॒ यस्य॑ रोम॒शं नि॑षे॒दुषो॑ वि॒जृम्भ॑ते॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ rámbate ǀ antarā́ ǀ sakthyā́ ǀ kápṛt ǀsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ romaśám ǀ ni-sedúṣaḥ ǀ vi-jṛ́mbhate ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The man who is impotent begets not progeny, but he who is endowed with vigour;Indrais above all(the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: न सेशे॒ यस्य॑ रोम॒शं नि॑षे॒दुषो॑ वि॒जृम्भ॑ते । सेदी॑शे॒ यस्य॒ रम्ब॑तेऽन्त॒रा स॒क्थ्या॒३॒॑ कपृ॒द्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ romaśám ǀ ni-sedúṣaḥ ǀ vi-jṛ́mbhate ǀsáḥ ǀ ít ǀ īśe ǀ yásya ǀ rámbate ǀ antarā́ ǀ sakthyā́ ǀ kápṛt ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indraspeaks]: He who is endowed with vigour begets not progeny, but he who is impotent; Indra isabove all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यमि॑न्द्र वृ॒षाक॑पि॒: पर॑स्वन्तं ह॒तं वि॑दत् । अ॒सिं सू॒नां नवं॑ च॒रुमादेध॒स्यान॒ आचि॑तं॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ indra ǀ vṛṣā́kapiḥ ǀ párasvantam ǀ hatám ǀ vidat ǀasím ǀ sūnā́m ǀ návam ǀ carúm ǀ ā́t ǀ édhasya ǀ ánaḥ ǀ ā́-citam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indrāṇīspeaks]: Let thisVṛṣākapi,Indra, take a dead wild ass, (let him take) a knife (to cut it up),a fire-plural ce (to cook it), a new saucepan, and a cart full of fuel; Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यमे॑मि वि॒चाक॑शद्विचि॒न्वन्दास॒मार्य॑म् । पिबा॑मि पाक॒सुत्व॑नो॒ऽभि धीर॑मचाकशं॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ emi ǀ vi-cā́kaśat ǀ vi-cinván ǀ dā́sam ǀ ā́ryam ǀpíbāmi ǀ pāka-sútvanaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ dhī́ram ǀ acākaśam ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “[Indraspeaks]: Here I come to the (sacrifice) looking upon (the worshippers), distinguishing the Dāsaand theĀrya; I drink (theSoma) of the (worshipper), who effuses (the Soma) with mature (mind); I look upon theintelligent (sacrificer); Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: धन्व॑ च॒ यत्कृ॒न्तत्रं॑ च॒ कति॑ स्वि॒त्ता वि योज॑ना । नेदी॑यसो वृषाक॒पेऽस्त॒मेहि॑ गृ॒हाँ उप॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: dhánva ǀ ca ǀ yát ǀ kṛntátram ǀ ca ǀ káti ǀ svit ǀ tā́ ǀ ví ǀ yójanā ǀnédīyasaḥ ǀ vṛṣākape ǀ ástam ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ gṛhā́n ǀ úpa ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Go home, Vṣs.ākapi, to the halls of sacrifice (from the lurking- plural ce of the enemy), which is desertand forest (how many leagues are there from there?) and from the nearest (lurking-plural ce);Indrais above all (theworld).”

shlokas.sanskrit: पुन॒रेहि॑ वृषाकपे सुवि॒ता क॑ल्पयावहै । य ए॒ष स्व॑प्न॒नंश॒नोऽस्त॒मेषि॑ प॒था पुन॒र्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ihi ǀ vṛṣākape ǀ suvitā́ ǀ kalpayāvahai ǀyáḥ ǀ eṣáḥ ǀ svapna-náṃśanaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ éṣi ǀ pathā́ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Come back,Vṛṣākapi, that we may do what is agreeable to you; you, who are the destroyer ofsleep, come home again by the road;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: यदुद॑ञ्चो वृषाकपे गृ॒हमि॒न्द्राज॑गन्तन । क्व१॒॑ स्य पु॑ल्व॒घो मृ॒गः कम॑गञ्जन॒योप॑नो॒ विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ údañcaḥ ǀ vṛṣākape ǀ gṛhám ǀ indra ǀ ájagantana ǀkvá ǀ syáḥ ǀ pulvagháḥ ǀ mṛgáḥ ǀ kám ǀ agan ǀ jana-yópanaḥ ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Rise up and come home,VṛṣākapiandIndra; where is that destructive beast, to what (region) has(that beast), the exhilarator of men, gone? Indra is above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: पर्शु॑र्ह॒ नाम॑ मान॒वी सा॒कं स॑सूव विंश॒तिम् । भ॒द्रं भ॑ल॒ त्यस्या॑ अभू॒द्यस्या॑ उ॒दर॒माम॑य॒द्विश्व॑स्मा॒दिन्द्र॒ उत्त॑रः
shlokas.transliteration: párśuḥ ǀ ha ǀ nā́ma ǀ mānavī́ ǀ sākám ǀ sasūva ǀ viṃśatím ǀbhadrám ǀ bhala ǀ tyásyai ǀ abhūt ǀ yásyāḥ ǀ udáram ǀ ā́mayat ǀ víśvasmāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ út-taraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The daughter ofManu,Parśuby name, bore twenty children at once; may good fortune, O arrow ofIndra, befall her whose belly was so prolific;Indrais above all (the world).”

shlokas.sanskrit: र॒क्षो॒हणं॑ वा॒जिन॒मा जि॑घर्मि मि॒त्रं प्रथि॑ष्ठ॒मुप॑ यामि॒ शर्म॑ । शिशा॑नो अ॒ग्निः क्रतु॑भि॒: समि॑द्ध॒: स नो॒ दिवा॒ स रि॒षः पा॑तु॒ नक्त॑म्
shlokas.meaning_en: “I offer clarified butter to the powerfulAgni, the slayer ofrākṣasas, I approach the most spaciousdwelling, the friend (of worshippers); Agni sharpening (his flames) is kindled by pious men; may he guard us frommalignant spirits by day and by night.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अयो॑दंष्ट्रो अ॒र्चिषा॑ यातु॒धाना॒नुप॑ स्पृश जातवेद॒: समि॑द्धः । आ जि॒ह्वया॒ मूर॑देवान्रभस्व क्र॒व्यादो॑ वृ॒क्त्व्यपि॑ धत्स्वा॒सन्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Jātavedas, who have teeth of iron, consume theYātudhānas' flame when kindled, destroy thedestructive (spirits) with your tongue, cut up the eaters of flesh, and put them in your mouth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒भोभ॑यावि॒न्नुप॑ धेहि॒ दंष्ट्रा॑ हिं॒स्रः शिशा॒नोऽव॑रं॒ परं॑ च । उ॒तान्तरि॑क्षे॒ परि॑ याहि राज॒ञ्जम्भै॒: सं धे॑ह्य॒भि या॑तु॒धाना॑न्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agni, the destroyer (of therākṣasas), who have two (rows of teeth), sharpening them both, applythem to (the rākṣasas, and preserve) both the upper and the lower (world); and march, radiant (Agni, againstthe rākṣasas) in the firmament, seize theyātudhānaswith your jaws.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒ज्ञैरिषू॑: सं॒नम॑मानो अग्ने वा॒चा श॒ल्याँ अ॒शनि॑भिर्दिहा॒नः । ताभि॑र्विध्य॒ हृद॑ये यातु॒धाना॑न्प्रती॒चो बा॒हून्प्रति॑ भङ्ध्येषाम्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agni, do you, bending your arrows by means on your sacrifices and praise, and sharpening thejavelins with your splendours, pierce with them theyātudhānasto the heart, break their arms when raisedagainst you.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अग्ने॒ त्वचं॑ यातु॒धान॑स्य भिन्धि हिं॒स्राशनि॒र्हर॑सा हन्त्वेनम् । प्र पर्वा॑णि जातवेदः शृणीहि क्र॒व्यात्क्र॑वि॒ष्णुर्वि चि॑नोतु वृ॒क्णम्
shlokas.meaning_en: “AgniJātavedas, cut through the skin of theyātudhānas, let your destructive thunderbolt destroyhim with its fire; sever his joints, may the flesh-desiring flesh-eater devour his mutilated body.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्रे॒दानीं॒ पश्य॑सि जातवेद॒स्तिष्ठ॑न्तमग्न उ॒त वा॒ चर॑न्तम् । यद्वा॒न्तरि॑क्षे प॒थिभि॒: पत॑न्तं॒ तमस्ता॑ विध्य॒ शर्वा॒ शिशा॑नः
shlokas.meaning_en: “Wherever you now behold him,AgniJātavedas, whether standing or moving, or passing along thepaths in the firmament, do you, O shooter sharpening (your arrows), transfix him with your shaft.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒ताल॑ब्धं स्पृणुहि जातवेद आलेभा॒नादृ॒ष्टिभि॑र्यातु॒धाना॑त् । अग्ने॒ पूर्वो॒ नि ज॑हि॒ शोशु॑चान आ॒माद॒: क्ष्विङ्का॒स्तम॑द॒न्त्वेनी॑:
shlokas.meaning_en: “And defend me,Jātavedas, with your darts when I am seized, (defend me) from the Yātudhānaswho has seized me; anticipating him, do you,Agni, blazing fiercely, slay him; may the swift-flying vultures, theflesh-eaters, devour him.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒ह प्र ब्रू॑हि यत॒मः सो अ॑ग्ने॒ यो या॑तु॒धानो॒ य इ॒दं कृ॒णोति॑ । तमा र॑भस्व स॒मिधा॑ यविष्ठ नृ॒चक्ष॑स॒श्चक्षु॑षे रन्धयैनम्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agni, youngest of the gods, announce (to me present) at this (your sacrifice), which is yourYātudhāna who does this; destroy him with your kindled flame; beholder of men, consume him with yourbrilliance.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ती॒क्ष्णेना॑ग्ने॒ चक्षु॑षा रक्ष य॒ज्ञं प्राञ्चं॒ वसु॑भ्य॒: प्र ण॑य प्रचेतः । हिं॒स्रं रक्षां॑स्य॒भि शोशु॑चानं॒ मा त्वा॑ दभन्यातु॒धाना॑ नृचक्षः
shlokas.meaning_en: “Protect this sacrifice,Agni, with your sharp glance; lead it sage (Agni) forward to (the acquisition of)riches; let not theYātudhānasharm you, beholder of men, the destroyer ofrākṣasasblazing fiercely.”

shlokas.sanskrit: नृ॒चक्षा॒ रक्ष॒: परि॑ पश्य वि॒क्षु तस्य॒ त्रीणि॒ प्रति॑ शृणी॒ह्यग्रा॑ । तस्या॑ग्ने पृ॒ष्टीर्हर॑सा शृणीहि त्रे॒धा मूलं॑ यातु॒धान॑स्य वृश्च
shlokas.meaning_en: “Regard, beholder of men, therākṣasasamong the people; cut off his three heads; cut off his flankswith your might; cut off the triple foot of theYātudhāna.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्रिर्या॑तु॒धान॒: प्रसि॑तिं त एत्वृ॒तं यो अ॑ग्ने॒ अनृ॑तेन॒ हन्ति॑ । तम॒र्चिषा॑ स्फू॒र्जय॑ञ्जातवेदः सम॒क्षमे॑नं गृण॒ते नि वृ॑ङ्धि
shlokas.meaning_en: “AgniJātavedas, let theYātudhāna, who defeats your truth with falsehood, come thrice into the”

shlokas.sanskrit: तद॑ग्ने॒ चक्षु॒: प्रति॑ धेहि रे॒भे श॑फा॒रुजं॒ येन॒ पश्य॑सि यातु॒धान॑म् । अ॒थ॒र्व॒वज्ज्योति॑षा॒ दैव्ये॑न स॒त्यं धूर्व॑न्तम॒चितं॒ न्यो॑ष
shlokas.meaning_en: “Cast,Agni, upon the two roaring (rākṣasas) that eye wherewith you behold theYātudhānastrikingwith his hoof; likeAtharvanwith celestial radiance burn down the ignorant (rākṣasas), who assails truth withfalsehood.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद॑ग्ने अ॒द्य मि॑थु॒ना शपा॑तो॒ यद्वा॒चस्तृ॒ष्टं ज॒नय॑न्त रे॒भाः । म॒न्योर्मन॑सः शर॒व्या॒३॒॑ जाय॑ते॒ या तया॑ विध्य॒ हृद॑ये यातु॒धाना॑न्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Today,Agni, when the married pair curse each other, then the praisers produce bitter words (in angeragainst each other), do you pierce theYātudhānasthrough the heart with your arrow, which is genitive rated fromyour wrathful mind.”

shlokas.sanskrit: परा॑ शृणीहि॒ तप॑सा यातु॒धाना॒न्परा॑ग्ने॒ रक्षो॒ हर॑सा शृणीहि । परा॒र्चिषा॒ मूर॑देवाञ्छृणीहि॒ परा॑सु॒तृपो॑ अ॒भि शोशु॑चानः
shlokas.meaning_en: “Destroy theYātudhānaswith your scorching fire; destroy therākṣasas,Agni, with your heat;destroy with your radiance those who believe in vaid gods, fiercely blazing, destroy the insatiable.”

shlokas.sanskrit: परा॒द्य दे॒वा वृ॑जि॒नं शृ॑णन्तु प्र॒त्यगे॑नं श॒पथा॑ यन्तु तृ॒ष्टाः । वा॒चास्ते॑नं॒ शर॑व ऋच्छन्तु॒ मर्म॒न्विश्व॑स्यैतु॒ प्रसि॑तिं यातु॒धान॑:
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let all the gods today destroy the murderous (Yātudhāna); let our sharp imprecations encounterhim; may the arrows hit the speaker of falsehood in a vital part; may the Yātudhāna go into the bondage of theall-pervadingAgni.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यः पौरु॑षेयेण क्र॒विषा॑ सम॒ङ्क्ते यो अश्व्ये॑न प॒शुना॑ यातु॒धान॑: । यो अ॒घ्न्याया॒ भर॑ति क्षी॒रम॑ग्ने॒ तेषां॑ शी॒र्षाणि॒ हर॒सापि॑ वृश्च
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheYātudhāna, who fills himself with the flesh of man, and he who fills himself with the flesh ofhorses or of other animals, and he who steals the milk of the cow-- cut off their heads with your flame.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सं॒व॒त्स॒रीणं॒ पय॑ उ॒स्रिया॑या॒स्तस्य॒ माशी॑द्यातु॒धानो॑ नृचक्षः । पी॒यूष॑मग्ने यत॒मस्तितृ॑प्सा॒त्तं प्र॒त्यञ्च॑म॒र्चिषा॑ विध्य॒ मर्म॑न्
shlokas.meaning_en: “The milk of the cow is annually produced, let not theYātudhānaconsume it, O beholder of men;whichever of them would like to satiate himself with the ambrosia, do you,Agni, pierce that contending(rākṣasa) with your flame in a vital part.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒षं गवां॑ यातु॒धाना॑: पिब॒न्त्वा वृ॑श्च्यन्ता॒मदि॑तये दु॒रेवा॑: । परै॑नान्दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता द॑दातु॒ परा॑ भा॒गमोष॑धीनां जयन्ताम्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let theYātudhānadrink poison from the cattle; let the (rākṣasas) hard to overcome be cut topieces for the sake ofAditi; may the divineSavitāgive them over (to destruction), may they be deprived of thefood of herbs.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒नाद॑ग्ने मृणसि यातु॒धाना॒न्न त्वा॒ रक्षां॑सि॒ पृत॑नासु जिग्युः । अनु॑ दह स॒हमू॑रान्क्र॒व्यादो॒ मा ते॑ हे॒त्या मु॑क्षत॒ दैव्या॑याः
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Agni, have from old time opposed theYātudhāna; therākṣasashave never overcome you inbattles; burn murderous flesh-eating (rākṣasas) one by one; let them not escape your divine weapon”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं नो॑ अग्ने अध॒रादुद॑क्ता॒त्त्वं प॒श्चादु॒त र॑क्षा पु॒रस्ता॑त् । प्रति॒ ते ते॑ अ॒जरा॑स॒स्तपि॑ष्ठा अ॒घशं॑सं॒ शोशु॑चतो दहन्तु
shlokas.meaning_en: “Do you,Agni, protect us on the south, on the north, on the west, and on the east; may these, yourundecaying, scorching, blazing (flames), consume the perpetrator of wickedness.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प॒श्चात्पु॒रस्ता॑दध॒रादुद॑क्तात्क॒विः काव्ये॑न॒ परि॑ पाहि राजन् । सखे॒ सखा॑यम॒जरो॑ जरि॒म्णेऽग्ने॒ मर्ताँ॒ अम॑र्त्य॒स्त्वं न॑:
shlokas.meaning_en: “RoyalAgni, who are a sage, protect us by your wisdom on the west, on the east, on the south, on thenorth; do you, O friend, who are undecaying, (preserve me), your friend, to old age; do you who are immortal,(protect) us who are mortal.”

shlokas.sanskrit: परि॑ त्वाग्ने॒ पुरं॑ व॒यं विप्रं॑ सहस्य धीमहि । धृ॒षद्व॑र्णं दि॒वेदि॑वे ह॒न्तारं॑ भङ्गु॒राव॑ताम्
shlokas.meaning_en: “We meditate, strength-bornAgni, on you, the accomplisher (of rites), the sage, of fearful form, thedestroyer of the treacherous day by day.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒षेण॑ भङ्गु॒राव॑त॒: प्रति॑ ष्म र॒क्षसो॑ दह । अग्ने॑ ति॒ग्मेन॑ शो॒चिषा॒ तपु॑रग्राभिॠ॒ष्टिभि॑:
shlokas.meaning_en: “Consume,Agni, the treacherousrākṣasaswith your all-pervading sharp flame, with yourflame-pointed darts.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रत्य॑ग्ने मिथु॒ना द॑ह यातु॒धाना॑ किमी॒दिना॑ । सं त्वा॑ शिशामि जागृ॒ह्यद॑ब्धं विप्र॒ मन्म॑भिः
shlokas.meaning_en: “Consume,Agni, these pairs ofYātudhānasand Kimīdins; I whet you, O sage, the invincible one,with my praises; wake up.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रत्य॑ग्ने॒ हर॑सा॒ हर॑: शृणी॒हि वि॒श्वत॒: प्रति॑ । या॒तु॒धान॑स्य र॒क्षसो॒ बलं॒ वि रु॑ज वी॒र्य॑म्
shlokas.meaning_en: “Destroy,Agni, with your flame, the impetuous might of theYātudhāna; break the strength of therākṣasa.”

shlokas.sanskrit: गी॒र्णं भुव॑नं॒ तम॒साप॑गूळ्हमा॒विः स्व॑रभवज्जा॒ते अ॒ग्नौ । तस्य॑ दे॒वाः पृ॑थि॒वी द्यौरु॒तापोऽर॑णय॒न्नोष॑धीः स॒ख्ये अ॑स्य
shlokas.transliteration: havíḥ ǀ pā́ntam ǀ ajáram ǀ svaḥ-vídi ǀ divi-spṛ́śi ǀ ā́-hutam ǀ júṣṭam ǀ agnáu ǀtásya ǀ bhármaṇe ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dhármaṇe ǀ kám ǀ svadháyā ǀ paprathanta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The whole world swallowed up, hidden in darkness, was made manifest whenAgniwas born; thegods, heaven and earth, the waters and the plural nts rejoiced in his friendship.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वेभि॒र्न्वि॑षि॒तो य॒ज्ञिये॑भिर॒ग्निं स्तो॑षाण्य॒जरं॑ बृ॒हन्त॑म् । यो भा॒नुना॑ पृथि॒वीं द्यामु॒तेमामा॑त॒तान॒ रोद॑सी अ॒न्तरि॑क्षम्
shlokas.transliteration: gīrṇám ǀ bhúvanam ǀ támasā ǀ ápa-gūḷham ǀ āvíḥ ǀ sváḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ jāté ǀ agnáu ǀtásya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ utá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ áraṇayan ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sakhyé ǀ asya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sent by adorable gods I praise the undecaying and mightyAgni, who by his radiance has spread forththe earth and this heaven, the two worlds and the firmament.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यो होतासी॑त्प्रथ॒मो दे॒वजु॑ष्टो॒ यं स॒माञ्ज॒न्नाज्ये॑ना वृणा॒नाः । स प॑त॒त्री॑त्व॒रं स्था जग॒द्यच्छ्वा॒त्रम॒ग्निर॑कृणोज्जा॒तवे॑दाः
shlokas.transliteration: devébhiḥ ǀ nú ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yajñíyebhiḥ ǀ agním ǀ stoṣāṇi ǀ ajáram ǀ bṛhántam ǀyáḥ ǀ bhānúnā ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ utá ǀ imā́m ǀ ā-tatā́na ǀ ródasī íti ǀ antárikṣam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Who propitiated by the gods was the first offerer of oblations, whom his worshippers anoint withclarified butter-- he,AgniJātavedas, quickly made that which can fly, that which can walk, that which isstationary, that which is moveable.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यज्जा॑तवेदो॒ भुव॑नस्य मू॒र्धन्नति॑ष्ठो अग्ने स॒ह रो॑च॒नेन॑ । तं त्वा॑हेम म॒तिभि॑र्गी॒र्भिरु॒क्थैः स य॒ज्ञियो॑ अभवो रोदसि॒प्राः
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ hótā ǀ ā́sīt ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ devá-juṣṭaḥ ǀ yám ǀ sam-ā́ñjan ǀ ā́jyena ǀ vṛṇānā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ patatrí ǀ itvarám ǀ sthā́ḥ ǀ jágat ǀ yát ǀ śvātrám ǀ agníḥ ǀ akṛṇot ǀ jātá-vedāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Inasmuch as you abide,AgniJātavedas, on the brow of the universe, together with the sun, we havecome to you with praises, with hymns, with prayers; you are adorable, the satisfier of heaven and earth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मू॒र्धा भु॒वो भ॑वति॒ नक्त॑म॒ग्निस्तत॒: सूर्यो॑ जायते प्रा॒तरु॒द्यन् । मा॒यामू॒ तु य॒ज्ञिया॑नामे॒तामपो॒ यत्तूर्णि॒श्चर॑ति प्रजा॒नन्
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀ bhúvanasya ǀ mūrdhán ǀ átiṣṭhaḥ ǀ agne ǀ sahá ǀ rocanéna ǀtám ǀ tvā ǀ ahema ǀ matí-bhiḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ uktháiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ yajñíyaḥ ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ rodasi-prā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agniis the head of all beings by night; then the sun rising early is born; (the wise know) this to be thewisdom of the adorable gods, that the swift- moving sun being intelligent moves through the firmameṇṭ”

shlokas.sanskrit: दृ॒शेन्यो॒ यो म॑हि॒ना समि॒द्धोऽरो॑चत दि॒वियो॑निर्वि॒भावा॑ । तस्मि॑न्न॒ग्नौ सू॑क्तवा॒केन॑ दे॒वा ह॒विर्विश्व॒ आजु॑हवुस्तनू॒पाः
shlokas.transliteration: mūrdhā́ ǀ bhuváḥ ǀ bhavati ǀ náktam ǀ agníḥ ǀ tátaḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ jāyate ǀ prātáḥ ǀ ut-yán ǀmāyā́m ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tú ǀ yajñíyānām ǀ etā́m ǀ ápaḥ ǀ yát ǀ tū́rṇiḥ ǀ cárati ǀ pra-jānán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who shines visible to all through his greatness radiant, having his station in the sky, resplendentinhim,Agni, the unversal gods, the guardians of men's bodies, have presented an oblation with the voice of”

shlokas.sanskrit: सू॒क्त॒वा॒कं प्र॑थ॒ममादिद॒ग्निमादिद्ध॒विर॑जनयन्त दे॒वाः । स ए॑षां य॒ज्ञो अ॑भवत्तनू॒पास्तं द्यौर्वे॑द॒ तं पृ॑थि॒वी तमाप॑:
shlokas.transliteration: dṛśényaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ mahinā́ ǀ sám-iddhaḥ ǀ árocata ǀ diví-yoniḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀtásmin ǀ agnáu ǀ sūkta-vākéna ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ havíḥ ǀ víśve ǀ ā́ ǀ ajuhavuḥ ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods first genitive rated the words of the hymn, thenAgni, then the oblation; he is the (object of the)sacrifice of these deities, the protector of the body; him the heaven knows, him the earth and the waters, know.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यं दे॒वासोऽज॑नयन्ता॒ग्निं यस्मि॒न्नाजु॑हवु॒र्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ । सो अ॒र्चिषा॑ पृथि॒वीं द्यामु॒तेमामृ॑जू॒यमा॑नो अतपन्महि॒त्वा
shlokas.transliteration: sūkta-vākám ǀ prathamám ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ agním ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ havíḥ ǀ ajanayanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ eṣām ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ tanū-pā́ḥ ǀ tám ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ veda ǀ tám ǀ pṛthivī́ ǀ tám ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agniwhom the gods genitive rated, in whom all beings have offered oblations-- he, the straight-going, haswarmed by his \radiance, by his might, the earth and his heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्तोमे॑न॒ हि दि॒वि दे॒वासो॑ अ॒ग्निमजी॑जन॒ञ्छक्ति॑भी रोदसि॒प्राम् । तमू॑ अकृण्वन्त्रे॒धा भु॒वे कं स ओष॑धीः पचति वि॒श्वरू॑पाः
shlokas.transliteration: yám ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ájanayanta ǀ agním ǀ yásmin ǀ ā́ ǀ ájuhavuḥ ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀsáḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ dyā́m ǀ utá ǀ imā́m ǀ ṛju-yámānaḥ ǀ atapat ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods have by praise engenderedAgniin the sky, who fills heaven and earth by his functions, theyappointed the joy-bestowing Agni to his three- fold condition, he brings the manifold plural nts to maturity.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒देदे॑न॒मद॑धुर्य॒ज्ञिया॑सो दि॒वि दे॒वाः सूर्य॑मादिते॒यम् । य॒दा च॑रि॒ष्णू मि॑थु॒नावभू॑ता॒मादित्प्राप॑श्य॒न्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑
shlokas.transliteration: stómena ǀ hí ǀ diví ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ agním ǀ ájījanan ǀ śákti-bhiḥ ǀ rodasi-prā́m ǀtám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ akṛṇvan ǀ tredhā́ ǀ bhuvé ǀ kám ǀ sáḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ pacati ǀ viśvá-rūpāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When the adorable gods, plural ced him andSūrya, the son ofAditi, in heaven; when the swift-movingpair (AgniandVaiśvānara) appeared, then all beings beheld them.”

shlokas.sanskrit: विश्व॑स्मा अ॒ग्निं भुव॑नाय दे॒वा वै॑श्वान॒रं के॒तुमह्ना॑मकृण्वन् । आ यस्त॒तानो॒षसो॑ विभा॒तीरपो॑ ऊर्णोति॒ तमो॑ अ॒र्चिषा॒ यन्
shlokas.transliteration: yadā́ ǀ ít ǀ enam ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ yajñíyāsaḥ ǀ diví ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ sū́ryam ǀ āditeyám ǀyadā́ ǀ cariṣṇū́ íti ǀ mithunáu ǀ ábhūtām ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ prá ǀ apaśyan ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods madeAgniVaiśvānara, the indicator of days, for the sake of the whole world, whostretched out the radiant dawns, and as he moves along scatters the darkness with his light.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वै॒श्वा॒न॒रं क॒वयो॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑सो॒ऽग्निं दे॒वा अ॑जनयन्नजु॒र्यम् । नक्ष॑त्रं प्र॒त्नममि॑नच्चरि॒ष्णु य॒क्षस्याध्य॑क्षं तवि॒षं बृ॒हन्त॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: víśvasmai ǀ agním ǀ bhúvanāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ vaiśvānarám ǀ ketúm ǀ áhnām ǀ akṛṇvan ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ tatā́na ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ vi-bhātī́ḥ ǀ ápo íti ǀ ūrṇoti ǀ támaḥ ǀ arcíṣā ǀ yán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The wise and adorable gods engendered the imperishableAgniVaiśvānara; he overcame (with hislight) the ancient swift-movingNakṣatra, the overseer of the adorable (deity), mighty and great.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वै॒श्वा॒न॒रं वि॒श्वहा॑ दीदि॒वांसं॒ मन्त्रै॑र॒ग्निं क॒विमच्छा॑ वदामः । यो म॑हि॒म्ना प॑रिब॒भूवो॒र्वी उ॒तावस्ता॑दु॒त दे॒वः प॒रस्ता॑त्
shlokas.transliteration: vaiśvānarám ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǀ agním ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ajanayan ǀ ajuryám ǀnákṣatram ǀ pratnám ǀ áminat ǀ cariṣṇú ǀ yakṣásya ǀ ádhi-akṣam ǀ taviṣám ǀ bṛhántam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We glorify daily with praises the brilliant and sageAgniVaiśvānara, the god who overcomes by hismight both heaven and earth, (burning) both below and above.”

shlokas.sanskrit: द्वे स्रु॒ती अ॑शृणवं पितॄ॒णाम॒हं दे॒वाना॑मु॒त मर्त्या॑नाम् । ताभ्या॑मि॒दं विश्व॒मेज॒त्समे॑ति॒ यद॑न्त॒रा पि॒तरं॑ मा॒तरं॑ च
shlokas.transliteration: vaiśvānarám ǀ viśváhā ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsam ǀ mántraiḥ ǀ agním ǀ kavím ǀ áccha ǀ vadāmaḥ ǀyáḥ ǀ mahimnā́ ǀ pari-babhū́va ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ utá ǀ avástāt ǀ utá ǀ deváḥ ǀ parástāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I have heard that there are two paths forPitṛs, gods and mortals; all this universe which is betweenthe paternal (heaven) and the maternal (earth) proceeds on its way by these two (paths).”

shlokas.sanskrit: द्वे स॑मी॒ची बि॑भृत॒श्चर॑न्तं शीर्ष॒तो जा॒तं मन॑सा॒ विमृ॑ष्टम् । स प्र॒त्यङ्विश्वा॒ भुव॑नानि तस्था॒वप्र॑युच्छन्त॒रणि॒र्भ्राज॑मानः
shlokas.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ srutī́ íti ǀ aśṛṇavam ǀ pitṝṇā́m ǀ ahám ǀ devā́nām ǀ utá ǀ mártyānām ǀtā́bhyām ǀ idám ǀ víśvam ǀ éjat ǀ sám ǀ eti ǀ yát ǀ antarā́ ǀ pitáram ǀ mātáram ǀ ca ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The associated two (heaven and earth) support (Agni) moving, born from the head, sanctified bypraise; diligent, rapid, radiant, he appears in the presence of all beings.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्रा॒ वदे॑ते॒ अव॑र॒: पर॑श्च यज्ञ॒न्यो॑: कत॒रो नौ॒ वि वे॑द । आ शे॑कु॒रित्स॑ध॒मादं॒ सखा॑यो॒ नक्ष॑न्त य॒ज्ञं क इ॒दं वि वो॑चत्
shlokas.transliteration: dvé íti ǀ samīcī́ íti sam-īcī́ ǀ bibhṛtaḥ ǀ cárantam ǀ śīrṣatáḥ ǀ jātám ǀ mánasā ǀ ví-mṛṣṭam ǀsáḥ ǀ pratyáṅ ǀ víśvā ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ tasthau ǀ ápra-yucchan ǀ taráṇiḥ ǀ bhrā́jamānaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When the lower and upper (fire) disputed "which of us twain leaders of sacrifice knows the work best?"then the friends (the priests) were competent (to offer) sacrifice, they came to the sacrifice; who declares this?”

shlokas.sanskrit: कत्य॒ग्नय॒: कति॒ सूर्या॑स॒: कत्यु॒षास॒: कत्यु॑ स्वि॒दाप॑: । नोप॒स्पिजं॑ वः पितरो वदामि पृ॒च्छामि॑ वः कवयो वि॒द्मने॒ कम्
shlokas.transliteration: yátra ǀ vádete íti ǀ ávaraḥ ǀ páraḥ ǀ ca ǀ yajña-nyóḥ ǀ kataráḥ ǀ nau ǀ ví ǀ veda ǀā́ ǀ śekuḥ ǀ ít ǀ sadha-mā́dam ǀ sákhāyaḥ ǀ nákṣanta ǀ yajñám ǀ káḥ ǀ idám ǀ ví ǀ vocat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “How many fires are there, how many suns, how many dawns, how many waters? I address you, OPitṛs, not in rivalry, I ask you, sages, in order to know (the truth).”

shlokas.sanskrit: या॒व॒न्मा॒त्रमु॒षसो॒ न प्रती॑कं सुप॒र्ण्यो॒३॒॑ वस॑ते मातरिश्वः । ताव॑द्दधा॒त्युप॑ य॒ज्ञमा॒यन्ब्रा॑ह्म॒णो होतु॒रव॑रो नि॒षीद॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: káti ǀ agnáyaḥ ǀ káti ǀ sū́ryāsaḥ ǀ káti ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ káti ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svit ǀ ā́paḥ ǀná ǀ upa-spíjam ǀ vaḥ ǀ pitaraḥ ǀ vadāmi ǀ pṛcchā́mi ǀ vaḥ ǀ kavayaḥ ǀ vidmáne ǀ kám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “As long,Mātariśvan, as the swiftly-moving (nights) cover the face of the dawn, (so long) theBrahman, the inferior sitting down (to perform the work) of theHotā, approaching the sacrifice supports (theceremony).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रं॑ स्तवा॒ नृत॑मं॒ यस्य॑ म॒ह्ना वि॑बबा॒धे रो॑च॒ना वि ज्मो अन्ता॑न् । आ यः प॒प्रौ च॑र्षणी॒धृद्वरो॑भि॒: प्र सिन्धु॑भ्यो रिरिचा॒नो म॑हि॒त्वा
shlokas.transliteration: índram ǀ stava ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ yásya ǀ mahnā́ ǀ vi-babādhé ǀ rocanā́ ǀ ví ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántān ǀā́ ǀ yáḥ ǀ papráu ǀ carṣaṇi-dhṛ́t ǀ váraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ prá ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ riricānáḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “PraiseIndra, the chief leadere (of rites), whose glory surpasses the lustre (of others), and the ends ofthe earth; the sustainer of man, who exceeding the ocean in magnitude, fills (heaven and earth) with radiance.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स सूर्य॒: पर्यु॒रू वरां॒स्येन्द्रो॑ ववृत्या॒द्रथ्ये॑व च॒क्रा । अति॑ष्ठन्तमप॒स्यं१॒॑ न सर्गं॑ कृ॒ष्णा तमां॑सि॒ त्विष्या॑ जघान
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ pári ǀ urú ǀ várāṃsi ǀ ā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vavṛtyāt ǀ ráthyā-iva ǀ cakrā́ ǀátiṣṭhantam ǀ apasyám ǀ ná ǀ sárgam ǀ kṛṣṇā́ ǀ támāṃsi ǀ tvíṣyā ǀ jaghāna ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The heroicIndracauses numerous rays of light revolve as a charioteer (effects the rotation of) thewheels of the chariot; he destroys by his radiance the black darkness like a restless active horse.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒मा॒नम॑स्मा॒ अन॑पावृदर्च क्ष्म॒या दि॒वो अस॑मं॒ ब्रह्म॒ नव्य॑म् । वि यः पृ॒ष्ठेव॒ जनि॑मान्य॒र्य इन्द्र॑श्चि॒काय॒ न सखा॑यमी॒षे
shlokas.transliteration: samānám ǀ asmai ǀ ánapa-vṛt ǀ arca ǀ kṣmayā́ ǀ diváḥ ǀ ásamam ǀ bráhma ǀ návyam ǀví ǀ yáḥ ǀ pṛṣṭhā́-iva ǀ jánimāni ǀ aryáḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ cikā́ya ǀ ná ǀ sákhāyam ǀ īṣé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sing along with me a new song, unceasing, surpassing heaven and earth, to him who like thepṛṣṭha(praises), born at sacrifices, overcomes his enemies,Indrawho desires no friend.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रा॑य॒ गिरो॒ अनि॑शितसर्गा अ॒पः प्रेर॑यं॒ सग॑रस्य बु॒ध्नात् । यो अक्षे॑णेव च॒क्रिया॒ शची॑भि॒र्विष्व॑क्त॒स्तम्भ॑ पृथि॒वीमु॒त द्याम्
shlokas.transliteration: índrāya ǀ gíraḥ ǀ ániśita-sargāḥ ǀ apáḥ ǀ prá ǀ īrayam ǀ ságarasya ǀ budhnā́t ǀyáḥ ǀ ákṣeṇa-iva ǀ cakríyā ǀ śácībhiḥ ǀ víṣvak ǀ tastámbha ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ utá ǀ dyā́m ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I will utter praises toIndrain unceasing flow, (I will send) waters from the depth of the firmament (tohim) who has fixed heaven and earth on both sides by his acts as the wheels of a chariot (are fixed) by the axle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आपा॑न्तमन्युस्तृ॒पल॑प्रभर्मा॒ धुनि॒: शिमी॑वा॒ञ्छरु॑माँ ऋजी॒षी । सोमो॒ विश्वा॑न्यत॒सा वना॑नि॒ नार्वागिन्द्रं॑ प्रति॒माना॑नि देभुः
shlokas.transliteration: ā́pānta-manyuḥ ǀ tṛpála-prabharmā ǀ dhúniḥ ǀ śímī-vān ǀ śáru-mān ǀ ṛjīṣī́ ǀsómaḥ ǀ víśvāni ǀ atasā́ ǀ vánāni ǀ ná ǀ arvā́k ǀ índram ǀ prati-mā́nāni ǀ debhuḥ ǁ
