shlokas.meaning_en: “Appeasing wrath, striking quickly, intimidating foes, doer of great deeds, armed with weapons,possessing the stale residue,Somanourishes all the Atasa woods, they oppose no impediments againstIndra.”

shlokas.sanskrit: न यस्य॒ द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी न धन्व॒ नान्तरि॑क्षं॒ नाद्र॑य॒: सोमो॑ अक्षाः । यद॑स्य म॒न्युर॑धिनी॒यमा॑नः शृ॒णाति॑ वी॒ळु रु॒जति॑ स्थि॒राणि॑
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ yásya ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ dhánva ǀ ná ǀ antárikṣam ǀ ná ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ akṣāríti ǀyát ǀ asya ǀ manyúḥ ǀ adhi-nīyámānaḥ ǀ śṛṇā́ti ǀ vīḷú ǀ rujáti ǀ sthirā́ṇi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Of whom neither heaven and earth, nor the water, nor the firmament, nor the mountains (are theobstructions) for him doth theSomaexude, when his wrath reaching his enemies destroys the strong and breaksthe firm.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ज॒घान॑ वृ॒त्रं स्वधि॑ति॒र्वने॑व रु॒रोज॒ पुरो॒ अर॑द॒न्न सिन्धू॑न् । बि॒भेद॑ गि॒रिं नव॒मिन्न कु॒म्भमा गा इन्द्रो॑ अकृणुत स्व॒युग्भि॑:
shlokas.transliteration: jaghā́na ǀ vṛtrám ǀ svá-dhitiḥ ǀ vánā-iva ǀ rurója ǀ púraḥ ǀ áradat ǀ ná ǀ síndhūn ǀbibhéda ǀ girím ǀ návam ǀ ít ǀ ná ǀ kumbhám ǀ ā́ ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ akṛṇuta ǀ svayúk-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Indra) slewVṛtraas an axe (cuts down) a tree; he demolished the cities (of the foes), he dug out therivers; he shattered the cloud like a new pitcher; with his allies (theMaruts) he recovered the cattle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं ह॒ त्यदृ॑ण॒या इ॑न्द्र॒ धीरो॒ऽसिर्न पर्व॑ वृजि॒ना शृ॑णासि । प्र ये मि॒त्रस्य॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ धाम॒ युजं॒ न जना॑ मि॒नन्ति॑ मि॒त्रम्
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ ha ǀ tyát ǀ ṛṇa-yā́ḥ ǀ indra ǀ dhī́raḥ ǀ asíḥ ǀ ná ǀ párva ǀ vṛjinā́ ǀ śṛṇāsi ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ mitrásya ǀ váruṇasya ǀ dhā́ma ǀ yújam ǀ ná ǀ jánāḥ ǀ minánti ǀ mitrám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Indra, who are wise, punish the guilt (of worshippers); you cut off their sins as a sword (cuts off)the limbs (of victims); (you cut off) the people who (ignorantly) injure the supporting (function) ofMitra, andVaruṇa, (which is) as it were their close friend.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र ये मि॒त्रं प्रार्य॒मणं॑ दु॒रेवा॒: प्र सं॒गिर॒: प्र वरु॑णं मि॒नन्ति॑ । न्य१॒॑मित्रे॑षु व॒धमि॑न्द्र॒ तुम्रं॒ वृष॒न्वृषा॑णमरु॒षं शि॑शीहि
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ yé ǀ mitrám ǀ prá ǀ aryamáṇam ǀ duḥ-évāḥ ǀ prá ǀ sam-gíraḥ ǀ prá ǀ váruṇam ǀ minánti ǀní ǀ amítreṣu ǀ vadhám ǀ indra ǀ túmram ǀ vṛ́ṣan ǀ vṛ́ṣāṇam ǀ aruṣám ǀ śiśīhi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Against those who sinfully offend againstMitra,Aryaman, your companons (theMaruts) andVaruṇa,against these your enemies sharpen,Indra, showerer (of benefits), your rapid showering radiant thunderbolt.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ दि॒व इन्द्र॑ ईशे पृथि॒व्या इन्द्रो॑ अ॒पामिन्द्र॒ इत्पर्व॑तानाम् । इन्द्रो॑ वृ॒धामिन्द्र॒ इन्मेधि॑राणा॒मिन्द्र॒: क्षेमे॒ योगे॒ हव्य॒ इन्द्र॑:
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ īśe ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ párvatānām ǀíndraḥ ǀ vṛdhā́m ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ médhirāṇām ǀ índraḥ ǀ kṣéme ǀ yóge ǀ hávyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrarules over heaven, Indra rules over earth, over the waters, and over the clouds; Indra rules overthe great and over the wise; Indra is to be invoked for the acquisition and preservation (of wealth).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्राक्तुभ्य॒ इन्द्र॒: प्र वृ॒धो अह॑भ्य॒: प्रान्तरि॑क्षा॒त्प्र स॑मु॒द्रस्य॑ धा॒सेः । प्र वात॑स्य॒ प्रथ॑स॒: प्र ज्मो अन्ता॒त्प्र सिन्धु॑भ्यो रिरिचे॒ प्र क्षि॒तिभ्य॑:
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ aktú-bhyaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ prá ǀ vṛdháḥ ǀ áha-bhyaḥ ǀ prá ǀ antárikṣāt ǀ prá ǀ samudrásya ǀ dhāséḥ ǀprá ǀ vā́tasya ǀ práthasaḥ ǀ prá ǀ jmáḥ ǀ ántāt ǀ prá ǀ síndhu-bhyaḥ ǀ ririce ǀ prá ǀ kṣití-bhyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrais vaster than the nights, vaster than the days, vaster than the firmament or the receptacle of theocean, vaster than the wind, or space or the ends of the earth; Indra exceeds the rivers and mankind.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र शोशु॑चत्या उ॒षसो॒ न के॒तुर॑सि॒न्वा ते॑ वर्ततामिन्द्र हे॒तिः । अश्मे॑व विध्य दि॒व आ सृ॑जा॒नस्तपि॑ष्ठेन॒ हेष॑सा॒ द्रोघ॑मित्रान्
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ śóśucatyāḥ ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ketúḥ ǀ asinvā́ ǀ te ǀ vartatām ǀ indra ǀ hetíḥ ǀáśmā-iva ǀ vidhya ǀ diváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sṛjānáḥ ǀ tápiṣṭhena ǀ héṣasā ǀ drógha-mitrān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May your unbroken weapon,Indra, proceed (against your foes), like the banner of the shining dawn,like a stone cast down from heaven, pierce those whose friendship is deceitful with your consumingloud-sounding (weapon).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अन्वह॒ मासा॒ अन्विद्वना॒न्यन्वोष॑धी॒रनु॒ पर्व॑तासः । अन्विन्द्रं॒ रोद॑सी वावशा॒ने अन्वापो॑ अजिहत॒ जाय॑मानम्
shlokas.transliteration: ánu ǀ áha ǀ mā́sāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ ít ǀ vánāni ǀ ánu ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ ánu ǀ párvatāsaḥ ǀánu ǀ índram ǀ ródasī íti ǀ vāvaśāné íti ǀ ánu ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ ajihata ǀ jā́yamānam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The months attend uponIndraas soon as born, the forests attend upon him, the plural nts, themountains, the affectionate heaven and earth, and the waters (attend upon) him.”

shlokas.sanskrit: कर्हि॑ स्वि॒त्सा त॑ इन्द्र चे॒त्यास॑द॒घस्य॒ यद्भि॒नदो॒ रक्ष॒ एष॑त् । मि॒त्र॒क्रुवो॒ यच्छस॑ने॒ न गाव॑: पृथि॒व्या आ॒पृग॑मु॒या शय॑न्ते
shlokas.transliteration: kárhi ǀ svit ǀ sā́ ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ cetyā́ ǀ asat ǀ aghásya ǀ yát ǀ bhinádaḥ ǀ rákṣaḥ ǀ ā-ī́ṣat ǀmitra-krúvaḥ ǀ yát ǀ śásane ǀ ná ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ ā-pṛ́k ǀ amuyā́ ǀ śáyante ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Where was your (shaft)Indra, (which ought) to be hurled (against your enemies) when you did cleavetherākṣasashastening to war, and when the Mitrakru lay on the ground there in confusion like cattle at theplace of immolation?”

shlokas.sanskrit: श॒त्रू॒यन्तो॑ अ॒भि ये न॑स्तत॒स्रे महि॒ व्राध॑न्त ओग॒णास॑ इन्द्र । अ॒न्धेना॒मित्रा॒स्तम॑सा सचन्तां सुज्यो॒तिषो॑ अ॒क्तव॒स्ताँ अ॒भि ष्यु॑:
shlokas.transliteration: śatru-yántaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ naḥ ǀ tatasré ǀ máhi ǀ vrā́dhantaḥ ǀ ogaṇā́saḥ ǀ indra ǀandhéna ǀ amítrāḥ ǀ támasā ǀ sacantām ǀ su-jyotíṣaḥ ǀ aktávaḥ ǀ tā́n ǀ abhí ǀ syuríti syuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May those adversaries,Indra, who press upon us, fiercely opposing us, and assembled in numbers,be overwhelmed with thick darkness, and may the bright (days) and nights overpower them. hymn you, and disregarding all other worshippers, come to us with your protection.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पु॒रूणि॒ हि त्वा॒ सव॑ना॒ जना॑नां॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि॒ मन्द॑न्गृण॒तामृषी॑णाम् । इ॒मामा॒घोष॒न्नव॑सा॒ सहू॑तिं ति॒रो विश्वाँ॒ अर्च॑तो याह्य॒र्वाङ्
shlokas.transliteration: purū́ṇi ǀ hí ǀ tvā ǀ sávanā ǀ jánānām ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ mándan ǀ gṛṇatā́m ǀ ṛ́ṣīṇām ǀimā́m ǀ ā-ghóṣan ǀ ávasā ǀ sá-hūtim ǀ tiráḥ ǀ víśvān ǀ árcataḥ ǀ yāhi ǀ arvā́ṅ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒वा ते॑ व॒यमि॑न्द्र भुञ्जती॒नां वि॒द्याम॑ सुमती॒नां नवा॑नाम् । वि॒द्याम॒ वस्तो॒रव॑सा गृ॒णन्तो॑ वि॒श्वामि॑त्रा उ॒त त॑ इन्द्र नू॒नम्
shlokas.transliteration: evá ǀ te ǀ vayám ǀ indra ǀ bhuñjatīnā́m ǀ vidyā́ma ǀ su-matīnā́m ǀ návānām ǀvidyā́ma ǀ vástoḥ ǀ ávasā ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ viśvā́mitrāḥ ǀ utá ǀ te ǀ indra ǀ nūnám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May we, the descendants ofViśvāmitra, sincerely praising you,Indra,by day for your protection,obtain your protecting (favours), may we obtain your recent (favours).”

shlokas.sanskrit: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्
shlokas.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We invoke in this conflict for our protection the pure, the opulentIndra, the most heroic in the fight,”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒हस्र॑शीर्षा॒ पुरु॑षः सहस्रा॒क्षः स॒हस्र॑पात् । स भूमिं॑ वि॒श्वतो॑ वृ॒त्वात्य॑तिष्ठद्दशाङ्गु॒लम्
shlokas.transliteration: sahásra-śīrṣā ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀ sahasra-akṣáḥ ǀ sahásra-pāt ǀsáḥ ǀ bhū́mim ǀ viśvátaḥ ǀ vṛtvā́ ǀ áti ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ daśa-aṅgulám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Puruṣa, who has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet, investing the earth in alldirections, exceeds (it by a space) measuring ten fingers.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पुरु॑ष ए॒वेदं सर्वं॒ यद्भू॒तं यच्च॒ भव्य॑म् । उ॒तामृ॑त॒त्वस्येशा॑नो॒ यदन्ने॑नाति॒रोह॑ति
shlokas.transliteration: púruṣaḥ ǀ evá ǀ idám ǀ sárvam ǀ yát ǀ bhūtám ǀ yát ǀ ca ǀ bhávyam ǀutá ǀ amṛta-tvásya ǀ ī́śānaḥ ǀ yát ǀ ánnena ǀ ati-róhati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Puruṣais verily all this (visible world), all that is, and all that is to be; he is also the lord of immortality;for he mounts beyond (his own condition) for the food (of living beings).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒तावा॑नस्य महि॒मातो॒ ज्यायाँ॑श्च॒ पूरु॑षः । पादो॑ऽस्य॒ विश्वा॑ भू॒तानि॑ त्रि॒पाद॑स्या॒मृतं॑ दि॒वि
shlokas.transliteration: etā́vān ǀ asya ǀ mahimā́ ǀ átaḥ ǀ jyā́yān ǀ ca ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀpā́daḥ ǀ asya ǀ víśvā ǀ bhūtā́ni ǀ tri-pā́t ǀ asya ǀ amṛ́tam ǀ diví ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Such is his greatness; andPuruṣais greater even than this; all beings are one-fourth of him; his otherthree-fourths, (being) immortal, (abide) in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्रि॒पादू॒र्ध्व उदै॒त्पुरु॑ष॒: पादो॑ऽस्ये॒हाभ॑व॒त्पुन॑: । ततो॒ विष्व॒ङ्व्य॑क्रामत्साशनानश॒ने अ॒भि
shlokas.transliteration: tri-pā́t ǀ ūrdhváḥ ǀ út ǀ ait ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀ pā́daḥ ǀ asya ǀ ihá ǀ abhavat ǀ púnaríti ǀtátaḥ ǀ víṣvaṅ ǀ ví ǀ akrāmat ǀ sāśanānaśané íti ǀ abhí ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Three-fourths ofPuruṣaascended; the other fourth that remained in this world proceeds repeatedly,and, diversified in various forms, went to all animate and inanimate creation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मा॑द्वि॒राळ॑जायत वि॒राजो॒ अधि॒ पूरु॑षः । स जा॒तो अत्य॑रिच्यत प॒श्चाद्भूमि॒मथो॑ पु॒रः
shlokas.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ virā́ṭ ǀ ajāyata ǀ vi-rā́jaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ púruṣaḥ ǀsáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ áti ǀ aricyata ǀ paścā́t ǀ bhū́mim ǀ átho íti ǀ puráḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From him was born Virāt. and from Virāt.Puruṣa; he, as soon as born, became manifested, andafterwards (created) the earth (and) then corporeal forms.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्पुरु॑षेण ह॒विषा॑ दे॒वा य॒ज्ञमत॑न्वत । व॒स॒न्तो अ॑स्यासी॒दाज्यं॑ ग्री॒ष्म इ॒ध्मः श॒रद्ध॒विः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ púruṣeṇa ǀ havíṣā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ átanvata ǀvasantáḥ ǀ asya ǀ āsīt ǀ ā́jyam ǀ grīṣmáḥ ǀ idhmáḥ ǀ śarát ǀ havíḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When the gods performed the sacrifice withPuruṣaas the offering, then Spring was its ghī, Summerthe fuel, and Autumn the oblation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तं य॒ज्ञं ब॒र्हिषि॒ प्रौक्ष॒न्पुरु॑षं जा॒तम॑ग्र॒तः । तेन॑ दे॒वा अ॑यजन्त सा॒ध्या ऋष॑यश्च॒ ये
shlokas.transliteration: tám ǀ yajñám ǀ barhíṣi ǀ prá ǀ aukṣan ǀ púruṣam ǀ jātám ǀ agratáḥ ǀténa ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ ayajanta ǀ sādhyā́ḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They immolated as the victim upon the sacred grassPuruṣa, born before (creation); with him thedeities who wereSādhyasand those who were Ṛṣis sacrificed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मा॑द्य॒ज्ञात्स॑र्व॒हुत॒: सम्भृ॑तं पृषदा॒ज्यम् । प॒शून्ताँश्च॑क्रे वाय॒व्या॑नार॒ण्यान्ग्रा॒म्याश्च॒ ये
shlokas.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ yajñā́t ǀ sarva-hútaḥ ǀ sám-bhṛtam ǀ pṛṣat-ājyám ǀpaśū́n ǀ tā́n ǀ cakre ǀ vāyavyā́n ǀ āraṇyā́n ǀ grāmyā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ yé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From that victim, in whom the universal oblation was offered, the mixture of curds and butter wasproduced, (then) he made those animals over whomVāyupresides, those that are wild, and those that aretame.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मा॑द्य॒ज्ञात्स॑र्व॒हुत॒ ऋच॒: सामा॑नि जज्ञिरे । छन्दां॑सि जज्ञिरे॒ तस्मा॒द्यजु॒स्तस्मा॑दजायत
shlokas.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ yajñā́t ǀ sarva-hútaḥ ǀ ṛ́caḥ ǀ sā́māni ǀ jajñire ǀchándāṃsi ǀ jajñire ǀ tásmāt ǀ yájuḥ ǀ tásmāt ǀ ajāyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From that victim, in whom the universal oblation was offered, the ṛccas andsāmanswere produced;from him the metres were born; from him theyajus. was born.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मा॒दश्वा॑ अजायन्त॒ ये के चो॑भ॒याद॑तः । गावो॑ ह जज्ञिरे॒ तस्मा॒त्तस्मा॑ज्जा॒ता अ॑जा॒वय॑:
shlokas.transliteration: tásmāt ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ ajāyanta ǀ yé ǀ ké ǀ ca ǀ ubhayā́dataḥ ǀgā́vaḥ ǀ ha ǀ jajñire ǀ tásmāt ǀ tásmāt ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ ajāváyaḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्पुरु॑षं॒ व्यद॑धुः कति॒धा व्य॑कल्पयन् । मुखं॒ किम॑स्य॒ कौ बा॒हू का ऊ॒रू पादा॑ उच्येते
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ púruṣam ǀ ví ǀ ádadhuḥ ǀ katidhā́ ǀ ví ǀ akalpayan ǀmúkham ǀ kím ǀ asya ǀ káu ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ káu ǀ ūrū́ íti ǀ pā́dau ǀ ucyete íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When they immolatedPuruṣa, into how many portions did they divide him? What was his mouth called, what his arms, what his thighs, what were his feet called?”

shlokas.sanskrit: ब्रा॒ह्म॒णो॑ऽस्य॒ मुख॑मासीद्बा॒हू रा॑ज॒न्य॑: कृ॒तः । ऊ॒रू तद॑स्य॒ यद्वैश्य॑: प॒द्भ्यां शू॒द्रो अ॑जायत
shlokas.transliteration: brāhmaṇáḥ ǀ asya ǀ múkham ǀ āsīt ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ rājanyáḥ ǀ kṛtáḥ ǀūrū́ íti ǀ tát ǀ asya ǀ yát ǀ váiśyaḥ ǀ pat-bhyā́m ǀ śūdráḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “His mouth became theBrāhmaṇa, his arms became theRājanya, his thighs became theVaiśya;theŚūdrawas born from his feet.”

shlokas.sanskrit: च॒न्द्रमा॒ मन॑सो जा॒तश्चक्षो॒: सूर्यो॑ अजायत । मुखा॒दिन्द्र॑श्चा॒ग्निश्च॑ प्रा॒णाद्वा॒युर॑जायत
shlokas.transliteration: candrámāḥ ǀ mánasaḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ cákṣoḥ ǀ sū́ryaḥ ǀ ajāyata ǀmúkhāt ǀ índraḥ ǀ ca ǀ agníḥ ǀ ca ǀ prāṇā́t ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ajāyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The moon was born from his mind; the sun was born from his eye;IndraandAgniwere born from his mouth,Vāyufrom his breath.”

shlokas.sanskrit: नाभ्या॑ आसीद॒न्तरि॑क्षं शी॒र्ष्णो द्यौः सम॑वर्तत । प॒द्भ्यां भूमि॒र्दिश॒: श्रोत्रा॒त्तथा॑ लो॒काँ अ॑कल्पयन्
shlokas.transliteration: nā́bhyāḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ antárikṣam ǀ śīrṣṇáḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ sám ǀ avartata ǀpat-bhyā́m ǀ bhū́miḥ ǀ díśaḥ ǀ śrótrāt ǀ táthā ǀ lokā́n ǀ akalpayan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From his navel came the firmament, from his head the heaven was produced, the earth from his feet,the quarters of space from his ear, so they constituted the world.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒प्तास्या॑सन्परि॒धय॒स्त्रिः स॒प्त स॒मिध॑: कृ॒ताः । दे॒वा यद्य॒ज्ञं त॑न्वा॒ना अब॑ध्न॒न्पुरु॑षं प॒शुम्
shlokas.transliteration: saptá ǀ asya ǀ āsan ǀ pari-dháyaḥ ǀ tríḥ ǀ saptá ǀ sam-ídhaḥ ǀ kṛtā́ḥ ǀdevā́ḥ ǀ yát ǀ yajñám ǀ tanvānā́ḥ ǀ ábadhnan ǀ púruṣam ǀ paśúm ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Seven were the enclosures of the sacrifice, thrice seven logs of fuel were prepared, when the gods,celebrating the rite, boundPuruṣaas the victim.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒ज्ञेन॑ य॒ज्ञम॑यजन्त दे॒वास्तानि॒ धर्मा॑णि प्रथ॒मान्या॑सन् । ते ह॒ नाकं॑ महि॒मान॑: सचन्त॒ यत्र॒ पूर्वे॑ सा॒ध्याः सन्ति॑ दे॒वाः
shlokas.transliteration: yajñéna ǀ yajñám ǀ ayajanta ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ tā́ni ǀ dhármāṇi ǀ prathamā́ni ǀ āsan ǀté ǀ ha ǀ nā́kam ǀ mahimā́naḥ ǀ sacanta ǀ yátra ǀ pū́rve ǀ sādhyā́ḥ ǀ sánti ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “By sacrifice the gods worshipped (him who is also) the sacrifice; those were the first duties. Thosegreat ones became partakers of the heaven where the ancient deities theSādhyasabide. 10.091.01 Damūnas, being glorified by his diligent (worshippers), desiring food upon the footmark of Iḷā, iskindled in the chamber (of sacrifice), the offerer of every oblation, the object of veneration, the lord, theresplendent, to him who desires his friendship.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सं जा॑गृ॒वद्भि॒र्जर॑माण इध्यते॒ दमे॒ दमू॑ना इ॒षय॑न्नि॒ळस्प॒दे । विश्व॑स्य॒ होता॑ ह॒विषो॒ वरे॑ण्यो वि॒भुर्वि॒भावा॑ सु॒षखा॑ सखीय॒ते
shlokas.transliteration: sám ǀ jāgṛvát-bhiḥ ǀ járamāṇaḥ ǀ idhyate ǀ dáme ǀ dámūnāḥ ǀ iṣáyan ǀ iḷáḥ ǀ padé ǀvíśvasya ǀ hótā ǀ havíṣaḥ ǀ váreṇyaḥ ǀ vi-bhúḥ ǀ vibhā́-vā ǀ su-sákhā ǀ sakhi-yaté ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: स द॑र्शत॒श्रीरति॑थिर्गृ॒हेगृ॑हे॒ वने॑वने शिश्रिये तक्व॒वीरि॑व । जनं॑जनं॒ जन्यो॒ नाति॑ मन्यते॒ विश॒ आ क्षे॑ति वि॒श्यो॒३॒॑ विशं॑विशम्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ darśata-śrī́ḥ ǀ átithiḥ ǀ gṛhé-gṛhe ǀ váne-vane ǀ śiśriye ǀ takvavī́ḥ-iva ǀjánam-janam ǀ jányaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áti ǀ manyate ǀ víśaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ kṣeti ǀ viśyáḥ ǀ víśam-viśam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Of manifest glory, he resorts as a guest to every house (of his worshippers) to every forest; friendly toman, like one going to all men, he disregards them not; kind to all, he dwells among all men, (he presides ove4r”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒दक्षो॒ दक्षै॒: क्रतु॑नासि सु॒क्रतु॒रग्ने॑ क॒विः काव्ये॑नासि विश्व॒वित् । वसु॒र्वसू॑नां क्षयसि॒ त्वमेक॒ इद्द्यावा॑ च॒ यानि॑ पृथि॒वी च॒ पुष्य॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: su-dákṣaḥ ǀ dákṣaḥ ǀ krátunā ǀ asi ǀ su-krátuḥ ǀ ágne ǀ kavíḥ ǀ kā́vyena ǀ asi ǀ viśva-vít ǀvásuḥ ǀ vásūnām ǀ kṣayasi ǀ tvám ǀ ékaḥ ǀ ít ǀ dyā́vā ǀ ca ǀ yā́ni ǀ pṛthivī́ íti ǀ ca ǀ púṣyataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Agni, are vigorous with vigour, you are active with acts (of piety), you are wise withwisdom, knowing all things. You are the dispenser ofwealth, you abide alone, you are lord of the treasures ofheaven and earth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र॒जा॒नन्न॑ग्ने॒ तव॒ योनि॑मृ॒त्विय॒मिळा॑यास्प॒दे घृ॒तव॑न्त॒मास॑दः । आ ते॑ चिकित्र उ॒षसा॑मि॒वेत॑योऽरे॒पस॒: सूर्य॑स्येव र॒श्मय॑:
shlokas.transliteration: pra-jānán ǀ agne ǀ táva ǀ yónim ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ íḷāyāḥ ǀ padé ǀ ghṛtá-vantam ǀ ā́ ǀ asadaḥ ǀā́ ǀ te ǀ cikitre ǀ uṣásām-iva ǀ étayaḥ ǀ arepásaḥ ǀ sū́ryasya-iva ǀ raśmáyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “SagaciousAgni, you sit at your station suited to the sacrifice and anointed with butter at the foot-markof Iḷā. your quick-moving rays are manifested like those of the dawns, beautiful as those of the sun.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तव॒ श्रियो॑ व॒र्ष्य॑स्येव वि॒द्युत॑श्चि॒त्राश्चि॑कित्र उ॒षसां॒ न के॒तव॑: । यदोष॑धीर॒भिसृ॑ष्टो॒ वना॑नि च॒ परि॑ स्व॒यं चि॑नु॒षे अन्न॑मा॒स्ये॑
shlokas.transliteration: táva ǀ śríyaḥ ǀ varṣyásya-iva ǀ vi-dyútaḥ ǀ citrā́ḥ ǀ cikitre ǀ uṣásām ǀ ná ǀ ketávaḥ ǀyát ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ abhí-sṛṣṭaḥ ǀ vánāni ǀ ca ǀ pári ǀ svayám ǀ cinuṣé ǀ ánnam ǀ āsyé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Your glories,Agni, like the lightnings of the rain-cloud are manifested many-tinted, like themanifestations of the dawn, when quitting the plural nts and the forests, you gather on all sides food for your mouth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तमोष॑धीर्दधिरे॒ गर्भ॑मृ॒त्वियं॒ तमापो॑ अ॒ग्निं ज॑नयन्त मा॒तर॑: । तमित्स॑मा॒नं व॒निन॑श्च वी॒रुधो॒ऽन्तर्व॑तीश्च॒ सुव॑ते च वि॒श्वहा॑
shlokas.transliteration: tám ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ gárbham ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ tám ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ agním ǀ janayanta ǀ mātáraḥ ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ samānám ǀ vanínaḥ ǀ ca ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ antáḥ-vatīḥ ǀ ca ǀ súvate ǀ ca ǀ viśváhā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The plural nts bear him as the embryo (conceived) in due season; the maternal waters bring forthAgni;yes, the trees and the pregnant creepers bring him forth daily like themselves.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वातो॑पधूत इषि॒तो वशाँ॒ अनु॑ तृ॒षु यदन्ना॒ वेवि॑षद्वि॒तिष्ठ॑से । आ ते॑ यतन्ते र॒थ्यो॒३॒॑ यथा॒ पृथ॒क्छर्धां॑स्यग्ने अ॒जरा॑णि॒ धक्ष॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: vā́ta-upadhūtaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ váśān ǀ ánu ǀ tṛṣú ǀ yát ǀ ánnā ǀ véviṣat ǀ vi-tíṣṭhase ǀā́ ǀ te ǀ yatante ǀ rathyáḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ pṛ́thak ǀ śárdhāṃsi ǀ agne ǀ ajárāṇi ǀ dhákṣataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, agitated by the wind and quickly moving through the beloved (trees), you spread aboutdevouring the food, the imperishable energies of you,Agni, the devourer, rush forth like charioteers.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मे॒धा॒का॒रं वि॒दथ॑स्य प्र॒साध॑नम॒ग्निं होता॑रं परि॒भूत॑मं म॒तिम् । तमिदर्भे॑ ह॒विष्या स॑मा॒नमित्तमिन्म॒हे वृ॑णते॒ नान्यं त्वत्
shlokas.transliteration: medhā-kārám ǀ vidáthasya ǀ pra-sā́dhanam ǀ agním ǀ hótāram ǀ pari-bhū́tamam ǀ matím ǀtám ǀ ít ǀ árbhe ǀ havíṣi ǀ ā́ ǀ samānám ǀ ít ǀ tám ǀ ít ǀ mahé ǀ vṛṇate ǀ ná ǀ anyám ǀ tvát ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(The priest) selects you, (Agni), the giver of intelligence, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the invokerof the gods, the chief overcomer of foes, the councillor, alike verily at the lesser and at the greater oblation andnone other than you.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वामिदत्र॑ वृणते त्वा॒यवो॒ होता॑रमग्ने वि॒दथे॑षु वे॒धस॑: । यद्दे॑व॒यन्तो॒ दध॑ति॒ प्रयां॑सि ते ह॒विष्म॑न्तो॒ मन॑वो वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः
shlokas.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ ít ǀ átra ǀ vṛṇate ǀ tvā-yávaḥ ǀ hótāram ǀ agne ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ vedhásaḥ ǀyát ǀ deva-yántaḥ ǀ dádhati ǀ práyāṃsi ǀ te ǀ havíṣmantaḥ ǀ mánavaḥ ǀ vṛktá-barhiṣaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The performers of sacred rites, devoted toAgni, to you, select you as the ministrant priest at sacrificesin this world, when the devout worshippers bearing oblations and strewing the clipped sacred grass offer youfood.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तवा॑ग्ने हो॒त्रं तव॑ पो॒त्रमृ॒त्वियं॒ तव॑ ने॒ष्ट्रं त्वम॒ग्निदृ॑ताय॒तः । तव॑ प्रशा॒स्त्रं त्वम॑ध्वरीयसि ब्र॒ह्मा चासि॑ गृ॒हप॑तिश्च नो॒ दमे॑
shlokas.transliteration: táva ǀ agne ǀ hotrám ǀ táva ǀ potrám ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ táva ǀ neṣṭrám ǀ tvám ǀ agnít ǀ ṛta-yatáḥ ǀtáva ǀ pra-śāstrám ǀ tvám ǀ adhvari-yasi ǀ brahmā́ ǀ ca ǀ ási ǀ gṛhá-patiḥ ǀ ca ǀ naḥ ǀ dáme ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Yours,Agni, is the function of theHotā, yours the duly-performed function of thePotā, yours thefunction of theNeṣṭā, you are the Agni of the sacrificer, yours is the office of the Praśāstā, you act asAdhvaryu, and you are theBrahmāand the lord of the mansion in our abode.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्तुभ्य॑मग्ने अ॒मृता॑य॒ मर्त्य॑: स॒मिधा॒ दाश॑दु॒त वा॑ ह॒विष्कृ॑ति । तस्य॒ होता॑ भवसि॒ यासि॑ दू॒त्य१॒॑मुप॑ ब्रूषे॒ यज॑स्यध्वरी॒यसि॑
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ túbhyam ǀ agne ǀ amṛ́tāya ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ sam-ídhā ǀ dā́śat ǀ utá ǀ vā ǀ havíḥ-kṛti ǀtásya ǀ hótā ǀ bhavasi ǀ yā́si ǀ dūtyám ǀ úpa ǀ brūṣe ǀ yájasi ǀ adhvari-yási ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The mortal,Agni, who presents to you, the immortal, fuel at the offering of the oblation-- you are hisHotā, you go on his errant (to the gods), you direct (the ceremonial), you offer the sacrifice, you act as theofficiating priest.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मा अ॑स्मै म॒तयो॒ वाचो॑ अ॒स्मदाँ ऋचो॒ गिर॑: सुष्टु॒तय॒: सम॑ग्मत । व॒सू॒यवो॒ वस॑वे जा॒तवे॑दसे वृ॒द्धासु॑ चि॒द्वर्ध॑नो॒ यासु॑ चा॒कन॑त्
shlokas.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ asmai ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ vā́caḥ ǀ asmát ǀ ā́ ǀ ṛ́caḥ ǀ gíraḥ ǀ su-stutáyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ agmata ǀvasu-yávaḥ ǀ vásave ǀ jātá-vedase ǀ vṛddhā́su ǀ cit ǀ várdhanaḥ ǀ yā́su ǀ cākánat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May these laudatory words, these eulogistic verses, these voices (proceeding) from us, reach him thegiver of wealth,Jātavedas; these wealth- desiring (words) in which when they are perfected, the perfecterdelights.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मां प्र॒त्नाय॑ सुष्टु॒तिं नवी॑यसीं वो॒चेय॑मस्मा उश॒ते शृ॒णोतु॑ नः । भू॒या अन्त॑रा हृ॒द्य॑स्य नि॒स्पृशे॑ जा॒येव॒ पत्य॑ उश॒ती सु॒वासा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: imā́m ǀ pratnā́ya ǀ su-stutím ǀ návīyasīm ǀ vocéyam ǀ asmai ǀ uśaté ǀ śṛṇótu ǀ naḥ ǀbhūyā́ḥ ǀ ántarā ǀ hṛdí ǀ asya ǀ ni-spṛ́śe ǀ jāyā́-iva ǀ pátye ǀ uśatī́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I will address this new laudatory hymn to the ancientAgni, who is gratified (by praise). May he hear uṣMay I be in the centre of his heart, to touch it, like a loving well-attired wife (in the heart) of her husband.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्मि॒न्नश्वा॑स ऋष॒भास॑ उ॒क्षणो॑ व॒शा मे॒षा अ॑वसृ॒ष्टास॒ आहु॑ताः । की॒ला॒ल॒पे सोम॑पृष्ठाय वे॒धसे॑ हृ॒दा म॒तिं ज॑नये॒ चारु॑म॒ग्नये॑
shlokas.transliteration: yásmin ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ṛṣabhā́saḥ ǀ ukṣáṇaḥ ǀ vaśā́ḥ ǀ meṣā́ḥ ǀ ava-sṛṣṭā́saḥ ǀ ā́-hutāḥ ǀkīlāla-pé ǀ sóma-pṛṣṭhāya ǀ vedháse ǀ hṛdā́ ǀ matím ǀ janaye ǀ cā́rum ǀ agnáye ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I offer graceful praise with all my heart toAgni, the drinker of water, whose back is sprinkled withSoma, the ordainer (of the rite), to whom vigorous horses and bulls and barren cows and sheep are consignedas burnt offerings.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अहा॑व्यग्ने ह॒विरा॒स्ये॑ ते स्रु॒ची॑व घृ॒तं च॒म्वी॑व॒ सोम॑: । वा॒ज॒सनिं॑ र॒यिम॒स्मे सु॒वीरं॑ प्रश॒स्तं धे॑हि य॒शसं॑ बृ॒हन्त॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: áhāvi ǀ agne ǀ havíḥ ǀ āsyé ǀ te ǀ srucí-iva ǀ ghṛtám ǀ camví-iva ǀ sómaḥ ǀvāja-sánim ǀ rayím ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-vī́ram ǀ pra-śastám ǀ dhehi ǀ yaśásam ǀ bṛhántam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The oblation has been poured,Agni, into your mouth, like butter into the ladle, likeSomainto thespoon. Bestow upon us riches conferring food, (comprehending)maleprogeny, excellent renowned andabundant.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒ज्ञस्य॑ वो र॒थ्यं॑ वि॒श्पतिं॑ वि॒शां होता॑रम॒क्तोरति॑थिं वि॒भाव॑सुम् । शोच॒ञ्छुष्का॑सु॒ हरि॑णीषु॒ जर्भु॑र॒द्वृषा॑ के॒तुर्य॑ज॒तो द्याम॑शायत
shlokas.transliteration: yajñásya ǀ vaḥ ǀ rathyám ǀ viśpátim ǀ viśā́m ǀ hótāram ǀ aktóḥ ǀ átithim ǀ vibhā́-vasum ǀśócan ǀ śúṣkāsu ǀ háriṇīṣu ǀ járbhurat ǀ vṛ́ṣā ǀ ketúḥ ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dyā́m ǀ aśāyata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You (gods, adore) the charioteer of the sacrifice, the lord of men, the invoker of the gods, the guest ofnight, the resplendent (Agni). Blazing amid the dry (bushes) preying upon the green, the showerer of desires, thebanner (of light), the adorable, he reposes in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मम॑ञ्ज॒स्पामु॒भये॑ अकृण्वत ध॒र्माण॑म॒ग्निं वि॒दथ॑स्य॒ साध॑नम् । अ॒क्तुं न य॒ह्वमु॒षस॑: पु॒रोहि॑तं॒ तनू॒नपा॑तमरु॒षस्य॑ निंसते
shlokas.transliteration: imám ǀ añjaḥ-pā́m ǀ ubháye ǀ akṛṇvata ǀ dharmā́ṇam ǀ agním ǀ vidáthasya ǀ sā́dhanam ǀaktúm ǀ ná ǀ yahvám ǀ uṣásaḥ ǀ puráḥ-hitam ǀ tanū́-nápātam ǀ aruṣásya ǀ niṃsate ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Both (men and gods) have madeAgnithe speedy protector, the upholder of duty, the accomplisher ofthe sacrifice; they have recourse to him (who is) vast as the sun, the precursor of the dawn, the son of thebrilliant (Vāyu).”

shlokas.sanskrit: बळ॑स्य नी॒था वि प॒णेश्च॑ मन्महे व॒या अ॑स्य॒ प्रहु॑ता आसु॒रत्त॑वे । य॒दा घो॒रासो॑ अमृत॒त्वमाश॒तादिज्जन॑स्य॒ दैव्य॑स्य चर्किरन्
shlokas.transliteration: báṭ ǀ asya ǀ nīthā́ ǀ ví ǀ paṇéḥ ǀ ca ǀ manmahe ǀ vayā́ḥ ǀ asya ǀ prá-hutāḥ ǀ āsuḥ ǀ áttave ǀyadā́ ǀ ghorā́saḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ ā́śata ǀ ā́t ǀ ít ǀ jánasya ǀ dáivyasya ǀ carkiran ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We desire that our notion of that adorable (Agni) may be true, and that our oblations may be to him forfood. When his formidable (flames) attain immortality, then may our priests scatter (oblations for the benefit) ofthe divine being.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒तस्य॒ हि प्रसि॑ति॒र्द्यौरु॒रु व्यचो॒ नमो॑ म॒ह्य१॒॑रम॑ति॒: पनी॑यसी । इन्द्रो॑ मि॒त्रो वरु॑ण॒: सं चि॑कित्रि॒रेऽथो॒ भग॑: सवि॒ता पू॒तद॑क्षसः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ prá-sitiḥ ǀ dyáuḥ ǀ urú ǀ vyácaḥ ǀ námaḥ ǀ mahī́ ǀ arámatiḥ ǀ pánīyasī ǀíndraḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ sám ǀ cikitrire ǀ átho íti ǀ bhágaḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ pūtá-dakṣasaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The vast heavven, the spacious firmament, the glorious unbounded earth, (do) homage (to theAgni)of the sacrifice; andIndra,Mitra,Varuṇa,Bhaga, andSavitā, whose strength is purified, unite to recognize (hisexcellence). the circumambient (Indra) sweeping over a wide space, roaring in the belly (of the firmament), sprinkles the wholeworld.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र रु॒द्रेण॑ य॒यिना॑ यन्ति॒ सिन्ध॑वस्ति॒रो म॒हीम॒रम॑तिं दधन्विरे । येभि॒: परि॑ज्मा परि॒यन्नु॒रु ज्रयो॒ वि रोरु॑वज्ज॒ठरे॒ विश्व॑मु॒क्षते॑
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ rudréṇa ǀ yayínā ǀ yanti ǀ síndhavaḥ ǀ tiráḥ ǀ mahī́m ǀ arámatim ǀ dadhanvire ǀyébhiḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ pari-yán ǀ urú ǀ jráyaḥ ǀ ví ǀ róruvat ǀ jaṭháre ǀ víśvam ǀ ukṣáte ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: क्रा॒णा रु॒द्रा म॒रुतो॑ वि॒श्वकृ॑ष्टयो दि॒वः श्ये॒नासो॒ असु॑रस्य नी॒ळय॑: । तेभि॑श्चष्टे॒ वरु॑णो मि॒त्रो अ॑र्य॒मेन्द्रो॑ दे॒वेभि॑रर्व॒शेभि॒रर्व॑शः
shlokas.transliteration: krāṇā́ḥ ǀ rudrā́ḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ viśvá-kṛṣṭayaḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ śyenā́saḥ ǀ ásurasya ǀ nīḷáyaḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ caṣṭe ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ índraḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ arvaśébhiḥ ǀ árvaśaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheMaruts, the sons ofRudra, mixing with men, the hawks of the sky, the inhabitants of the cloud,(are) performing (their functions); with those horse-owing deities,Varuṇa,Mitra,Aryaman, andIndra, the lord ofhorses contemplates (the rite).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रे॒ भुजं॑ शशमा॒नास॑ आशत॒ सूरो॒ दृशी॑के॒ वृष॑णश्च॒ पौंस्ये॑ । प्र ये न्व॑स्या॒र्हणा॑ ततक्षि॒रे युजं॒ वज्रं॑ नृ॒षद॑नेषु का॒रव॑:
shlokas.transliteration: índre ǀ bhújam ǀ śaśamānā́saḥ ǀ āśata ǀ sū́raḥ ǀ dṛ́śīke ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ ca ǀ páuṃsye ǀprá ǀ yé ǀ nú ǀ asya ǀ arháṇā ǀ tatakṣiré ǀ yújam ǀ vájram ǀ nṛ-sádaneṣu ǀ kārávaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Those who praise him find protection inIndra; (those who praise him find) universal vision in the sun;(those who praise him find) manly vigour in the vigorous (Indra); those worshippers who diligently offer adorationto Indra (acquire) the thunderbolt as their ally in the dwellings of men.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सूर॑श्चि॒दा ह॒रितो॑ अस्य रीरम॒दिन्द्रा॒दा कश्चि॑द्भयत॒ज तवी॑यसः । भी॒मस्य॒ वृष्णो॑ ज॒ठरा॑दभि॒श्वसो॑ दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ सहु॑रिः स्त॒न्नबा॑धितः
shlokas.transliteration: sū́raḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǀ harítaḥ ǀ asya ǀ rīramat ǀ índrāt ǀ ā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ cit ǀ bhayate ǀ távīyasaḥ ǀbhīmásya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ jaṭhárāt ǀ abhi-śvásaḥ ǀ divé-dive ǀ sáhuriḥ ǀ stan ǀ ábādhitaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The sun urging his steeds (in obedience to) his (commands) delights (in his presence); every (god) isin fear of the powerfulIndra; from the belly of the formidable sighing showerer (of benefits) the all-enduringirresistible (deity) thunders day by day.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्तोमं॑ वो अ॒द्य रु॒द्राय॒ शिक्व॑से क्ष॒यद्वी॑राय॒ नम॑सा दिदिष्टन । येभि॑: शि॒वः स्ववाँ॑ एव॒याव॑भिर्दि॒वः सिष॑क्ति॒ स्वय॑शा॒ निका॑मभिः
shlokas.transliteration: stómam ǀ vaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ rudrā́ya ǀ śíkvase ǀ kṣayát-vīrāya ǀ námasā ǀ didiṣṭana ǀyébhiḥ ǀ śiváḥ ǀ svá-vān ǀ evayā́va-bhiḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ sísakti ǀ svá-yaśāḥ ǀ níkāma-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Address praise today with reverence toRudrathe powerful destroyer of the heroes, (who isaccompanied) by the mounted (Maruts), the granters of wishes, together with whom he, propitious, possessingkinsmen, besprinkles (the worshippers) from heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते हि प्र॒जाया॒ अभ॑रन्त॒ वि श्रवो॒ बृह॒स्पति॑र्वृष॒भः सोम॑जामयः । य॒ज्ञैरथ॑र्वा प्रथ॒मो वि धा॑रयद्दे॒वा दक्षै॒र्भृग॑व॒: सं चि॑कित्रिरे
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ pra-jā́yāḥ ǀ ábharanta ǀ ví ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ sóma-jāmayaḥ ǀyajñáiḥ ǀ átharvā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ ví ǀ dhārayat ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ dákṣaiḥ ǀ bhṛ́gavaḥ ǀ sám ǀ cikitrire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Inasmuch asBṛhaspati, the showerer (of benefits) and the kindred ofSoma(the Visvedevās),bestow food (for the support) of people,Atharvanwas the first to invigorate (the gods) with sacrifices; withstrength the gods andBhṛgusdiscovered (the cattle).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते हि द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी भूरि॑रेतसा॒ नरा॒शंस॒श्चतु॑रङ्गो य॒मोऽदि॑तिः । दे॒वस्त्वष्टा॑ द्रविणो॒दा ऋ॑भु॒क्षण॒: प्र रो॑द॒सी म॒रुतो॒ विष्णु॑रर्हिरे
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ hí ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ bhū́ri-retasā ǀ nárāśáṃsaḥ ǀ cátuḥ-aṅgaḥ ǀ yamáḥ ǀ áditiḥ ǀdeváḥ ǀ tváṣṭā ǀ draviṇaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣáṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ rodasī́ íti ǀ marútaḥ ǀ víṣṇuḥ ǀ arhire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They the heaven and earth, abounding with waters, the Narāśaṃsa rite with its four fires,Yama,Aditi, the divineTvaṣṭā, (Agni) the giver of wealth, theṚbhus,Rodasī, theMaruts, andViṣṇuareworshipped (by us).”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त स्य न॑ उ॒शिजा॑मुर्वि॒या क॒विरहि॑: शृणोतु बु॒ध्न्यो॒३॒॑ हवी॑मनि । सूर्या॒मासा॑ वि॒चर॑न्ता दिवि॒क्षिता॑ धि॒या श॑मीनहुषी अ॒स्य बो॑धतम्
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ syáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ uśíjām ǀ urviyā́ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ áhiḥ ǀ śṛṇotu ǀ budhnyáḥ ǀ hávīmani ǀsū́ryāmā́sā ǀ vi-cárantā ǀ divi-kṣítā ǀ dhiyā́ ǀ śamīnahuṣī íti ǀ asyá ǀ bodhatam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “And may the wise Ahi of the firmament hear the copious (pulse) of us eager (worshippers) at theoffering of oblations. May the revolving sun and moon dwelling in heaven, the earth and sky, comprehend bytheir intelligence (the purport) of this (our praise).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र न॑: पू॒षा च॒रथं॑ वि॒श्वदे॑व्यो॒ऽपां नपा॑दवतु वा॒युरि॒ष्टये॑ । आ॒त्मानं॒ वस्यो॑ अ॒भि वात॑मर्चत॒ तद॑श्विना सुहवा॒ याम॑नि श्रुतम्
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ naḥ ǀ pūṣā́ ǀ carátham ǀ viśvá-devyaḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ nápāt ǀ avatu ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ iṣṭáye ǀātmā́nam ǀ vásyaḥ ǀ abhí ǀ vā́tam ǀ arcata ǀ tát ǀ aśvinā ǀ su-havā ǀ yā́mani ǀ śrutam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayPūṣanprotect all our moveable (property); mayVāyu, the friend of theViśvedevās, thegrandson of the waters, preserve us for the celebration of the sacrifice. Worship the wind, thesoulof all, (toobtain) excellent (food);Aśvins, who are worthy to be invoked, hear us on your way.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒शामा॒सामभ॑यानामधि॒क्षितं॑ गी॒र्भिरु॒ स्वय॑शसं गृणीमसि । ग्नाभि॒र्विश्वा॑भि॒रदि॑तिमन॒र्वण॑म॒क्तोर्युवा॑नं नृ॒मणा॒ अधा॒ पति॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: viśā́m ǀ āsā́m ǀ ábhayānām ǀ adhi-kṣítam ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ gṛṇīmasi ǀgnā́bhiḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ áditim ǀ anarváṇam ǀ aktóḥ ǀ yúvānam ǀ nṛ-mánāḥ ǀ ádha ǀ pátim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We glorify with praisesAgni, the self-famous, who dwells among these fearless beings; we praise theirresistibleAditi, together with all the wives (of the gods); we praise the young (lord) of night (the moon), wepraise the friend of man (the sun), we praise (Indra) the lord (of all).”

shlokas.sanskrit: रेभ॒दत्र॑ ज॒नुषा॒ पूर्वो॒ अङ्गि॑रा॒ ग्रावा॑ण ऊ॒र्ध्वा अ॒भि च॑क्षुरध्व॒रम् । येभि॒र्विहा॑या॒ अभ॑वद्विचक्ष॒णः पाथ॑: सु॒मेकं॒ स्वधि॑ति॒र्वन॑न्वति
shlokas.transliteration: rébhat ǀ átra ǀ janúṣā ǀ pū́rvaḥ ǀ áṅgirāḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ūrdhvā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǀ cakṣuḥ ǀ adhvarám ǀyébhiḥ ǀ ví-hāyāḥ ǀ ábhavat ǀ vi-cakṣaṇáḥ ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ su-mékam ǀ svá-dhitiḥ ǀ vánan-vati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Aṅgirasa, the prior in birth, praises (the gods, here); the uplifted stones behold (theSomaof) thesacrifice, through which (stones) the sageIndrahas been exalted, (and his) thunderbolt brings forth excellentwater, (producing) food on watery way.”

shlokas.sanskrit: महि॑ द्यावापृथिवी भूतमु॒र्वी नारी॑ य॒ह्वी न रोद॑सी॒ सदं॑ नः । तेभि॑र्नः पातं॒ सह्य॑स ए॒भिर्न॑: पातं शू॒षणि॑
shlokas.transliteration: máhi ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ bhūtam ǀ urvī́ íti ǀ nā́rī íti ǀ yahvī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ ródasī íti ǀ sádam ǀ naḥ ǀtébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pātam ǀ sáhyasaḥ ǀ ebhíḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pātam ǀ śūṣáṇi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Heaven and earth, be great and spacious; mightyRodasī, be ever with us like wives; with these (yourprotections), protect us from (the foe who is) stronger (than we), with these protect us in the might (of ourenemies).”

shlokas.sanskrit: य॒ज्ञेय॑ज्ञे॒ स मर्त्यो॑ दे॒वान्त्स॑पर्यति । यः सु॒म्नैर्दी॑र्घ॒श्रुत्त॑म आ॒विवा॑सत्येनान्
shlokas.transliteration: yajñé-yajñe ǀ sáḥ ǀ mártyaḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ saparyati ǀyáḥ ǀ sumnáiḥ ǀ dīrghaśrút-tamaḥ ǀ ā-vívāsāti ǀ enān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “That man plural ases the gods at every sacrifice who, being most versed in protracted texts, worshipsthem with gratifying (oblations).”

shlokas.sanskrit: विश्वे॑षामिरज्यवो दे॒वानां॒ वार्म॒हः । विश्वे॒ हि वि॒श्वम॑हसो॒ विश्वे॑ य॒ज्ञेषु॑ य॒ज्ञिया॑:
shlokas.transliteration: víśveṣām ǀ irajyavaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ vā́ḥ ǀ maháḥ ǀvíśve ǀ hí ǀ viśvá-mahasaḥ ǀ víśve ǀ yajñéṣu ǀ yajñíyāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lords of all worlds, (give us) the abundant wealth of the gods; for (you) all are endowed with greatglory (you) all are to be worshipped at the sacrifices.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते घा॒ राजा॑नो अ॒मृत॑स्य म॒न्द्रा अ॑र्य॒मा मि॒त्रो वरु॑ण॒: परि॑ज्मा । कद्रु॒द्रो नृ॒णां स्तु॒तो म॒रुत॑: पू॒षणो॒ भग॑:
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ gha ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ amṛ́tasya ǀ mandrā́ḥ ǀ aryamā́ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀkát ǀ rudráḥ ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀ stutáḥ ǀ marútaḥ ǀ pūṣáṇaḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They are the lords of the ambrosia, adorable,Aryaman,Mitra, the circumambientVaruṇa,Rudra, whois hymned by the priests, theMaruts,Pūṣan,Bhaga.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त नो॒ नक्त॑म॒पां वृ॑षण्वसू॒ सूर्या॒मासा॒ सद॑नाय सध॒न्या॑ । सचा॒ यत्साद्ये॑षा॒महि॑र्बु॒ध्नेषु॑ बु॒ध्न्य॑:
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ náktam ǀ apā́m ǀ vṛṣaṇvasū íti vṛṣaṇ-vasū ǀ sū́ryāmā́sā ǀ sádanāya ǀ sa-dhanyā́ ǀsácā ǀ yát ǀ sā́di ǀ eṣām ǀ áhiḥ ǀ budhnéṣu ǀ budhnyáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “And (you twoAśvins) showering wealth, (you) sun and moon, (lords) of the waters, equally rich,(come) by night to our abode, whenAhirbudhnyasits down in their company in the firmamental (clouds).”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त नो॑ दे॒वाव॒श्विना॑ शु॒भस्पती॒ धाम॑भिर्मि॒त्रावरु॑णा उरुष्यताम् । म॒हः स रा॒य एष॒तेऽति॒ धन्वे॑व दुरि॒ता
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ deváu ǀ aśvínā ǀ śubháḥ ǀ pátī íti ǀ dhā́ma-bhiḥ ǀ mitrā́váruṇau ǀ uruṣyatām ǀmaháḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ rāyáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īṣate ǀ áti ǀ dhánva-iva ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “And may the divineAśvins, the lords of pure (water), andMitraandVaruṇaprotect us with theirbodies; he (whom they protect) acquires ample riches, (and passes) through misfortunes as (a traveller through)a desert.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त नो॑ रु॒द्रा चि॑न्मृळताम॒श्विना॒ विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॒ रथ॒स्पति॒र्भग॑: । ऋ॒भुर्वाज॑ ऋभुक्षण॒: परि॑ज्मा विश्ववेदसः
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ naḥ ǀ rudrā́ ǀ cit ǀ mṛḷatām ǀ aśvínā ǀ víśve ǀ devā́saḥ ǀ ráthaḥpátiḥ ǀ bhágaḥ ǀṛbhúḥ ǀ vā́jaḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣaṇaḥ ǀ pári-jmā ǀ viśva-vedasaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “And may theRudras, theAśvins, make us happy, (may) the universal gods, the lord of chariots,Bhaga,Ṛbhu,Vāja, Ribhukṣaṇa, the circumambient (Vāyu) and the omniscient (deities make us happy).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒भुॠ॑भु॒क्षा ऋ॒भुर्वि॑ध॒तो मद॒ आ ते॒ हरी॑ जूजुवा॒नस्य॑ वा॒जिना॑ । दु॒ष्टरं॒ यस्य॒ साम॑ चि॒दृध॑ग्य॒ज्ञो न मानु॑षः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛbhúḥ ǀ ṛbhukṣā́ḥ ǀ ṛbhúḥ ǀ vidhatáḥ ǀ mádaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ te ǀ hárī íti ǀ jūjuvānásya ǀ vājínā ǀdustáram ǀ yásya ǀ sā́ma ǀ cit ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ná ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The mighty (Indra) is resplendent (through the sacrifice), the joy of the worshipper is resplendent;vigorous are the two horses of you rapidly approaching, whose hymn is unassailable (by therākṣasas); (this)sacrifice is apart, not human.”

shlokas.sanskrit: कृ॒धी नो॒ अह्र॑यो देव सवित॒: स च॑ स्तुषे म॒घोना॑म् । स॒हो न॒ इन्द्रो॒ वह्नि॑भि॒र्न्ये॑षां चर्षणी॒नां च॒क्रं र॒श्मिं न यो॑युवे
shlokas.transliteration: kṛdhí ǀ naḥ ǀ áhrayaḥ ǀ deva ǀ savitaríti ǀ sáḥ ǀ ca ǀ stuṣe ǀ maghónām ǀsahó íti ǀ naḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ váhni-bhiḥ ǀ ní ǀ eṣām ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀ cakrám ǀ raśmím ǀ ná ǀ yoyuve ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Make us, divineSavitā, free from shame; you are praised (by the priests) of the opulent; mayIndra,accompanied by the bearers (of water), unite the strength of us men here, like the chariot-wheel and reinṣ”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऐषु॑ द्यावापृथिवी धातं म॒हद॒स्मे वी॒रेषु॑ वि॒श्वच॑र्षणि॒ श्रव॑: । पृ॒क्षं वाज॑स्य सा॒तये॑ पृ॒क्षं रा॒योत तु॒र्वणे॑
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ eṣu ǀ dyāvāpṛthivī íti ǀ dhātam ǀ mahát ǀ asmé íti ǀ vīréṣu ǀ viśvá-carṣaṇi ǀ śrávaḥ ǀpṛkṣám ǀ vā́jasya ǀ sātáye ǀ pṛkṣám ǀ rāyā́ ǀ utá ǀ turváṇe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Heaven and earth, grant to these our sons great renown, extending over all mankind; grantsustenance for the acquisition of strength, sustenance together with wealth for the overthrow (of enemies).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒तं शंस॑मिन्द्रास्म॒युष्ट्वं कूचि॒त्सन्तं॑ सहसावन्न॒भिष्ट॑ये । सदा॑ पाह्य॒भिष्ट॑ये मे॒दतां॑ वे॒दता॑ वसो
shlokas.transliteration: etám ǀ śáṃsam ǀ indra ǀ asma-yúḥ ǀ tvám ǀ kū́-cit ǀ sántam ǀ sahasā-van ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀ sádā ǀ pāhi ǀ abhíṣṭaye ǀmedátām ǀ vedátā ǀ vaso íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MightyIndra, do you, who are well affected towards us, ever protect this worshipper wherever he maybe, so that he may attain his desire; instrumental uct me,Vasu, by your wisdom.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒तं मे॒ स्तोमं॑ त॒ना न सूर्ये॑ द्यु॒तद्या॑मानं वावृधन्त नृ॒णाम् । सं॒वन॑नं॒ नाश्व्यं॒ तष्टे॒वान॑पच्युतम्
shlokas.transliteration: etám ǀ me ǀ stómam ǀ tanā́ ǀ ná ǀ sū́rye ǀ dyutát-yāmānam ǀ vavṛdhanta ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀsam-vánanam ǀ ná ǀ áśvyam ǀ táṣṭā-iva ǀ ánapa-cyutam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May (the priests) strengthen this my hymn, the destroyer of the enemies (of the gods), of brilliant pathlike, the rays in the sun, as the carpenter (sends forth) the upright car.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वा॒वर्त॒ येषां॑ रा॒या यु॒क्तैषां॑ हिर॒ण्ययी॑ । ने॒मधि॑ता॒ न पौंस्या॒ वृथे॑व वि॒ष्टान्ता॑
shlokas.transliteration: vavárta ǀ yéṣām ǀ rāyā́ ǀ yuktā́ ǀ eṣām ǀ hiraṇyáyī ǀnemá-dhitā ǀ ná ǀ páuṃsyā ǀ vṛ́thā-iva ǀ viṣṭá-antā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Those whose (praise) arrives, accompanied by wealth, of them it is (as) a golden (ornament), likemanly powers in battle reaching the conclusion as it were, without an effort.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र तद्दु॒:शीमे॒ पृथ॑वाने वे॒ने प्र रा॒मे वो॑च॒मसु॑रे म॒घव॑त्सु । ये यु॒क्त्वाय॒ पञ्च॑ श॒तास्म॒यु प॒था वि॒श्राव्ये॑षाम्
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ tát ǀ duḥ-śī́me ǀ pṛ́thavāne ǀ vené ǀ prá ǀ rāmé ǀ vocam ǀ ásure ǀ maghávat-su ǀyé ǀ yuktvā́ya ǀ páñca ǀ śatā́ ǀ asma-yú ǀ pathā́ ǀ vi-śrā́vi ǀ eṣām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “This I proclaim in the presence of Duśīma, Pṛthavāna,Vena, the mightyRāma, and (other)opulent (princes); those who (come), having yoked five hundred (chariots), their affection for us is renowned onthe road.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अधीन्न्वत्र॑ सप्त॒तिं च॑ स॒प्त च॑ । स॒द्यो दि॑दिष्ट॒ तान्व॑: स॒द्यो दि॑दिष्ट पा॒र्थ्यः स॒द्यो दि॑दिष्ट माय॒वः
shlokas.transliteration: ádhi ǀ ít ǀ nú ǀ átra ǀ saptatím ǀ ca ǀ saptá ǀ ca ǀsadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ tā́nvaḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ pārthyáḥ ǀ sadyáḥ ǀ didiṣṭa ǀ māyaváḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Strongest of themTānvapromptly demanded seven and seventy (cows), Pārthya demandedall three names may refer to the same person n].”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रैते व॑दन्तु॒ प्र व॒यं व॑दाम॒ ग्राव॑भ्यो॒ वाचं॑ वदता॒ वद॑द्भ्यः । यद॑द्रयः पर्वताः सा॒कमा॒शव॒: श्लोकं॒ घोषं॒ भर॒थेन्द्रा॑य सो॒मिन॑:
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ eté ǀ vadantu ǀ prá ǀ vayám ǀ vadāma ǀ grā́va-bhyaḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ vadata ǀ vádat-bhyaḥ ǀyát ǀ adrayaḥ ǀ parvatāḥ ǀ sākám ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ ślókam ǀ ghóṣam ǀ bháratha ǀ índrāya ǀ somínaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let these (stones) speak; let us reply to the speaking stones, and do you (priests) utter (praise); when,you solid, quick-moving stones, you utter the noise of praise together toIndra, (then you become) full of theSoma.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒ते व॑दन्ति श॒तव॑त्स॒हस्र॑वद॒भि क्र॑न्दन्ति॒ हरि॑तेभिरा॒सभि॑: । वि॒ष्ट्वी ग्रावा॑णः सु॒कृत॑: सुकृ॒त्यया॒ होतु॑श्चि॒त्पूर्वे॑ हवि॒रद्य॑माशत
shlokas.transliteration: eté ǀ vadanti ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásra-vat ǀ abhí ǀ krandanti ǀ háritebhiḥ ǀ āsá-bhiḥ ǀviṣṭvī́ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ su-kṛ́taḥ ǀ su-kṛtyáyā ǀ hótuḥ ǀ cit ǀ pū́rve ǀ haviḥ-ádyam ǀ āśata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They roar like a hundred, like a thousand (men); they cry aloud with green-tinted faces; obtaining thesacrifice, the pious stones through their piety partake of the sacrificial food, even before (Agni), the invoker (ofthe gods).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒ते व॑द॒न्त्यवि॑दन्न॒ना मधु॒ न्यू॑ङ्खयन्ते॒ अधि॑ प॒क्व आमि॑षि । वृ॒क्षस्य॒ शाखा॑मरु॒णस्य॒ बप्स॑त॒स्ते सूभ॑र्वा वृष॒भाः प्रेम॑राविषुः
shlokas.transliteration: eté ǀ vadanti ǀ ávidan ǀ anā́ ǀ mádhu ǀ ní ǀ ūṅkhayante ǀ ádhi ǀ pakvé ǀ ā́miṣi ǀvṛkṣásya ǀ śā́khām ǀ aruṇásya ǀ bápsataḥ ǀ té ǀ sū́bharvāḥ ǀ vṛṣabhā́ḥ ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ arāviṣuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They speak, they received into their mouth the sweet (Soma), they roar (like the eaters of flesh) overthe roasted meat; chewing the branch of the purplle tree, the voracious bulls have bellowed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृ॒हद्व॑दन्ति मदि॒रेण॑ म॒न्दिनेन्द्रं॒ क्रोश॑न्तोऽविदन्न॒ना मधु॑ । सं॒रभ्या॒ धीरा॒: स्वसृ॑भिरनर्तिषुराघो॒षय॑न्तः पृथि॒वीमु॑प॒ब्दिभि॑:
shlokas.transliteration: bṛhát ǀ vadanti ǀ madiréṇa ǀ mandínā ǀ índram ǀ króśantaḥ ǀ avidan ǀ anā́ ǀ mádhu ǀsam-rábhya ǀ dhī́rāḥ ǀ svásṛ-bhiḥ ǀ anartiṣuḥ ǀ ā-ghoṣáyantaḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ upabdí-bhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “They cry aloud calling uponIndrawith the intoxicating effused (Soma), they took the sweet Soma intotheir mouth, seized by the sister (fingers) the bold stones danced, filling the earth with shouts.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒प॒र्णा वाच॑मक्र॒तोप॒ द्यव्या॑ख॒रे कृष्णा॑ इषि॒रा अ॑नर्तिषुः । न्य१॒॑ङ्नि य॒न्त्युप॑रस्य निष्कृ॒तं पु॒रू रेतो॑ दधिरे सूर्य॒श्वित॑:
shlokas.transliteration: su-parṇā́ḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ akrata ǀ úpa ǀ dyávi ǀ ā-kharé ǀ kṛ́ṣṇāḥ ǀ iṣirā́ḥ ǀ anartiṣuḥ ǀnyák ǀ ní ǀ yanti ǀ úparasya ǀ niḥ-kṛtám ǀ purú ǀ rétaḥ ǀ dadhire ǀ sūrya-śvítaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The well-gliding stones made a noise in the firmament; they danced (like) the black deer in the stall;they exude down from the upper stone the expressed (Soma); white as the sun they yield abundant moisture.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒ग्रा इ॑व प्र॒वह॑न्तः स॒माय॑मुः सा॒कं यु॒क्ता वृष॑णो॒ बिभ्र॑तो॒ धुर॑: । यच्छ्व॒सन्तो॑ जग्रसा॒ना अरा॑विषुः शृ॒ण्व ए॑षां प्रो॒थथो॒ अर्व॑तामिव
shlokas.transliteration: ugrā́ḥ-iva ǀ pra-váhantaḥ ǀ sam-ā́yamuḥ ǀ sākám ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇaḥ ǀ bíbhrataḥ ǀ dhúraḥ ǀyát ǀ śvasántaḥ ǀ jagrasānā́ḥ ǀ árāviṣuḥ ǀ śṛṇvé ǀ eṣām ǀ protháthaḥ ǀ árvatām-iva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bearing the burden of the sacrifice, yoked with (theSoma), they extend themselves like spiritedhorses; when panting and extracting (the Soma), they cried aloud, their snoring is heard like that of horses.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दशा॑वनिभ्यो॒ दश॑कक्ष्येभ्यो॒ दश॑योक्त्रेभ्यो॒ दश॑योजनेभ्यः । दशा॑भीशुभ्यो अर्चता॒जरे॑भ्यो॒ दश॒ धुरो॒ दश॑ यु॒क्ता वह॑द्भ्यः
shlokas.transliteration: dáśāvani-bhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-kakṣyebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-yoktrebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa-yojanebhyaḥ ǀdáśābhīśu-bhyaḥ ǀ arcata ǀ ajárebhyaḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ dhúraḥ ǀ dáśa ǀ yuktā́ḥ ǀ váhat-bhyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Worship (priests), those imperishable (stones) which have ten workers, ten girths, ten yokes, tenagents, ten encompassers, which are possessed of ten burdens, which bear (the sacrifice).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते अद्र॑यो॒ दश॑यन्त्रास आ॒शव॒स्तेषा॑मा॒धानं॒ पर्ये॑ति हर्य॒तम् । त ऊ॑ सु॒तस्य॑ सो॒म्यस्यान्ध॑सों॒ऽशोः पी॒यूषं॑ प्रथ॒मस्य॑ भेजिरे
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ dáśa-yantrāsaḥ ǀ āśávaḥ ǀ téṣām ǀ ā-dhā́nam ǀ pári ǀ eti ǀ haryatám ǀté ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ sutásya ǀ somyásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǀ aṃśóḥ ǀ pīyū́ṣam ǀ prathamásya ǀ bhejire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These stones, having ten reins, swiftly moving, their delightful whirling goes round; they first tasted theambrosia of the fragment of food of the expressedSoma.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ते सो॒मादो॒ हरी॒ इन्द्र॑स्य निंसतें॒ऽशुं दु॒हन्तो॒ अध्या॑सते॒ गवि॑ । तेभि॑र्दु॒ग्धं प॑पि॒वान्त्सो॒म्यं मध्विन्द्रो॑ वर्धते॒ प्रथ॑ते वृषा॒यते॑
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ soma-ádaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ índrasya ǀ niṃsate ǀ aṃśúm ǀ duhántaḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ āsate ǀ gávi ǀtébhiḥ ǀ dugdhám ǀ papi-vā́n ǀ somyám ǀ mádhu ǀ índraḥ ǀ vardhate ǀ práthate ǀ vṛṣa-yáte ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These devourers ofSomakissIndra's horses, milking forth the juice they repose upon the cow, Indrahaving quaffed the sweet Soma milked forth by them increases, waxes broad, grows vigour.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वृषा॑ वो अं॒शुर्न किला॑ रिषाथ॒नेळा॑वन्त॒: सद॒मित्स्थ॒नाशि॑ताः । रै॒व॒त्येव॒ मह॑सा॒ चार॑वः स्थन॒ यस्य॑ ग्रावाणो॒ अजु॑षध्वमध्व॒रम्
shlokas.transliteration: vṛ́ṣā ǀ vaḥ ǀ aṃśúḥ ǀ ná ǀ kíla ǀ riṣāthana ǀ íḷā-vantaḥ ǀ sádam ǀ ít ǀ sthana ǀ ā́śitāḥ ǀraivatyā́-iva ǀ máhasā ǀ cā́ravaḥ ǀ sthana ǀ yásya ǀ grāvāṇaḥ ǀ ájuṣadhvam ǀ adhvarám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheSomais your showerer (at the sacrifice); you are unharmed, (like those) abounding in food, youare constantly feeding; like the wealthy (possessed) of splendour, you, O stones, are beautiful (at the sacrifice ofhim) whose sacrifice you delighted in.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तृ॒दि॒ला अतृ॑दिलासो॒ अद्र॑योऽश्रम॒णा अशृ॑थिता॒ अमृ॑त्यवः । अ॒ना॒तु॒रा अ॒जरा॒: स्थाम॑विष्णवः सुपी॒वसो॒ अतृ॑षिता॒ अतृ॑ष्णजः
shlokas.transliteration: tṛdilā́ḥ ǀ átṛdilāsaḥ ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ aśramaṇā́ḥ ǀ áśṛthitāḥ ǀ ámṛtyavaḥ ǀanāturā́ḥ ǀ ajárāḥ ǀ stha ǀ ámaviṣṇavaḥ ǀ su-pīvásaḥ ǀ átṛṣitāḥ ǀ átṛṣṇa-jaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Splitting, but unsplit, you, O stones, are untiring, unrelaxing, immortal, free from disease, undecaying,rising and falling, powerful, unthirsting, not genitive rating thirst.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ध्रु॒वा ए॒व व॑: पि॒तरो॑ यु॒गेयु॑गे॒ क्षेम॑कामास॒: सद॑सो॒ न यु॑ञ्जते । अ॒जु॒र्यासो॑ हरि॒षाचो॑ ह॒रिद्र॑व॒ आ द्यां रवे॑ण पृथि॒वीम॑शुश्रवुः
shlokas.transliteration: dhruvā́ḥ ǀ evá ǀ vaḥ ǀ pitáraḥ ǀ yugé-yuge ǀ kṣéma-kāmāsaḥ ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yuñjate ǀajuryā́saḥ ǀ hari-sā́caḥ ǀ harídravaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ dyā́m ǀ ráveṇa ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ aśuśravuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Your progenitors (the mountains), stable from age to age, desirous of repose, seek not to mix with(religious) assemblies; exempt from decay, enjoying theSoma, flowing green (with Soma), they made heavenand earth resound with their clamour.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तदिद्व॑द॒न्त्यद्र॑यो वि॒मोच॑ने॒ याम॑न्नञ्ज॒स्पा इ॑व॒ घेदु॑प॒ब्दिभि॑: । वप॑न्तो॒ बीज॑मिव धान्या॒कृत॑: पृ॒ञ्चन्ति॒ सोमं॒ न मि॑नन्ति॒ बप्स॑तः
shlokas.transliteration: tát ǀ ít ǀ vadanti ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ vi-mócane ǀ yā́man ǀ añjaḥpā́ḥ-iva ǀ gha ǀ ít ǀ upabdí-bhiḥ ǀvápantaḥ ǀ bī́jam-iva ǀ dhānya-kṛ́taḥ ǀ pṛñcánti ǀ sómam ǀ ná ǀ minanti ǀ bápsataḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The stones proclaim it with their clamour at the issue of theSoma, like the quick-protecting (chariots)on the road; like cultivators sowing the seed, they, devouring the Soma, mix it, and do not hurt it.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒ते अ॑ध्व॒रे अधि॒ वाच॑मक्र॒ता क्री॒ळयो॒ न मा॒तर॑ु तु॒दन्त॑: । वि षू मु॑ञ्चा सुषु॒वुषो॑ मनी॒षां वि व॑र्तन्ता॒मद्र॑य॒श्चाय॑मानाः
shlokas.transliteration: suté ǀ adhvaré ǀ ádhi ǀ vā́cam ǀ akrata ǀ ā́ ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ mātáram ǀ tudántaḥ ǀví ǀ sú ǀ muñca ǀ susu-vúṣaḥ ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ ví ǀ vartantām ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ cā́yamānāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(TheSoma) being effused at the sacrifice, they made a noise like (children) at plural y, striking theirmother. Proclaim the praise of (the stone), which has effused (the Soma), let the honoured stones revolve.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ह॒ये जाये॒ मन॑सा॒ तिष्ठ॑ घोरे॒ वचां॑सि मि॒श्रा कृ॑णवावहै॒ नु । न नौ॒ मन्त्रा॒ अनु॑दितास ए॒ते मय॑स्कर॒न्पर॑तरे च॒नाह॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: hayé ǀ jā́ye ǀ mánasā ǀ tíṣṭha ǀ ghore ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ miśrā́ ǀ kṛṇavāvahai ǀ nú ǀná ǀ nau ǀ mántrāḥ ǀ ánuditāsaḥ ǀ eté ǀ máyaḥ ǀ karan ǀ pára-tare ǀ caná ǀ áhan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā) speaks). How indignant wife, with mind (relenting), stay awhile, let us now interchangediscourse. These, our secret thoughts, while unspoken, did not yield us happiness even at the last day.”

shlokas.sanskrit: किमे॒ता वा॒चा कृ॑णवा॒ तवा॒हं प्राक्र॑मिषमु॒षसा॑मग्रि॒येव॑ । पुरू॑रव॒: पुन॒रस्तं॒ परे॑हि दुराप॒ना वात॑ इवा॒हम॑स्मि
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ etā́ ǀ vācā́ ǀ kṛṇava ǀ táva ǀ ahám ǀ prá ǀ akramiṣam ǀ uṣásām ǀ agriyā́-iva ǀpúrūravaḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ ástam ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ duḥ-āpanā́ ǀ vā́taḥ-iva ǀ ahám ǀ asmi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī. What can we accomplish through such discourse? I have passed away from you like thefirst of the dawns. ReturnPurūravā, to your dwelling; I am as hard to catch as the wind.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इषु॒र्न श्रि॒य इ॑षु॒धेर॑स॒ना गो॒षाः श॑त॒सा न रंहि॑: । अ॒वीरे॒ क्रतौ॒ वि द॑विद्युत॒न्नोरा॒ न मा॒युं चि॑तयन्त॒ धुन॑यः
shlokas.transliteration: íṣuḥ ǀ ná ǀ śriyé ǀ iṣu-dhéḥ ǀ asanā́ ǀ go-sā́ḥ ǀ śata-sā́ḥ ǀ ná ǀ ráṃhiḥ ǀavī́re ǀ krátau ǀ ví ǀ davidyutat ǀ ná ǀ úrā ǀ ná ǀ māyúm ǀ citayanta ǀ dhúnayaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). The arrow is not to be cast from the quiver for glory. I am no longer the impetuousdespoiler of the cattle (of the enemy), nor of their hundred-fold (riches). My prowess having lost its strength, (mymight) no longer flashes forth; (my warriors) the terrifiers (of the foe) hear not my shout in battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सा वसु॒ दध॑ती॒ श्वशु॑राय॒ वय॒ उषो॒ यदि॒ वष्ट्यन्ति॑गृहात् । अस्तं॑ ननक्षे॒ यस्मि॑ञ्चा॒कन्दिवा॒ नक्तं॑ श्नथि॒ता वै॑त॒सेन॑
shlokas.transliteration: sā́ ǀ vásu ǀ dádhatī ǀ śváśurāya ǀ váyaḥ ǀ úṣaḥ ǀ yádi ǀ váṣṭi ǀ ánti-gṛhāt ǀástam ǀ nanakṣe ǀ yásmin ǀ cākán ǀ dívā ǀ náktam ǀ śnathitā́ ǀ vaitaséna ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśi). If, Uṣas, thisŪrvaśī, offering food and wealth to her father-in-law, loves (her husband),she has gone from the neighbouring house to her husband's home, where she loved (her lord), being delightednight and day by his embraces.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्रिः स्म॒ माह्न॑: श्नथयो वैत॒सेनो॒त स्म॒ मेऽव्य॑त्यै पृणासि । पुरू॑र॒वोऽनु॑ ते॒ केत॑मायं॒ राजा॑ मे वीर त॒न्व१॒॑स्तदा॑सीः
shlokas.transliteration: tríḥ ǀ sma ǀ mā ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ śnathayaḥ ǀ vaitaséna ǀ utá ǀ sma ǀ me ǀ ávyatyai ǀ pṛṇāsi ǀpúrūravaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ te ǀ kétam ǀ āyam ǀ rā́jā ǀ me ǀ vīra ǀ tanváḥ ǀ tát ǀ āsīḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Thrice a day,Purūravā, have you embraced me, you have loved me without a rival; I have followed(you) to your dwelling, you, hero, have been the sovereign of my person n.”

shlokas.sanskrit: या सु॑जू॒र्णिः श्रेणि॑: सु॒म्नआ॑पिर्ह्र॒देच॑क्षु॒र्न ग्र॒न्थिनी॑ चर॒ण्युः । ता अ॒ञ्जयो॑ऽरु॒णयो॒ न स॑स्रुः श्रि॒ये गावो॒ न धे॒नवो॑ऽनवन्त
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ ǀ su-jūrṇíḥ ǀ śréṇiḥ ǀ sumné-āpiḥ ǀ hradé-cakṣuḥ ǀ ná ǀ granthínī ǀ caraṇyúḥ ǀtā́ḥ ǀ añjáyaḥ ǀ aruṇáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ sasruḥ ǀ śriyé ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ anavanta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). Sujūraṇi,Śreṇi, Sumna-āpi, Hradecakṣus, Granthinī, and the swift-moving(Ūrvaśiwho arrived) they, decorated and purple-tinted, did not go first, they lowed like kine for protection.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सम॑स्मि॒ञ्जाय॑मान आसत॒ ग्ना उ॒तेम॑वर्धन्न॒द्य१॒॑: स्वगू॑र्ताः । म॒हे यत्त्वा॑ पुरूरवो॒ रणा॒याव॑र्धयन्दस्यु॒हत्या॑य दे॒वाः
shlokas.transliteration: sám ǀ asmin ǀ jā́yamāne ǀ āsata ǀ gnā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀ īm ǀ avardhan ǀ nadyáḥ ǀ svá-gūrtāḥ ǀmahé ǀ yát ǀ tvā ǀ purūravaḥ ǀ ráṇāya ǀ ávardhayan ǀ dasyu-hátyāya ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī). As soon as he was born the wives (of the gods) surrounded him, the spontaneouslyflowing rivers nourished him, for the gods reared you,Purūravā, for a mighty conflict, for the slaughter of theDasyus. (Nirukta, 3.47).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सचा॒ यदा॑सु॒ जह॑ती॒ष्वत्क॒ममा॑नुषीषु॒ मानु॑षो नि॒षेवे॑ । अप॑ स्म॒ मत्त॒रस॑न्ती॒ न भु॒ज्युस्ता अ॑त्रसन्रथ॒स्पृशो॒ नाश्वा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sácā ǀ yát ǀ āsu ǀ jáhatīṣu ǀ átkam ǀ ámānuṣīṣu ǀ mā́nuṣaḥ ǀ ni-séve ǀápa ǀ sma ǀ mát ǀ tarásantī ǀ ná ǀ bhujyúḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ atrasan ǀ ratha-spṛ́śaḥ ǀ ná ǀ áśvāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). When, becoming their companion, (Purūravā) the mortal associated with theseimmortal (nymphs) who had abandoned their bodies, they fled from me like a timid doe, like horses harnessed toa chariot.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यदा॑सु॒ मर्तो॑ अ॒मृता॑सु नि॒स्पृक्सं क्षो॒णीभि॒: क्रतु॑भि॒र्न पृ॒ङ्क्ते । ता आ॒तयो॒ न त॒न्व॑: शुम्भत॒ स्वा अश्वा॑सो॒ न क्री॒ळयो॒ दन्द॑शानाः
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ āsu ǀ mártaḥ ǀ amṛ́tāsu ǀ ni-spṛ́k ǀ sám ǀ kṣoṇī́bhiḥ ǀ krátu-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ pṛṅkté ǀtā́ḥ ǀ ātáyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śumbhata ǀ svā́ḥ ǀ áśvāsaḥ ǀ ná ǀ krīḷáyaḥ ǀ dándaśānāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When a mortal mixing with these immortal nymphs has conversed with them with words and actions,they (becoming) ducks do not show their bodies, like plural yful horses champing (the bit).”

shlokas.sanskrit: वि॒द्युन्न या पत॑न्ती॒ दवि॑द्यो॒द्भर॑न्ती मे॒ अप्या॒ काम्या॑नि । जनि॑ष्टो अ॒पो नर्य॒: सुजा॑त॒: प्रोर्वशी॑ तिरत दी॒र्घमायु॑:
shlokas.transliteration: vi-dyút ǀ ná ǀ yā́ ǀ pátantī ǀ dávidyot ǀ bhárantī ǀ me ǀ ápyā ǀ kā́myāni ǀjániṣṭo íti ǀ apáḥ ǀ náryaḥ ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ prá ǀ urváśī ǀ tirata ǀ dīrghám ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī) who shone like flashing lightning, bringing me the desirable dews (of heaven, hasappeared); a son able in act and friendly to man has been born; Ūrvaśī has prolonged my lengthenedexistence.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ज॒ज्ञि॒ष इ॒त्था गो॒पीथ्या॑य॒ हि द॒धाथ॒ तत्पु॑रूरवो म॒ ओज॑: । अशा॑सं त्वा वि॒दुषी॒ सस्मि॒न्नह॒न्न म॒ आशृ॑णो॒: किम॒भुग्व॑दासि
shlokas.transliteration: jajñiṣé ǀ itthā́ ǀ go-pī́thyāya ǀ hí ǀ dadhā́tha ǀ tát ǀ purūravaḥ ǀ me ǀ ójaḥ ǀáśāsam ǀ tvā ǀ vidúṣī ǀ sásmin ǀ áhan ǀ ná ǀ me ǀ ā́ ǀ aśṛṇoḥ ǀ kím ǀ abhúk ǀ vadāsi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī). you have been born thus to protect the earth; you have deposited this vigour in me;knowing (the future) I have instrumental ucted you (what to do) every day; you have not listened to me; why do you nowaddress me, neglectful (of my instrumental uction)?”

shlokas.sanskrit: क॒दा सू॒नुः पि॒तरं॑ जा॒त इ॑च्छाच्च॒क्रन्नाश्रु॑ वर्तयद्विजा॒नन् । को दम्प॑ती॒ सम॑नसा॒ वि यू॑यो॒दध॒ यद॒ग्निः श्वशु॑रेषु॒ दीद॑यत्
shlokas.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ sūnúḥ ǀ pitáram ǀ jātáḥ ǀ icchāt ǀ cakrán ǀ ná ǀ áśru ǀ vartayat ǀ vi-jānán ǀkáḥ ǀ dámpatī íti dám-patī ǀ sá-manasā ǀ ví ǀ yūyot ǀ ádha ǀ yát ǀ agníḥ ǀ śváśureṣu ǀ dī́dayat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). When shall a son (born of you) claim me as a father, and crying, shed a tear onrecognizing (me)? What son shall sever husband and wife who are of one mind, now that the fire shines uponyour husband's parents?”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रति॑ ब्रवाणि व॒र्तय॑ते॒ अश्रु॑ च॒क्रन्न क्र॑न्ददा॒ध्ये॑ शि॒वायै॑ । प्र तत्ते॑ हिनवा॒ यत्ते॑ अ॒स्मे परे॒ह्यस्तं॑ न॒हि मू॑र॒ माप॑:
shlokas.transliteration: práti ǀ bravāṇi ǀ vartáyate ǀ áśru ǀ cakrán ǀ ná ǀ krandat ǀ ā-dhyé ǀ śivā́yai ǀprá ǀ tát ǀ te ǀ hinava ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ asmé íti ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀ ástam ǀ nahí ǀ mūra ǀ mā ǀ ā́paḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī). Let me reply. (Your son) will shed tears, crying out and calling aloud when the expectedauspicious time arrives; I will send you that (child) which is yours in me, depart to your house, you cannot,simpleton, detain me.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सु॒दे॒वो अ॒द्य प्र॒पते॒दना॑वृत्परा॒वतं॑ पर॒मां गन्त॒वा उ॑ । अधा॒ शयी॑त॒ निॠ॑तेरु॒पस्थेऽधै॑नं॒ वृका॑ रभ॒सासो॑ अ॒द्युः
shlokas.transliteration: su-deváḥ ǀ adyá ǀ pra-pátet ǀ ánāvṛt ǀ parā-vátam ǀ paramā́m ǀ gántavái ǀ ūṃ íti ǀádha ǀ śáyīta ǀ níḥ-ṛteḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ ádha ǀ enam ǀ vṛ́kāḥ ǀ rabhasā́saḥ ǀ adyúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). (Your husband) who sports with you may now depart, never to return, (depart) toproceed to a distant region. Either let him sleep upon the lap ofNirṛti, or let the swift-moving wolves devour hiṃ”

shlokas.sanskrit: पुरू॑रवो॒ मा मृ॑था॒ मा प्र प॑प्तो॒ मा त्वा॒ वृका॑सो॒ अशि॑वास उ क्षन् । न वै स्त्रैणा॑नि स॒ख्यानि॑ सन्ति सालावृ॒काणां॒ हृद॑यान्ये॒ता
shlokas.transliteration: púrūravaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ mṛthāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ prá ǀ paptaḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ tvā ǀ vṛ́kāsaḥ ǀ áśivāsaḥ ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ kṣan ǀná ǀ vái ǀ stráiṇāni ǀ sakhyā́ni ǀ santi ǀ sālāvṛkā́ṇām ǀ hṛ́dayāni ǀ etā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśi). Die not,Purūravā, fall not, let not the hideous wolves devour you. feminine le friendships donot exist, their hearts are the hearts of jackals.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्विरू॒पाच॑रं॒ मर्त्ये॒ष्वव॑सं॒ रात्री॑: श॒रद॒श्चत॑स्रः । घृ॒तस्य॑ स्तो॒कं स॒कृदह्न॑ आश्नां॒ तादे॒वेदं ता॑तृपा॒णा च॑रामि
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ ví-rūpā ǀ ácaram ǀ mártyeṣu ǀ ávasam ǀ rā́trīḥ ǀ śarádaḥ ǀ cátasraḥ ǀghṛtásya ǀ stokám ǀ sakṛ́t ǀ áhnaḥ ǀ āśnām ǀ tā́t ǀ evá ǀ idám ǀ tatṛpāṇā́ ǀ carāmi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When changed in form I wandered among mortals. I dwelt (with them) four delightful years. I ate oncea day a small quantity of butter; satisfied with that I now depart.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒न्त॒रि॒क्ष॒प्रां रज॑सो वि॒मानी॒मुप॑ शिक्षाम्यु॒र्वशीं॒ वसि॑ष्ठः । उप॑ त्वा रा॒तिः सु॑कृ॒तस्य॒ तिष्ठा॒न्नि व॑र्तस्व॒ हृद॑यं तप्यते मे
shlokas.transliteration: antarikṣa-prā́m ǀ rájasaḥ ǀ vi-mā́nīm ǀ úpa ǀ śikṣāmi ǀ urváśīm ǀ vásiṣṭhaḥ ǀúpa ǀ tvā ǀ rātíḥ ǀ su-kṛtásya ǀ tíṣṭhāt ǀ ní ǀ vartasva ǀ hṛ́dayam ǀ tapyate ǀ me ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Purūravā). I,Vasiṣṭha, bring under subjectionŪrvaśīwho fills the firmament (with lustre) andmeasures out the rain. May (Purūravā), the bestower of the auspicious rite, abide near you; come back-- myheart is burning.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इति॑ त्वा दे॒वा इ॒म आ॑हुरैळ॒ यथे॑मे॒तद्भव॑सि मृ॒त्युब॑न्धुः । प्र॒जा ते॑ दे॒वान्ह॒विषा॑ यजाति स्व॒र्ग उ॒ त्वमपि॑ मादयासे
shlokas.transliteration: íti ǀ tvā ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ imé ǀ āhuḥ ǀ aiḷa ǀ yáthā ǀ īm ǀ etát ǀ bhávasi ǀ mṛtyú-bandhuḥ ǀpra-jā́ ǀ te ǀ devā́n ǀ havíṣā ǀ yajāti ǀ svaḥ-gé ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ tvám ǀ ápi ǀ mādayāse ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Ūrvaśī). These gods said to you, Aiḷa, since you are indeed subject to death, let your progenypropitiate your gods with oblations, you shall rejoice (with me) in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र ते॑ म॒हे वि॒दथे॑ शंसिषं॒ हरी॒ प्र ते॑ वन्वे व॒नुषो॑ हर्य॒तं मद॑म् । घृ॒तं न यो हरि॑भि॒श्चारु॒ सेच॑त॒ आ त्वा॑ विशन्तु॒ हरि॑वर्पसं॒ गिर॑:
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ mahé ǀ vidáthe ǀ śaṃsiṣam ǀ hárī íti ǀ prá ǀ te ǀ vanve ǀ vanúṣaḥ ǀ haryatám ǀ mádam ǀghṛtám ǀ ná ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ cā́ru ǀ sécate ǀ ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ viśantu ǀ hári-varpasam ǀ gíraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I glorified your bay horses,Indra, at the great sacrifice. I solicit the agreeable exhilaration of you, thedestroyer. May my praises attain to you, whose form is yellow, who, with your horses, shower (water) likebeautiful butter.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हरिं॒ हि योनि॑म॒भि ये स॒मस्व॑रन्हि॒न्वन्तो॒ हरी॑ दि॒व्यं यथा॒ सद॑: । आ यं पृ॒णन्ति॒ हरि॑भि॒र्न धे॒नव॒ इन्द्रा॑य शू॒षं हरि॑वन्तमर्चत
shlokas.transliteration: hárim ǀ hí ǀ yónim ǀ abhí ǀ yé ǀ sam-ásvaran ǀ hinvántaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ divyám ǀ yáthā ǀ sádaḥ ǀā́ ǀ yám ǀ pṛṇánti ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ ná ǀ dhenávaḥ ǀ índrāya ǀ śūṣám ǀ hári-vantam ǀ arcata ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You, who have praised the horse, the seat ofIndra, urging the horses so that (Indra may reach) thedivine assembly, do you worship the horse- possessing might of Indra, whom men delight with the golden-tintedSoma as kine (with their milk).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सो अ॑स्य॒ वज्रो॒ हरि॑तो॒ य आ॑य॒सो हरि॒र्निका॑मो॒ हरि॒रा गभ॑स्त्योः । द्यु॒म्नी सु॑शि॒प्रो हरि॑मन्युसायक॒ इन्द्रे॒ नि रू॒पा हरि॑ता मिमिक्षिरे
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ asya ǀ vájraḥ ǀ háritaḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ háriḥ ǀ ní-kāmaḥ ǀ háriḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gábhastyoḥ ǀdyumnī́ ǀ su-śipráḥ ǀ hárimanyu-sāyakaḥ ǀ índre ǀ ní ǀ rūpā́ ǀ háritā ǀ mimikṣire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “That is his thunderbolt, yellow, made of iron, the destroyer (of foes), desirable, the destroyer (of foes),it is in hishands; he is) possessed of riches, handsome jawed, possessed of a shaft and anger which deestroys(his foes)-- many golden-tinted forms are mixed inIndra.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दि॒वि न के॒तुरधि॑ धायि हर्य॒तो वि॒व्यच॒द्वज्रो॒ हरि॑तो॒ न रंह्या॑ । तु॒ददहिं॒ हरि॑शिप्रो॒ य आ॑य॒सः स॒हस्र॑शोका अभवद्धरिम्भ॒रः
shlokas.transliteration: diví ǀ ná ǀ ketúḥ ǀ ádhi ǀ dhāyi ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ vivyácat ǀ vájraḥ ǀ háritaḥ ǀ ná ǀ ráṃhyā ǀtudát ǀ áhim ǀ hári-śipraḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ sahásra-śokāḥ ǀ abhavat ǀ harim-bharáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He has been plural ced (by his worshippers) in the sky, like the banner (of light, the sun). His desirablebolt reaches (the foe) as the bay horses (of the sun reach their aim) through speed. The iron (thunderbolt), withyellow jaws, which smote Ahi, (he,Indra), lord of horses, shone with a thousand lustres.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वंत्व॑महर्यथा॒ उप॑स्तुत॒: पूर्वे॑भिरिन्द्र हरिकेश॒ यज्व॑भिः । त्वं ह॑र्यसि॒ तव॒ विश्व॑मु॒क्थ्य१॒॑मसा॑मि॒ राधो॑ हरिजात हर्य॒तम्
shlokas.transliteration: tvám-tvam ǀ aharyathāḥ ǀ úpa-stutaḥ ǀ pū́rvebhiḥ ǀ indra ǀ hari-keśa ǀ yájva-bhiḥ ǀtvám ǀ haryasi ǀ táva ǀ víśvam ǀ ukthyám ǀ ásāmi ǀ rā́dhaḥ ǀ hari-jāta ǀ haryatám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, with yellow locks, when praised by ancient worshippers, you did desire the oblation; you whoare manifested of a golden hue desire your universal praise, your peculiar and delightful (sacrificial) food.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ता व॒ज्रिणं॑ म॒न्दिनं॒ स्तोम्यं॒ मद॒ इन्द्रं॒ रथे॑ वहतो हर्य॒ता हरी॑ । पु॒रूण्य॑स्मै॒ सव॑नानि॒ हर्य॑त॒ इन्द्रा॑य॒ सोमा॒ हर॑यो दधन्विरे
shlokas.transliteration: tā́ ǀ vajríṇam ǀ mandínam ǀ stómyam ǀ máde ǀ índram ǀ ráthe ǀ vahataḥ ǀ haryatā́ ǀ hárī íti ǀpurū́ṇi ǀ asmai ǀ sávanāni ǀ háryate ǀ índrāya ǀ sómāḥ ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ dadhanvire ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These two delightful bay horses bring the thunderer, the rejoicing and laudableIndra, in his car to theexhilaration (of theSoma); for him the beloved one many libations of the yellow-tinted Soma are stored up.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अरं॒ कामा॑य॒ हर॑यो दधन्विरे स्थि॒राय॑ हिन्व॒न्हर॑यो॒ हरी॑ तु॒रा । अर्व॑द्भि॒र्यो हरि॑भि॒र्जोष॒मीय॑ते॒ सो अ॑स्य॒ कामं॒ हरि॑वन्तमानशे
shlokas.transliteration: áram ǀ kā́māya ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ dadhanvire ǀ sthirā́ya ǀ hinvan ǀ hárayaḥ ǀ hárī íti ǀ turā́ ǀárvat-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ jóṣam ǀ ī́yate ǀ sáḥ ǀ asya ǀ kā́mam ǀ hári-vantam ǀ ānaśe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Yellow-tinted (Soma) is stored up sufficient to whet his desires, the yellow-tinted Soma urges his twoswift bay horses for the salwart (Indra). His (chariot) which rushes with spirited bay horses to the conflict, hasreached his desire (the sacrifice) in which the Soma is presented.”

shlokas.sanskrit: हरि॑श्मशारु॒र्हरि॑केश आय॒सस्तु॑र॒स्पेये॒ यो ह॑रि॒पा अव॑र्धत । अर्व॑द्भि॒र्यो हरि॑भिर्वा॒जिनी॑वसु॒रति॒ विश्वा॑ दुरि॒ता पारि॑ष॒द्धरी॑
shlokas.transliteration: hári-śmaśāruḥ ǀ hári-keśaḥ ǀ āyasáḥ ǀ turaḥ-péye ǀ yáḥ ǀ hari-pā́ḥ ǀ ávardhata ǀárvat-bhiḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ hári-bhiḥ ǀ vājínī-vasuḥ ǀ áti ǀ víśvā ǀ duḥ-itā́ ǀ pā́riṣat ǀ hárī íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The yellow-bearded, yellow-haired, iron-heartedIndra, the drinker of the yellow (Soma), who has beeninvigorated by the Soma which has to be quickly quaffed, who is rich in sacrificial food through his swift bayhorses, may he drive his two bay horses safe through all difficulties.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स्रुवे॑व॒ यस्य॒ हरि॑णी विपे॒ततु॒: शिप्रे॒ वाजा॑य॒ हरि॑णी॒ दवि॑ध्वतः । प्र यत्कृ॒ते च॑म॒से मर्मृ॑ज॒द्धरी॑ पी॒त्वा मद॑स्य हर्य॒तस्यान्ध॑सः
shlokas.transliteration: srúvā-iva ǀ yásya ǀ háriṇī íti ǀ vi-petátuḥ ǀ śípre íti ǀ vā́jāya ǀ háriṇī íti ǀ dávidhvataḥ ǀprá ǀ yát ǀ kṛté ǀ camasé ǀ mármṛjat ǀ hárī íti ǀ pītvā́ ǀ mádasya ǀ haryatásya ǀ ándhasaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He whose bay horses alight (upon theSoma) like two ladies, whose yellow jaws tremble (witheagerness) for the sacrificial food, (is praised) when having drunk of the delicious exhilarating Soma in theprepared cup, he rubs down his bay horses.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त स्म॒ सद्म॑ हर्य॒तस्य॑ प॒स्त्यो॒३॒॑रत्यो॒ न वाजं॒ हरि॑वाँ अचिक्रदत् । म॒ही चि॒द्धि धि॒षणाह॑र्य॒दोज॑सा बृ॒हद्वयो॑ दधिषे हर्य॒तश्चि॒दा
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ sma ǀ sádma ǀ haryatásya ǀ pastyóḥ ǀ átyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ vā́jam ǀ hári-vān ǀ acikradat ǀmahī́ ǀ cit ǀ hí ǀ dhiṣáṇā ǀ áharyat ǀ ójasā ǀ bṛhát ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dadhiṣe ǀ haryatáḥ ǀ cit ǀ ā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The dwelling of the gracious (Indra) is in heaven and earth; exhilarated by theSomahe rushesimpetuously as a charger to battle. The earnest prayer desires (Indra endowed) with might; you bestow amplefood on the devout (worshipper).”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ रोद॑सी॒ हर्य॑माणो महि॒त्वा नव्यं॑नव्यं हर्यसि॒ मन्म॒ नु प्रि॒यम् । प्र प॒स्त्य॑मसुर हर्य॒तं गोरा॒विष्कृ॑धि॒ हर॑ये॒ सूर्या॑य
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ródasī íti ǀ háryamāṇaḥ ǀ mahi-tvā́ ǀ návyam-navyam ǀ haryasi ǀ mánma ǀ nú ǀ priyám ǀprá ǀ pastyám ǀ asura ǀ haryatám ǀ góḥ ǀ āvíḥ ǀ kṛdhi ǀ háraye ǀ sū́ryāya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You (Indra) who are the object of desire (fill) heaven and earth with your greatness, you desire gratefulpraise ever new and new; O powerful one, make manifest the desirable dwelling of the water to the”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ त्वा॑ ह॒र्यन्तं॑ प्र॒युजो॒ जना॑नां॒ रथे॑ वहन्तु॒ हरि॑शिप्रमिन्द्र । पिबा॒ यथा॒ प्रति॑भृतस्य॒ मध्वो॒ हर्य॑न्य॒ज्ञं स॑ध॒मादे॒ दशो॑णिम्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tvā ǀ haryántam ǀ pra-yújaḥ ǀ jánānām ǀ ráthe ǀ vahantu ǀ hári-śipram ǀ indra ǀpíba ǀ yáthā ǀ práti-bhṛtasya ǀ mádhvaḥ ǀ háryan ǀ yajñám ǀ sadha-mā́de ǀ dáśa-oṇim ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let your horses yoked to the chariot bring you,Indra, the yellow- jawed, desiring (the sacrifice), to (thevicinity) of the worshippers; when you, desiring the sacrifice, prepared by the ten fingers, drink of the collectedsweet-flavouredSoma, (let them bring you) to the battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अपा॒: पूर्वे॑षां हरिवः सु॒ताना॒मथो॑ इ॒दं सव॑नं॒ केव॑लं ते । म॒म॒द्धि सोमं॒ मधु॑मन्तमिन्द्र स॒त्रा वृ॑षञ्ज॒ठर॒ आ वृ॑षस्व
shlokas.transliteration: ápāḥ ǀ pū́rveṣām ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ sutā́nām ǀ átho íti ǀ idám ǀ sávanam ǀ kévalam ǀ te ǀmamaddhí ǀ sómam ǀ mádhu-mantam ǀ indra ǀ satrā́ ǀ vṛṣan ǀ jaṭháre ǀ ā́ ǀ vṛṣasva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lord of horses, you did drink of previous libations, this sacrifice is for you alone; exhilarate yourself.Indrawith the sweetSoma; showerer of copious rain, shower it into your belly.”

shlokas.sanskrit: या ओष॑धी॒: पूर्वा॑ जा॒ता दे॒वेभ्य॑स्त्रियु॒गं पु॒रा । मनै॒ नु ब॒भ्रूणा॑म॒हं श॒तं धामा॑नि स॒प्त च॑
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ pū́rvāḥ ǀ jātā́ḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ tri-yugám ǀ purā́ ǀmánai ǀ nú ǀ babhrū́ṇām ǀ ahám ǀ śatám ǀ dhā́māni ǀ saptá ǀ ca ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I think of the hundred and seven applications of the brown-tinted plural nts, which are ancient, beinggenerated for the gods before the three ages.”

shlokas.sanskrit: श॒तं वो॑ अम्ब॒ धामा॑नि स॒हस्र॑मु॒त वो॒ रुह॑: । अधा॑ शतक्रत्वो यू॒यमि॒मं मे॑ अग॒दं कृ॑त
shlokas.transliteration: śatám ǀ vaḥ ǀ amba ǀ dhā́māni ǀ sahásram ǀ utá ǀ vaḥ ǀ rúhaḥ ǀádha ǀ śata-kratvaḥ ǀ yūyám ǀ imám ǀ me ǀ agadám ǀ kṛta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Mothers (of mankind) a hundred are your applications, a thousandfold is your growth; do you who fulfila hundred functions, make this my (people) free from disease.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ओष॑धी॒: प्रति॑ मोदध्वं॒ पुष्प॑वतीः प्र॒सूव॑रीः । अश्वा॑ इव स॒जित्व॑रीर्वी॒रुध॑: पारयि॒ष्ण्व॑:
shlokas.transliteration: óṣadhīḥ ǀ práti ǀ modadhvam ǀ púṣpa-vatīḥ ǀ pra-sū́varīḥ ǀáśvāḥ-iva ǀ sa-jítvarīḥ ǀ vīrúdhaḥ ǀ pārayiṣṇváḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Rejoice, plural nts, bearing abundant flowers and fruit, triumphing together (over disease) like (victorious)horses, sprouting forth, bearing (men safe) beyond (disease).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ओष॑धी॒रिति॑ मातर॒स्तद्वो॑ देवी॒रुप॑ ब्रुवे । स॒नेय॒मश्वं॒ गां वास॑ आ॒त्मानं॒ तव॑ पूरुष
shlokas.transliteration: óṣadhīḥ ǀ íti ǀ mātaraḥ ǀ tát ǀ vaḥ ǀ devīḥ ǀ úpa ǀ bruve ǀsanéyam ǀ áśvam ǀ gā́m ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ ātmā́nam ǀ táva ǀ puruṣa ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “"plural nts!" thus I hail you, the divine mothers (of mankind). I will give to you, oḥ physician, a horse, acow, a garment-- yes, even myself.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒श्व॒त्थे वो॑ नि॒षद॑नं प॒र्णे वो॑ वस॒तिष्कृ॒ता । गो॒भाज॒ इत्किला॑सथ॒ यत्स॒नव॑थ॒ पूरु॑षम्
shlokas.transliteration: aśvatthé ǀ vaḥ ǀ ni-sádanam ǀ parṇé ǀ vaḥ ǀ vasatíḥ ǀ kṛtā́ ǀgo-bhā́jaḥ ǀ ít ǀ kíla ǀ asatha ǀ yát ǀ sanávatha ǀ púruṣam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Your abode is in theAśvattha, your dwelling is established in thePalāśa, you are assuredly thedistributer of cattle, inasmuch as you bestow them on the physician.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यत्रौष॑धीः स॒मग्म॑त॒ राजा॑न॒: समि॑ताविव । विप्र॒: स उ॑च्यते भि॒षग्र॑क्षो॒हामी॑व॒चात॑नः
shlokas.transliteration: yátra ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sam-ágmata ǀ rā́jānaḥ ǀ sámitau-iva ǀvípraḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ ucyate ǀ bhiṣák ǀ rakṣaḥ-hā́ ǀ amīva-cā́tanaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Where, plural nts, you are congregated like princes (assembled) in battle, there the sage is designated aphysician, the destroyer of evil spirits, the extirpator of disease.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒श्वा॒व॒तीं सो॑माव॒तीमू॒र्जय॑न्ती॒मुदो॑जसम् । आवि॑त्सि॒ सर्वा॒ ओष॑धीर॒स्मा अ॑रि॒ष्टता॑तये
shlokas.transliteration: aśva-vatī́m ǀ soma-vatī́m ǀ ūrjáyantīm ǀ út-ojasam ǀā́ ǀ avitsi ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ asmái ǀ ariṣṭá-tātaye ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheAśvāvatī, theSomāvatī, the Urjayantī, the Udojasā)-- all these plural nts I praise for thepurpose of overcoming this disease.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उच्छुष्मा॒ ओष॑धीनां॒ गावो॑ गो॒ष्ठादि॑वेरते । धनं॑ सनि॒ष्यन्ती॑नामा॒त्मानं॒ तव॑ पूरुष
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ śúṣmāḥ ǀ óṣadhīnām ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ gosthā́t-iva ǀ īrate ǀdhánam ǀ saniṣyántīnām ǀ ātmā́nam ǀ táva ǀ puruṣa ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The virtues of the plural nts which are desirous of bestowing wealth issue from them, man, (towards) yourbody like cattle from the pen.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इष्कृ॑ति॒र्नाम॑ वो मा॒ताथो॑ यू॒यं स्थ॒ निष्कृ॑तीः । सी॒राः प॑त॒त्रिणी॑: स्थन॒ यदा॒मय॑ति॒ निष्कृ॑थ
shlokas.transliteration: íṣkṛtiḥ ǀ nā́ma ǀ vaḥ ǀ mātā́ ǀ átho íti ǀ yūyám ǀ stha ǀ níḥ-kṛtīḥ ǀsīrā́ḥ ǀ patatríṇīḥ ǀ sthana ǀ yát ǀ āmáyati ǀ níḥ ǀ kṛtha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Verily Iṣkṛti is your mother, therefore are you (also)Niṣkṛtis; you are flying streams; if (a man) is illyou cure him.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अति॒ विश्वा॑: परि॒ष्ठा स्ते॒न इ॑व व्र॒जम॑क्रमुः । ओष॑धी॒: प्राचु॑च्यवु॒र्यत्किं च॑ त॒न्वो॒३॒॑ रप॑:
shlokas.transliteration: áti ǀ víśvāḥ ǀ pari-sthā́ḥ ǀ stenáḥ-iva ǀ vrajám ǀ akramuḥ ǀóṣadhīḥ ǀ prá ǀ acucyavuḥ ǀ yát ǀ kím ǀ ca ǀ tanváḥ ǀ rápaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The universal all-pervading plural nts assail (diseases) as a thief (attacks) a cow-shed; they drive outwhatever infirmity of body there may be.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यदि॒मा वा॒जय॑न्न॒हमोष॑धी॒र्हस्त॑ आद॒धे । आ॒त्मा यक्ष्म॑स्य नश्यति पु॒रा जी॑व॒गृभो॑ यथा
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ imā́ḥ ǀ vājáyan ǀ ahám ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ háste ǀ ā-dadhé ǀātmā́ ǀ yákṣmasya ǀ naśyati ǀ purā́ ǀ jīva-gṛ́bhaḥ ǀ yathā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “As soon as I take these plural nts in myhandmaking (the sick man) strong, thesoulof the maladyperishes before (their application) as (life is driven away from the presence) of the seizer of life.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यस्यौ॑षधीः प्र॒सर्प॒थाङ्ग॑मङ्गं॒ परु॑ष्परुः । ततो॒ यक्ष्मं॒ वि बा॑धध्व उ॒ग्रो म॑ध्यम॒शीरि॑व
shlokas.transliteration: yásya ǀ oṣadhīḥ ǀ pra-sárpatha ǀ áṅgam-aṅgam ǀ páruḥ-paruḥ ǀtátaḥ ǀ yákṣmam ǀ ví ǀ bādhadhve ǀ ugráḥ ǀ madhyamaśī́ḥ-iva ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “From him, oḥ plural nts, in whom you creep from limb to limb, from joint to joint, you drive away diseaselike a mighty (prince) stationed in the midst of his host.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सा॒कं य॑क्ष्म॒ प्र प॑त॒ चाषे॑ण किकिदी॒विना॑ । सा॒कं वात॑स्य॒ ध्राज्या॑ सा॒कं न॑श्य नि॒हाक॑या
shlokas.transliteration: sākám ǀ yakṣma ǀ prá ǀ pata ǀ cā́ṣeṇa ǀ kikidīvínā ǀsākám ǀ vā́tasya ǀ dhrā́jyā ǀ sākám ǀ naśya ǀ ni-hā́kayā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Fly forth, sickness, with the jay, with the blue jay, with the velocity of the wind, perish along with theiguana.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒न्या वो॑ अ॒न्याम॑वत्व॒न्यान्यस्या॒ उपा॑वत । ताः सर्वा॑: संविदा॒ना इ॒दं मे॒ प्राव॑ता॒ वच॑:
shlokas.transliteration: anyā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ anyā́m ǀ avatu ǀ anyā́ ǀ anyásyāḥ ǀ úpa ǀ avata ǀtā́ḥ ǀ sárvāḥ ǀ sam-vidānā́ḥ ǀ idám ǀ me ǀ prá ǀ avata ǀ vácaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let each of you, plural nts, go to the other, approach the one (to the vicinity) of the other; thus being allmutually joined together, attend to this my speech.”

shlokas.sanskrit: याः फ॒लिनी॒र्या अ॑फ॒ला अ॑पु॒ष्पा याश्च॑ पु॒ष्पिणी॑: । बृह॒स्पति॑प्रसूता॒स्ता नो॑ मुञ्च॒न्त्वंह॑सः
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ phalínīḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ aphalā́ḥ ǀ apuṣpā́ḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ puṣpíṇīḥ ǀbṛ́haspáti-prasūtāḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ muñcantu ǀ áṃhasaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Whether bearing fruit or barren, whether flowering or flowerless, may they, the progeny ofBṛhaspati,liberate us from sin.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मु॒ञ्चन्तु॑ मा शप॒थ्या॒३॒॑दथो॑ वरु॒ण्या॑दु॒त । अथो॑ य॒मस्य॒ पड्बी॑शा॒त्सर्व॑स्माद्देवकिल्बि॒षात्
shlokas.transliteration: muñcántu ǀ mā ǀ śapathyā́t ǀ átho íti ǀ varuṇyā́t ǀ utá ǀátho íti ǀ yamásya ǀ páḍbīśāt ǀ sárvasmāt ǀ deva-kilbiṣā́t ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May they liberate me from the sin produced by curse, from the sin caused byVaruṇa, from the fettersOYama, from all guilt caused by the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒व॒पत॑न्तीरवदन्दि॒व ओष॑धय॒स्परि॑ । यं जी॒वम॒श्नवा॑महै॒ न स रि॑ष्याति॒ पूरु॑षः
shlokas.transliteration: ava-pátantīḥ ǀ avadan ǀ diváḥ ǀ óṣadhayaḥ ǀ pári ǀyám ǀ jīvám ǀ aśnávāmahai ǀ ná ǀ sáḥ ǀ riṣyāti ǀ púruṣaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The plural nts, falling from heaven, said, "The man, whom living we pervade, will not perish".”

shlokas.sanskrit: या ओष॑धी॒: सोम॑राज्ञीर्ब॒ह्वीः श॒तवि॑चक्षणाः । तासां॒ त्वम॑स्युत्त॒मारं॒ कामा॑य॒ शं हृ॒दे
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sóma-rājñīḥ ǀ bahvī́ḥ ǀ śatá-vicakṣaṇāḥ ǀtā́sām ǀ tvám ǀ asi ǀ ut-tamā́ ǀ áram ǀ kā́māya ǀ śám ǀ hṛdé ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The which have theSomafor their king, and are numerous and all- seeking of them you (O Soma) arethe best; be very bountiful to the affectionate heart.”

shlokas.sanskrit: या ओष॑धी॒: सोम॑राज्ञी॒र्विष्ठि॑ताः पृथि॒वीमनु॑ । बृह॒स्पति॑प्रसूता अ॒स्यै सं द॑त्त वी॒र्य॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ óṣadhīḥ ǀ sóma-rājñīḥ ǀ ví-sthitāḥ ǀ pṛthivī́m ǀ ánu ǀbṛ́haspáti-prasūtāḥ ǀ asyái ǀ sám ǀ datta ǀ vīryám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “plural nts, which have theSomafor your king, who are scattered over the earth, the offspring ofBṛhaspati, give vigour to this (infirm body).”

shlokas.sanskrit: मा वो॑ रिषत्खनि॒ता यस्मै॑ चा॒हं खना॑मि वः । द्वि॒पच्चतु॑ष्पद॒स्माकं॒ सर्व॑मस्त्वनातु॒रम्
shlokas.transliteration: mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ riṣat ǀ khanitā́ ǀ yásmai ǀ ca ǀ ahám ǀ khánāmi ǀ vaḥ ǀdvi-pát ǀ cátuḥ-pat ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sárvam ǀ astu ǀ anāturám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let not the digger hurt you, not (the sick person n) for whom I dig you up; may all my bipeds andquadrupeds be free from disease.”

shlokas.sanskrit: याश्चे॒दमु॑पशृ॒ण्वन्ति॒ याश्च॑ दू॒रं परा॑गताः । सर्वा॑: सं॒गत्य॑ वीरुधो॒ऽस्यै सं द॑त्त वी॒र्य॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ idám ǀ upa-śṛṇvánti ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ca ǀ dūrám ǀ párā-gatāḥ ǀsárvāḥ ǀ sam-gátya ǀ vīrudhaḥ ǀ asyái ǀ sám ǀ datta ǀ vīryám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Both the plural nts that I hear this (prayer), and those which are removed far off, all coming together,give vigour to this (infirm body).”

shlokas.sanskrit: ओष॑धय॒: सं व॑दन्ते॒ सोमे॑न स॒ह राज्ञा॑ । यस्मै॑ कृ॒णोति॑ ब्राह्म॒णस्तं रा॑जन्पारयामसि
shlokas.transliteration: óṣadhayaḥ ǀ sám ǀ vadante ǀ sómena ǀ sahá ǀ rā́jñā ǀyásmai ǀ kṛṇóti ǀ brāhmaṇáḥ ǀ tám ǀ rājan ǀ pārayāmasi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “All the plural nts, together withSomatheir king, declare, "We save him, O king, to whom the Brāhmaṇaadministers (us)".”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वमु॑त्त॒मास्यो॑षधे॒ तव॑ वृ॒क्षा उप॑स्तयः । उप॑स्तिरस्तु॒ सो॒३॒॑ऽस्माकं॒ यो अ॒स्माँ अ॑भि॒दास॑ति
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ ut-tamā́ ǀ asi ǀ oṣadhe ǀ táva ǀ vṛkṣā́ḥ ǀ úpastayaḥ ǀúpastiḥ ǀ astu ǀ sáḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yáḥ ǀ asmā́n ǀ abhi-dā́sati ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You (Soma) are the best of the plural nts, to you (all) trees are prostrate; may he be prostrate to us, whoattacks us.”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृह॑स्पते॒ प्रति॑ मे दे॒वता॑मिहि मि॒त्रो वा॒ यद्वरु॑णो॒ वासि॑ पू॒षा । आ॒दि॒त्यैर्वा॒ यद्वसु॑भिर्म॒रुत्वा॒न्त्स प॒र्जन्यं॒ शंत॑नवे वृषाय
shlokas.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ práti ǀ me ǀ devátām ǀ ihi ǀ mitráḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ vā ǀ ási ǀ pūṣā́ ǀādityáiḥ ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ marútvān ǀ sáḥ ǀ parjányam ǀ śám-tanave ǀ vṛṣaya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “: Go,Bṛhaspati, on my behalf to the gods, whether you areMitra, orVaruṇa, orPūṣan, orassociated with theĀdityas, theVasus, or theMaruts-- do you causeParjanyato send down rain forŚantanu.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ दे॒वो दू॒तो अ॑जि॒रश्चि॑कि॒त्वान्त्वद्दे॑वापे अ॒भि माम॑गच्छत् । प्र॒ती॒ची॒नः प्रति॒ मामा व॑वृत्स्व॒ दधा॑मि ते द्यु॒मतीं॒ वाच॑मा॒सन्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ ajiráḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ tvát ǀ deva-āpe ǀ abhí ǀ mā́m ǀ agacchat ǀpratīcīnáḥ ǀ práti ǀ mā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ vavṛtsva ǀ dádhāmi ǀ te ǀ dyu-mátīm ǀ vā́cam ǀ āsán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let a divine messenger quick and intelligent sent,Devāpi, by you come to me. Come,Bṛhaspati, tome, turning towards me; I have in my mouth a brilliant eulogium for you.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒स्मे धे॑हि द्यु॒मतीं॒ वाच॑मा॒सन्बृह॑स्पते अनमी॒वामि॑षि॒राम् । यया॑ वृ॒ष्टिं शंत॑नवे॒ वना॑व दि॒वो द्र॒प्सो मधु॑माँ॒ आ वि॑वेश
shlokas.transliteration: asmé íti ǀ dhehi ǀ dyu-mátīm ǀ vā́cam ǀ āsán ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ anamīvā́m ǀ iṣirā́m ǀyáyā ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ śám-tanave ǀ vánāva ǀ diváḥ ǀ drapsáḥ ǀ mádhu-mān ǀ ā́ ǀ viveśa ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Put,Bṛhaspati, in my mouth a brilliant eulogium, prompt and free from defect, by which we two mayobtain rain from heaven forŚantanu, the sweet drop (sent by you) has entered (our voice).”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ नो॑ द्र॒प्सा मधु॑मन्तो विश॒न्त्विन्द्र॑ दे॒ह्यधि॑रथं स॒हस्र॑म् । नि षी॑द हो॒त्रमृ॑तु॒था य॑जस्व दे॒वान्दे॑वापे ह॒विषा॑ सपर्य
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ drapsā́ḥ ǀ mádhu-mantaḥ ǀ viśantu ǀ índra ǀ dehí ǀ ádhi-ratham ǀ sahásram ǀní ǀ sīda ǀ hotrám ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ yajasva ǀ devā́n ǀ deva-āpe ǀ havíṣā ǀ saparya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the sweet drops of rain fall upon us; grant us,Indra, a thousand chariot-loads. Sit down,Devāpi,to your duties asHotā; in due season sacrifice to the gods, worship them with oblations. functions as Hotā. He has brought down from the upper to the lower ocean the rain waters of heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒र्ष्टि॒षे॒णो हो॒त्रमृषि॑र्नि॒षीद॑न्दे॒वापि॑र्देवसुम॒तिं चि॑कि॒त्वान् । स उत्त॑रस्मा॒दध॑रं समु॒द्रम॒पो दि॒व्या अ॑सृजद्व॒र्ष्या॑ अ॒भि
