shlokas.transliteration: ārṣṭiṣeṇáḥ ǀ hotrám ǀ ṛ́ṣiḥ ǀ ni-sī́dan ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ deva-sumatím ǀ cikitvā́n ǀsáḥ ǀ út-tarasmāt ǀ ádharam ǀ samudrám ǀ apáḥ ǀ divyā́ḥ ǀ asṛjat ǀ varṣyā́ḥ ǀ abhí ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒स्मिन्त्स॑मु॒द्रे अध्युत्त॑रस्मि॒न्नापो॑ दे॒वेभि॒र्निवृ॑ता अतिष्ठन् । ता अ॑द्रवन्नार्ष्टिषे॒णेन॑ सृ॒ष्टा दे॒वापि॑ना॒ प्रेषि॑ता मृ॒क्षिणी॑षु
shlokas.transliteration: asmín ǀ samudré ǀ ádhi ǀ út-tarasmin ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ ní-vṛtāḥ ǀ atiṣṭhan ǀtā́ḥ ǀ adravan ǀ ārṣṭiṣeṇéna ǀ sṛṣṭā́ḥ ǀ devá-āpinā ǀ prá-iṣitāḥ ǀ mṛkṣíṇīṣu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In this upper ocean the waters stood dammed up by the gods; set free byDevāpi, the son ofṚṣṭiṣeṇa, they were sent forth over the plural ins.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यद्दे॒वापि॒: शंत॑नवे पु॒रोहि॑तो हो॒त्राय॑ वृ॒तः कृ॒पय॒न्नदी॑धेत् । दे॒व॒श्रुतं॑ वृष्टि॒वनिं॒ ररा॑णो॒ बृह॒स्पति॒र्वाच॑मस्मा अयच्छत्
shlokas.transliteration: yát ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ śám-tanave ǀ puráḥ-hitaḥ ǀ hotrā́ya ǀ vṛtáḥ ǀ kṛpáyan ǀ ádīdhet ǀdeva-śrútam ǀ vṛṣṭi-vánim ǀ rárāṇaḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vā́cam ǀ asmai ǀ ayacchat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “WhenDevāpi, thePurohitaforŚantanu, engaged in his functions ofHotā, compassionating (him),slicitedBṛhaspati, to whom the gods listen, who begs for rain, (Bṛhaspati) being plural ased gave him a voice.”

shlokas.sanskrit: यं त्वा॑ दे॒वापि॑: शुशुचा॒नो अ॑ग्न आर्ष्टिषे॒णो म॑नु॒ष्य॑: समी॒धे । विश्वे॑भिर्दे॒वैर॑नुम॒द्यमा॑न॒: प्र प॒र्जन्य॑मीरया वृष्टि॒मन्त॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: yám ǀ tvā ǀ devá-āpiḥ ǀ śuśucānáḥ ǀ agne ǀ ārṣṭiṣeṇáḥ ǀ manuṣyáḥ ǀ sam-īdhé ǀvíśvebhiḥ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ anu-madyámānaḥ ǀ prá ǀ parjányam ǀ īraya ǀ vṛṣṭi-mántam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agni, whom the mortalDevāpi, the son of Ṛṣṭiseṇa, lighting you, has kindled, do you, beingpropitiated with all the gods, send down the rain- laden cloud.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वां पूर्व॒ ऋष॑यो गी॒र्भिरा॑य॒न्त्वाम॑ध्व॒रेषु॑ पुरुहूत॒ विश्वे॑ । स॒हस्रा॒ण्यधि॑रथान्य॒स्मे आ नो॑ य॒ज्ञं रो॑हिद॒श्वोप॑ याहि
shlokas.transliteration: tvā́m ǀ pū́rve ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ gīḥ-bhíḥ ǀ āyan ǀ tvā́m ǀ adhvaréṣu ǀ puru-hūta ǀ víśve ǀsahásrāṇi ǀ ádhi-rathāni ǀ asmé íti ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ rohit-aśva ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You have ancient sages approached, with hymns; you, O invoked of many, all worshippers (address)at sacrifice; (give) us thousands of chariot-loads, come to our sacrifice, lord of red horses.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒तान्य॑ग्ने नव॒तिर्नव॒ त्वे आहु॑ता॒न्यधि॑रथा स॒हस्रा॑ । तेभि॑र्वर्धस्व त॒न्व॑: शूर पू॒र्वीर्दि॒वो नो॑ वृ॒ष्टिमि॑षि॒तो रि॑रीहि
shlokas.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ agne ǀ navatíḥ ǀ náva ǀ tvé íti ǀ ā́-hutāni ǀ ádhi-rathā ǀ sahásrā ǀtébhiḥ ǀ vardhasva ǀ tanváḥ ǀ śūra ǀ pūrvī́ḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛṣṭím ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ rirīhi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These ninety-and-nine thousands of chariot-lords have been offered,Agni, to you; with them, O hero,nourish your many bodies; and thus solicited sends us rain from heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒तान्य॑ग्ने नव॒तिं स॒हस्रा॒ सं प्र य॑च्छ॒ वृष्ण॒ इन्द्रा॑य भा॒गम् । वि॒द्वान्प॒थ ऋ॑तु॒शो दे॑व॒याना॒नप्यौ॑ला॒नं दि॒वि दे॒वेषु॑ धेहि
shlokas.transliteration: etā́ni ǀ agne ǀ navatím ǀ sahásrā ǀ sám ǀ prá ǀ yaccha ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ índrāya ǀ bhāgám ǀvidvā́n ǀ patháḥ ǀ ṛtu-śáḥ ǀ deva-yā́nān ǀ ápi ǀ aulānám ǀ diví ǀ devéṣu ǀ dhehi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Give,Agni, these ninety thousands to the showerer,Indra, as his share; knowing the paths traversedby the gods in due season plural ce the Aulāna (Śantanu), in heaven among the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अग्ने॒ बाध॑स्व॒ वि मृधो॒ वि दु॒र्गहापामी॑वा॒मप॒ रक्षां॑सि सेध । अ॒स्मात्स॑मु॒द्राद्बृ॑ह॒तो दि॒वो नो॒ऽपां भू॒मान॒मुप॑ नः सृजे॒ह
shlokas.transliteration: ágne ǀ bā́dhasva ǀ ví ǀ mṛ́dhaḥ ǀ ví ǀ duḥ-gáhā ǀ ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ ápa ǀ rákṣāṃsi ǀ sedha ǀasmā́t ǀ samudrā́t ǀ bṛhatáḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ apā́m ǀ bhūmā́nam ǀ úpa ǀ naḥ ǀ sṛja ǀ ihá ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Demolish,Agni, our enemies, demolish their strongholds, drive away disease, drive away therākṣasas from this ocean, from vast heaven send own upon us here abundance of rain.”

shlokas.sanskrit: कं न॑श्चि॒त्रमि॑षण्यसि चिकि॒त्वान्पृ॑थु॒ग्मानं॑ वा॒श्रं वा॑वृ॒धध्यै॑ । कत्तस्य॒ दातु॒ शव॑सो॒ व्यु॑ष्टौ॒ तक्ष॒द्वज्रं॑ वृत्र॒तुर॒मपि॑न्वत्
shlokas.transliteration: kám ǀ naḥ ǀ citrám ǀ iṣaṇyasi ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ pṛthu-gmā́nam ǀ vāśrám ǀ vavṛdhádhyai ǀkát ǀ tásya ǀ dā́tu ǀ śávasaḥ ǀ ví-uṣṭau ǀ tákṣat ǀ vájram ǀ vṛtra-túram ǀ ápinvat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “What marvellous (wealth), comprehensive and laudable, do you,Indra, knowing (what is needed),bestow upon us for our advantage? What gift (has been made to us) upon the development of his strength? Hefabricated theVṛtra- slaying thunderbolt, and let the waters flow.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स हि द्यु॒ता वि॒द्युता॒ वेति॒ साम॑ पृ॒थुं योनि॑मसुर॒त्वा स॑साद । स सनी॑ळेभिः प्रसहा॒नो अ॑स्य॒ भ्रातु॒र्न ऋ॒ते स॒प्तथ॑स्य मा॒याः
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ dyutā́ ǀ vi-dyútā ǀ véti ǀ sā́ma ǀ pṛthúm ǀ yónim ǀ asura-tvā́ ǀ ā́ ǀ sasāda ǀsáḥ ǀ sá-nīḷebhiḥ ǀ pra-sahānáḥ ǀ asya ǀ bhrā́tuḥ ǀ ná ǀ ṛté ǀ saptáthasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Armed with the bright lightning he goes to the (scene of) adoration; endowed with might he has seatedhimself on the spacious plural ce (of sacrifice); he (is) triumphant with his companions (theMaruts); the wiles of hisseventh brother do not (prevail) at the rite.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स वाजं॒ याताप॑दुष्पदा॒ यन्त्स्व॑र्षाता॒ परि॑ षदत्सनि॒ष्यन् । अ॒न॒र्वा यच्छ॒तदु॑रस्य॒ वेदो॒ घ्नञ्छि॒श्नदे॑वाँ अ॒भि वर्प॑सा॒ भूत्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vā́jam ǀ yā́tā ǀ ápaduḥ-padā ǀ yán ǀ sváḥ-sātā ǀ pári ǀ sadat ǀ saniṣyán ǀanarvā́ ǀ yát ǀ śatá-durasya ǀ védaḥ ǀ ghnán ǀ śiśná-devān ǀ abhí ǀ várpasā ǀ bhū́t ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Going to the battle, marching with easy gait, desiring the spoil, he set himself to the acquisition of all(wealth). Invincible, destroying the phallus-worshippers, he won by his prowess whatever wealth (was concealedin the city) with the hundred gates.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स य॒ह्व्यो॒३॒॑ऽवनी॒र्गोष्वर्वा जु॑होति प्रध॒न्या॑सु॒ सस्रि॑: । अ॒पादो॒ यत्र॒ युज्या॑सोऽर॒था द्रो॒ण्य॑श्वास॒ ईर॑ते घृ॒तं वाः
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ yahvyáḥ ǀ avánīḥ ǀ góṣu ǀ árvā ǀ ā́ ǀ juhoti ǀ pra-dhanyā́su ǀ sásriḥ ǀapā́daḥ ǀ yátra ǀ yújyāsaḥ ǀ arathā́ḥ ǀ droṇí-aśvāsaḥ ǀ ī́rate ǀ ghṛtám ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The victoriousIndra, coming among the clouds, quickly moving, offers the abundant waters on the rich(plural ins) where his associates (the rivers) footless, and without conveyances, having pitchers for horses, pour outwater like ghī.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स रु॒द्रेभि॒रश॑स्तवार॒ ऋभ्वा॑ हि॒त्वी गय॑मा॒रेअ॑वद्य॒ आगा॑त् । व॒म्रस्य॑ मन्ये मिथु॒ना विव॑व्री॒ अन्न॑म॒भीत्या॑रोदयन्मुषा॒यन्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ rudrébhiḥ ǀ áśasta-vāraḥ ǀ ṛ́bhvā ǀ hitvī́ ǀ gáyam ǀ āré-avadyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀvamrásya ǀ manye ǀ mithunā́ ǀ vívavrī íti ví-vavrī ǀ ánnam ǀ abhi-ítya ǀ arodayat ǀ muṣāyán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May he, our unsolicited benefactor, the mighty one, from whom blame is far removed, come with theRudras, having quit his dwelling. I think of the two (parents) of Vamra, who are free from fever. Having obtained(the enemy's) food, he called aloud while stealing it.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स इद्दासं॑ तुवी॒रवं॒ पति॒र्दन्ष॑ळ॒क्षं त्रि॑शी॒र्षाणं॑ दमन्यत् । अ॒स्य त्रि॒तो न्वोज॑सा वृधा॒नो वि॒पा व॑रा॒हमयो॑अग्रया हन्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ ít ǀ dā́sam ǀ tuvi-rávam ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǀ ṣaṭ-akṣám ǀ tri-śīrṣā́ṇam ǀ damanyat ǀasyá ǀ tritáḥ ǀ nú ǀ ójasā ǀ vṛdhānáḥ ǀ vipā́ ǀ varāhám ǀ áyaḥ-agrayā ǀ hanníti han ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The sovereignIndraattacking him overcame the loud-shouting, six- eyed, three-headedDāsa, andTrita, invigorated by his strength, smote the water-laden (cloud) with his iron-tipped finger.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स द्रुह्व॑णे॒ मनु॑ष ऊर्ध्वसा॒न आ सा॑विषदर्शसा॒नाय॒ शरु॑म् । स नृत॑मो॒ नहु॑षो॒ऽस्मत्सुजा॑त॒: पुरो॑ऽभिन॒दर्ह॑न्दस्यु॒हत्ये॑
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ drúhvaṇe ǀ mánuṣe ǀ ūrdhvasānáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ arśasānā́ya ǀ śárum ǀsáḥ ǀ nṛ́-tamaḥ ǀ náhuṣaḥ ǀ asmát ǀ sú-jātaḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ abhinat ǀ árhan ǀ dasyu-hátye ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: सो अ॒भ्रियो॒ न यव॑स उद॒न्यन्क्षया॑य गा॒तुं वि॒दन्नो॑ अ॒स्मे । उप॒ यत्सीद॒दिन्दुं॒ शरी॑रैः श्ये॒नोऽयो॑पाष्टिर्हन्ति॒ दस्यू॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ abhríyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ yávase ǀ udanyán ǀ kṣáyāya ǀ gātúm ǀ vidát ǀ naḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀúpa ǀ yát ǀ sī́dat ǀ índum ǀ śárīraiḥ ǀ śyenáḥ ǀ áyaḥ-apāṣṭiḥ ǀ hanti ǀ dásyūn ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Like the aggregated cloud desiring to pour water on the pasturage, he found the way to our dwellingwhen he approached theSomawith his limbs, like a hawk with heel of metal he smites theDasyus.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स व्राध॑तः शवसा॒नेभि॑रस्य॒ कुत्सा॑य॒ शुष्णं॑ कृ॒पणे॒ परा॑दात् । अ॒यं क॒विम॑नयच्छ॒स्यमा॑न॒मत्कं॒ यो अ॑स्य॒ सनि॑तो॒त नृ॒णाम्
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ vrā́dhataḥ ǀ śavasānébhiḥ ǀ asya ǀ kútsāya ǀ śúṣṇam ǀ kṛpáṇe ǀ párā ǀ adāt ǀayám ǀ kavím ǀ anayat ǀ śasyámānam ǀ átkam ǀ yáḥ ǀ asya ǀ sánitā ǀ utá ǀ nṛṇā́m ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Let him overthrow the mighty with powerful (weapons); he destroyedŚuṣṇafor the sake of the liberalKutsa; he humiliatedKavi, who praised him, who was the giver of form toIndraand his men.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यं द॑श॒स्यन्नर्ये॑भिरस्य द॒स्मो दे॒वेभि॒र्वरु॑णो॒ न मा॒यी । अ॒यं क॒नीन॑ ऋतु॒पा अ॑वे॒द्यमि॑मीता॒ररुं॒ यश्चतु॑ष्पात्
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ daśasyán ǀ náryebhiḥ ǀ asya ǀ dasmáḥ ǀ devébhiḥ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ ná ǀ māyī́ ǀayám ǀ kanī́naḥ ǀ ṛtu-pā́ḥ ǀ avedi ǀ ámimīta ǀ arárum ǀ yáḥ ǀ cátuḥ-pāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bountiful (to his worshippers) with his (Maruts) friendly to men, wonderful with brilliancies, havingmagical power likeVaruṇa, he was known as desirable, protecting the seasons, he destroyed,Araru, who wasfour-footed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒स्य स्तोमे॑भिरौशि॒ज ऋ॒जिश्वा॑ व्र॒जं द॑रयद्वृष॒भेण॒ पिप्रो॑: । सुत्वा॒ यद्य॑ज॒तो दी॒दय॒द्गीः पुर॑ इया॒नो अ॒भि वर्प॑सा॒ भूत्
shlokas.transliteration: asyá ǀ stómebhiḥ ǀ auśijáḥ ǀ ṛjíśvā ǀ vrajám ǀ darayat ǀ vṛṣabhéṇa ǀ píproḥ ǀsútvā ǀ yát ǀ yajatáḥ ǀ dīdáyat ǀ gī́ḥ ǀ púraḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ abhí ǀ várpasā ǀ bhū́t ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Ṛjiśvā, the son ofUśijawithIndra's praises shattered the cow pen of Pipru with the thunderbolt;when having expressed (theSoma), the venerable sage recited his praises, (Indra) proceeding against the cities(of the enemy) triumphed with his body.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒वा म॒हो अ॑सुर व॒क्षथा॑य वम्र॒कः प॒ड्भिरुप॑ सर्प॒दिन्द्र॑म् । स इ॑या॒नः क॑रति स्व॒स्तिम॑स्मा॒ इष॒मूर्जं॑ सुक्षि॒तिं विश्व॒माभा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: evá ǀ maháḥ ǀ asura ǀ vakṣáthāya ǀ vamrakáḥ ǀ paṭ-bhíḥ ǀ úpa ǀ sarpat ǀ índram ǀsáḥ ǀ iyānáḥ ǀ karati ǀ svastím ǀ asmai ǀ íṣam ǀ ū́rjam ǀ su-kṣitím ǀ víśvam ǀ ā́ ǀ abhārítyabhāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In this manner, O mighty (Indra), Vamraka approached Indra on foot, to bring an ample oblation. Mayhe, being approached, grant us prosperity, may he bring us food, drink, a secure dwelling and all (good things).”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॒ दृह्य॑ मघव॒न्त्वाव॒दिद्भु॒ज इ॒ह स्तु॒तः सु॑त॒पा बो॑धि नो वृ॒धे । दे॒वेभि॑र्नः सवि॒ता प्राव॑तु श्रु॒तमा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: índra ǀ dṛ́hya ǀ magha-van ǀ tvā́-vat ǀ ít ǀ bhujé ǀ ihá ǀ stutáḥ ǀ suta-pā́ḥ ǀ bodhi ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛdhé ǀdevébhiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ prá ǀ avatu ǀ śrutám ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Consume, afluentIndra, (the foe that is) like you (in might); praised on this occasion, do you who arethe drinker of the libation be favourable to our advancement. MaySavitā, with the gods, defend our sacrifice;we long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भरा॑य॒ सु भ॑रत भा॒गमृ॒त्वियं॒ प्र वा॒यवे॑ शुचि॒पे क्र॒न्ददि॑ष्टये । गौ॒रस्य॒ यः पय॑सः पी॒तिमा॑न॒श आ स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: bhárāya ǀ sú ǀ bharata ǀ bhāgám ǀ ṛtvíyam ǀ prá ǀ vāyáve ǀ śuci-pé ǀ krandát-iṣṭaye ǀgaurásya ǀ yáḥ ǀ páyasaḥ ǀ pītím ǀ ānaśé ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Offer to (Indra) the cherisher (of all) the share suited to the season; (offer it) toVāyu, the drinker ofthe pure (Soma), who clamours as he travels, who obtains a draught of white milk; we long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ नो॑ दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता सा॑विष॒द्वय॑ ऋजूय॒ते यज॑मानाय सुन्व॒ते । यथा॑ दे॒वान्प्र॑ति॒भूषे॑म पाक॒वदा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ váyaḥ ǀ ṛju-yaté ǀ yájamānāya ǀ sunvaté ǀyáthā ǀ devā́n ǀ prati-bhū́ṣema ǀ pāka-vát ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the divineSavitāgenitive rate well-dressed food for our sincereyajamānaas he offers the libation,so that we may be in good favour with the gods; we long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ अ॒स्मे सु॒मना॑ अस्तु वि॒श्वहा॒ राजा॒ सोम॑: सुवि॒तस्याध्ये॑तु नः । यथा॑यथा मि॒त्रधि॑तानि संद॒धुरा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ su-mánāḥ ǀ astu ǀ viśváhā ǀ rā́jā ǀ sómaḥ ǀ suvitásya ǀ ádhi ǀ etu ǀ naḥ ǀyáthā-yathā ǀ mitrá-dhitāni ǀ sam-dadhúḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayIndrabe favourably disposed towards us every day, may the royalSomaaccept our praise, sothat they may bestow upon us friendly treasures; we long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑ उ॒क्थेन॒ शव॑सा॒ परु॑र्दधे॒ बृह॑स्पते प्रतरी॒तास्यायु॑षः । य॒ज्ञो मनु॒: प्रम॑तिर्नः पि॒ता हि क॒मा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ ukthéna ǀ śávasā ǀ páruḥ ǀ dadhe ǀ bṛ́haspate ǀ pra-tarītā́ ǀ asi ǀ ā́yuṣaḥ ǀyajñáḥ ǀ mánuḥ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ pitā́ ǀ hí ǀ kam ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “By his laudable strengthIndrasupports my limb; you,Bṛhaspati, are the prolonger of my life. May thesacrifice, the sageManu, (being) our protector, (grant) us happiness. We long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑स्य॒ नु सुकृ॑तं॒ दैव्यं॒ सहो॒ऽग्निर्गृ॒हे ज॑रि॒ता मेधि॑रः क॒विः । य॒ज्ञश्च॑ भूद्वि॒दथे॒ चारु॒रन्त॑म॒ आ स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: índrasya ǀ nú ǀ sú-kṛtam ǀ dáivyam ǀ sáhaḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ gṛhé ǀ jaritā́ ǀ médhiraḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀyajñáḥ ǀ ca ǀ bhūt ǀ vidáthe ǀ cā́ruḥ ǀ ántamaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The divine force ofIndrais well constructed;Agni(abides) in our dwelling, the praiser of the gods, thereceiver of oblations, the sage, and is worthy of sacrifice at the altar, beautiful and most near (to us). We long forthe universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: न वो॒ गुहा॑ चकृम॒ भूरि॑ दुष्कृ॒तं नाविष्ट्यं॑ वसवो देव॒हेळ॑नम् । माकि॑र्नो देवा॒ अनृ॑तस्य॒ वर्प॑स॒ आ स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ vaḥ ǀ gúhā ǀ cakṛma ǀ bhū́ri ǀ duḥ-kṛtám ǀ ná ǀ āvíḥ-tyam ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ deva-héḷanam ǀmā́kiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ devāḥ ǀ ánṛtasya ǀ várpasaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We have not done any great evil in secret from you, nor any open (action) causing the anger of thegods, O you givers of wealth; let not, O gods, (the possession) of an unreal form be our (lot). We long for theuniversalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अपामी॑वां सवि॒ता सा॑विष॒न्न्य१॒॑ग्वरी॑य॒ इदप॑ सेध॒न्त्वद्र॑यः । ग्रावा॒ यत्र॑ मधु॒षुदु॒च्यते॑ बृ॒हदा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: ápa ǀ ámīvām ǀ savitā́ ǀ sāviṣat ǀ nyák ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ ápa ǀ sedhantu ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀgrā́vā ǀ yátra ǀ madhu-sút ǀ ucyáte ǀ bṛhát ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MaySavitādrive away (our) disease, may the mountains keep off our most heinous (sin), where thestone( the effuser) of the sweetSomais abundantly praised. We long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊ॒र्ध्वो ग्रावा॑ वसवोऽस्तु सो॒तरि॒ विश्वा॒ द्वेषां॑सि सनु॒तर्यु॑योत । स नो॑ दे॒वः स॑वि॒ता पा॒युरीड्य॒ आ स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: ūrdhváḥ ǀ grā́vā ǀ vasavaḥ ǀ astu ǀ sotári ǀ víśvā ǀ dvéṣāṃsi ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yuyota ǀsáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ deváḥ ǀ savitā́ ǀ pāyúḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the stone be uplifted, gods, when I make the libation; disperse all my secret adversaries; the godSavitā is our adorable protector. We long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊर्जं॑ गावो॒ यव॑से॒ पीवो॑ अत्तन ऋ॒तस्य॒ याः सद॑ने॒ कोशे॑ अ॒ङ्ग्ध्वे । त॒नूरे॒व त॒न्वो॑ अस्तु भेष॒जमा स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: ū́rjam ǀ gāvaḥ ǀ yávase ǀ pī́vaḥ ǀ attana ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ sádane ǀ kóśe ǀ aṅgdhvé ǀtanū́ḥ ǀ evá ǀ tanváḥ ǀ astu ǀ bheṣajám ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Eat abundant fodder in the pasture, O cows, who are anointed in the hall of sacrifice in the cow-stall;may (your) body be the remedy for (our) body. We long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: क्र॒तु॒प्रावा॑ जरि॒ता शश्व॑ता॒मव॒ इन्द्र॒ इद्भ॒द्रा प्रम॑तिः सु॒ताव॑ताम् । पू॒र्णमूध॑र्दि॒व्यं यस्य॑ सि॒क्तय॒ आ स॒र्वता॑ति॒मदि॑तिं वृणीमहे
shlokas.transliteration: kratu-prā́vā ǀ jaritā́ ǀ śáśvatām ǀ ávaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ ít ǀ bhadrā́ ǀ prá-matiḥ ǀ sutá-vatām ǀpūrṇám ǀ ū́dhaḥ ǀ divyám ǀ yásya ǀ siktáye ǀ ā́ ǀ sarvá-tātim ǀ áditim ǀ vṛṇīmahe ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrais the fulfiller of pious acts, the glorifier of all, the guardian of the offerers of libations, theauspicious forethought, for his libation the divine pitcher is filled (withSoma). We long for the universalAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: चि॒त्रस्ते॑ भा॒नुः क्र॑तु॒प्रा अ॑भि॒ष्टिः सन्ति॒ स्पृधो॑ जरणि॒प्रा अधृ॑ष्टाः । रजि॑ष्ठया॒ रज्या॑ प॒श्व आ गोस्तूतू॑र्षति॒ पर्यग्रं॑ दुव॒स्युः
shlokas.transliteration: citráḥ ǀ te ǀ bhānúḥ ǀ kratu-prā́ḥ ǀ abhiṣṭíḥ ǀ sánti ǀ spṛ́dhaḥ ǀ jaraṇi-prā́ḥ ǀ ádhṛṣṭāḥ ǀrájiṣṭhayā ǀ rájyā ǀ paśváḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ góḥ ǀ tū́tūrṣati ǀ pári ǀ ágram ǀ duvasyúḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Your splendour,Indra, is wonderful, fulfilling our pious acts, desirable; your efforts replenishing thewealth of your worshippers are irresistible; (therefore) Duvasyu hastens in front of the victim cow, (leading it) witha straight cord.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उद्बु॑ध्यध्वं॒ सम॑नसः सखाय॒: सम॒ग्निमि॑न्ध्वं ब॒हव॒: सनी॑ळाः । द॒धि॒क्राम॒ग्निमु॒षसं॑ च दे॒वीमिन्द्रा॑व॒तोऽव॑से॒ नि ह्व॑ये वः
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ budhyadhvam ǀ sá-manasaḥ ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ sám ǀ agním ǀ indhvam ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ sá-nīḷāḥ ǀdadhi-krā́m ǀ agním ǀ uṣásam ǀ ca ǀ devī́m ǀ índra-vataḥ ǀ ávase ǀ ní ǀ hvaye ǀ vaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Awake, friends, being all agreed; many in number, abiding in one dwelling, kindleAgni. I invoke you,Dadhikra, Agni, and the divine Uṣas, who are associated withIndra, for our protection.”

shlokas.sanskrit: म॒न्द्रा कृ॑णुध्वं॒ धिय॒ आ त॑नुध्वं॒ नाव॑मरित्र॒पर॑णीं कृणुध्वम् । इष्कृ॑णुध्व॒मायु॒धारं॑ कृणुध्वं॒ प्राञ्चं॑ य॒ज्ञं प्र ण॑यता सखायः
shlokas.transliteration: mandrā́ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ tanudhvam ǀ nā́vam ǀ aritra-páraṇīm ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀíṣkṛṇudhvam ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ áram ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ prā́ñcam ǀ yajñám ǀ prá ǀ nayata ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Construct exhilarating (hymns), spread forth praises, construct the ship which is propelled by oars,prepare your weapons, make ready, lead forth, O friends, the herald, the adorable (Agni).”

shlokas.sanskrit: यु॒नक्त॒ सीरा॒ वि यु॒गा त॑नुध्वं कृ॒ते योनौ॑ वपते॒ह बीज॑म् । गि॒रा च॑ श्रु॒ष्टिः सभ॑रा॒ अस॑न्नो॒ नेदी॑य॒ इत्सृ॒ण्य॑: प॒क्वमेया॑त्
shlokas.transliteration: yunákta ǀ sī́rā ǀ ví ǀ yugā́ ǀ tanudhvam ǀ kṛté ǀ yónau ǀ vapata ǀ ihá ǀ bī́jam ǀgirā́ ǀ ca ǀ śruṣṭíḥ ǀ sá-bharāḥ ǀ ásat ǀ naḥ ǀ nédīyaḥ ǀ ít ǀ sṛṇyáḥ ǀ pakvám ǀ ā́ ǀ iyāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Harness the plural ughs, fit on the yokes, now that the womb of earth is ready, sow the seed therein, andthrough our praise may there be abundant food; may (the grain) fall ripe towards the sickle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सीरा॑ युञ्जन्ति क॒वयो॑ यु॒गा वि त॑न्वते॒ पृथ॑क् । धीरा॑ दे॒वेषु॑ सुम्न॒या
shlokas.transliteration: sī́rā ǀ yuñjanti ǀ kaváyaḥ ǀ yugā́ ǀ ví ǀ tanvate ǀ pṛ́thak ǀdhī́rāḥ ǀ devéṣu ǀ sumna-yā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The wise (priests) harness the plural ughs, they lay the yokes apart, firmly devoted through the desire ofhappiness.”

shlokas.sanskrit: निरा॑हा॒वान्कृ॑णोतन॒ सं व॑र॒त्रा द॑धातन । सि॒ञ्चाम॑हा अव॒तमु॒द्रिणं॑ व॒यं सु॒षेक॒मनु॑पक्षितम्
shlokas.transliteration: níḥ ǀ ā-hāvā́n ǀ kṛṇotana ǀ sám ǀ varatrā́ḥ ǀ dadhātana ǀsiñcā́mahai ǀ avatám ǀ udríṇam ǀ vayám ǀ su-sékam ǀ ánupa-kṣitam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Set up the cattle-troughs, bind the straps to it; let us pour out (the water of) the well, which is full ofwater, fit to be poured out, and not easily exhausted.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इष्कृ॑ताहावमव॒तं सु॑वर॒त्रं सु॑षेच॒नम् । उ॒द्रिणं॑ सिञ्चे॒ अक्षि॑तम्
shlokas.transliteration: íṣkṛta-āhāvam ǀ avatám ǀ su-varatrám ǀ su-secanám ǀudríṇam ǀ siñce ǀ ákṣitam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I pour out (the water of) the well, whose cattle troughs are prepared, well fitted with straps, fit to bepoured out, full of water, inexhaustible.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्री॒णी॒ताश्वा॑न्हि॒तं ज॑याथ स्वस्ति॒वाहं॒ रथ॒मित्कृ॑णुध्वम् । द्रोणा॑हावमव॒तमश्म॑चक्र॒मंस॑त्रकोशं सिञ्चता नृ॒पाण॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: prīṇītá ǀ áśvān ǀ hitám ǀ jayātha ǀ svasti-vā́ham ǀ rátham ǀ ít ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀdróṇa-āhāvam ǀ avatám ǀ áśma-cakram ǀ áṃsatra-kośam ǀ siñcata ǀ nṛ-pā́nam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Satisfy the horses, accomplish the good work (of plural ughing), equip a car laden with good fortune, pourout (the water of) the well, having wooden cattle-troughs having a stone rim, having a receptable like armour, fitfor the drinking of men.”

shlokas.sanskrit: व्र॒जं कृ॑णुध्वं॒ स हि वो॑ नृ॒पाणो॒ वर्म॑ सीव्यध्वं बहु॒ला पृ॒थूनि॑ । पुर॑: कृणुध्व॒माय॑सी॒रधृ॑ष्टा॒ मा व॑: सुस्रोच्चम॒सो दृंह॑ता॒ तम्
shlokas.transliteration: vrajám ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ vaḥ ǀ nṛ-pā́naḥ ǀ várma ǀ sīvyadhvam ǀ bahulā́ ǀ pṛthū́ni ǀpúraḥ ǀ kṛṇudhvam ǀ ā́yasīḥ ǀ ádhṛṣṭāḥ ǀ mā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ susrot ǀ camasáḥ ǀ dṛ́ṃhata ǀ tám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Construct the cow-stall, for that is the drinking plural ce of your leaders (the gods), fabricate armour,manifold and ample; make cities of metal and impregnable; let not the ladle leak, make it strong.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ वो॒ धियं॑ य॒ज्ञियां॑ वर्त ऊ॒तये॒ देवा॑ दे॒वीं य॑ज॒तां य॒ज्ञिया॑मि॒ह । सा नो॑ दुहीय॒द्यव॑सेव ग॒त्वी स॒हस्र॑धारा॒ पय॑सा म॒ही गौः
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ dhíyam ǀ yajñíyām ǀ varte ǀ ūtáye ǀ dévāḥ ǀ devī́m ǀ yajatā́m ǀ yajñíyām ǀ ihá ǀsā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ duhīyat ǀ yávasā-iva ǀ gatvī́ ǀ sahásra-dhārā ǀ páyasā ǀ mahī́ ǀ gáuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “I attract, O gods, for my protection, your adorable, divine mine, which is deserving of sacrifice andworship here; may it milk forth for us, like a large cow with milk, giving a thousand strreams, (having eaten)fodder and returned.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ तू षि॑ञ्च॒ हरि॑मीं॒ द्रोरु॒पस्थे॒ वाशी॑भिस्तक्षताश्म॒न्मयी॑भिः । परि॑ ष्वजध्वं॒ दश॑ क॒क्ष्या॑भिरु॒भे धुरौ॒ प्रति॒ वह्निं॑ युनक्त
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ tú ǀ siñca ǀ hárim ǀ īm ǀ dróḥ ǀ upá-sthe ǀ vā́śībhiḥ ǀ takṣata ǀ aśman-máyībhiḥ ǀpári ǀ svajadhvam ǀ dáśa ǀ kakṣyā́bhiḥ ǀ ubhé íti ǀ dhúrau ǀ práti ǀ váhnim ǀ yunakta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Pour out the golden-tintedSomainto the bowl of the wooden cup, fabricate it with the stone axes, girdit with ten bands, harness the beast of burden to the two poles (of the cart).”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒भे धुरौ॒ वह्नि॑रा॒पिब्द॑मानो॒ऽन्तर्योने॑व चरति द्वि॒जानि॑: । वन॒स्पतिं॒ वन॒ आस्था॑पयध्वं॒ नि षू द॑धिध्व॒मख॑नन्त॒ उत्स॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: ubhé íti ǀ dhúrau ǀ váhniḥ ǀ ā-píbdamānaḥ ǀ antáḥ ǀ yónā-iva ǀ carati ǀ dvi-jā́niḥ ǀvánaspátim ǀ váne ǀ ā́ ǀ asthāpayadhvam ǀ ní ǀ sú ǀ dadhidhvam ǀ ákhanantaḥ ǀ útsam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The beast of burden pressed with the two cart-poles, moves as if on the womb of sacrifice having twowives. plural ce the chariot in the wood, without digging store up theSoma.”

shlokas.sanskrit: कपृ॑न्नरः कपृ॒थमुद्द॑धातन चो॒दय॑त खु॒दत॒ वाज॑सातये । नि॒ष्टि॒ग्र्य॑: पु॒त्रमा च्या॑वयो॒तय॒ इन्द्रं॑ स॒बाध॑ इ॒ह सोम॑पीतये
shlokas.transliteration: kápṛt ǀ naraḥ ǀ kapṛthám ǀ út ǀ dadhātana ǀ codáyata ǀ khudáta ǀ vā́ja-sātaye ǀniṣṭigryáḥ ǀ putrám ǀ ā́ ǀ cyavaya ǀ ūtáye ǀ índram ǀ sa-bā́dhaḥ ǀ ihá ǀ sóma-pītaye ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, you leaders, is the giver of happiness; excite the giver of happiness, stimulate him, sport withhim for the acquisition of food, bring down here, O priests, Indra, the son of Niṣṭigrī, to drink theSoma.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्र ते॒ रथं॑ मिथू॒कृत॒मिन्द्रो॑ऽवतु धृष्णु॒या । अ॒स्मिन्ना॒जौ पु॑रुहूत श्र॒वाय्ये॑ धनभ॒क्षेषु॑ नोऽव
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ te ǀ rátham ǀ mithu-kṛ́tam ǀ índraḥ ǀ avatu ǀ dhṛṣṇu-yā́ ǀasmín ǀ ājáu ǀ puru-hūta ǀ śravā́yye ǀ dhana-bhakṣéṣu ǀ naḥ ǀ ava ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May (Indra) by his prowess protect your cart (mudgala) that has no companion, defend us, O invokedof many, in this memorable conflict in the recovery of our wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उत्स्म॒ वातो॑ वहति॒ वासो॑ऽस्या॒ अधि॑रथं॒ यदज॑यत्स॒हस्र॑म् । र॒थीर॑भून्मुद्ग॒लानी॒ गवि॑ष्टौ॒ भरे॑ कृ॒तं व्य॑चेदिन्द्रसे॒ना
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ sma ǀ vā́taḥ ǀ vahati ǀ vā́saḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ ádhi-ratham ǀ yát ǀ ájayat ǀ sahásram ǀrathī́ḥ ǀ abhūt ǀ mudgalā́nī ǀ gó-iṣṭau ǀ bháre ǀ kṛtám ǀ ví ǀ acet ǀ indra-senā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The wind raised her vesture when she won a thousand cart-loads. Mudgalānī was the charioteer inthe quest of the cattle, the army ofIndrarecovered (the spoil) taken in battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒न्तर्य॑च्छ॒ जिघां॑सतो॒ वज्र॑मिन्द्राभि॒दास॑तः । दास॑स्य वा मघव॒न्नार्य॑स्य वा सनु॒तर्य॑वया व॒धम्
shlokas.transliteration: antáḥ ǀ yaccha ǀ jíghāṃsataḥ ǀ vájram ǀ indra ǀ abhi-dā́sataḥ ǀdā́sasya ǀ vā ǀ magha-van ǀ ā́ryasya ǀ vā ǀ sanutáḥ ǀ yavaya ǀ vadhám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Restrain,Indra, the thunderbolt of the malignant threatening (foe); ward off,Maghavan, the secretweapon (of our foe), be heDāsaorĀrya.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒द्नो ह्र॒दम॑पिब॒ज्जर्हृ॑षाण॒: कूटं॑ स्म तृं॒हद॒भिमा॑तिमेति । प्र मु॒ष्कभा॑र॒: श्रव॑ इ॒च्छमा॑नोऽजि॒रं बा॒हू अ॑भर॒त्सिषा॑सन्
shlokas.transliteration: udnáḥ ǀ hradám ǀ apibat ǀ járhṛṣāṇaḥ ǀ kū́ṭam ǀ sma ǀ tṛṃhát ǀ abhí-mātim ǀ eti ǀprá ǀ muṣká-bhāraḥ ǀ śrávaḥ ǀ icchámānaḥ ǀ ajirám ǀ bāhū́ íti ǀ abharat ǀ sísāsan ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Rejoicing, he drank up the pool of water, he cleft the mountain peak, he went against the enemy;endowed with vigour, eager for fame, assailing the quick-moving (foe), he seized him with his two arms.”

shlokas.sanskrit: न्य॑क्रन्दयन्नुप॒यन्त॑ एन॒ममे॑हयन्वृष॒भं मध्य॑ आ॒जेः । तेन॒ सूभ॑र्वं श॒तव॑त्स॒हस्रं॒ गवां॒ मुद्ग॑लः प्र॒धने॑ जिगाय
shlokas.transliteration: ní ǀ akrandayan ǀ upa-yántaḥ ǀ enam ǀ ámehayan ǀ vṛṣabhám ǀ mádhye ǀ ājéḥ ǀténa ǀ sū́bharvam ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásram ǀ gávām ǀ múdgalaḥ ǀ pra-dháne ǀ jigāya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Approaching the bull, they made him roar in the midst of the battle. I,Mudgala, have thereby gained inwar hundreds and thousands of cattle well- pastured.”

shlokas.sanskrit: क॒कर्द॑वे वृष॒भो यु॒क्त आ॑सी॒दवा॑वची॒त्सार॑थिरस्य के॒शी । दुधे॑र्यु॒क्तस्य॒ द्रव॑तः स॒हान॑स ऋ॒च्छन्ति॑ ष्मा नि॒ष्पदो॑ मुद्ग॒लानी॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: kakárdave ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ yuktáḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ ávāvacīt ǀ sā́rathiḥ ǀ asya ǀ keśī́ ǀdúdheḥ ǀ yuktásya ǀ drávataḥ ǀ sahá ǀ ánasā ǀ ṛcchánti ǀ sma ǀ niḥ-pádaḥ ǀ mudgalā́nīm ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The bull has been yoked for the destruction of the enemy; his long- haired yoke-fellow made him roar;”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒त प्र॒धिमुद॑हन्नस्य वि॒द्वानुपा॑युन॒ग्वंस॑ग॒मत्र॒ शिक्ष॑न् । इन्द्र॒ उदा॑व॒त्पति॒मघ्न्या॑ना॒मरं॑हत॒ पद्या॑भिः क॒कुद्मा॑न्
shlokas.transliteration: utá ǀ pra-dhím ǀ út ǀ ahan ǀ asya ǀ vidvā́n ǀ úpa ǀ ayunak ǀ váṃsagam ǀ átra ǀ śíkṣan ǀíndraḥ ǀ út ǀ āvat ǀ pátim ǀ ághnyānām ǀ áraṃhata ǀ pádyābhiḥ ǀ kakút-mān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The sage (Mudgala) has fitted up the frame of the cart, he has harnessed the bull, training him to hiswork;Indraprotected the lord of the inviolable (cows), the buffalo rushed along with speed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: शु॒नम॑ष्ट्रा॒व्य॑चरत्कप॒र्दी व॑र॒त्रायां॒ दार्वा॒नह्य॑मानः । नृ॒म्णानि॑ कृ॒ण्वन्ब॒हवे॒ जना॑य॒ गाः प॑स्पशा॒नस्तवि॑षीरधत्त
shlokas.transliteration: śunám ǀ aṣṭrā-vī́ ǀ acarat ǀ kapardī́ ǀ varatrā́yām ǀ dā́ru ǀ ā-náhyamānaḥ ǀnṛmṇā́ni ǀ kṛṇván ǀ baháve ǀ jánāya ǀ gā́ḥ ǀ paspaśānáḥ ǀ táviṣīḥ ǀ adhatta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Wielding the goad (Indra) with the braided hair proceeded happily, fastening the strap to the wood (ofwon hundreds and thousands of cattle in war.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मं तं प॑श्य वृष॒भस्य॒ युञ्जं॒ काष्ठा॑या॒ मध्ये॑ द्रुघ॒णं शया॑नम् । येन॑ जि॒गाय॑ श॒तव॑त्स॒हस्रं॒ गवां॒ मुद्ग॑लः पृत॒नाज्ये॑षु
shlokas.transliteration: imám ǀ tám ǀ paśya ǀ vṛṣabhásya ǀ yúñjam ǀ kā́ṣṭhāyāḥ ǀ mádhye ǀ dru-ghanám ǀ śáyānam ǀyéna ǀ jigā́ya ǀ śatá-vat ǀ sahásram ǀ gávām ǀ múdgalaḥ ǀ pṛtanā́jyeṣu ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒रे अ॒घा को न्वि१॒॑त्था द॑दर्श॒ यं यु॒ञ्जन्ति॒ तम्वा स्था॑पयन्ति । नास्मै॒ तृणं॒ नोद॒कमा भ॑र॒न्त्युत्त॑रो धु॒रो व॑हति प्र॒देदि॑शत्
shlokas.transliteration: āré ǀ aghā́ ǀ káḥ ǀ nú ǀ itthā́ ǀ dadarśa ǀ yám ǀ yuñjánti ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ ā́ ǀ sthāpayanti ǀná ǀ asmai ǀ tṛ́ṇam ǀ ná ǀ udakám ǀ ā́ ǀ bharanti ǀ út-taraḥ ǀ dhuráḥ ǀ vahati ǀ pra-dédiśat ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Who has thus beheld the evils near athand? The (bull) which they yoke, they stop; to him they bringneither fodder nor water. Being above (the bull) he bears the chariot-pole announcing (victory to his lord).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प॒रि॒वृ॒क्तेव॑ पति॒विद्य॑मान॒ट् पीप्या॑ना॒ कूच॑क्रेणेव सि॒ञ्चन् । ए॒षै॒ष्या॑ चिद्र॒थ्या॑ जयेम सुम॒ङ्गलं॒ सिन॑वदस्तु सा॒तम्
shlokas.transliteration: parivṛktā́-iva ǀ pati-vídyam ǀ ānaṭ ǀ pī́pyānā ǀ kū́cakreṇa-iva ǀ siñcán ǀeṣa-eṣyā́ ǀ cit ǀ rathyā́ ǀ jayema ǀ su-maṅgálam ǀ sína-vat ǀ astu ǀ sātám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “As a wife who has been abandoned rejoices to find her husband, as a cloud expanding when pouringforth rain with the aid of the earth's disc; with her eager (to recover the cattle) for our charioteer, may we win (theprize), may good fortune, together with food, be given to us.”

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वं विश्व॑स्य॒ जग॑त॒श्चक्षु॑रिन्द्रासि॒ चक्षु॑षः । वृषा॒ यदा॒जिं वृष॑णा॒ सिषा॑ससि चो॒दय॒न्वध्रि॑णा यु॒जा
shlokas.transliteration: tvám ǀ víśvasya ǀ jágataḥ ǀ cákṣuḥ ǀ indra ǀ asi ǀ cákṣuṣaḥ ǀvṛ́ṣā ǀ yát ǀ ājím ǀ vṛ́ṣaṇā ǀ sísāsasi ǀ codáyan ǀ vádhriṇā ǀ yujā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You,Indra, are the eye of the whole world, when, showerer (of benefits), urging on your two vigoroussteeds, harnessed to the car, you engage in battle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒शुः शिशा॑नो वृष॒भो न भी॒मो घ॑नाघ॒नः क्षोभ॑णश्चर्षणी॒नाम् । सं॒क्रन्द॑नोऽनिमि॒ष ए॑कवी॒रः श॒तं सेना॑ अजयत्सा॒कमिन्द्र॑:
shlokas.transliteration: āśúḥ ǀ śíśānaḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ ná ǀ bhīmáḥ ǀ ghanāghanáḥ ǀ kṣóbhaṇaḥ ǀ carṣaṇīnā́m ǀsam-krándanaḥ ǀ ani-miṣáḥ ǀ eka-vīráḥ ǀ śatám ǀ sénāḥ ǀ ajayat ǀ sākám ǀ índraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The fleet-goingIndra, like a formidable bull sharpening (his horns), the slayer of foes, the exciter ofmen, loud-shouting, ever-vigilant, the chief of heroes overthrew at once a hundred hosts.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सं॒क्रन्द॑नेनानिमि॒षेण॑ जि॒ष्णुना॑ युत्का॒रेण॑ दुश्च्यव॒नेन॑ धृ॒ष्णुना॑ । तदिन्द्रे॑ण जयत॒ तत्स॑हध्वं॒ युधो॑ नर॒ इषु॑हस्तेन॒ वृष्णा॑
shlokas.transliteration: sam-krándanena ǀ ani-miṣéṇa ǀ jiṣṇúnā ǀ yut-kāréṇa ǀ duḥ-cyavanéna ǀ dhṛṣṇúnā ǀtát ǀ índreṇa ǀ jayata ǀ tát ǀ sahadhvam ǀ yúdhaḥ ǀ naraḥ ǀ íṣu-hastena ǀ vṛ́ṣṇā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “WithIndrathe loud-shouting, the vigilant, the vigtorious, the warlike, the unconquerable, the daring,the hurler of arrows, the showerer, (as your ally) conquer you warriors, you leaders, that (hostile host) andovercome it.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स इषु॑हस्तै॒: स नि॑ष॒ङ्गिभि॑र्व॒शी संस्र॑ष्टा॒ स युध॒ इन्द्रो॑ ग॒णेन॑ । सं॒सृ॒ष्ट॒जित्सो॑म॒पा बा॑हुश॒र्ध्यु१॒॑ग्रध॑न्वा॒ प्रति॑हिताभि॒रस्ता॑
shlokas.transliteration: sáḥ ǀ íṣu-hastaiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ niṣaṅgí-bhiḥ ǀ vaśī́ ǀ sám-sraṣṭā ǀ sáḥ ǀ yúdhaḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ gaṇéna ǀsaṃsṛṣṭa-jít ǀ soma-pā́ḥ ǀ bāhu-śardhī́ ǀ ugrá-dhanvā ǀ práti-hitābhiḥ ǀ ástā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, with the arrow-bearing (maruts), armed with swords, the subduer, the warrior, who encountershim, the drinker of theSoma, the strong- armed, having a powerful bow, who shoots with well-aimed arrows(conquer with his help).”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृह॑स्पते॒ परि॑ दीया॒ रथे॑न रक्षो॒हामित्राँ॑ अप॒बाध॑मानः । प्र॒भ॒ञ्जन्त्सेना॑: प्रमृ॒णो यु॒धा जय॑न्न॒स्माक॑मेध्यवि॒ता रथा॑नाम्
shlokas.transliteration: bṛ́haspate ǀ pári ǀ dīya ǀ ráthena ǀ rakṣaḥ-hā́ ǀ amítrān ǀ apa-bā́dhamānaḥ ǀpra-bhañján ǀ sénāḥ ǀ pra-mṛṇáḥ ǀ yudhā́ ǀ jáyan ǀ asmā́kam ǀ edhi ǀ avitā́ ǀ ráthānām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Come with your chariot,Bṛhaspati, who are the slayer ofRākṣasas, discomfiting your enemies,”

shlokas.sanskrit: ब॒ल॒वि॒ज्ञा॒यः स्थवि॑र॒: प्रवी॑र॒: सह॑स्वान्वा॒जी सह॑मान उ॒ग्रः । अ॒भिवी॑रो अ॒भिस॑त्वा सहो॒जा जैत्र॑मिन्द्र॒ रथ॒मा ति॑ष्ठ गो॒वित्
shlokas.transliteration: bala-vijñāyáḥ ǀ stháviraḥ ǀ prá-vīraḥ ǀ sáhasvān ǀ vājī́ ǀ sáhamānaḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀabhí-vīraḥ ǀ abhí-satvā ǀ sahaḥ-jā́ḥ ǀ jáitram ǀ indra ǀ rátham ǀ ā́ ǀ tiṣṭha ǀ go-vít ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Known by his strength mighty, heroic, overpowering, vigorous, enduring, fierce, attended by heroes,attended by mighty men, the offspring of strength, the possessor of water, do you,Indra, ascend your triumphantchariot.”

shlokas.sanskrit: गो॒त्र॒भिदं॑ गो॒विदं॒ वज्र॑बाहुं॒ जय॑न्त॒मज्म॑ प्रमृ॒णन्त॒मोज॑सा । इ॒मं स॑जाता॒ अनु॑ वीरयध्व॒मिन्द्रं॑ सखायो॒ अनु॒ सं र॑भध्वम्
shlokas.transliteration: gotra-bhídam ǀ go-vídam ǀ vájra-bāhum ǀ jáyantam ǀ ájma ǀ pra-mṛṇántam ǀ ójasā ǀimám ǀ sa-jātāḥ ǀ ánu ǀ vīrayadhvam ǀ índram ǀ sakhāyaḥ ǀ ánu ǀ sám ǀ rabhadhvam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Imitate in heroism, you kindred warriors, follow, friends, in prowess thisIndra, who is the breaker ofmountains, the acquirer of water, armed with the thunderbolt, conquering the swift (foe), destroying (the enemy)by his might.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒भि गो॒त्राणि॒ सह॑सा॒ गाह॑मानोऽद॒यो वी॒रः श॒तम॑न्यु॒रिन्द्र॑: । दु॒श्च्य॒व॒नः पृ॑तना॒षाळ॑यु॒ध्यो॒३॒॑ऽस्माकं॒ सेना॑ अवतु॒ प्र यु॒त्सु
shlokas.transliteration: abhí ǀ gotrā́ṇi ǀ sáhasā ǀ gā́hamānaḥ ǀ adayáḥ ǀ vīráḥ ǀ śatá-manyuḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀduḥ-cyavanáḥ ǀ pṛtanāṣā́ṭ ǀ ayudhyáḥ ǀ asmā́kam ǀ sénāḥ ǀ avatu ǀ prá ǀ yut-sú ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayIndra, bursting open the clouds with force; pitiless, heroic, with hundredfold anger, invincible, theoverthrower of armies, irresistible, protect our armies in battles.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑ आसां ने॒ता बृह॒स्पति॒र्दक्षि॑णा य॒ज्ञः पु॒र ए॑तु॒ सोम॑: । दे॒व॒से॒नाना॑मभिभञ्जती॒नां जय॑न्तीनां म॒रुतो॑ य॒न्त्वग्र॑म्
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ āsām ǀ netā́ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ puráḥ ǀ etu ǀ sómaḥ ǀdeva-senā́nām ǀ abhi-bhañjatīnā́m ǀ jáyantīnām ǀ marútaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ ágram ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayIndrabe the leader of these (hosts), mayBṛhaspati,Dakṣiṇā,Yajña, andSomago before, lettheMarutsmarch in the van of the destroying and victorious armies of the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑स्य॒ वृष्णो॒ वरु॑णस्य॒ राज्ञ॑ आदि॒त्यानां॑ म॒रुतां॒ शर्ध॑ उ॒ग्रम् । म॒हाम॑नसां भुवनच्य॒वानां॒ घोषो॑ दे॒वानां॒ जय॑ता॒मुद॑स्थात्
shlokas.transliteration: índrasya ǀ vṛ́ṣṇaḥ ǀ váruṇasya ǀ rā́jñaḥ ǀ ādityā́nām ǀ marútām ǀ śárdhaḥ ǀ ugrám ǀmahā́-manasām ǀ bhuvana-cyavā́nām ǀ ghóṣaḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ jáyatām ǀ út ǀ asthāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(May) the mighty force of the showererIndra, of the royalVaruṇa, of theĀdityasandMaruts(beours). The shout of the magnanimous and victorious deities, the subverters of the worlds, has arisen.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उद्ध॑र्षय मघव॒न्नायु॑धा॒न्युत्सत्व॑नां माम॒कानां॒ मनां॑सि । उद्वृ॑त्रहन्वा॒जिनां॒ वाजि॑ना॒न्युद्रथा॑नां॒ जय॑तां यन्तु॒ घोषा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: út ǀ harṣaya ǀ magha-van ǀ ā́yudhāni ǀ út ǀ sátvanām ǀ māmakā́nām ǀ mánāṃsi ǀút ǀ vṛtra-han ǀ vājínām ǀ vā́jināni ǀ út ǀ ráthānām ǀ jáyatām ǀ yantu ǀ ghóṣāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Excite,Maghavan, my weapons, (excite) the spirits of my heroes; slayer ofVṛtra, let the speed of thehorses be accelerated, let the noises of the chariots be increased.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒स्माक॒मिन्द्र॒: समृ॑तेषु ध्व॒जेष्व॒स्माकं॒ या इष॑व॒स्ता ज॑यन्तु । अ॒स्माकं॑ वी॒रा उत्त॑रे भवन्त्व॒स्माँ उ॑ देवा अवता॒ हवे॑षु
shlokas.transliteration: asmā́kam ǀ índraḥ ǀ sám-ṛteṣu ǀ dhvajéṣu ǀ asmā́kam ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ íṣavaḥ ǀ tā́ḥ ǀ jayantu ǀasmā́kam ǀ vīrā́ḥ ǀ út-tare ǀ bhavantu ǀ asmā́n ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ devāḥ ǀ avata ǀ háveṣu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When the banners are intermingled, mayIndrabe our (defender), may those arrows which are ours bevictorious may our warriors be triumphant; gods, protect us in battles.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒मीषां॑ चि॒त्तं प्र॑तिलो॒भय॑न्ती गृहा॒णाङ्गा॑न्यप्वे॒ परे॑हि । अ॒भि प्रेहि॒ निर्द॑ह हृ॒त्सु शोकै॑र॒न्धेना॒मित्रा॒स्तम॑सा सचन्ताम्
shlokas.transliteration: amī́ṣām ǀ cittám ǀ prati-lobháyantī ǀ gṛhāṇá ǀ áṅgāni ǀ apve ǀ párā ǀ ihi ǀabhí ǀ prá ǀ ihi ǀ níḥ ǀ daha ǀ hṛt-sú ǀ śókaiḥ ǀ andhéna ǀ amítrāḥ ǀ támasā ǀ sacantām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Bewildering the mind of our foes, Apva, seize their limbs and depart, proceed against them, burn intheir hearts with sorrow, let our enemies be covered with thick darkness.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रेता॒ जय॑ता नर॒ इन्द्रो॑ व॒: शर्म॑ यच्छतु । उ॒ग्रा व॑: सन्तु बा॒हवो॑ऽनाधृ॒ष्या यथास॑थ
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ ita ǀ jáyata ǀ naraḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ śárma ǀ yacchatu ǀugrā́ḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ santu ǀ bāhávaḥ ǀ anādhṛṣyā́ḥ ǀ yáthā ǀ ásatha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Advance, warriors, and conquer; mayIndragrant you happiness, may your arms be strong, so that youmay be invincible.”

shlokas.sanskrit: असा॑वि॒ सोम॑: पुरुहूत॒ तुभ्यं॒ हरि॑भ्यां य॒ज्ञमुप॑ याहि॒ तूय॑म् । तुभ्यं॒ गिरो॒ विप्र॑वीरा इया॒ना द॑धन्वि॒र इ॑न्द्र॒ पिबा॑ सु॒तस्य॑
shlokas.transliteration: ásāvi ǀ sómaḥ ǀ puru-hūta ǀ túbhyam ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ yajñám ǀ úpa ǀ yāhi ǀ tū́yam ǀtúbhyam ǀ gíraḥ ǀ vípra-vīrāḥ ǀ iyānā́ḥ ǀ dadhanviré ǀ indra ǀ píba ǀ sutásya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “TheSomahas been effused for you, (Indra), the invoked of many, come quickly to the sacrifice withyour two bay horses; our praises recited by the wise, moving quickly, are addressed to you; drink, Indra, of thelibation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒प्सु धू॒तस्य॑ हरिव॒: पिबे॒ह नृभि॑: सु॒तस्य॑ ज॒ठरं॑ पृणस्व । मि॒मि॒क्षुर्यमद्र॑य इन्द्र॒ तुभ्यं॒ तेभि॑र्वर्धस्व॒ मद॑मुक्थवाहः
shlokas.transliteration: ap-sú ǀ dhūtásya ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ píba ǀ ihá ǀ nṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ sutásya ǀ jaṭháram ǀ pṛṇasva ǀmimikṣúḥ ǀ yám ǀ ádrayaḥ ǀ indra ǀ túbhyam ǀ tébhiḥ ǀ vardhasva ǀ mádam ǀ uktha-vāhaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lord of bay steeds, drink at this ceremony of theSomathat has been shaken up with the water, fillyour belly with the libation offered by the priests, which the grinding-stones desired to express for you,Indra; doyou who are carried by hymns enhance your exhilaration with these (hymns).”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रोग्रां पी॒तिं वृष्ण॑ इयर्मि स॒त्यां प्र॒यै सु॒तस्य॑ हर्यश्व॒ तुभ्य॑म् । इन्द्र॒ धेना॑भिरि॒ह मा॑दयस्व धी॒भिर्विश्वा॑भि॒: शच्या॑ गृणा॒नः
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ ugrā́m ǀ pītím ǀ vṛ́ṣṇe ǀ iyarmi ǀ satyā́m ǀ pra-yái ǀ sutásya ǀ hari-aśva ǀ túbhyam ǀíndra ǀ dhénābhiḥ ǀ ihá ǀ mādayasva ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ víśvābhiḥ ǀ śácyā ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lord of bay steeds, showerer (of benefits), I send you strong good drink that you may proceed;Indra,who are glorified for your prowess, be exhilarated at this (ceremony) with praises, with all rites.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊ॒ती श॑चीव॒स्तव॑ वी॒र्ये॑ण॒ वयो॒ दधा॑ना उ॒शिज॑ ऋत॒ज्ञाः । प्र॒जाव॑दिन्द्र॒ मनु॑षो दुरो॒णे त॒स्थुर्गृ॒णन्त॑: सध॒माद्या॑सः
shlokas.transliteration: ūtī́ ǀ śacī-vaḥ ǀ táva ǀ vīryéṇa ǀ váyaḥ ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ uśíjaḥ ǀ ṛta-jñā́ḥ ǀprajā́-vat ǀ indra ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ tasthúḥ ǀ gṛṇántaḥ ǀ sadha-mā́dyāsaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “PowerfulIndra, they stood in the dwelling of the man (who instrumental tuted the rite), enjoying food togetherwith the offspring, through your protection and prowess, desiring you, knowing the ceremonies, glorifying you,and partaking of the exhilaration.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रणी॑तिभिष्टे हर्यश्व सु॒ष्टोः सु॑षु॒म्नस्य॑ पुरु॒रुचो॒ जना॑सः । मंहि॑ष्ठामू॒तिं वि॒तिरे॒ दधा॑ना स्तो॒तार॑ इन्द्र॒ तव॑ सू॒नृता॑भिः
shlokas.transliteration: pránīti-bhiḥ ǀ te ǀ hari-aśva ǀ su-stóḥ ǀ su-sumnásya ǀ puru-rúcaḥ ǀ jánāsaḥ ǀmáṃhiṣṭhām ǀ ūtím ǀ vi-tíre ǀ dádhānāḥ ǀ stotā́raḥ ǀ indra ǀ táva ǀ sūnṛ́tābhiḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lord of bay horses, by the right guidance of you who are deservedly praised, the bestower ofhappiness the illustrious, the men your praisers, OIndra, have acquired your most gracious assistance forexcelling (other suppliants) through your favours.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि हरिवो॒ हरि॑भ्यां॒ सोम॑स्य याहि पी॒तये॑ सु॒तस्य॑ । इन्द्र॑ त्वा य॒ज्ञः क्षम॑माणमानड्दा॒श्वाँ अ॑स्यध्व॒रस्य॑ प्रके॒तः
shlokas.transliteration: úpa ǀ bráhmāṇi ǀ hari-vaḥ ǀ hári-bhyām ǀ sómasya ǀ yāhi ǀ pītáye ǀ sutásya ǀíndra ǀ tvā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ kṣámamāṇam ǀ ānaṭ ǀ dāśvā́n ǀ asi ǀ adhvarásya ǀ pra-ketáḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Lord of bay horses, come with your two bays to our adorations to drink of the effusedSoma; thesacrifice,Indra, reaches to you who are enduring; cognizant of the sacrifice, you are the donor of the reward.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒हस्र॑वाजमभिमाति॒षाहं॑ सु॒तेर॑णं म॒घवा॑नं सुवृ॒क्तिम् । उप॑ भूषन्ति॒ गिरो॒ अप्र॑तीत॒मिन्द्रं॑ नम॒स्या ज॑रि॒तुः प॑नन्त
shlokas.transliteration: sahásra-vājam ǀ abhimāti-sáham ǀ suté-raṇam ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ su-vṛktím ǀúpa ǀ bhūṣanti ǀ gíraḥ ǀ áprati-itam ǀ índram ǀ namasyā́ḥ ǀ jaritúḥ ǀ pananta ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Our praises celebrate the irresistibleIndra, the dispenser of abundant food, the overcomer of enemies,the delighter in the libation, the possessor of opulence, the well-praised; the adorations of the worshipper glorify(him).”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒प्तापो॑ दे॒वीः सु॒रणा॒ अमृ॑क्ता॒ याभि॒: सिन्धु॒मत॑र इन्द्र पू॒र्भित् । न॒व॒तिं स्रो॒त्या नव॑ च॒ स्रव॑न्तीर्दे॒वेभ्यो॑ गा॒तुं मनु॑षे च विन्दः
shlokas.transliteration: saptá ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ su-ráṇāḥ ǀ ámṛktāḥ ǀ yā́bhiḥ ǀ síndhum ǀ átaraḥ ǀ indra ǀ pūḥ-bhít ǀnavatím ǀ srotyā́ḥ ǀ náva ǀ ca ǀ srávantīḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ gātúm ǀ mánuṣe ǀ ca ǀ vindaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The seven divine meandering rivers with which you,Indra, the destroyer of cities, replenished theocean, flow unimpeded; you did discover the nine-and-ninety flowing rivers (and their) path for gods and men.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒पो म॒हीर॒भिश॑स्तेरमु॒ञ्चोऽजा॑गरा॒स्वधि॑ दे॒व एक॑: । इन्द्र॒ यास्त्वं वृ॑त्र॒तूर्ये॑ च॒कर्थ॒ ताभि॑र्वि॒श्वायु॑स्त॒न्वं॑ पुपुष्याः
shlokas.transliteration: apáḥ ǀ mahī́ḥ ǀ abhí-śasteḥ ǀ amuñcaḥ ǀ ájāgaḥ ǀ āsu ǀ ádhi ǀ deváḥ ǀ ékaḥ ǀíndra ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ tvám ǀ vṛtra-tū́rye ǀ cakártha ǀ tā́bhiḥ ǀ viśvá-āyuḥ ǀ tanvám ǀ pupuṣyāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You did release the great waters from the malignant (obstructer), you were the only god who watchedover them; with those waters which you have employed for the destruction ofVṛtra, may you, all vivifyingIndra,cherish your own person n.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वी॒रेण्य॒: क्रतु॒रिन्द्र॑: सुश॒स्तिरु॒तापि॒ धेना॑ पुरुहू॒तमी॑ट्टे । आर्द॑यद्वृ॒त्रमकृ॑णोदु लो॒कं स॑सा॒हे श॒क्रः पृत॑ना अभि॒ष्टिः
shlokas.transliteration: vīréṇyaḥ ǀ krátuḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ su-śastíḥ ǀ utá ǀ ápi ǀ dhénā ǀ puru-hūtám ǀ īṭṭe ǀā́rdayat ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ákṛṇot ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ lokám ǀ sasahé ǀ śakráḥ ǀ pṛ́tanāḥ ǀ abhiṣṭíḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrais the chief of heroes, the doer of great deeds, to whom praise is well offered; yes, and the voiceof praise lauds him the invoked of many. He slewVṛtra, he created light;Śakra, the conqueror, has overcome(hostile) hosts.”

shlokas.sanskrit: शु॒नं हु॑वेम म॒घवा॑न॒मिन्द्र॑म॒स्मिन्भरे॒ नृत॑मं॒ वाज॑सातौ । शृ॒ण्वन्त॑मु॒ग्रमू॒तये॑ स॒मत्सु॒ घ्नन्तं॑ वृ॒त्राणि॑ सं॒जितं॒ धना॑नाम्
shlokas.transliteration: śunám ǀ huvema ǀ maghá-vānam ǀ índram ǀ asmín ǀ bháre ǀ nṛ́-tamam ǀ vā́ja-sātau ǀśṛṇvántam ǀ ugrám ǀ ūtáye ǀ samát-su ǀ ghnántam ǀ vṛtrā́ṇi ǀ sam-jítam ǀ dhánānām ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “We invoke for our protection the opulentIndra, distinguished in this combat; the leader in thefood-bestowing strife, hearing (our praises), terrible in battles the destroyer of foes, the conqueror of wealth.”

shlokas.sanskrit: क॒दा व॑सो स्तो॒त्रं हर्य॑त॒ आव॑ श्म॒शा रु॑ध॒द्वाः । दी॒र्घं सु॒तं वा॒ताप्या॑य
shlokas.transliteration: kadā́ ǀ vaso íti ǀ stotrám ǀ háryate ǀ ā́ ǀ áva ǀ śmaśā́ ǀ rudhat ǀ vā́ríti vā́ḥ ǀdīrghám ǀ sutám ǀ vātā́pyāya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When,Vasu, (will our) praise (reach) you desiring it? (when) will he, (like) a dam, obstruct and letloose the long-protracted for the sake of wind- driven (rain)?”

shlokas.sanskrit: हरी॒ यस्य॑ सु॒युजा॒ विव्र॑ता॒ वेरर्व॒न्तानु॒ शेपा॑ । उ॒भा र॒जी न के॒शिना॒ पति॒र्दन्
shlokas.transliteration: hárī íti ǀ yásya ǀ su-yújā ǀ ví-vratā ǀ véḥ ǀ árvantā ǀ ánu ǀ śépā ǀubhā́ ǀ rajī́ íti ǀ ná ǀ keśínā ǀ pátiḥ ǀ dán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(OIndra), to whom belong the two bay horses, well-trained, active, swift, courageous, brilliant as thetwo worlds, do you, who are lord (of bay horses), bestowing (wealth upon us), desire (our praises).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अप॒ योरिन्द्र॒: पाप॑ज॒ आ मर्तो॒ न श॑श्रमा॒णो बि॑भी॒वान् । शु॒भे यद्यु॑यु॒जे तवि॑षीवान्
shlokas.transliteration: ápa ǀ yóḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ pā́paje ǀ ā́ ǀ mártaḥ ǀ ná ǀ śaśramāṇáḥ ǀ bibhīvā́n ǀśubhé ǀ yát ǀ yuyujé ǀ táviṣī-vān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indrarepelled (him), being like a mortal tired and frightened in (the combat with) the offspring ofiniquity (Vṛtra), when being associated with the forces (of theMaruts), he has been prepared for splendour.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सचा॒योरिन्द्र॒श्चर्कृ॑ष॒ आँ उ॑पान॒सः स॑प॒र्यन् । न॒दयो॒र्विव्र॑तयो॒: शूर॒ इन्द्र॑:
shlokas.transliteration: sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǀ índraḥ ǀ cárkṛṣe ǀ ā́ ǀ upānasáḥ ǀ saparyán ǀnadáyoḥ ǀ ví-vratayoḥ ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ índraḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, the friend of man, for his exhilaration, comes mounted in his chariot, granting him favour, thehero Indra, (the driver) of the two neighing and prancing (steeds).”

shlokas.sanskrit: अधि॒ यस्त॒स्थौ केश॑वन्ता॒ व्यच॑स्वन्ता॒ न पु॒ष्ट्यै । व॒नोति॒ शिप्रा॑भ्यां शि॒प्रिणी॑वान्
shlokas.transliteration: ádhi ǀ yáḥ ǀ tastháu ǀ kéśa-vantā ǀ vyácasvantā ǀ ná ǀ puṣṭyái ǀvanóti ǀ śíprābhyām ǀ śipríṇī-vān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He who has mounted the two long-maned and all pervading steeds for the nourishment (of thesacrificer) asks (for theSoma) with his two jaws, possessing mighty jaws.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रास्तौ॑दृ॒ष्वौजा॑ ऋ॒ष्वेभि॑स्त॒तक्ष॒ शूर॒: शव॑सा । ऋ॒भुर्न क्रतु॑भिर्मात॒रिश्वा॑
shlokas.transliteration: prá ǀ astaut ǀ ṛṣvá-ojāḥ ǀ ṛṣvébhiḥ ǀ tatákṣa ǀ śū́raḥ ǀ śávasā ǀṛbhúḥ ǀ ná ǀ krátu-bhiḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Of glorious strength (associated) with the glorious (maruts) he was renowned; the hero abiding in thefirmament wrought with his strength as theṚbhuswith their wonderful works.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वज्रं॒ यश्च॒क्रे सु॒हना॑य॒ दस्य॑वे हिरीम॒शो हिरी॑मान् । अरु॑तहनु॒रद्भु॑तं॒ न रज॑:
shlokas.transliteration: vájram ǀ yáḥ ǀ cakré ǀ su-hánāya ǀ dásyave ǀ hirīmaśáḥ ǀ hírīmān ǀáruta-hanuḥ ǀ ádbhutam ǀ ná ǀ rájaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The golden-bearded (Indra), lord of bay horses, who made the thunderbolt for the easy destruction oftheDasyu, who has irresistible jaws like the vast firmament.”

shlokas.sanskrit: अव॑ नो वृजि॒ना शि॑शीह्यृ॒चा व॑नेमा॒नृच॑: । नाब्र॑ह्मा य॒ज्ञ ऋध॒ग्जोष॑ति॒ त्वे
shlokas.transliteration: áva ǀ naḥ ǀ vṛjinā́ ǀ śiśīhi ǀ ṛcā́ ǀ vanema ǀ anṛ́caḥ ǀná ǀ ábrahmā ǀ yajñáḥ ǀ ṛ́dhak ǀ jóṣati ǀ tvé íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Mitigate,Indra, our iniquities, may we, by our hymns, extermiante those who offer no hymns. Thesacrifice, unaccompanied by prayer, distinct (from that which is performed with prayer), is not grateful to you. in the hall of sacrifice, accompanied by the sacrifice, you, the friend of man, (ascend) the vessel of your glory.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऊ॒र्ध्वा यत्ते॑ त्रे॒तिनी॒ भूद्य॒ज्ञस्य॑ धू॒र्षु सद्म॑न् । स॒जूर्नावं॒ स्वय॑शसं॒ सचा॒योः
shlokas.transliteration: ūrdhvā́ ǀ yát ǀ te ǀ tretínī ǀ bhū́t ǀ yajñásya ǀ dhūḥ-sú ǀ sádman ǀsa-jū́ḥ ǀ nā́vam ǀ svá-yaśasam ǀ sácā ǀ āyóḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: श्रि॒ये ते॒ पृश्नि॑रुप॒सेच॑नी भूच्छ्रि॒ये दर्वि॑ररे॒पाः । यया॒ स्वे पात्रे॑ सि॒ञ्चस॒ उत्
shlokas.transliteration: śriyé ǀ te ǀ pṛ́śniḥ ǀ upa-sécanī ǀ bhūt ǀ śriyé ǀ dárviḥ ǀ arepā́ḥ ǀyáyā ǀ své ǀ pā́tre ǀ siñcáse ǀ út ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the spotted cow yield milk for mixing with your (Soma), may the ladle for the mixture wherewithyou pour it into your own vessel be free from defect.”

shlokas.sanskrit: श॒तं वा॒ यद॑सुर्य॒ प्रति॑ त्वा सुमि॒त्र इ॒त्थास्तौ॑द्दुर्मि॒त्र इ॒त्थास्तौ॑त् । आवो॒ यद्द॑स्यु॒हत्ये॑ कुत्सपु॒त्रं प्रावो॒ यद्द॑स्यु॒हत्ये॑ कुत्सव॒त्सम्
shlokas.transliteration: śatám ǀ vā ǀ yát ǀ asurya ǀ práti ǀ tvā ǀ su-mitráḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ astaut ǀ duḥ-mitráḥ ǀ itthā́ ǀ astaut ǀā́vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ dasyu-hátye ǀ kutsa-putrám ǀ prá ǀ ā́vaḥ ǀ yát ǀ dasyu-hátye ǀ kutsa-vatsám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “When, you, mighty (Indra, gave) hundredfold (riches),Sumitrapraised you thus,Durmitrapraised youthus, when at the slaughter of theDasyusyou did protectKutsa's son, when at the slaughter of the Dasyus youprotected Kutsa's darling.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒भा उ॑ नू॒नं तदिद॑र्थयेथे॒ वि त॑न्वाथे॒ धियो॒ वस्त्रा॒पसे॑व । स॒ध्री॒ची॒ना यात॑वे॒ प्रेम॑जीगः सु॒दिने॑व॒ पृक्ष॒ आ तं॑सयेथे
shlokas.transliteration: ubháu ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ nūnám ǀ tát ǀ ít ǀ arthayethe íti ǀ ví ǀ tanvāthe íti ǀ dhíyaḥ ǀ vástrā ǀ apásā-iva ǀsadhrīcīnā́ ǀ yā́tave ǀ prá ǀ īm ǀ ajīgaríti ǀ sudínā-iva ǀ pṛ́kṣaḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ taṃsayethe íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You both demand the oblation (Aśvins), you spread out the ceremonials as two weavers (strentch)cloths; (the instrumental tutor of the rite) praised you associated together to attain (his desires); like two fortunate daysyou bestow food.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒ष्टारे॑व॒ फर्व॑रेषु श्रयेथे प्रायो॒गेव॒ श्वात्र्या॒ शासु॒रेथ॑: । दू॒तेव॒ हि ष्ठो य॒शसा॒ जने॑षु॒ माप॑ स्थातं महि॒षेवा॑व॒पाना॑त्
shlokas.transliteration: uṣṭā́rā-iva ǀ phárvareṣu ǀ śrayethe íti ǀ prāyogā́-iva ǀ śvā́tryā ǀ śā́suḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ ithaḥ ǀdūtā́-iva ǀ hí ǀ stháḥ ǀ yaśásā ǀ jáneṣu ǀ mā́ ǀ ápa ǀ sthātam ǀ mahiṣā́-iva ǀ ava-pā́nāt ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Like two longing oxen (to the pastures), you have recourse to those who fill you (with oblations); youapproach like two horses prepared for the fray; employed to bring treasure; you are like two (royal) messengersrenowned among the people; turn not away (from our oblation) like two buffaloes from the drinking-trough.”

shlokas.sanskrit: सा॒कं॒युजा॑ शकु॒नस्ये॑व प॒क्षा प॒श्वेव॑ चि॒त्रा यजु॒रा ग॑मिष्टम् । अ॒ग्निरि॑व देव॒योर्दी॑दि॒वांसा॒ परि॑ज्मानेव यजथः पुरु॒त्रा
shlokas.transliteration: sākam-yújā ǀ śakunásya-iva ǀ pakṣā́ ǀ paśvā́-iva ǀ citrā́ ǀ yájuḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ gamiṣṭam ǀagníḥ-iva ǀ deva-yóḥ ǀ dīdi-vā́ṃsā ǀ párijmānā-iva ǀ yajathaḥ ǀ puru-trā́ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Connected toegether like the two wings of a bird, you came to the sacrifice like two choice animals;radiant asAgni(at the offering) of the devout (worshipper), like two perambulating priests you celebrate worshipin many plural ces.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒पी वो॑ अ॒स्मे पि॒तरे॑व पु॒त्रोग्रेव॑ रु॒चा नृ॒पती॑व तु॒र्यै । इर्ये॑व पु॒ष्ट्यै कि॒रणे॑व भु॒ज्यै श्रु॑ष्टी॒वाने॑व॒ हव॒मा ग॑मिष्टम्
shlokas.transliteration: āpī́ íti ǀ vaḥ ǀ asmé íti ǀ pitárā-iva ǀ putrā́ ǀ ugrā́-iva ǀ rucā́ ǀ nṛpátī ivéti nṛpátī-iva ǀ turyái ǀíryā-iva ǀ puṣṭyái ǀ kiráṇā-iva ǀ bhujyái ǀ śruṣṭīvā́nā-iva ǀ hávam ǀ ā́ ǀ gamiṣṭam ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You are kinsmen to us, like parents (to) sons, like two fierce shining fires, like two princes hastening togive protection, like two bestowers of food are you for the nourishment of men, like two luminaries for theenjoyment (of our worshippers), like two quick horses you came to our invocation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वंस॑गेव पूष॒र्या॑ शि॒म्बाता॑ मि॒त्रेव॑ ऋ॒ता श॒तरा॒ शात॑पन्ता । वाजे॑वो॒च्चा वय॑सा घर्म्ये॒ष्ठा मेषे॑वे॒षा स॑प॒र्या॒३॒॑ पुरी॑षा
shlokas.transliteration: váṃsagā-iva ǀ pūṣaryā́ ǀ śimbā́tā ǀ mitrā́-íva ǀ ṛtā́ ǀ śatárā ǀ śā́tapantā ǀvā́jā-iva ǀ uccā́ ǀ váyasā ǀ gharmye-sthā́ ǀ méṣā-iva ǀ iṣā́ ǀ saparyā́ ǀ púrīṣā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You are like two plural asantly moving well-fed (hills) likeMitraandVaruṇa, the two bestowers of felicity,veracious, possessors of infinite wealth, happy, like two horses plural mp with fodder, abiding in the firmament, liketwo rams (are you) to be nourished with sacrificial food, to be cherished (with oblations).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सृ॒ण्ये॑व ज॒र्भरी॑ तु॒र्फरी॑तू नैतो॒शेव॑ तु॒र्फरी॑ पर्फ॒रीका॑ । उ॒द॒न्य॒जेव॒ जेम॑ना मदे॒रू ता मे॑ ज॒राय्व॒जरं॑ म॒रायु॑
shlokas.transliteration: sṛṇyā́-iva ǀ jarbhárī íti ǀ turphárītū íti ǀ naitośā́-iva ǀ turphárī íti ǀ parpharī́kā ǀudanyajā́-iva ǀ jémanā ǀ maderū́ íti ǀ tā́ ǀ me ǀ jarā́yu ǀ ajáram ǀ marā́yu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “You are like two mad elephants bending their forequarters and smiting the foe, like the two sons ofare victorious, (render) my decaying mortal body free from decay.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प॒ज्रेव॒ चर्च॑रं॒ जारं॑ म॒रायु॒ क्षद्मे॒वार्थे॑षु तर्तरीथ उग्रा । ऋ॒भू नाप॑त्खरम॒ज्रा ख॒रज्रु॑र्वा॒युर्न प॑र्फरत्क्षयद्रयी॒णाम्
shlokas.transliteration: pajrā́-iva ǀ cárcaram ǀ jā́ram ǀ marā́yu ǀ kṣádma-iva ǀ ártheṣu ǀ tartarīthaḥ ǀ ugrā ǀṛbhū́ íti ǀ ná ǀ āpat ǀ kharamajrā́ ǀ khará-jruḥ ǀ vāyúḥ ǀ ná ǀ parpharat ǀ kṣayat ǀ rayīṇā́m ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Fierce (Aśvins), like two powerful (heroes), you enable this moving, perishable mortal (frame) to crossover to the objects (of its destination) as over water; extremely strong, like theṚbhus, your chariot attained itsdestination swift as the wind, it pervaded (everywhere), it dispensed riches.”

shlokas.sanskrit: घ॒र्मेव॒ मधु॑ ज॒ठरे॑ स॒नेरू॒ भगे॑विता तु॒र्फरी॒ फारि॒वार॑म् । प॒त॒रेव॑ चच॒रा च॒न्द्रनि॑र्णि॒ङ्मन॑ऋङ्गा मन॒न्या॒३॒॑ न जग्मी॑
shlokas.transliteration: gharmā́-iva ǀ mádhu ǀ jaṭháre ǀ sanérū íti ǀ bháge-avitā ǀ turphárī íti ǀ phā́rivā ǀ áram ǀpatarā́-iva ǀ cacarā́ ǀ candrá-nirnik ǀ mánaḥ-ṛṅgā ǀ mananyā́ ǀ ná ǀ jágmī íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “With your bellies full of theSoma, like two saucepans, preservers of wealth, destroyers of enemies,(you are), armed with hatchets, moving like two flying (birds) with forms like the moon, attaining success throughthe mind, like two laudable beings, (you are) approaching (the sacrifice).”

shlokas.sanskrit: बृ॒हन्ते॑व ग॒म्भरे॑षु प्रति॒ष्ठां पादे॑व गा॒धं तर॑ते विदाथः । कर्णे॑व॒ शासु॒रनु॒ हि स्मरा॒थोंऽशे॑व नो भजतं चि॒त्रमप्न॑:
shlokas.transliteration: bṛhántā-iva ǀ gambháreṣu ǀ prati-sthā́m ǀ pā́dā-iva ǀ gādhám ǀ tárate ǀ vidāthaḥ ǀkárṇā-iva ǀ śā́suḥ ǀ ánu ǀ hí ǀ smárāthaḥ ǀ áṃśā-iva ǀ naḥ ǀ bhajatam ǀ citrám ǀ ápnaḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒र॒ङ्ग॒रेव॒ मध्वेर॑येथे सार॒घेव॒ गवि॑ नी॒चीन॑बारे । की॒नारे॑व॒ स्वेद॑मासिष्विदा॒ना क्षामे॑वो॒र्जा सू॑यव॒सात्स॑चेथे
shlokas.transliteration: āraṅgarā́-iva ǀ mádhu ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayethe íti ǀ sāraghā́-iva ǀ gávi ǀ nīcī́na-bāre ǀkīnā́rā-iva ǀ svédam ǀ ā-sisvidānā́ ǀ kṣā́ma-iva ǀ ūrjā́ ǀ suyavasa-át ǀ sacethe íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Like two loud-sounding (clouds), you send forth the sweet (Soma); like two bees (you deposit milk) in(the udder of) the cow which has its opening turned downwards; like two labourers you are dripping withperspiration, like a tired cow eating sweet herbage, you attend.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒ध्याम॒ स्तोमं॑ सनु॒याम॒ वाज॒मा नो॒ मन्त्रं॑ स॒रथे॒होप॑ यातम् । यशो॒ न प॒क्वं मधु॒ गोष्व॒न्तरा भू॒तांशो॑ अ॒श्विनो॒: काम॑मप्राः
shlokas.transliteration: ṛdhyā́ma ǀ stómam ǀ sanuyā́ma ǀ vā́jam ǀ ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ mántram ǀ sa-ráthā ǀ ihá ǀ úpa ǀ yātam ǀyáśaḥ ǀ ná ǀ pakvám ǀ mádhu ǀ góṣu ǀ antáḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ bhūtá-aṃśaḥ ǀ aśvínoḥ ǀ kā́mam ǀ aprāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May we increase our praise, (Aśvins), may we offer you food, come hither in the same chariot to ourworship; and accept the sweet food prepared from within the cows. Bhūtāṃs;a has fulfilled the desires of thelearned.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒विर॑भू॒न्महि॒ माघो॑नमेषां॒ विश्वं॑ जी॒वं तम॑सो॒ निर॑मोचि । महि॒ ज्योति॑: पि॒तृभि॑र्द॒त्तमागा॑दु॒रुः पन्था॒ दक्षि॑णाया अदर्शि
shlokas.transliteration: āvíḥ ǀ abhūt ǀ máhi ǀ mā́ghonam ǀ eṣām ǀ víśvam ǀ jīvám ǀ támasaḥ ǀ níḥ ǀ amoci ǀmáhi ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pitṛ́-bhiḥ ǀ dattám ǀ ā́ ǀ agāt ǀ urúḥ ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀ adarśi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The great (splendour) ofMaghavanhas becomemanifest (for the rites) of these (worshippers); all lifehas been extricated from darkness, the vast light bestowed by the progenitors has arrived, a spacious path forthedakṣiṇāhas been displayed. (I Maghavan: Mqaghavan = the sun, at whose rising and at midday thedakṣiṇā is to be given, not at sunset; cf. RV. 5.77.2].”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒च्चा दि॒वि दक्षि॑णावन्तो अस्थु॒र्ये अ॑श्व॒दाः स॒ह ते सूर्ये॑ण । हि॒र॒ण्य॒दा अ॑मृत॒त्वं भ॑जन्ते वासो॒दाः सो॑म॒ प्र ति॑रन्त॒ आयु॑:
shlokas.transliteration: uccā́ ǀ diví ǀ dákṣiṇā-vantaḥ ǀ asthuḥ ǀ yé ǀ aśva-dā́ḥ ǀ sahá ǀ té ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀhiraṇya-dā́ḥ ǀ amṛta-tvám ǀ bhajante ǀ vāsaḥ-dā́ḥ ǀ soma ǀ prá ǀ tirante ǀ ā́yuḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Saramā). I come, the appointed messenger ofIndra, desiring,Paṇis, your great hidden treasures;through fear of being crossed the (water) helped us, thus I passed over the waters of theRasā.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दैवी॑ पू॒र्तिर्दक्षि॑णा देवय॒ज्या न क॑वा॒रिभ्यो॑ न॒हि ते पृ॒णन्ति॑ । अथा॒ नर॒: प्रय॑तदक्षिणासोऽवद्यभि॒या ब॒हव॑: पृणन्ति
shlokas.transliteration: dáivī ǀ pūrtíḥ ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ deva-yajyā́ ǀ ná ǀ kava-aríbhyaḥ ǀ nahí ǀ té ǀ pṛṇánti ǀátha ǀ náraḥ ǀ práyata-dakṣiṇāsaḥ ǀ avadya-bhiyā́ ǀ bahávaḥ ǀ pṛṇanti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(ThePaṇis). What isIndralike, OSaramā? What is the appearance of him as whose messenger youhave come to this plural ce from afar? (They then say to one another:) Let her approach; let us make friends withher, and let her be the lord of our cattle.”

shlokas.sanskrit: श॒तधा॑रं वा॒युम॒र्कं स्व॒र्विदं॑ नृ॒चक्ष॑स॒स्ते अ॒भि च॑क्षते ह॒विः । ये पृ॒णन्ति॒ प्र च॒ यच्छ॑न्ति संग॒मे ते दक्षि॑णां दुहते स॒प्तमा॑तरम्
shlokas.transliteration: śatá-dhāram ǀ vāyúm ǀ arkám ǀ svaḥ-vídam ǀ nṛ-cákṣasaḥ ǀ té ǀ abhí ǀ cakṣate ǀ havíḥ ǀyé ǀ pṛṇánti ǀ prá ǀ ca ǀ yácchanti ǀ sam-gamé ǀ té ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ duhate ǀ saptá-mātaram ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Saramā). I do not believe that he can be subdued; he as whose messenger I have come to thisplace from afar subdues (his enemies). The deep rivers do not conceal him; you,Paṇis, slain byIndra, will sleep(in death).”

shlokas.sanskrit: दक्षि॑णावान्प्रथ॒मो हू॒त ए॑ति॒ दक्षि॑णावान्ग्राम॒णीरग्र॑मेति । तमे॒व म॑न्ये नृ॒पतिं॒ जना॑नां॒ यः प्र॑थ॒मो दक्षि॑णामावि॒वाय॑
shlokas.transliteration: dákṣiṇā-vān ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ hūtáḥ ǀ eti ǀ dákṣiṇā-vān ǀ grāma-nī́ḥ ǀ ágram ǀ eti ǀtám ǀ evá ǀ manye ǀ nṛ-pátim ǀ jánānām ǀ yáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ ā-vivā́ya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(ThePaṇis). These are the cows which you, auspiciousSaramā, coming to the extremities of thesky, demand. Who will give them up to you without a combat? And our weapons are sharp.”

shlokas.sanskrit: तमे॒व ऋषिं॒ तमु॑ ब्र॒ह्माण॑माहुर्यज्ञ॒न्यं॑ साम॒गामु॑क्थ॒शास॑म् । स शु॒क्रस्य॑ त॒न्वो॑ वेद ति॒स्रो यः प्र॑थ॒मो दक्षि॑णया र॒राध॑
shlokas.transliteration: tám ǀ evá ǀ ṛ́ṣim ǀ tám ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ brahmā́ṇam ǀ āhuḥ ǀ yajña-nyám ǀ sāma-gā́m ǀ uktha-śásam ǀsáḥ ǀ śukrásya ǀ tanváḥ ǀ veda ǀ tisráḥ ǀ yáḥ ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ dákṣiṇayā ǀ rarā́dha ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Saramā). Your words,Paṇis, are not in the plural ce of armies; your sinful bodies will not be equal toarrows. Let your path be difficult to follow, letBṛhaspatishow no favour to either (your words or your person ns).”

shlokas.sanskrit: दक्षि॒णाश्वं॒ दक्षि॑णा॒ गां द॑दाति॒ दक्षि॑णा च॒न्द्रमु॒त यद्धिर॑ण्यम् । दक्षि॒णान्नं॑ वनुते॒ यो न॑ आ॒त्मा दक्षि॑णां॒ वर्म॑ कृणुते विजा॒नन्
shlokas.transliteration: dákṣiṇā ǀ áśvam ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ gā́m ǀ dadāti ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ candrám ǀ utá ǀ yát ǀ híraṇyam ǀdákṣiṇā ǀ ánnam ǀ vanute ǀ yáḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ ātmā́ ǀ dákṣiṇām ǀ várma ǀ kṛṇute ǀ vi-jānán ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(ThePaṇis). This treasure,Saramā, secured in the mountain is composed of cows, horses andriches; the Paṇis protect it who are good watchers; you have come to this lonely spot in vain.”

shlokas.sanskrit: न भो॒जा म॑म्रु॒र्न न्य॒र्थमी॑यु॒र्न रि॑ष्यन्ति॒ न व्य॑थन्ते ह भो॒जाः । इ॒दं यद्विश्वं॒ भुव॑नं॒ स्व॑श्चै॒तत्सर्वं॒ दक्षि॑णैभ्यो ददाति
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ mamruḥ ǀ ná ǀ ni-arthám ǀ īyuḥ ǀ ná ǀ riṣyanti ǀ ná ǀ vyathante ǀ ha ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀidám ǀ yát ǀ víśvam ǀ bhúvanam ǀ sváḥ ǀ ca ǀ etát ǀ sárvam ǀ dákṣiṇā ǀ ebhyaḥ ǀ dadāti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Saramā). Excited by theSoma, the Ṛṣis, theAṅgirasasof the nine months' rite, headed byAyasya,will come here; they will partition this herd of cattle, then thePaṇiswill retract their words.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भो॒जा जि॑ग्युः सुर॒भिं योनि॒मग्रे॑ भो॒जा जि॑ग्युर्व॒ध्वं१॒॑ या सु॒वासा॑: । भो॒जा जि॑ग्युरन्त॒:पेयं॒ सुरा॑या भो॒जा जि॑ग्यु॒र्ये अहू॑ताः प्र॒यन्ति॑
shlokas.transliteration: bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ surabhím ǀ yónim ǀ ágre ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ vadhvám ǀ yā́ ǀ su-vā́sāḥ ǀbhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ antaḥ-péyam ǀ súrāyāḥ ǀ bhojā́ḥ ǀ jigyuḥ ǀ yé ǀ áhūtāḥ ǀ pra-yánti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(ThePaṇis). You have indeed come here,Saramā, constrained by divine power; we will make youour sister, do not return, we will share the cattle with you auspicious one.”

shlokas.sanskrit: भो॒जायाश्वं॒ सं मृ॑जन्त्या॒शुं भो॒जाया॑स्ते क॒न्या॒३॒॑ शुम्भ॑माना । भो॒जस्ये॒दं पु॑ष्क॒रिणी॑व॒ वेश्म॒ परि॑ष्कृतं देवमा॒नेव॑ चि॒त्रम्
shlokas.transliteration: bhojā́ya ǀ áśvam ǀ sám ǀ mṛjanti ǀ āśúm ǀ bhojā́ya ǀ āste ǀ kanyā́ ǀ śúmbhamānā ǀbhojásya ǀ idám ǀ puṣkaríṇī-iva ǀ véśma ǀ pári-kṛtam ǀ devamānā́-iva ǀ citrám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(Saramā). I recognize not fraternity nor sisterhood;Indraand the terribleAṅgirasasknow (mykindred); my (masters) desiring the cattle overshadowed (yoru habitation) when I came; depart hence,Paṇisto adistant (spot).”

shlokas.sanskrit: भो॒जमश्वा॑: सुष्ठु॒वाहो॑ वहन्ति सु॒वृद्रथो॑ वर्तते॒ दक्षि॑णायाः । भो॒जं दे॑वासोऽवता॒ भरे॑षु भो॒जः शत्रू॑न्त्समनी॒केषु॒ जेता॑
shlokas.transliteration: bhojám ǀ áśvāḥ ǀ suṣṭhu-vā́haḥ ǀ vahanti ǀ su-vṛ́t ǀ ráthaḥ ǀ vartate ǀ dákṣiṇāyāḥ ǀbhojám ǀ devāsaḥ ǀ avata ǀ bháreṣu ǀ bhojáḥ ǀ śátrūn ǀ sam-anīkéṣu ǀ jétā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Go hence,Paṇis, to a far-off distant (spot), let the cattle come forth in due order bursting through (thedoor) the concealed cattle whichBṛhaspati, theSoma, the grinding stones and the wise Ṛṣis have found.”

shlokas.sanskrit: किमि॒च्छन्ती॑ स॒रमा॒ प्रेदमा॑नड्दू॒रे ह्यध्वा॒ जगु॑रिः परा॒चैः । कास्मेहि॑ति॒: का परि॑तक्म्यासीत्क॒थं र॒साया॑ अतर॒: पयां॑सि
shlokas.transliteration: kím ǀ icchántī ǀ sarámā ǀ prá ǀ idám ǀ ānaṭ ǀ dūré ǀ hí ǀ ádhvā ǀ jáguriḥ ǀ parācáiḥ ǀkā́ ǀ asmé-hitiḥ ǀ kā́ ǀ pári-takmyā ǀ āsīt ǀ kathám ǀ rasā́yāḥ ǀ ataraḥ ǀ páyāṃsi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “(ThePaṇis). With what intention hasSaramācome to this plural ce? Verily the way is long and difficultto be traversed by the person vering. What is the motive of your coming to us? What sort of wandering was yours?How have you crossed the waters of theRasā?”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॑स्य दू॒तीरि॑षि॒ता च॑रामि म॒ह इ॒च्छन्ती॑ पणयो नि॒धीन्व॑: । अ॒ति॒ष्कदो॑ भि॒यसा॒ तन्न॑ आव॒त्तथा॑ र॒साया॑ अतरं॒ पयां॑सि
shlokas.transliteration: índrasya ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ iṣitā́ ǀ carāmi ǀ maháḥ ǀ icchántī ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ ni-dhī́n ǀ vaḥ ǀati-skádaḥ ǀ bhiyásā ǀ tám ǀ naḥ ǀ āvat ǀ táthā ǀ rasā́yāḥ ǀ ataram ǀ páyāṃsi ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: की॒दृङ्ङिन्द्र॑: सरमे॒ का दृ॑शी॒का यस्ये॒दं दू॒तीरस॑रः परा॒कात् । आ च॒ गच्छा॑न्मि॒त्रमे॑ना दधा॒माथा॒ गवां॒ गोप॑तिर्नो भवाति
shlokas.transliteration: kīdṛ́ṅ ǀ índraḥ ǀ sarame ǀ kā́ ǀ dṛśīkā́ ǀ yásya ǀ idám ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ ásaraḥ ǀ parākā́t ǀā́ ǀ ca ǀ gácchāt ǀ mitrám ǀ ena ǀ dadhāma ǀ átha ǀ gávām ǀ gó-patiḥ ǀ naḥ ǀ bhavāti ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: नाहं तं वे॑द॒ दभ्यं॒ दभ॒त्स यस्ये॒दं दू॒तीरस॑रं परा॒कात् । न तं गू॑हन्ति स्र॒वतो॑ गभी॒रा ह॒ता इन्द्रे॑ण पणयः शयध्वे
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ tám ǀ veda ǀ dábhyam ǀ dábhat ǀ sáḥ ǀ yásya ǀ idám ǀ dūtī́ḥ ǀ ásaram ǀ parākā́t ǀná ǀ tám ǀ gūhanti ǀ sravátaḥ ǀ gabhīrā́ḥ ǀ hatā́ḥ ǀ índreṇa ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ śayadhve ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: इ॒मा गाव॑: सरमे॒ या ऐच्छ॒: परि॑ दि॒वो अन्ता॑न्त्सुभगे॒ पत॑न्ती । कस्त॑ एना॒ अव॑ सृजा॒दयु॑ध्व्यु॒तास्माक॒मायु॑धा सन्ति ति॒ग्मा
shlokas.transliteration: imā́ḥ ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ sarame ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ áicchaḥ ǀ pári ǀ diváḥ ǀ ántān ǀ su-bhage ǀ pátantī ǀkáḥ ǀ te ǀ enāḥ ǀ áva ǀ sṛjāt ǀ áyudhvī ǀ utá ǀ asmā́kam ǀ ā́yudhā ǀ santi ǀ tigmā́ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒से॒न्या व॑: पणयो॒ वचां॑स्यनिष॒व्यास्त॒न्व॑: सन्तु पा॒पीः । अधृ॑ष्टो व॒ एत॒वा अ॑स्तु॒ पन्था॒ बृह॒स्पति॑र्व उभ॒या न मृ॑ळात्
shlokas.transliteration: asenyā́ ǀ vaḥ ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ vácāṃsi ǀ aniṣavyā́ḥ ǀ tanváḥ ǀ santu ǀ pāpī́ḥ ǀádhṛṣṭaḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ étavái ǀ astu ǀ pánthāḥ ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ vaḥ ǀ ubhayā́ ǀ ná ǀ mṛḷāt ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: अ॒यं नि॒धिः स॑रमे॒ अद्रि॑बुध्नो॒ गोभि॒रश्वे॑भि॒र्वसु॑भि॒र्न्यृ॑ष्टः । रक्ष॑न्ति॒ तं प॒णयो॒ ये सु॑गो॒पा रेकु॑ प॒दमल॑क॒मा ज॑गन्थ
shlokas.transliteration: ayám ǀ ni-dhíḥ ǀ sarame ǀ ádri-budhnaḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ áśvebhiḥ ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ ní-ṛṣṭaḥ ǀrákṣanti ǀ tám ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ yé ǀ su-gopā́ḥ ǀ réku ǀ padám ǀ álakam ǀ ā́ ǀ jagantha ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: एह ग॑म॒न्नृष॑य॒: सोम॑शिता अ॒यास्यो॒ अङ्गि॑रसो॒ नव॑ग्वाः । त ए॒तमू॒र्वं वि भ॑जन्त॒ गोना॒मथै॒तद्वच॑: प॒णयो॒ वम॒न्नित्
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ ihá ǀ gaman ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ sóma-śitāḥ ǀ ayā́syaḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ náva-gvāḥ ǀté ǀ etám ǀ ūrvám ǀ ví ǀ bhajanta ǀ gónām ǀ átha ǀ etát ǀ vácaḥ ǀ paṇáyaḥ ǀ váman ǀ ít ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: ए॒वा च॒ त्वं स॑रम आज॒गन्थ॒ प्रबा॑धिता॒ सह॑सा॒ दैव्ये॑न । स्वसा॑रं त्वा कृणवै॒ मा पुन॑र्गा॒ अप॑ ते॒ गवां॑ सुभगे भजाम
shlokas.transliteration: evá ǀ ca ǀ tvám ǀ sarame ǀ ā-jagántha ǀ prá-bādhitā ǀ sáhasā ǀ dáivyena ǀsvásāram ǀ tvā ǀ kṛṇavai ǀ mā́ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ gāḥ ǀ ápa ǀ te ǀ gávām ǀ su-bhage ǀ bhajāma ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: नाहं वे॑द भ्रातृ॒त्वं नो स्व॑सृ॒त्वमिन्द्रो॑ विदु॒रङ्गि॑रसश्च घो॒राः । गोका॑मा मे अच्छदय॒न्यदाय॒मपात॑ इत पणयो॒ वरी॑यः
shlokas.transliteration: ná ǀ ahám ǀ veda ǀ bhrātṛ-tvám ǀ nó íti ǀ svasṛ-tvám ǀ índraḥ ǀ viduḥ ǀ áṅgirasaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ghorā́ḥ ǀgó-kāmāḥ ǀ me ǀ acchadayan ǀ yát ǀ ā́yam ǀ ápa ǀ átaḥ ǀ ita ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ várīyaḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: दू॒रमि॑त पणयो॒ वरी॑य॒ उद्गावो॑ यन्तु मिन॒तीॠ॒तेन॑ । बृह॒स्पति॒र्या अवि॑न्द॒न्निगू॑ळ्हा॒: सोमो॒ ग्रावा॑ण॒ ऋष॑यश्च॒ विप्रा॑:
shlokas.transliteration: dūrám ǀ ita ǀ paṇayaḥ ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ út ǀ gā́vaḥ ǀ yantu ǀ minatī́ḥ ǀ ṛténa ǀbṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ yā́ḥ ǀ ávindat ǀ ní-gūḷhāḥ ǀ sómaḥ ǀ grā́vāṇaḥ ǀ ṛ́ṣayaḥ ǀ ca ǀ víprāḥ ǁ

shlokas.sanskrit: ते॑ऽवदन्प्रथ॒मा ब्र॑ह्मकिल्बि॒षेऽकू॑पारः सलि॒लो मा॑त॒रिश्वा॑ । वी॒ळुह॑रा॒स्तप॑ उ॒ग्रो म॑यो॒भूरापो॑ दे॒वीः प्र॑थम॒जा ऋ॒तेन॑
shlokas.transliteration: té ǀ avadan ǀ prathamā́ḥ ǀ brahma-kilbiṣé ǀ ákūpāraḥ ǀ saliláḥ ǀ mātaríśvā ǀvīḷú-harāḥ ǀ tápaḥ ǀ ugráḥ ǀ mayaḥ-bhū́ḥ ǀ ā́paḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ prathama-jā́ḥ ǀ ṛténa ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “These spoke first aboutBrahmā's sin, the boundless (sun), the water- god (Varuṇa), the wind-god(Vāyu), the fierce, wide-consuming fire, the source of happiness, (Soma), the divine waters, the first-born sonsof the truthful (Brahmā).”

shlokas.sanskrit: सोमो॒ राजा॑ प्रथ॒मो ब्र॑ह्मजा॒यां पुन॒: प्राय॑च्छ॒दहृ॑णीयमानः । अ॒न्व॒र्ति॒ता वरु॑णो मि॒त्र आ॑सीद॒ग्निर्होता॑ हस्त॒गृह्या नि॑नाय
shlokas.transliteration: sómaḥ ǀ rā́jā ǀ prathamáḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ púnaríti ǀ prá ǀ ayacchat ǀ áhṛṇīyamānaḥ ǀanu-artitā́ ǀ váruṇaḥ ǀ mitráḥ ǀ āsīt ǀ agníḥ ǀ hótā ǀ hasta-gṛ́hya ǀ ā́ ǀ nināya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “First, the royalSoma, without being ashamed, restoredBrahmā's wife (toBṛhaspati),Varuṇawasthe inviter, andMitra,Agnias the ministrant priest taking her by thehand, led her (to her husband).”

shlokas.sanskrit: हस्ते॑नै॒व ग्रा॒ह्य॑ आ॒धिर॑स्या ब्रह्मजा॒येयमिति॒ चेदवो॑चन् । न दू॒ताय॑ प्र॒ह्ये॑ तस्थ ए॒षा तथा॑ रा॒ष्ट्रं गु॑पि॒तं क्ष॒त्रिय॑स्य
shlokas.transliteration: hástena ǀ evá ǀ grāhyáḥ ǀ ā-dhíḥ ǀ asyāḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́ ǀ iyám ǀ íti ǀ ca ǀ ít ǀ ávocan ǀná ǀ dūtā́ya ǀ pra-hyé ǀ tasthe ǀ eṣā́ ǀ táthā ǀ rāṣṭrám ǀ gupitám ǀ kṣatríyasya ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “And (the gods) said (toBṛhaspati), "This plural dge of hers is to be taken by thehand, this is the wife ofBrahmā; she has not made herself known to the messenger sent (to seek her), so is the kingdom of a kṣatriyaprotected".”

shlokas.sanskrit: दे॒वा ए॒तस्या॑मवदन्त॒ पूर्वे॑ सप्तऋ॒षय॒स्तप॑से॒ ये नि॑षे॒दुः । भी॒मा जा॒या ब्रा॑ह्म॒णस्योप॑नीता दु॒र्धां द॑धाति पर॒मे व्यो॑मन्
shlokas.transliteration: devā́ḥ ǀ etásyām ǀ avadanta ǀ pū́rve ǀ sapta-ṛṣáyaḥ ǀ tápase ǀ yé ǀ ni-sedúḥ ǀbhīmā́ ǀ jāyā́ ǀ brāhmaṇásya ǀ úpa-nītā ǀ duḥ-dhā́m ǀ dadhāti ǀ paramé ǀ ví-oman ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The ancient deities spoke about her, the seven Ṛṣis who were engaged in penance. The terrible wifeofBrahmahas been brought back (to her husband); (penance) elevates into the highest heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ब्र॒ह्म॒चा॒री च॑रति॒ वेवि॑ष॒द्विष॒: स दे॒वानां॑ भव॒त्येक॒मङ्ग॑म् । तेन॑ जा॒यामन्व॑विन्द॒द्बृह॒स्पति॒: सोमे॑न नी॒तां जु॒ह्वं१॒॑ न दे॑वाः
shlokas.transliteration: brahma-cārī́ ǀ carati ǀ véviṣat ǀ víṣaḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ bhavati ǀ ékam ǀ áṅgam ǀténa ǀ jāyā́m ǀ ánu ǀ avindat ǀ bṛ́haspátiḥ ǀ sómena ǀ nītā́m ǀ juhvám ǀ ná ǀ devāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “He leads the life of aBrahmacārin, even adoring all the gods; he becomes a portion of the gods;therefore,Bṛhaspatiobtained his wife (formerly) brought him bySoma, as the gods receive an offering.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पुन॒र्वै दे॒वा अ॑ददु॒: पुन॑र्मनु॒ष्या॑ उ॒त । राजा॑नः स॒त्यं कृ॑ण्वा॒ना ब्र॑ह्मजा॒यां पुन॑र्ददुः
shlokas.transliteration: púnaḥ ǀ vái ǀ devā́ḥ ǀ adaduḥ ǀ púnaḥ ǀ manuṣyā́ḥ ǀ utá ǀrā́jānaḥ ǀ satyám ǀ kṛṇvānā́ḥ ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ púnaḥ ǀ daduḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods gave her back again, men also gave her back, and kings confirming (the gift) gaveBrahmā's wife back again.”

shlokas.sanskrit: पु॒न॒र्दाय॑ ब्रह्मजा॒यां कृ॒त्वी दे॒वैर्नि॑किल्बि॒षम् । ऊर्जं॑ पृथि॒व्या भ॒क्त्वायो॑रुगा॒यमुपा॑सते
shlokas.transliteration: punaḥ-dā́ya ǀ brahma-jāyā́m ǀ kṛtvī́ ǀ deváiḥ ǀ ni-kilbiṣám ǀū́rjam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ bhaktvā́ya ǀ uru-gāyám ǀ úpa ǀ āsate ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The gods having given backBrahmā's wife, and made her free from sin, having partaken of the foodof the earth, sat down to (the sacrifice of) the widely hymnedBṛhaspati.”

shlokas.sanskrit: समि॑द्धो अ॒द्य मनु॑षो दुरो॒णे दे॒वो दे॒वान्य॑जसि जातवेदः । आ च॒ वह॑ मित्रमहश्चिकि॒त्वान्त्वं दू॒तः क॒विर॑सि॒ प्रचे॑ताः
shlokas.transliteration: sám-iddhaḥ ǀ adyá ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ duroṇé ǀ deváḥ ǀ devā́n ǀ yajasi ǀ jāta-vedaḥ ǀā́ ǀ ca ǀ váha ǀ mitra-mahaḥ ǀ cikitvā́n ǀ tvám ǀ dūtáḥ ǀ kavíḥ ǀ asi ǀ prá-cetāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Kindled today,Jātavedas, in the dwelling of the worshipper, you who are divine, sacrifice to the godṣBear (the oblation), you who respect your friends, who are intelligent; you are the wise, far-seeing messenger (ofthe gods).”

shlokas.sanskrit: तनू॑नपात्प॒थ ऋ॒तस्य॒ याना॒न्मध्वा॑ सम॒ञ्जन्त्स्व॑दया सुजिह्व । मन्मा॑नि धी॒भिरु॒त य॒ज्ञमृ॒न्धन्दे॑व॒त्रा च॑ कृणुह्यध्व॒रं न॑:
shlokas.transliteration: tánū-napāt ǀ patháḥ ǀ ṛtásya ǀ yā́nān ǀ mádhvā ǀ sam-añján ǀ svadaya ǀ su-jihva ǀmánmāni ǀ dhībhíḥ ǀ utá ǀ yajñám ǀ ṛndhán ǀ deva-trā́ ǀ ca ǀ kṛṇuhi ǀ adhvarám ǀ naḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Pure-tonguedTanūnapāt, flavour the paths of the sacrifice which lead (to success), moisteningthem with the sweet (Soma); elevating our praises and our rite by understanding, convey our sacrifice to thegods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ॒जुह्वा॑न॒ ईड्यो॒ वन्द्य॒श्चा या॑ह्यग्ने॒ वसु॑भिः स॒जोषा॑: । त्वं दे॒वाना॑मसि यह्व॒ होता॒ स ए॑नान्यक्षीषि॒तो यजी॑यान्
shlokas.transliteration: ā-júhvānaḥ ǀ ī́ḍyaḥ ǀ vándyaḥ ǀ ca ǀ ā́ ǀ yāhi ǀ agne ǀ vásu-bhiḥ ǀ sa-jóṣāḥ ǀtvám ǀ devā́nām ǀ asi ǀ yahva ǀ hótā ǀ sáḥ ǀ enān ǀ yakṣi ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yájīyān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Agni, who are the invoker (of the gods), and are to be solicited and praised, come, being propitiated,along with theVasus; you, O mighty (Agni), are the invoker of the gods; do you, who are most entitled to worship,solicited by us, offer them adoration.”

shlokas.sanskrit: प्रा॒चीनं॑ ब॒र्हिः प्र॒दिशा॑ पृथि॒व्या वस्तो॑र॒स्या वृ॑ज्यत॒र अग्रे॒ अह्ना॑म् । व्यु॑ प्रथते वित॒रं वरी॑यो दे॒वेभ्यो॒ अदि॑तये स्यो॒नम्
shlokas.transliteration: prācī́nam ǀ barhíḥ ǀ pra-díśā ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ vástoḥ ǀ asyā́ḥ ǀ vṛjyate ǀ ágre ǀ áhnām ǀví ǀ ūṃ íti ǀ prathate ǀ vi-tarám ǀ várīyaḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ áditaye ǀ syonám ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “In the beginning of the day the sacred grass, pointing eastwards, is strewn with the prescribed (text)as a covering for the earth (of the altar); they spread it out far and wide as a plural asant (seat) for the gods andAditi.”

shlokas.sanskrit: व्यच॑स्वतीरुर्वि॒या वि श्र॑यन्तां॒ पति॑भ्यो॒ न जन॑य॒: शुम्भ॑मानाः । देवी॑र्द्वारो बृहतीर्विश्वमिन्वा दे॒वेभ्यो॑ भवत सुप्राय॒णाः
shlokas.transliteration: vyácasvatīḥ ǀ urviyā́ ǀ ví ǀ śrayantām ǀ páti-bhyaḥ ǀ ná ǀ jánayaḥ ǀ śúmbhamānāḥ ǀdévīḥ ǀ dvāraḥ ǀ bṛhatīḥ ǀ viśvam-invāḥ ǀ devébhyaḥ ǀ bhavata ǀ supra-ayanā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Expanding wide, let the doors give access as gracefully decorated wives give access to theirhusbands, divine doors, spacious and admitting all, be easy of entry for the gods.”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ सु॒ष्वय॑न्ती यज॒ते उपा॑के उ॒षासा॒नक्ता॑ सदतां॒ नि योनौ॑ । दि॒व्ये योष॑णे बृह॒ती सु॑रु॒क्मे अधि॒ श्रियं॑ शुक्र॒पिशं॒ दधा॑ने
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ susváyantī íti ǀ yajaté íti ǀ úpāke íti ǀ uṣásānáktā ǀ sadatām ǀ ní ǀ yónau ǀdivyé íti ǀ yóṣaṇe íti ǀ bṛhatī́ íti ǀ surukmé íti su-rukmé ǀ ádhi ǀ śríyam ǀ śukra-píśam ǀ dádhāne íti ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “May the adorable Day and Night, the givers of sound repose, having approached, sit down in theplace (of sacrifice), two divine feminine les, majestic and richly ornamented, bearing beauty of a bright form.”

shlokas.sanskrit: दैव्या॒ होता॑रा प्रथ॒मा सु॒वाचा॒ मिमा॑ना य॒ज्ञं मनु॑षो॒ यज॑ध्यै । प्र॒चो॒दय॑न्ता वि॒दथे॑षु का॒रू प्रा॒चीनं॒ ज्योति॑: प्र॒दिशा॑ दि॒शन्ता॑
shlokas.transliteration: dáivyā ǀ hótārā ǀ prathamā́ ǀ su-vā́cā ǀ mímānā ǀ yajñám ǀ mánuṣaḥ ǀ yájadhyai ǀpra-codáyantā ǀ vidátheṣu ǀ kārū́ íti ǀ prācī́nam ǀ jyótiḥ ǀ pra-díśā ǀ diśántā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Divine ministers, prior (to those of earth), repeaters of pious praise, instrumental tuting the sacrifice at whichmen are to worship, (sit down) stimulating (the priests) at the sacrifices, makers (of praises), indicating theeastern fire with the prescribed (text).”

shlokas.sanskrit: आ नो॑ य॒ज्ञं भार॑ती॒ तूय॑मे॒त्विळा॑ मनु॒ष्वदि॒ह चे॒तय॑न्ती । ति॒स्रो दे॒वीर्ब॒र्हिरेदं स्यो॒नं सर॑स्वती॒ स्वप॑सः सदन्तु
shlokas.transliteration: ā́ ǀ naḥ ǀ yajñám ǀ bhā́ratī ǀ tū́yam ǀ etu ǀ íḷā ǀ manuṣvát ǀ ihá ǀ cetáyantī ǀtisráḥ ǀ devī́ḥ ǀ barhíḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ idám ǀ syonám ǀ sárasvatī ǀ su-ápasaḥ ǀ sadantu ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “MayBhāratīcome quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḷā thinking (of what she has to do), like a humanbeing; maySarasvatīalso-- the three gracious goddesses, sit down upon this plural asant sacred grass.”

shlokas.sanskrit: य इ॒मे द्यावा॑पृथि॒वी जनि॑त्री रू॒पैरपिं॑श॒द्भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ । तम॒द्य हो॑तरिषि॒तो यजी॑यान्दे॒वं त्वष्टा॑रमि॒ह य॑क्षि वि॒द्वान्
shlokas.transliteration: yáḥ ǀ imé íti ǀ dyā́vāpṛthivī́ íti ǀ jánitrī íti ǀ rūpáiḥ ǀ ápiṃśat ǀ bhúvanāni ǀ víśvā ǀtám ǀ adyá ǀ hotaḥ ǀ iṣitáḥ ǀ yájīyān ǀ devám ǀ tváṣṭāram ǀ ihá ǀ yakṣi ǀ vidvā́n ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “To the divineTvaṣṭā, who decked the parental heaven and earth and all the worlds with livingforms, to him, O priest, who are venerable and wise, being solicited byu us, offer oblation here today.”

shlokas.sanskrit: उ॒पाव॑सृज॒ त्मन्या॑ सम॒ञ्जन्दे॒वानां॒ पाथ॑ ऋतु॒था ह॒वींषि॑ । वन॒स्पति॑: शमि॒ता दे॒वो अ॒ग्निः स्वद॑न्तु ह॒व्यं मधु॑ना घृ॒तेन॑
shlokas.transliteration: upa-ávasṛja ǀ tmányā ǀ sam-añján ǀ devā́nām ǀ pā́thaḥ ǀ ṛtu-thā́ ǀ havī́ṃṣi ǀvánaspátiḥ ǀ śamitā́ ǀ deváḥ ǀ agníḥ ǀ svádantu ǀ havyám ǀ mádhunā ǀ ghṛténa ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Offer of your own will in due season the food (and other) oblations of the gods besmearing it. LetVanaspati,Śamitā, the divineAgni, sweeten the oblation with honey and butter.”

shlokas.sanskrit: स॒द्यो जा॒तो व्य॑मिमीत य॒ज्ञम॒ग्निर्दे॒वाना॑मभवत्पुरो॒गाः । अ॒स्य होतु॑: प्र॒दिश्यृ॒तस्य॑ वा॒चि स्वाहा॑कृतं ह॒विर॑दन्तु दे॒वाः
shlokas.transliteration: sadyáḥ ǀ jātáḥ ǀ ví ǀ amimīta ǀ yajñám ǀ agníḥ ǀ devā́nām ǀ abhavat ǀ puraḥ-gā́ḥ ǀasyá ǀ hótuḥ ǀ pra-díśi ǀ ṛtásya ǀ vācí ǀ svā́hā-kṛtam ǀ havíḥ ǀ adantu ǀ devā́ḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “As soon as he was born,Agniconstructed a sacrifice, he was the preceder of the gods; may the godspartake of the oblation presented with thesvāhāthrough the voice of him thehotāof the sacrifice at theeastern station.”

shlokas.sanskrit: मनी॑षिण॒: प्र भ॑रध्वं मनी॒षां यथा॑यथा म॒तय॒: सन्ति॑ नृ॒णाम् । इन्द्रं॑ स॒त्यैरेर॑यामा कृ॒तेभि॒: स हि वी॒रो गि॑र्वण॒स्युर्विदा॑नः
shlokas.transliteration: mánīṣiṇaḥ ǀ prá ǀ bharadhvam ǀ manīṣā́m ǀ yáthā-yathā ǀ matáyaḥ ǀ sánti ǀ nṛṇā́m ǀíndram ǀ satyáiḥ ǀ ā́ ǀ īrayāma ǀ kṛtébhiḥ ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ vīráḥ ǀ girvaṇasyúḥ ǀ vídānaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Offer, worshippers, toIndrapraise agreeable to the thoughts of men; let us incite Indra hither withsincere adoration, for he, the hero, capable (of granting our wishes, is desirous of laudation.”

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋ॒तस्य॒ हि सद॑सो धी॒तिरद्यौ॒त्सं गा॑र्ष्टे॒यो वृ॑ष॒भो गोभि॑रानट् । उद॑तिष्ठत्तवि॒षेणा॒ रवे॑ण म॒हान्ति॑ चि॒त्सं वि॑व्याचा॒ रजां॑सि
shlokas.transliteration: ṛtásya ǀ hí ǀ sádasaḥ ǀ dhītíḥ ǀ ádyaut ǀ sám ǀ gārṣṭeyáḥ ǀ vṛṣabháḥ ǀ góbhiḥ ǀ ānaṭ ǀút ǀ atiṣṭhat ǀ taviṣéṇa ǀ ráveṇa ǀ mahā́nti ǀ cit ǀ sám ǀ vivyāca ǀ rájāṃsi ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Sustainer of the abode of the water, (the firmament), he shone brightly; the bull, the offspring of a cowwhich has only borne once, met the cows, with a loud roar he sprung up, he pervaded the vast worlds.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्र॒: किल॒ श्रुत्या॑ अ॒स्य वे॑द॒ स हि जि॒ष्णुः प॑थि॒कृत्सूर्या॑य । आन्मेनां॑ कृ॒ण्वन्नच्यु॑तो॒ भुव॒द्गोः पति॑र्दि॒वः स॑न॒जा अप्र॑तीतः
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ kíla ǀ śrútyai ǀ asyá ǀ veda ǀ sáḥ ǀ hí ǀ jiṣṇúḥ ǀ pathi-kṛ́t ǀ sū́ryāya ǀā́t ǀ ménām ǀ kṛṇván ǀ ácyutaḥ ǀ bhúvat ǀ góḥ ǀ pátiḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ sana-jā́ḥ ǀ áprati-itaḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “On hearing our praiseIndraknows our wishes; victorious, he opens a path for the sun; making himselfMenā, he came (to the sacrifice), he was unassailable, the lord of cattle, (the lord) of heaven, eternal,unsurpassed.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ म॒ह्ना म॑ह॒तो अ॑र्ण॒वस्य॑ व्र॒तामि॑ना॒दङ्गि॑रोभिर्गृणा॒नः । पु॒रूणि॑ चि॒न्नि त॑ताना॒ रजां॑सि दा॒धार॒ यो ध॒रुणं॑ स॒त्यता॑ता
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ mahnā́ ǀ mahatáḥ ǀ arṇavásya ǀ vratā́ ǀ amināt ǀ áṅgiraḥ-bhiḥ ǀ gṛṇānáḥ ǀpurū́ṇi ǀ cit ǀ ní ǀ tatāna ǀ rájāṃsi ǀ dādhā́ra ǀ yáḥ ǀ dharúṇam ǀ satyá-tātā ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Praised by theAṅgirasas,Indrahas by his might injured the functions of the mighty cloud; he has sentdown abundant rains, he who (at other times) has supported the supporting (cloud) in heaven.”

shlokas.sanskrit: इन्द्रो॑ दि॒वः प्र॑ति॒मानं॑ पृथि॒व्या विश्वा॑ वेद॒ सव॑ना॒ हन्ति॒ शुष्ण॑म् । म॒हीं चि॒द्द्यामात॑नो॒त्सूर्ये॑ण चा॒स्कम्भ॑ चि॒त्कम्भ॑नेन॒ स्कभी॑यान्
shlokas.transliteration: índraḥ ǀ diváḥ ǀ prati-mā́nam ǀ pṛthivyā́ḥ ǀ víśvā ǀ veda ǀ sávanā ǀ hánti ǀ śúṣṇam ǀmahī́m ǀ cit ǀ dyā́m ǀ ā́ ǀ atanot ǀ sū́ryeṇa ǀ cāskámbha ǀ cit ǀ skámbhanena ǀ skábhīyān ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “Indra, the counterpart of heaven and earth, is cognizant of all sacrifices, he is the slayer ofŚuṣṇa; hespread out the spacious heaven with the sun (to light it up); best of proppers, he propped up (the heaven) with aprop.”

shlokas.sanskrit: वज्रे॑ण॒ हि वृ॑त्र॒हा वृ॒त्रमस्त॒रदे॑वस्य॒ शूशु॑वानस्य मा॒याः । वि धृ॑ष्णो॒ अत्र॑ धृष॒ता ज॑घ॒न्थाथा॑भवो मघवन्बा॒ह्वो॑जाः
shlokas.transliteration: vájreṇa ǀ hí ǀ vṛtra-hā́ ǀ vṛtrám ǀ ástaḥ ǀ ádevasya ǀ śū́śuvānasya ǀ māyā́ḥ ǀví ǀ dhṛṣṇo íti ǀ átra ǀ dhṛṣatā́ ǀ jaghantha ǀ átha ǀ abhavaḥ ǀ magha-van ǀ bāhú-ojāḥ ǁ
shlokas.meaning_en: “The slayer ofVṛtra, you have laid him low with the thunderbolt; resoluteIndra, you have nowovercome by your powerful (bolt), the devices of the impious (asura), confiding in his own strength; you,Maghavan, were strong-armed.”
